name: Build the sequence from the main footage's properties
what: Premiere performs best when the sequence settings match most of the assets (frame aspect, PAR, frame rate, fields, audio rate, codec); Final Cut Pro sets the whole project from the first video clip added, so add a clip that matches the delivery first
how: read the main clip first: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,sample_aspect_ratio -of csv=p=0 main.mp4`, then set the HyperFrames root `data-width`/`data-height` to the delivery size (new HyperFrames videos default to 1920x1080 at 30 fps). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/conform-frame-sizes-and-rates-ver3363b44e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Lock the project frame rate before editing
what: Premiere locks the timebase once a sequence is created; Final Cut Pro warns that changing a project's frame rate can shift every edit point and cannot change it once the timeline has clips
how: decide fps first and keep one rate through the job; convert odd sources with the fps filter before editing, e.g. `ffmpeg -i H120.mp4 -vf fps=fps=25:round=down -an fd.mp4` (25 fps out). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/conform-frame-sizes-and-rates-ver3363b44e/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/final-cut-pro-project-settings-ver1b946a4ff/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Timebase by delivery region
what: Premiere's guidance: 24 for motion-picture film, 25 for PAL/SECAM video, 29.97 for NTSC video; a 23.976 preset needs the Custom editing mode
how: the ffmpeg fps filter has named rates for these: `fps=film` (24), `fps=pal` (25), `fps=ntsc` (30000/1001), `fps=ntsc_film` (24000/1001).

name: Drop-frame timecode for 29.97 material
what: Premiere: with NTSC assets use 30-fps drop-frame timecode so the displayed duration is accurate
how: burn a drop-frame counter with drawtext's timecode option (the doc gives the format hh:mm:ss[:;.]ff): `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf "fps=30000/1001,drawtext=timecode='00\:00\:00;00':rate=30000/1001:fontcolor=white:fontsize=28:x=20:y=20" -an -frames:v 5 tcd.mp4`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Give the program a start timecode
what: Resolve's new-timeline dialog defaults the start timecode to 01:00:00:00, and Final Cut Pro projects and compound clips have a Starting Timecode field
how: stamp it on the delivered file: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -c copy -timecode 01:00:00:00 tc.mov`, then check with `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream_tags=timecode -of csv=p=0 tc.mov` (prints 01:00:00:00). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-a-new-project-verdb79783e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Don't shrink the frame size to get smoother playback
what: Premiere: don't change the sequence frame size to compensate for slow playback; change the playback quality instead and set the final size at export
how: keep the root `data-width`/`data-height` at delivery size and preview with `npx hyperframes render --quality draft` (or Studio preview) instead of editing the canvas size.

name: Use timeline proxy resolution for heavy previews
what: Resolve's Timeline Proxy Resolution plays a 1920x1080 timeline at 960x540 (Half) or 480x270 (Quarter) without changing the project, separate from proxy media files
how: for a quick look at an ffmpeg composite, render a half-size review copy: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf scale=iw/2:-2 review.mp4`; the delivery render stays full size.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.8 "Improving Performance, Proxies, and the Render Cache", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Convert anamorphic pixels to square before compositing
what: Premiere's PAR table: 720x480 is D1/DV NTSC 0.91 (4:3) or 1.21 (16:9), 720x576 PAL 1.09/1.46, 1440x1080 HDV 1.33; images look distorted when non-square pixels are shown on square-pixel screens
how: check `sample_aspect_ratio` and resample to square pixels: `ffmpeg -i SD.mp4 -vf "scale=iw*sar:ih,setsar=1" -frames:v 1 sq.png` turned an 8:9 720x480 clip into 640x480 at 1:1. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Override a wrongly flagged pixel aspect
what: Premiere's Interpret Footage lets you 'Conform To' a different PAR when a file's flag is wrong, and says to fix PAR before frame aspect, because a wrong PAR causes a wrong frame aspect
how: re-flag without resampling: `ffmpeg -i SD.mp4 -vf setsar=1 -an -c:v libx264 par1.mp4` (ffprobe then reports 1:1). setsar only changes the flag; setdar/setsar doc: DAR = W/H x SAR. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Swap field order instead of guessing
what: Premiere's Interpret Footage offers No Fields (progressive), Upper Field First or Lower Field First; check camera docs or metadata before changing, and preview the result
how: ffmpeg's fieldorder shifts the picture a line to convert tff/bff and does nothing to frames not flagged interlaced; tested chain: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf "tinterlace=mode=interleave_top,setfield=tff,fieldorder=bff" -an -frames:v 10 fo.mp4`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Four spatial-conform choices for mismatched frame sizes
what: Final Cut Pro offers Fit (default, no crop, bars), Fill (crop the long side) and None (native size, cropped or surrounded by black); Resolve adds Stretch; Premiere's Properties panel has Fit to frame / Fill frame
how: Fit `scale=1280:720:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1280:720:-1:-1`; Fill `scale=1280:720:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1280:720`; None `pad=1280:720:-1:-1`; Stretch `scale=1280:720,setsar=1` (all four gave 1280x720 from a 720x480 clip). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/conform-frame-sizes-and-rates-ver3363b44e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.50 "Compositing and Transforms in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Treat high-frame-rate clips as slow motion on purpose
what: Final Cut Pro's Automatic Speed plays every frame of a 120 fps clip at the 30 fps project rate, so the action takes longer with no skipped or duplicated frames
how: `ffmpeg -i H120.mp4 -vf "setpts=4*PTS,fps=30" -an hfr.mp4`: a 1 s, 120-frame clip became 4 s with all 120 frames. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/change-clip-speed-ver40b00150/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Reinterpret a clip's frame rate (duration changes too)
what: Premiere's 'Assume this frame rate' changes the whole clip, audio included; a 10 s 24 fps clip set to 48 fps becomes 5 s
how: rescale input timestamps with `-itsscale`: `ffmpeg -itsscale 2 -i A.mp4 -c:v libx264 -an its.mp4` turned a 3 s clip into ~6 s. For one instance only, use setpts on that clip instead. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Choose floor or nearest when conforming frame rate
what: Final Cut Pro's Rate Conform offers Fast (Floor) (duplicates or rounds down, default) and Fast (Nearest Frame) (rounds up or down; fewer artifacts but may stutter), then frame blending and optical flow
how: the fps filter exposes the same rounding choice: `fps=fps=25:round=down` vs `fps=fps=25:round=near` (default is near). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/conform-frame-sizes-and-rates-ver3363b44e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Insert edit = split, add, ripple
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: An insert edit pushes everything after the edit point later; inserted in the middle of a clip, Final Cut Pro cuts that clip and moves its second half after the new clip (Premiere: comma key; FCP: W; Resolve F9)
how: ffmpeg: trim the host clip into two and concat with the new clip between: `[0:v]trim=0:1.5,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a1];...[1:v]trim=0:1,...[b];[0:v]trim=1.5:3,...[a2];[a1][x1][b][y][a2][x2]concat=n=3:v=1:a=1` (3 s + 1 s = 120 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/insert-clips-ver4e2eff6/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Overwrite edit keeps the program length
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Overwrite replaces frames for the incoming clip's duration and ripples nothing; in Final Cut Pro it works on a range, not clip boundaries (D; Premiere period key; Resolve F10)
how: keep A 0-1 s, B 1 s, A 2-3 s: `[0:v]trim=0:1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a1];[1:v]trim=0:1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[b];[0:v]trim=2:3,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a2];[a1][b][a2]concat=n=3:v=1:a=0` with the original audio mapped (90 frames out, same as in). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/overwrite-clips-ver4e30026/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Append = start after the previous clip
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Append (FCP E, Resolve Append to End Shift-F12) always puts the clip after the last clip, ignoring the playhead
how: in HyperFrames write `data-start="clipA + 0"` so the clip starts when clipA ends; `npx hyperframes timeline --json` resolved it to 3 s after a 3 s clipA. A typo silently resolves to 0, so snapshot it. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/append-clips-to-your-project-ver7a77f584/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Connect / place on top for B-roll and titles
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP connect (Q) attaches a clip above the primary storyline; Resolve's Place on Top always uses the first empty track above (video) or below (audio) and creates tracks; upper tracks cover lower ones except where alpha is transparent
how: HyperFrames paints by `z-index` (track index is only a lane), so give the overlay the highest z-index; in ffmpeg: `[1:v]scale=320:-2,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+1/TB[pip];[0:v][pip]overlay=x=W-w-20:y=20:enable='between(t,1,2)':eof_action=pass`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/connect-clips-ver7a77ef9e/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Backtimed edit (align the out point)
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Final Cut Pro's backtimed three-point edit (Shift-D overwrite, Shift-Q connect) lines the source end up with the timeline mark, e.g. to end exactly on a beat; Resolve's Close Up/Place On Top/Overwrite also backtime when only a timeline Out is set
how: start = out - duration; for a 1 s clip ending at 2.5 s: `[1:v]trim=0:1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+(2.5-1)/TB[b];[0:v][b]overlay=enable='between(t,1.5,2.5)':eof_action=pass`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/three-point-edit-examples-ver549f253e/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Three-point rule: which marks win
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: With source In+Out and a timeline In, the source marks set the duration; with source In and timeline In+Out, the timeline range sets it; source In+Out with only a timeline Out backtimes; FCP needs range selections for most three-point edits
how: write the rule into the edit list: duration = (timeline out - timeline in) if both are set, else (source out - source in); start = timeline in, or timeline out - duration when only an out is given.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/three-point-editing-guidelines-verf44671a73/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-three-point-editing-ver549f2208/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Fit to Fill (four-point edit retimes the clip)
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Fit to Fill uses all four marks and changes speed so a source range fills a timeline range; Resolve: it doesn't ripple; Premiere's Rate Stretch tool does the same by dragging; FCP has 'Replace with Retime to Fit'
how: speed factor = target/source: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf "setpts=PTS*(2/3)" -an -r 30 -t 2 ftf2.mp4` fit 3 s into exactly 60 frames (without `-t` it came out 62 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/replace-clips-ver4e2fcf0/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Replace from Start / Replace from End
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP replace options: Replace (source length, ripples), Replace from Start (source from its first frame, target length), Replace from End (source end aligned, target length); replace works on whole clips
how: from start: `ffmpeg -i B.mp4 -t 1.2 -an rfs.mp4`; from end: `ffmpeg -sseof -1.2 -i B.mp4 -an rfe.mp4` (both 36 frames for a 1.2 s slot). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/replace-clips-ver4e2fcf0/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Replace edit aligned on a matching frame
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Resolve's Replace (F11) uses the timeline clip's duration and lines up the frame under the Source playhead with the frame under the Timeline playhead, e.g. swapping a VFX version over the camera original
how: pick the source frame S that must sit at timeline time T inside a clip starting at C: new media start = S - (T - C); in HyperFrames set that as `data-media-start` and keep `data-start`/`data-duration`.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Ripple Overwrite swaps a clip and fixes the length
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Resolve's Ripple Overwrite substitutes the clip at the playhead (or an In/Out range) with a clip of a different length and ripples later clips to fill or make room
how: in HyperFrames change the clip's src/duration, then move every later clip by the length difference (GSAP-style `shiftChildren`, or `npx hyperframes timeline apply plan.json` with one move per clip, moving the last clip first).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Video-only and audio-only edits
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP Edit menu Video Only (Shift-2) / Audio Only (Shift-3) / All (Shift-1); Resolve Cut page has Audio Only and Video Only toggles
how: take one side of a source: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -an -c copy vo.mp4` (video stream only) and `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vn -c copy ao.m4a` (audio only). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-only-a-clips-video-or-audio-ver1632d091/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Close Up edit from a wide shot
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Resolve's Close Up edit adds the incoming clip at about 150% scale and repositions any detected face; meant for 4K-in-1080 or 8K-in-4K timelines so the punch-in loses no quality
how: a 150% punch-in is a crop of 1/1.5 of the frame scaled back: `crop=iw/1.5:ih/1.5,scale=1920:1080` (or tween `scale: 1.5` on a wrapper in HyperFrames); face finding needs a detector (see Missing tools).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Source overwrite for synced cameras
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Resolve's Source Overwrite (and 'Insert Selected Clips to Timeline Using Timecode') places a cutaway from another camera at the matching timecode, so it lands in sync automatically
how: with a known camera offset O (B started O s after A), the B frames for timeline range t1-t2 are B time t1-O to t2-O: `[1:v]trim=t1-O:t2-O,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+t1/TB` then overlay with `enable='between(t,t1,t2)'`.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Insert clips with handles for a quick montage
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Resolve's 'Insert Selected Clips to Timeline With Handles' trims the default handle length off each end so the default transition (Command-T) has media; no handles are added if a clip is shorter than the handles
how: trim each source to [handle, len-handle] when building the concat list, then join with xfade whose duration <= 2 x handle; for clips already cut tight, pad first with `tpad=stop_mode=clone` (see the insufficient-media skill).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.39 "Three- and Four-Point Editing", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.36 "Editing Basics", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Gap clip (slug) holds time
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP's gap clip (Option-W) is blank video and silent audio of any length, the film term is slug; it keeps timing and reserves space for a later clip
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=black:s=640x360:r=30:d=2 -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo -t 2 -shortest -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac gap.mp4` (60 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/insert-clips-ver4e2eff6/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Placeholder clips that say what goes there
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP's Placeholder generator (Option-Command-W) fills a gap with a hint of the final shot (close-up, wide, group...) and can show notes
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=gray:s=640x360:r=30:d=2 -vf "drawtext=text='WIDE SHOT - TBD':fontcolor=white:fontsize=36:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2" -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p ph.mp4`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-placeholders-verca9ea012/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Synthetic black, color and transparent clips
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Premiere makes Black Video, Color Matte and Transparent Video items sized to the sequence; empty track areas show black if nothing is below
how: black/color: `color=black:s=1920x1080:r=30:d=2`; transparent: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=black@0.0:s=640x360:r=30:d=1,format=rgba -c:v qtrle tr.mov` (ffprobe: argb). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Counting leader with a two-pop
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Premiere's Universal Counting Leader is 11 s, matched to the sequence size/rate, with options for a beep at the 2-second mark (two-pop) or at every second; used to check sync and playback
how: bars: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i smptehdbars=s=1280x720:r=30:d=2 -f lavfi -i sine=f=1000:d=2 ...`; a one-frame 1 kHz pop padded to 2 s: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=f=1000:d=0.0333 -af apad=whole_dur=2 pop.wav`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Know the default still duration
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP stills and freeze frames default to 4 s (Editing settings), layered graphics files to one minute; Change Duration (Control-D) resets many at once. HyperFrames gives an `` without `data-duration` 3 s
how: always write `data-duration` on images; ffmpeg still-to-clip: `ffmpeg -loop 1 -i st.png -t 4 -r 30 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p still.mp4` (120 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-still-images-verfc8a3df7/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/editing-settings-verb8e60d02/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Import a numbered image sequence at the right rate
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: Premiere sets the rate from Indeterminate Media Timebase and needs the same number of digits in every filename (file000.bmp, file001.bmp...)
how: the image2 demuxer default is 25 fps, so always give it: `ffmpeg -framerate 24 -i seq/f_%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p seq24.mp4` (30 frames -> 1.25 s). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Export an image sequence for finishing tools
section: Putting clips into the timeline (edit types)
what: FCP's Export Image Sequence writes sequentially numbered stills for compositing and grading apps (the destination must be added first)
how: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -t 1 seq/f_%04d.png` wrote 30 PNGs; zero-padded names keep the order. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/export-image-sequences-ver2732ab3b4/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Lift leaves a gap, extract closes it
what: Premiere Lift removes frames and leaves the gap; Extract/Ripple Delete closes it (and Extract removes sequence markers in that range); FCP Replace with Gap (Shift-Delete) keeps project timing
how: lift 1-2 s: `-vf "drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=iw:h=ih:color=black:t=fill:enable='between(t,1,2)'" -af "volume=0:enable='between(t,1,2)'"` (still 3 s); extract: `-vf "select='not(between(t,1,2))',setpts=N/FRAME_RATE/TB" -af "aselect='not(between(t,1,2))',asetpts=N/SR/TB"` (2 s). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/remove-clips-from-projects-verc5d34129/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Disable instead of delete
what: Premiere Clip > Enable, FCP V and Resolve D turn a clip off: it stays in place but doesn't play, render or export, and you can turn it back on
how: HyperFrames: add `data-hidden` (hidden in preview and render, reversible); lint stayed at 0 errors on a test project with a hidden clip. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/solo-or-disable-clips-ver4e2fbd2/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.38 "Modifying Clips", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Find gaps and flash frames before delivery
what: Premiere's Sequence Index flags flash frames in red; Resolve's Boring Detector marks clips shorter than a set number of frames (2 finds accidental flash frames) and clips longer than a set number of seconds; Resolve also jumps to the next gap
how: from `npx hyperframes timeline --json`, sort video rows by absStart, flag `next.absStart > prev.absEnd` (gap), `<` (overlap), and clips under 3 frames or over 4 s; tested with a short Python loop over the JSON. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.36 "Editing Basics", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Delete gaps without breaking sync
what: Resolve's Delete Gaps ripples every gap closed but never past the point where clips would overlap, and only on Auto Select tracks; clips on tracks with Auto Select off don't move
how: for HyperFrames, list gaps with the jq one-liner #4 in the CLI reference (positive delta = gap), then move each later clip left by its gap, applying moves in a plan file from left to right.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.36 "Editing Basics", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Slide edit (move a clip, neighbours absorb it)
what: A slide keeps the clip's media and duration and moves it; the previous clip's Out and the next clip's In change by the same frames, and total length stays the same; both neighbours need handles (Premiere U, FCP Option-drag with Trim tool)
how: slide by d: previous `data-duration` + d; this clip `data-start` + d; next clip `data-start` + d, `data-media-start` + d, `data-duration` - d.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/make-slide-edits-ver1632caff/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Split creates a through edit, rejoining is lossless
what: FCP and Resolve show a cut inside continuous media as a dotted 'through edit'; Join Clips / Delete Through Edit removes it with no visible change
how: proof in ffmpeg: split at 1.5 s and concat back, then compare per-frame hashes: `[0:v]split[a][b];[a]trim=0:1.5,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[x];[b]trim=1.5:3,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[y];[x][y]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0` -> `-f framemd5` identical to the source. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/cut-clips-in-two-ver4e30479/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.38 "Modifying Clips", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Split in HyperFrames, then re-point relative starts
what: Blade (FCP B / Premiere Razor C) splits one clip into two instances with new In/Out points
how: `npx hyperframes timeline split '#clipA' 1.5` wrote clipA (0-1.5, media-start 0) and clipA-2 (1.5-3, media-start 1.5); a later clip with `data-start="clipA + 0"` then started at 1.5 and overlapped clipA-2, so change it to `clipA-2 + 0`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/cut-clips-in-two-ver4e30479/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Blade All cuts every layer at one time
what: FCP Blade All (Shift-Command-B) cuts all storyline and connected clips at the skimmer; Blade (Command-B) cuts only selected clips
how: ffmpeg segment filter cuts a stream at times: `[0:v]segment=timestamps=1|2[s0][s1][s2]` gave 30/30/30 frames; in HyperFrames run `timeline split` on every clip whose absStart <= T < absEnd (jq one-liner #1). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/cut-clips-in-two-ver4e30479/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Trim Start / Trim End to the playhead
what: FCP Trim Start/End (Option-[ / ]) and Resolve Trim Start/End (Shift-[ / ]) move the In or Out of clips under the playhead to the playhead, a 'top and tail' edit; Resolve trims all intersecting clips on Auto Select tracks
how: `npx hyperframes timeline trim '#clipC' --duration 2` (or `--start`/`--end` in seconds); it refuses overlaps unless `--overwrite` and refuses ends past the root `data-duration`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/extend-or-shorten-clips-ver9847ec25/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Extend edit to the playhead
what: Extend Edit (FCP Shift-X, Resolve E) moves the selected edit point to the playhead: a ripple if one side is selected, a roll if both; Resolve also slips a selected clip so the frame under the playhead becomes its In
how: roll = trim the left clip's end and the right clip's start to the same new time in one plan file; slip-to-In = new `data-media-start` = old + (T - absStart) x rate (1.3 s in a tested calc for T=3.8, clip at 3 s, media 0.5). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/make-roll-edits-ver1632d9ae/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Relative trims by frames
what: Premiere accepts relative timecode like -5 (five frames back); Resolve +20. adds 20 s; FCP nudges with comma/period (1 frame) and Shift for 10 frames (Resolve's Shift nudge is 5 frames by default)
how: HyperFrames times are seconds: frames / fps (5 frames at 30 fps = 0.1667 s); keep one helper so every nudge is a whole number of frames.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/arrange-clips-in-the-timeline-verc147f195/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Read NLE timecode shorthand correctly
what: FCP: '1612' = 16 s 12 f, '3.' = 3 s, '3...' = 3 h (each period is a pair of zeros); Resolve: '2..' from 01:10:10:10 = 01:02:00:00, untyped left pairs keep their old value
how: a small parser that right-aligns the digits into hh mm ss ff (period = '00') gave 1.0 s for '1.', 120 s for '2..', 16.4 s for '1612' at 30 fps. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/navigate-using-timecode-ver1632d762/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: NLE In/Out are inclusive, ffmpeg end is exclusive
what: In Premiere the duration between In and Out includes both marked frames (same timecode for In and Out = one frame)
how: ffmpeg trim's `end` is 'the first frame that will be dropped' and `end_frame` is the first frame dropped; HyperFrames shows a clip over [start, start+duration). So an NLE Out at frame 89 = ffmpeg `end_frame=90`.

name: Ripple only what starts after the edit
what: Resolve's ripple rule: clips whose In is left of the rippled edit stay put, clips to the right move (linked split-edit audio moves with its video); Premiere's Ripple Sequence Markers setting decides if markers move too
how: GSAP `shiftChildren(amount, adjustLabels, ignoreBeforeTime)`: `tl.shiftChildren(0.5, true, 2)` moved children at 2 s and 4 s to 2.5/4.5 and the label from 4 to 4.5, leaving the child at 0 s. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Shorten a run of titles evenly
what: Resolve: select 14 credit edits and ripple them together; Command-drag, timecode entry or nudge trims every selected edit by the same frames, plain dragging removes frames one edit at a time left to right
how: for N titles shortened k frames each: title i loses k/fps s and starts i*k/fps s earlier; write one move+trim pair per title into a `timeline apply` plan (moves processed so nothing overlaps).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Apply several edits atomically and in a safe order
what: Editors make multi-clip changes in one operation (Resolve multi-selection trims, Premiere rearrange)
how: `npx hyperframes timeline apply plan.json` checks the whole plan: moving clipB onto clipC first was refused ('would overlap #clipC'), and a move past the root length was refused ('beyond composition duration 8'); reorder the moves or raise `data-duration` first. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Undo a timeline edit with its receipt
what: Premiere's History panel and FCP/Resolve undo step back through edits
how: every `timeline` edit prints a receipt; `npx hyperframes timeline undo r2.json` restored a trimmed clip (duration 2 back to 4). Undo is refused when the file changed after the receipt, so undo the latest edit first; for whole turns use `history undo`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Look at both sides of a cut (two-up)
what: Premiere Trim mode shows the outgoing frame left and incoming frame right; FCP's 'Show 2-Up When Trimming' and Resolve's 2-up/4-up displays do the same for ripple, roll, slip and slide
how: `ffmpeg -sseof -0.04 -i A.mp4 -frames:v 1 out_last.png`, `ffmpeg -i B.mp4 -frames:v 1 in_first.png`, then `-filter_complex hstack` -> one 1280x360 image to judge continuity. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/show-a-two-up-display-in-the-viewer-ver3363b235/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Frame strip around a cut instead of JKL trimming
what: Dynamic JKL trimming (Premiere Trim mode, Resolve W) shuttles around an edit to pick the exact frame
how: we can't shuttle, so tile the frames around the cut: `ffmpeg -i CUTS.mp4 -vf "select='between(n,26,33)',scale=160:-2,tile=8x1" -frames:v 1 -fps_mode passthrough cutstrip.png` (frame numbers count from 0). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Play around the edit (preroll and postroll)
what: Premiere's Play Around (Shift-K) uses 3 s preroll and 2 s postroll by default; Resolve's '/' plays around the selection with customizable pre/post-roll
how: cut a review clip: `ffmpeg -ss $(python3 -c 'print(max(0,CUT-3))') -i in.mp4 -t 5 around.mp4`, or `npx hyperframes snapshot --range a,b --frames 8` on the project. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Missing handles become frozen frames
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: Premiere: with insufficient media it warns and builds the handle by repeating end frames (a freeze), drawn with diagonal warning bars; 'trim at least 15 frames off each clip for a centred 1:00 transition'
how: make the handle explicitly so you know it is a freeze: `ffmpeg -i B.mp4 -vf tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=0.5 -an tpc.mp4` (90 -> 105 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: xfade overlaps the clips (the timeline gets shorter)
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: FCP: a transition without media handles can overlap the two clips instead, which is effectively a ripple edit and shortens the project
how: ffmpeg xfade always overlaps by `duration`: two 3 s clips with `xfade=transition=fade:duration=1:offset=2` give 5 s, not 6 s; pad both clips first if the length must stay. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/how-transitions-are-created-ver761c7150/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Centre, start or end the transition on the cut
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: Premiere's alignment: Center at Cut (both ends move), Start at Cut (only the end moves), End at Cut (only the start moves); FCP keeps the centre fixed when you change the duration
how: xfade's offset is measured on the first input; for a planned cut at C with duration D: centre = C - D/2 (D/2 of handle each side), start at cut = C (outgoing needs D after C), end at cut = C - D (incoming needs D before its In). Tested centre: both clips padded 0.5 s with `tpad=...:clone`, then `xfade=transition=fade:duration=1:offset=2.5` -> 6 s total. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/adjust-transitions-in-the-timeline-vercf3c662c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Single-sided transition when one side has no handle
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: Premiere applies a single-sided transition to one clip only (End at Cut / Start at Cut, or automatically when the clip has no neighbour), e.g. one shot leaving with a wipe and the next fading in
how: fade only the incoming clip: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf fade=in:0:30 -an fin.mp4` (first 30 frames), or `fade=t=out:st=2:d=1` on the outgoing clip. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One default transition everywhere, then change by exception
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: Premiere's defaults are Cross Dissolve and Constant Power crossfade at 1 s; 'Apply Default Transitions to Selection' fills every edit where two selected clips touch; FCP's default duration is a setting; replacing a transition keeps its alignment and duration but resets its settings
how: generate the xfade chain from a list in Python (offset_i = running length - D) with one default name/duration, and override per edit; swapping `transition=` keeps offset/duration unchanged.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/set-the-default-duration-for-transitions-verad58cdd16/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Dip to black is not a fade of one layer
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: Premiere notes Dip to Black at a clip's start or end also affects video on lower tracks, and Cross Dissolve may suit a simple fade of the targeted clip better
how: dip between two clips: `[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition=fadeblack:duration=1:offset=2` (5 s); to fade only an upper layer, fade its alpha (`fade=...:alpha=1`) instead of the composite. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fade the whole stack, not each clip
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: FCP: to include connected clips in a fade, select them with the clip and make a compound clip before adding the Cross Dissolve
how: apply the fade after the overlay so it hits the composite: `[1:v]scale=320:-2[p];[0:v][p]overlay=20:20,fade=t=out:st=2:d=1`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-transitions-and-fades-ver761c7432/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Fade in and out to the playhead
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: Resolve's Trim menu 'Fade In to Playhead' / 'Fade Out to Playhead' set a fade length from the playhead position, for video and audio; FCP fade handles do the same in the Video Animation editor
how: convert the playhead time to `fade=t=out:st=T:d=END-T` plus `afade=t=out:st=T:d=END-T`; tested `-vf fade=t=out:st=2:d=1 -af afade=t=out:st=2:d=1`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.50 "Compositing and Transforms in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/adjust-effect-curves-ver8e3f1f04/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Audio follows a video transition
section: Transitions as an NLE thinks about them
what: FCP adds a crossfade to attached audio when you add a video transition (not when audio is detached/expanded); Premiere's default audio transition is Constant Power crossfade
how: pair every xfade with `acrossfade=d=1` on the audio (two 3 s tracks -> about 5 s), or keep separate audio and fade it yourself when it is detached. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-transitions-ver2833f6b2/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Speed change with or without ripple
what: FCP Custom Speed has a Ripple checkbox: off, a slowed clip keeps its length and shows less of the action (a sped-up one leaves a gap); Premiere Speed/Duration has 'Ripple Edit, shift trailing clips'; Resolve has 'Ripple Sequence'
how: no ripple: slow and cut to the old length, `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf "setpts=2*PTS" -an -t 3 snr.mp4` (89 frames, half the action); ripple: let it run 6 s and move later clips. HyperFrames: `data-playback-rate` with the duration you want. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/change-clip-speed-ver40b00150/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Hold segment inside a clip
what: FCP Hold (Shift-H) adds a 2 s still at the playhead and makes the clip longer; Premiere freezes part of a clip with a 0% Time Remapping keyframe; Resolve's retime Freeze Frame adds two speed points
how: loop one frame: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf "loop=loop=59:size=1:start=45,setpts=N/FRAME_RATE/TB" -an hold.mp4` held frame 45 for 2 s (90 -> 149 frames). HyperFrames' own advice: export the still and place it as its own clip. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-hold-segments-ver4c2173c9/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Freeze frames from a chosen frame without a new clip
what: Premiere Frame Hold shows one frame (In, Out, Marker 0 or a timecode) for the clip's whole duration; Resolve Freeze Frame (Shift-R) turns the whole clip into the frame under the playhead
how: ffmpeg freezeframes replaces a frame range with one frame of a second input: `[0:v][1:v]freezeframes=first=30:last=59:replace=30` (length unchanged, 90 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Rewind segment: forward, back fast, forward again
what: FCP Rewind duplicates the range, plays the copy backwards at 1x/2x/4x, then plays the range forward again; Resolve's Rewind preset adds two speed points the same way
how: `[0:v]trim=0:2,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,split=3[f1][r][f2];[r]reverse,setpts=0.5*PTS[rv];[f1][rv][f2]concat=n=3:v=1:a=0` -> 2 s + 1 s (2x back) + 2 s; reverse buffers the whole clip, so trim first. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/reverse-or-rewind-clips-ver15f879b3/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Instant Replay: append the range again at a new speed
what: FCP Instant Replay appends a copy of the range at the chosen speed after the original (and adds an 'Instant Replay' title)
how: `[0:v]split[o][c];[c]trim=1:2,setpts=2*(PTS-STARTPTS)[sl];[o][sl]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0` -> the 3 s clip then its 1-2 s range at half speed (5 s). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-instant-replays-ver40affee3/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Jump cut at markers to compress time
what: FCP 'Jump Cut at Markers' skips 3, 5, 10, 20 or 30 frames at each marker, e.g. a long walk shortened without fast motion
how: drop frame ranges and retime: `-vf "select='not(between(n,30,39)+between(n,60,69))',setpts=N/FRAME_RATE/TB"` removed 10 frames at frames 30 and 60 (90 -> 70). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/speed-up-a-clip-with-jump-cuts-ver9b215183d/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Stair-step speed ramp presets
what: Resolve's Speed Ramp preset makes five segments at 10, 30, 50, 70 and 90%; FCP's Speed Ramp to 0% / from 0% makes four segments and adds speed transitions between them, whose length sets how fast the ramp changes
how: HyperFrames: a `rate` lane in `data-automation` (t in clip seconds, v 0.1-10) overrides the constant rate, so write points like 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 across the clip.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-variable-speed-effects-ver95783cbbc/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-speed-transitions-ver41a2cd3ae/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Piecewise speed with one setpts expression
what: Resolve's Retime Frame curve maps source frames (vertical) to timeline frames (horizontal): shallow segments are slow, steep ones fast, a falling segment plays backwards
how: two segments in one expression: `setpts='if(lt(T,1),2*T,T+1)/TB'` plays the first second at half speed then normal (3 s -> 4 s, with `-r 30`). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Posterize time (lock to a lower frame rate)
what: Premiere's Posterize Time locks a clip to a specific frame rate; animating its Frame Rate allows only Hold interpolation
how: drop to the rate and back to the project rate so frames repeat: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf "fps=8,fps=30" -an post.mp4` (still 90 frames, 8 distinct per second). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Echo: mix frames from different times
what: Premiere's Echo combines frames from different times in a clip and only shows a result where there is motion
how: the ffmpeg filter that mixes successive frames is tmix: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf tmix=frames=5 -an tmx.mp4` (frame count unchanged; weights are settable). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stretch animation with the clip, or keep its timing
what: Resolve's speed dialog: Maintain Timing keeps keyframes in place, Stretch scales them with the clip; FCP Paste Attributes: Maintain or Stretch to Fit; Premiere presets: Scale, Anchor to In Point, Anchor to Out Point
how: GSAP `tl.duration(d)` as a setter changes timeScale to fit: a 4 s timeline set to 2 kept duration() 4 with timeScale() 2 (stretch); for 'anchor to out', place exit tweens at `clipDur - 1` (tested start 4 for a 5 s clip). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.51 "Speed Effects", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/copy-effects-between-clips-ver3029fc422/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Filter order changes the picture
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: FCP: effect order matters (Artifacts before Aged Paper ages the circles, after it leaves them white); Premiere renders standard effects top to bottom, then Motion, then Opacity, and fixed effects can't be reordered (use Transform/Alpha Adjust to move them)
how: ffmpeg applies a chain left to right: `drawtext=...,rotate=PI/6` and `rotate=PI/6,drawtext=...` gave different PNG hashes; write the chain in the order you want the stack. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/change-clip-effect-order-ver761c7810/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Adjustment layer = filter after the overlay
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere, FCP (Option-A) and Resolve adjustment clips apply their effects to every clip on tracks below, for as long as the adjustment clip runs
how: put the filter after the composite, limited in time: `[0:v][p]overlay=20:20,hue=s=0:enable='between(t,0,1)'`. In HyperFrames footage looks go through `media-treatment`, not CSS filters. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-adjustment-clips-verfda63436e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Resize an adjustment layer to touch only part of the frame
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere: scale and position an adjustment layer (Motion) to affect only a region, and trim it to limit when
how: split, filter a crop, overlay it back: `[0:v]split[a][b];[b]crop=320:180:0:0,hue=s=0[c];[a][c]overlay=0:0`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Effect only over a time range
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Effects on an adjustment layer or keyframed on/off apply only where the layer exists; FCP lets you turn a clip effect off and keep its settings
how: ffmpeg timeline editing: filters that support `enable` run only where the expression is non-zero, e.g. `hue=s=0:enable='between(t,1,2)'`; `enable=0` keeps the filter in the graph but off (`ffmpeg -filters` shows a T for timeline support). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/remove-or-turn-off-effects-ver4e321d5/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Alternative looks as switchable variants
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: FCP: stack several adjustment clips with different looks, disable all but one, or give each a subrole and switch roles in the timeline index before export; adjustment clips can also go in an audition
how: HyperFrames: make the look a variable (boolean/enum) and render each value with `render --batch rows.json --output "renders/{name}.mp4"`, or compare them on one sheet with `npx hyperframes compare`.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-adjustment-clips-verfda63436e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Source effects apply to every use of a clip
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere source-clip effects (Project panel, Source tab) are inherited by all sequence instances; Motion, Opacity, Speed, Warp Stabilizer and audio effects can't be source effects
how: bake the shared fix once into an intermediate in assets/ (e.g. `ffmpeg -i raw.mp4 -vf <fix> -c:v prores_ks -profile:v hq fixed.mov`) and point every HyperFrames clip at that file.

name: Effects that make their own image need a transparent layer
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere puts generated effects (Lightning, Timecode) on a Transparent Video clip on the top track so the layers below stay visible
how: draw on a transparent canvas and overlay it: `color=black@0:s=640x360:r=30:d=3,format=rgba,drawtext=text='LIVE':fontcolor=red:fontsize=48:x=20:y=20[g];[0:v][g]overlay=shortest=1`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Opacity below 100% mixes with black when nothing is underneath
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Resolve: a clip with opacity under 100 mixes with the clip below, or with black if there is none; Premiere composites from the lowest track up and empty areas are black
how: half-transparent clip over a black base: `[1:v]format=rgba,colorchannelmixer=aa=0.5[t];[0:v][t]overlay=shortest=1` with `color=black` as input 0; in HyperFrames give the root a full-bleed background child. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.50 "Compositing and Transforms in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Mix an effect with the original (Blend slider)
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Fusion's Settings tab has a Blend slider on every node to blend between the effect and the original image
how: `[0:v]split[o][e];[e]hue=s=0[g];[g][o]blend=all_mode=normal:all_opacity=0.5` (tested command; blend's opacity applies with the component modes). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.79 "Compositing Layers in Fusion", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Track matte (luma or alpha from another layer)
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Resolve: a top clip in Foreground mode takes its transparency from the clip below set to Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Lum or Inverted Lum; Premiere has Track Matte Key
how: ffmpeg alphamerge copies the grayscale of a second input into the first input's alpha: `[1:v]format=gray[m];[0:v][m]alphamerge[fg];[bg][fg]overlay=shortest=1`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.50 "Compositing and Transforms in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Line two layers up with Difference
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere: put one layer over an identical one, set Difference, and move one until the element turns black, meaning the pixels are stacked exactly
how: measure it: `[0:v][1:v]blend=all_mode=difference,signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=da.txt`; identical layers gave YAVG=0, a 4 px shift gave about 5. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Straight vs premultiplied alpha
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere: straight alpha keeps colour only in the alpha channel, premultiplied multiplies it into RGB; Fusion's Merge expects premultiplied foregrounds and its Subtractive/Additive slider fixes fringing from non-premultiplied ones
how: tell ffmpeg's overlay which kind it gets: `overlay=alpha=straight` or `alpha=premultiplied` (default auto); tested `[1:v][0:v]overlay=alpha=straight` with a 50% red rgba layer. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.79 "Compositing Layers in Fusion", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Crop by edge percentages
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere's Crop effect removes a percentage from Left/Top/Right/Bottom with Fit or Fill; Resolve crops in pixels and the cropped area becomes transparent
how: `crop=iw*0.8:ih*0.8:iw*0.1:ih*0.1` takes 10% off each edge (640x360 -> 512x288); overlay it on a lower layer to get Resolve's 'shows what is underneath'. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.50 "Compositing and Transforms in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Crop-and-fill vs trim-to-a-window
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: FCP's Crop mode removes areas and the result expands to fill the screen; its Trim mode trims edges independently to make a window over the clip below
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/crop-clips-verb8e5db98/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/trim-the-edges-of-the-video-frame-verfc8a496f/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Flip horizontally or vertically
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Premiere Horizontal Flip mirrors left-right while playing forward; Vertical Flip turns the clip upside down and can't be keyframed
how: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf hflip -frames:v 1 hf.png` and `-vf vflip`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rotate around an anchor point
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: FCP Transform rotates around the anchor (Anchor X/Y only in the inspector); Premiere's Motion has Position, Scale, Rotation and Anchor Point
how: ffmpeg rotate takes radians clockwise and fills the uncovered area: `rotate=a=PI/12:c=black`; in HyperFrames tween the wrapper and set its transformOrigin on the anchor, as the repo's phone-edit recipe does for faces. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/resize-move-and-rotate-clips-verfc8a4713/mac, checked 2026-10-24
repo: CLAUDE.md (Editing a phone video, step 5)

name: Corner pin / distort
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: FCP's Distort drags each corner and edge independently for a skew or 3D-perspective look; Premiere has Corner Pin
how: send the source corners to new points: `perspective=x0=40:y0=20:x1=600:y1=0:x2=0:y2=360:x3=640:y3=330:sense=destination` (order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/skew-a-clips-perspective-verfc8a4a9d/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Lens distortion correction
section: Effects stack, adjustment layers and compositing
what: Resolve's Video Inspector has Lens Correction; Premiere's accelerated list includes Lens Distortion
how: `lenscorrection=k1=-0.2:k2=0.05` (k1 quadratic, k2 double-quadratic term, -1..1, centre cx/cy 0.5); the doc suggests OpenCV calibration or trial and error for the values. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.50 "Compositing and Transforms in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Linear keyframes = ease 'none'
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere Linear interpolation is an even rate of change that starts and stops abruptly; FCP's Linear curve keeps a constant rate
how: GSAP's default ease is power1.out, so write `ease: "none"` for linear; tested: value 2.5 at 25% of a 0->10 tween. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/adjust-effect-curves-ver8e3f1f04/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Hold keyframe = tl.set at the next key
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere's Hold changes a value with no gradual transition (flat line after the key); Fusion's Step In holds the previous value then jumps at the next key, Step Out switches at once and holds
how: `tl.set(obj, {v: 5}, 2)` held 0 at 1.9 s and gave 5 at 2.0 s (Step In); `ease: "steps(1)"` jumped to the end value already at mid-tween (Step Out). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.72 "Animating in Fusion's Spline Editor", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Several keyframes on one tween
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere Auto/Continuous Bezier smooths a change through a keyframe; FCP Option-K adds keyframes along one parameter
how: GSAP keyframes in one `to()`: array `keyframes: {x: [0,100,50]}` spreads values evenly (default per-keyframe ease power1.inOut, change with `easeEach`); percentage keyframes `{"0%":..., "50%":..., "100%":...}`; tested x=100 at the middle of `[0,100,50]` with ease none. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-video-effect-keyframes-ver8e3f20ea/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: NLE 'ease in' names the landing
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere: Ease In slows value changes entering a keyframe, Ease Out accelerates leaving one; FCP's Ken Burns 'Ease In' limits easing to the end of the move and 'Ease Out' to the beginning
how: so an NLE ease-in onto a final key is the arrival ease, which HyperFrames motion guidance writes as a long-tailed `.out` (`expo.out`, `power4.out`); check direction by eye before copying names across.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/pan-and-zoom-clips-verb8e5de9c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Place keys with the position parameter
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere pastes copied keyframes with the earliest at the playhead and the rest in relative order; FCP pastes at the playhead and replaces keys in that time range
how: GSAP position parameter: number = absolute, `"<"` start of previous, `">-0.25"` end of previous minus 0.25, `"<0.5"`; tested starts 0, 0.5, 1.25 for three chained 1 s tweens. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/copy-and-paste-keyframes-verc32e6a04c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Snap keyframe times to whole frames
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere's Effect Controls can snap a dragged keyframe into alignment with other objects (chosen in Snap To, e.g. Video Keyframes)
how: `gsap.utils.snap(1/30, t)` rounds a time to the 30 fps grid (1.2345 -> 1.2333); snap to beats with an array: `gsap.utils.snap([0,0.75,1.5,2.25], 1.2)` -> 1.5. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Loop and ping-pong a keyed move
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Fusion's spline editor offers Set Loop, Ping-Pong (each repeat reversed) and Relative Loop; Duplicate repeats a set number of times
how: GSAP `repeat: 3, yoyo: true` plays forward/back/forward/back (tested value 0.5 at 1.5 s on a 1 s linear tween); HyperFrames forbids `repeat: -1`, so give a finite count. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.72 "Animating in Fusion's Spline Editor", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Read back what the keyframes really do
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere's Effect Controls can filter to Show Only Keyframed Properties and step between keys with the keyframe navigator
how: `npx hyperframes keyframes --json [--selector '#id']` lists every tween's target, start, duration and ease (it reported the title fade as fromTo, 0.3 s, power4.out); `--shot motion.png` draws the path. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Velocity handles need CustomEase
section: Keyframes and interpolation in GSAP terms
what: Premiere's Velocity graph handles set how fast a value approaches and leaves a key, and 'influence' sets how quickly the graph reaches it
how: GSAP's CustomEase takes a drawn curve or a cubic-bezier string like ".17,.67,.83,.67", but it is a plugin outside the core and not in assets/vendor: needs CustomEase (missing).

name: Markers as GSAP labels
what: Markers flag sync points and notes (FCP: blue standard, orange chapter, red to-do, green done; Premiere: comment, chapter, segmentation, web link); Resolve markers can carry duration
how: inside a scene, `tl.addLabel("drop", 3.47)` then place tweens at `"drop"` or `"drop+=1"` (tested starts 3.47 and 4.47). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-markers-ver397279dd/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Chapter markers into the MP4
what: Resolve writes chapters only for QuickTime/MP4 from markers of one colour ('Chapters from Markers'); FCP chapter markers work on iPhone, Apple TV, QuickTime Player, podcast apps and DVD/Blu-ray
how: write an ffmetadata file with `[CHAPTER] TIMEBASE=1/1000 START=0 END=1500 title=Intro` blocks and mux: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -i ch.txt -map_metadata 1 -map_chapters 1 -c copy chap.mp4`; `ffprobe -show_chapters` listed both. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.41 "Marking and Finding Clips in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-chapter-markers-verc9cacc031/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Chapter thumbnail a few frames after the marker
what: FCP's chapter thumbnail pin sits 11 frames after the chapter marker by default and uses the composited frame (titles included)
how: grab that frame from the render: `ffmpeg -ss $(python3 -c 'print(1.5+11/30)') -i A.mp4 -frames:v 1 ch_thumb.jpg`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-chapter-markers-verc9cacc031/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Ranges as markers with duration
what: Resolve converts In/Out to a 'Duration Marker' so one clip can hold several logged regions; FCP sets multiple ranges in a browser clip (Shift-Command-I/O) and editing commands use only the yellow (selected) ones
how: log selects as JSON `{src, in, out, note}`; feed them to the concat demuxer as `inpoint`/`outpoint` lines (see the paper-edit skill).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.41 "Marking and Finding Clips in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/set-multiple-ranges-in-the-browser-veradbf2dce/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Favourites and rejects before cutting
what: FCP: F marks a range favourite (green line), Delete marks it rejected (red), U unrates; hide rejected clips while editing
how: keep a selects list with ratings and build the stringout from favourites only; nothing is deleted from the source folder.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/rate-clips-ver30ccd91f/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/lines-marking-event-clips-ver3bf664ce4/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Marker list out of the timeline
what: Resolve exports Timeline Markers to EDL and the Edit Index as CSV/TXT; Premiere's Sequence Index exports filtered rows as CSV
how: `npx hyperframes timeline --json | jq -r '.timeline.tracks[].rows[] | [.id,.absStart,.absEnd,.src] | @csv'` gives a clip list for notes or handoff.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.187 "Exporting Timelines to Other Applications", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Sync clips by identically named markers
what: Premiere multicam can sync on a clip marker placed at a clap, flash or cymbal hit in every clip, named the same in each; FCP can use the first marker in each angle and refine with audio
how: offset of clip B = marker_A - marker_B; trim B by that amount (or `-itsoffset`) before stacking.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-multicam-clips-ver23c764f1/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Nested sequence = sub-composition
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: A Premiere nested sequence / FCP compound clip / Resolve nested timeline is a whole sequence used as one clip; you can trim it and add effects like a clip
how: mount a scene file: `<div id="title" data-composition-id="title" data-composition-src="compositions/title.html" data-start="1" data-duration="2">`; host id, scene root id and timeline key must match or renders wait 45 s per scene. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-compound-clips-verbbd3496b/mac, checked 2026-10-24

Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.43 "Take Selectors, Compound Clips, and Nested Timelines", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: A host shorter or longer than its scene
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Premiere: shortening the source sequence leaves black/silence in the nest; FCP: content beyond the compound clip's boundary (crosshatched) doesn't appear
how: HyperFrames: the host's `data-duration` is the slot; a shorter scene timeline holds its last frame, and a slot shorter than the video goes blank when it ends.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/edit-compound-clips-verca9e8672/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: One scene file, many mounts
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Editing a nested source sequence or a parent compound clip updates every instance; FCP's Reference New Parent Clip makes an instance independent
how: mounting the same `data-composition-src` twice shares edits; per-mount text/media differences go in `data-variable-values`; copy the file to break the link.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-compound-clips-verca9e8d33/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Nest before effects that need sequence-sized input
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Premiere: Warp Stabilizer requires the clip dimensions to match the sequence; nest the clip and stabilize the nest. Premiere also says video effects are clip-based, so use a nest to apply one effect to several clips
how: conform first (`scale`/`pad` to the sequence size), then stabilize or effect the conformed stream; for several clips, render the concatenated group and treat that file.

name: Primary storyline and connected clips
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: In FCP's magnetic timeline, clips connected to a primary-storyline clip move and delete with it, keeping B-roll, titles and sound tied to their moment; holding ` moves the primary clip without its connections
how: HyperFrames: put an overlay inside the scene it belongs to (a nested clip counts its `data-start` from the composition and shows only while its parent shows); keep it at root level when it must stay put while scenes move.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-the-magnetic-timeline-verb8fcfc133/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/connect-clips-ver7a77ef9e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Position tool vs magnetic moves
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: FCP's Position tool (P) overwrites at the new spot and leaves a gap clip; normal drags ripple other clips to make room
how: `npx hyperframes timeline move <ref> <time>` refuses to overlap a neighbour unless `--overwrite`; follow-up clips are moved explicitly (or with relative `data-start`). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/arrange-clips-in-the-timeline-verc147f195/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-the-magnetic-timeline-verb8fcfc133/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Keep linked video and audio together
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Premiere linked selection, FCP expand/detach audio and Resolve linking keep A/V in sync; Resolve flags out-of-sync parts with red offset indicators and offers Slip/Move into place
how: HyperFrames linked clips share `data-link` and `data-sync-origin`, and every member keeps the same `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-media-start` and `data-playback-rate`; unlink by removing `data-link` from all of them (lint rule `linked_clips_out_of_sync`).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.36 "Editing Basics", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-split-edits-ver1632d82c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Auditions / take selectors as variables
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: FCP auditions and Resolve Take Selectors hold alternate takes in one timeline slot; the pick plays, Finalize Audition keeps it; Resolve's Ripple Take option ripples when a take has a different length
how: make the media a variable (`data-var-src`, keep a real fallback `src`) and render each take with `render --batch`, or compare stills with `npx hyperframes compare <a> <b> --at <s>`.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-auditions-verbbd3587d/mac, checked 2026-10-24

Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.43 "Take Selectors, Compound Clips, and Nested Timelines", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Timeline index from the CLI
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: FCP's timeline index and Premiere's Sequence Index list every clip with timecode and filter by offline media, effects, flash frames and more
how: `npx hyperframes timeline --json` gives every clip (nested included) with absStart, absEnd, file, src, mediaStart and playbackRate; read it instead of opening each HTML file. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/view-your-project-in-the-timeline-index-ver4e30596/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Match frame from the timeline
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Premiere F, FCP Reveal Source (Shift-F) and Resolve Match Frame open the source at the same frame as the timeline playhead, e.g. to re-add audio left behind
how: source time = mediaStart + (t - absStart) x playbackRate from the timeline JSON (tested: 1.5 s in B.mp4 at t=4 for a clip starting at 3 with media start 0.5). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/find-a-project-clips-source-clip-ver7a77f37c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.41 "Marking and Finding Clips in the Timeline", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Find repeated uses of the same footage
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Resolve's Duplicate Frame Detection and FCP's Show Duplicate Ranges mark media used more than once; Premiere lists every sequence location of a clip; Resolve flags mark every clip from the same source
how: group timeline rows by `src` and compare their media ranges [mediaStart, mediaStart+duration); a tested Python check found two overlapping uses of A.mp4. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.34 "Creating and Working with Timelines", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/show-clips-with-duplicate-ranges-vercefac2468/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Find through edits and buried clips
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Resolve's Edit Index can list only through edits; its Clean Up Video Tracks finds clips fully hidden under superimposed clips (flatten, disable or recolour them)
how: from the JSON: same src, butt-joined, media continuous = through edit; a clip covered in time by a higher z-index clip = buried; a tested Python pass found one of each. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.38 "Modifying Clips", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: See which source ranges are still unused
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: FCP draws an orange line under browser clips at the ranges used in the open project (View > Browser > Used Media Ranges)
how: collect [mediaStart, mediaStart+duration) per src from the timeline JSON; whatever falls outside is unused material to mine for cutaways. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/intro-to-adding-clips-ver15f852e7/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/lines-marking-event-clips-ver3bf664ce4/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Compare two versions of a cut
section: Nesting, compound clips and the magnetic timeline in HyperFrames
what: Resolve's Timeline Comparison shows two timelines with ganged playheads, highlights changed sections and builds a Difference Index
how: diff the two `timeline --json` outputs by id/absStart/absEnd for the edit list, and `npx hyperframes compare <dirA> <dirB> --at <s> --labels old,new` for pictures.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.34 "Creating and Working with Timelines", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Sync angles by audio cross-correlation
what: Premiere, FCP ('Use audio for synchronization') and Resolve (Sync by Audio, Auto Align Clips) line up cameras by their waveforms; record audio on every camera for this
how: decode both to 16 kHz mono and take the FFT cross-correlation peak in numpy; a pink-noise test delayed 370 ms was found as offset 0.37 s. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/multicam-editing-workflow-ver10e087fd/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.38 "Modifying Clips", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Content-created dates only sync to a second
what: FCP's Content Created sync is about 1 s accurate because cameras store date/time in whole seconds; refine with audio sync or by hand
how: use file creation times only as a starting window for the audio cross-correlation, never as the final offset.
