refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-multicam-clips-ver23c764f1/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/sync-audio-and-video-verc1fabc30/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Cut the line edit from a list of angle switches
what: Multicam editing cuts between synced angles while playing (Premiere number keys, FCP angle viewer, Resolve Sync Bin) and fine-tunes the cuts after
how: with synced files, every segment takes the same timeline times from its angle: `[0:v]trim=0:1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a];[1:v]trim=1:2,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[b];[0:v]trim=2:3,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[c];[a][b][c]concat=n=3:v=1:a=0` with the master audio mapped (3 s). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/cut-and-switch-camera-angles-ver23c76c9c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: One audio for the whole multicam cut
what: Premiere's 'Camera 1' audio setting uses only camera 1's audio while video switches; FCP can switch video only and keep the audio angle; with double-system sound FCP can disable the camera reference audio
how: map one audio source across all video cuts (`-map 0:a -c:a copy` above), or replace camera audio with the recorder: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -i B.mp4 -map 0:v -map 1:a -c copy -shortest dual.mp4`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/cut-and-switch-camera-angles-ver23c76c9c/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/sync-audio-and-video-verc1fabc30/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Sync on a clap at the In point
what: Premiere and Resolve can sync clips by user In points set at a slate clap or flash (or Out points at a tail slate)
how: offset = In_B - In_A in seconds; start angle B with `-ss` that much later than angle A so the claps coincide.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Make proxies the NLE way
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere's Create Proxies defaults to Half frame size and ProRes Proxy, appends '_Proxy' and puts them in a Proxies folder; FCP makes ProRes 422 Proxy or HEVC at 12.5-100%; Resolve offers Half to Sixteenth and ProRes/DNxHR/H.264/H.265
how: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf scale=iw/2:-2 -c:v prores_ks -profile:v proxy -c:a pcm_s16le A_Proxy.mov` (320x180, same 90 frames as the original); an HEVC quarter-size proxy also worked with libx265. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-optimized-and-proxy-files-verb8e5f6fd/mac, checked 2026-10-24

Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.8 "Improving Performance, Proxies, and the Render Cache", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Proxies must match to relink
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere attaches proxies by file name, extension, tape name and timecode; Resolve keeps proxies linked by metadata; changing names or folders breaks automatic relinking
how: keep the same base name and frame count (check `ffprobe -count_frames`), and record the original path next to each proxy. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Switch back to originals before the final render
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere exports full resolution unless 'Use Proxies' is ticked; FCP says to switch playback back to Optimized/Original before sharing
how: if a HyperFrames project points at proxy files, rewrite the `src` paths to the originals before `render --quality delivery` and check with `timeline --json`.
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-optimized-and-proxy-files-verb8e5f6fd/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Optimized (intra-frame) media for smooth editing
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: FCP's optimized media is ProRes 422 for better editing performance, faster renders and better compositing colour; Resolve also makes optimized media
how: `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -c:v prores_ks -profile:v standard -c:a pcm_s16le A_opt.mov`, or an all-I-frame H.264: `-c:v libx264 -g 1` (every frame came out I). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/create-optimized-and-proxy-files-verb8e5f6fd/mac, checked 2026-10-24

Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.8 "Improving Performance, Proxies, and the Render Cache", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Render and replace a heavy section (with handles)
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere's Render and Replace flattens clips/After Effects comps with 0-100 handle frames, makes rendered effects non-editable, and only CineForm-with-alpha keeps alpha; Restore Unrendered brings back the original
how: pre-render to a file and keep the original next to it; for alpha use ProRes 4444: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=red@0.5:s=320x180:r=30:d=1,format=rgba -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 4444 -pix_fmt yuva444p10le rr.mov` (ffprobe: 4444, yuva444p12le). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Smart rendering = stream copy
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere smart renders by copying matching source data without recompressing, only when codec, frame size, frame rate and bit rate match the export exactly
how: `-c copy` copies packets untouched; with `-ss` before `-i` ffmpeg seeks to the nearest seek point before the time, so a copied 1 s cut came out 1.1 s; cut on keyframes or re-encode the cut. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Join same-format clips without re-encoding
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Smart rendering and Resolve's stringout timelines string many clips together quickly when formats match
how: concat demuxer: a list `file 'A.mp4'` x2 with `-f concat -safe 0 -i l2.txt -c copy` gave 6 s with no re-encode; all files need the same streams and codecs. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Paper edit straight from in/out ranges
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere's Paper Edit builds a rough-cut sequence from selected transcript sentences; text-based editing applies a ripple when you cut text
how: write the kept ranges as an ffconcat script with `inpoint`/`outpoint` per file; on an all-intra source two ranges (1 s + 0.5 s) gave exactly 45 frames with `-c copy`, while long-GOP sources include extra frames before the In point (the doc warns), so re-encode those. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Archive only what the cut uses, plus handles
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere's Project Manager can exclude unused clips and keep 0-999 handle frames around each used range; FCP Consolidate gathers media into one location
how: for each used range, copy [in - handle, out + handle]: a 1 s range with 10-frame handles came out 1.67 s with `ffmpeg -ss s -to e -i src ...`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/consolidate-projects-and-libraries-ver9c7660349/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Verify copies when ingesting cards
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere's Media Browser ingest recommends 'Copy With MD5 Verification' when copying camera cards
how: `(cd card && md5sum A.mp4) > m.md5` then `(cd dst && md5sum -c ../m.md5)` -> 'A.mp4: OK'. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep media where relinking can find it
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere relinks by history and by searching the project folder, then its parent; renamed files, moved trees, changed extensions (.mov -> .mp4) and unmounted drives need manual relinking
how: keep all media in the project's `assets/` with root-relative paths (HyperFrames requires root-relative asset paths, in sub-compositions too).

name: Clear cached renders when space runs low
section: Media management, proxies and render shortcuts
what: Premiere deletes render files for the work area or the whole sequence; FCP Delete Generated Files removes render, optimized and proxy files (originals stay)
how: `npx hyperframes clean --dry-run`, then `clean`; never delete `.hyperframes` (it holds history).
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/manage-render-files-ver68a8c250/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Scene edit detection on a finished video
what: Premiere's Scene Edit Detection can cut, make subclips or add markers at detected cuts (linked audio is cut too unless separated); FCP Detect Edits (Shift-E) splits at hard cuts and may miss fades
how: `ffmpeg -i CUTS.mp4 -vf scdet=threshold=10,metadata=print:key=lavfi.scd.time:file=sc.txt -f null -` logged cuts at 1 s and 2 s (doc: good thresholds 8-14); `select='gt(scene,0.3)'` with showinfo found the same frames. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/detect-and-restore-edits-verfe2eedc5f/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Split a file into shots at the detected times
what: Detected cuts become separate clips (Premiere bin of subclips, FCP separate clips with through edits)
how: re-encode and cut exactly: `[0:v]segment=timestamps=1|2[s0][s1][s2]`; the segment muxer instead starts each file on the next keyframe after the time, so force keyframes and give it slightly early times (`-force_key_frames 1,2 -f segment -segment_times 0.99,1.99` gave three 1 s files). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Timecode and clip-name burn-in for review copies
what: Premiere's Metadata & Timecode Burn-in shows up to five lines (timecodes, file name, frame rate); FCP's Timecode generator overlays project timecode for reviewers
how: `-vf "drawtext=timecode='01\:00\:00\:00':rate=30:fontcolor=white:fontsize=28:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.6:x=20:y=h-50,drawtext=text='A.mp4':fontcolor=white:fontsize=24:x=20:y=20"` on a review copy only. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/add-timecode-counters-verca9e960b/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Aspect-ratio guide matte on the review copy
what: FCP custom overlays (a PNG with alpha) show a target framing such as a 2.35:1 letterbox while you reframe, and never reach the export; Resolve's Safe Area menu has 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 1.91:1, 1.85, 2.35 guides
how: draw the bars only on a review render: `drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=iw:h=(ih-iw/2.35)/2:color=black:t=fill,drawbox=x=0:y=ih-(ih-iw/2.35)/2:w=iw:h=(ih-iw/2.35)/2:color=black:t=fill`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/use-overlays-in-the-viewer-verded6d49d7/mac, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Fast review sheet of long rushes
what: Resolve's Fast Review plays long clips faster than short ones so you can watch a lot of media quickly; its Source Tape strings a whole bin into one scrubbable strip
how: a still sheet every 15 frames: `ffmpeg -i CUTS.mp4 -vf "framestep=15,scale=160:-2,tile=6x1" -frames:v 1 -fps_mode passthrough review.png`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Source-tape stringout with names burned in
what: Resolve's Source Tape shows every clip in a bin one after another in sort order and selects the clip under the playhead; a new timeline can include all Media Pool clips as a stringout
how: `[0:v]drawtext=text='A.mp4':...[a];[1:v]drawtext=text='B.mp4':...[b];[a][0:a][b][1:a]concat=n=2:v=1:a=1` -> one review file that says which clip is playing. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Export a still named with its timecode
what: Premiere's Export Frame saves a still, can re-import it, and names it with the frame's timecode (e.g. ClipName.00_14_23_00.Still001.jpg); FCP Save Current Frame does the same job
how: `ffmpeg -ss 1.4 -i A.mp4 -frames:v 1 "A.00_00_01_12.Still001.png"` (1.4 s = 1 s 12 f at 30 fps). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/export-still-images-verd9d1ff4cf/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Expect lossy handoffs between editors
what: Premiere imports FCP X only via XtoCC-converted XML; keyframed FCP speed becomes one constant average speed, unsupported transitions become Cross Dissolve, other blend modes are dropped; EDLs work best with one video track, two stereo audio tracks and no nests
how: hand over a flat clip list (timeline JSON/CSV) plus a reference render; an EDL/XML/OTIO writer needs OpenTimelineIO (missing).

name: OTIO vs OTIOZ
what: Resolve imports/exports OpenTimelineIO: .otio holds only timeline metadata (the receiver relinks media), .otioz bundles the full media files and can be very large
how: needs OpenTimelineIO (missing); until then send JSON + media folder.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.187 "Exporting Timelines to Other Applications", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: A Fusion node graph is an ffmpeg filtergraph
what: Fusion builds composites from nodes: MediaIn to effects to Merge (background input orange, foreground green) to MediaOut; dropping a Media Pool clip on a connection line creates a Merge with that clip as the foreground
how: write it as labelled pads: `[0:v]...[bg];[1:v]...[fg];[bg][fg]overlay[out]` (overlay's first input is the main/background, the second is laid on top).
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.79 "Compositing Layers in Fusion", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Smart Insert: snap to the nearest existing cut
what: Resolve's Cut-page Smart Insert puts the incoming clip at the edit point nearest the playhead (shown by the Smart Indicator) and won't insert at an arbitrary frame; Place On Top also snaps to an edit within five frames
how: keep a list of edit times and snap the wanted time to it: `gsap.utils.snap([0,3,5,8], 4.2)` -> 5, `snap([0,3,5,8], 6.9)` -> 8; then insert there. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Extend a clip past its media with black filler
what: Resolve's Change Clip Duration (Command-D) has 1/5/15 s presets, 'End' (to the last media frame) and, in the Cut page, 'Extend Beyond Clip Length', which appends black filler
how: `ffmpeg -i B.mp4 -vf tpad=stop_mode=add:stop_duration=1 -af apad=whole_dur=4 ext4.mp4` turned a 3 s clip into 4 s with a black, silent tail. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.28 "Fast Editing in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Reorder shots by reordering the list
what: Premiere's rearrange edit (Ctrl/Command+Alt/Option drag) inserts the clip elsewhere and shifts only the destination track; Resolve's Shuffle/Swap Insert (Command-Shift drag) and Cut-page swap move clips and close gaps
how: change the order of `file` lines in the concat list: `file 'B.mp4'` then `file 'A.mp4'` with `-f concat -safe 0 -i re.txt -c copy` (6 s, no re-encode). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.38 "Modifying Clips", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24
Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.29 "Trimming in the Cut Page", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Audio follows video when switching angles
what: Premiere's multicam 'Switch Audio' setting makes each angle's audio switch with its video (audio-follows-video); FCP's default switch mode switches video and audio together
how: take audio and video from the same angle for each segment: `[0:v]trim=0:1...[a];[0:a]atrim=0:1,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[aa];[1:v]trim=1:2...[b];[1:a]atrim=1:2,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[ba];[a][aa][b][ba]concat=n=2:v=1:a=1` (2 s). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/cut-and-switch-camera-angles-ver23c76c9c/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Decide which lanes ripple (sync lock / auto select)
what: Premiere: on insert, ripple delete or ripple trim, other tracks shift only if their Sync Lock is on; Resolve: rippling happens only on tracks with Auto Select enabled, so a music or title lane can stay put
how: in a HyperFrames plan file, include a move only for clips on lanes that must follow the edit; leave the music bed and long titles out of the plan.
refs: Blackmagic, DaVinci Resolve 19.1 Reference Manual ch.44 "Trimming", https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_19_Reference_Manual.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Frame numbering: NLE frame counts vs ffmpeg n
what: Premiere's Frame Count display can start at 0 or 1, or use Timecode Conversion (10 s at 30 fps = frame 300)
how: ffmpeg's select/showinfo `n` starts at 0, so 'frame 1' in an NLE that counts from 1 is `n=0`; seconds = n / fps.

name: No Motion = virtual tripod
what: Premiere Warp Stabilizer's Result 'No Motion' tries to remove all camera motion (Smooth Motion keeps a smoothed move); FCP InertiaCam can offer a Tripod Mode for a static-camera look
how: vid.stab's tripod option ('equivalent to relative=0:smoothing=0'): `ffmpeg -i A.mp4 -vf vidstabdetect=tripod=1:result=tri.trf -f null -` then `-vf vidstabtransform=input=tri.trf:tripod=1`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/correct-shaky-video-verbacf92b/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Deinterlace before freezing or slowing interlaced clips
what: Premiere's 'Always Deinterlace' field option is meant for interlaced clips you play in slow motion or freeze (it keeps the dominant field and interpolates the rest); FCP's Deinterlace setting doubles the frame rate (29.97 -> 59.94)
how: `bwdif=mode=send_field` doubled a 15 fps interlaced test clip to 30 fps (45 -> 90 frames); then freeze: `bwdif=mode=send_frame,trim=start_frame=10:end_frame=11,loop=loop=29:size=1:start=0` (30-frame hold). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/conform-frame-sizes-and-rates-ver3363b44e/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Transition direction = pick the mirrored xfade
what: Premiere transitions have edge selectors (e.g. Barn Doors vertical or horizontal) and a Reverse option (Clock Wipe counter-clockwise); FCP sets a wipe's Direction
how: xfade has no direction switch but lists mirrored pairs: wipeleft/wiperight, slideup/slidedown, vertopen/horzopen, circleopen/circleclose; tested `xfade=transition=horzopen:duration=1:offset=2` and `wiperight`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/adjust-transitions-inspector-viewer-vercf3c6b27/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Beat grid for cutting to music
what: FCP Beat Detection (Option-B) shows song parts, bars and beats as a grid that edit points snap to; it works best with 4/4 music
how: `npx hyperframes beats --json` on a project whose music `<audio>` has `data-timeline-role="music"` wrote `beats/assets/music.mp3.json` (127 beats, 129 BPM, each with time and strength); snap cut times to those beat times with `gsap.utils.snap(beatTimes, t)`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Apple Final Cut Pro guide, https://support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro/edit-to-the-beat-ver65b55a2b7/mac, checked 2026-10-24

name: Read all five colour properties first
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: every decoded frame needs primaries, transfer, matrix and range to become light, plus chroma location. If any is missing or wrong the encode still "works" but colours shift, blacks lift or crush, or HDR looks flat
how: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=pix_fmt,color_range,color_space,color_transfer,color_primaries,chroma_location -of default=nw=1 in.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Look at the first frame for HDR side data
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: mastering display, content light level, Dolby Vision and HDR10+ data usually sit per frame in the bitstream, not on the stream
how: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -read_intervals "%+#1" -show_frames in.mp4` and look for `side_data_type=Mastering display metadata` / `Content light level metadata` (tested here 2026-10-24 on an x265 HDR10 clip: printed red_x=34000/50000, max_luminance=10000000/10000, max_content=1000, max_average=400)

name: Tagging is not converting
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: there are three different jobs: preserve (keep samples and tags), retag (change only the metadata, right only when the source was mis-tagged), convert (change the samples, then tag the new system). Writing bt709 onto BT.601 pixels makes the colours wrong. Tagging PQ as bt709 does not tone-map it
how: decide which of the three you are doing before writing any filter. Use `setparams` to retag and `zscale`/`scale`/`colorspace` to convert.

name: Players guess untagged video differently
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: mpv 0.41 picks the BT.709 matrix when width >= 1280 or height > 576, otherwise BT.601. It picks the transfer as BT.1886 for limited range and sRGB for full range. So an untagged 720x480 file can look right in one player and slightly green in another
how: tag every export, and never assume an untagged source is BT.709. Check where it came from.

name: Guess the truth of unknown tags from the source
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: DVDs are BT.601 (smpte170m NTSC, bt470bg PAL), HD Blu-ray/broadcast are BT.709, UHD Blu-ray HDR is BT.2020 + PQ. A 1080p upscale of a DVD can still carry BT.601 colours
how: use the origin, not the resolution, to pick values for `setparams`.

name: Retag frames with setparams
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: `setparams` marks colour range, primaries, trc and colorspace on the frames without changing the input pixels. It affects how later filters/encoders treat the frame
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf setparams=color_primaries=smpte170m:color_trc=smpte170m:colorspace=smpte170m:range=tv -c:v libx264 -crf 18 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24; ffprobe then showed tv/smpte170m on all three)

name: Retag H.264 without re-encoding
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: the h264_metadata bitstream filter rewrites colour_primaries, transfer_characteristics and matrix_coefficients in the VUI (H.273 numbers). Pass the same values as output options so the container agrees
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v h264_metadata=colour_primaries=1:transfer_characteristics=1:matrix_coefficients=1 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Retag HEVC without re-encoding
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: hevc_metadata has the same colour description options (and video_full_range_flag, chroma_sample_loc_type)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v hevc_metadata=colour_primaries=9:transfer_characteristics=18:matrix_coefficients=9 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix only the range flag in the bitstream
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: when samples are limited but the file is tagged pc, flip `video_full_range_flag` and set `-color_range` so the container matches
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v h264_metadata=video_full_range_flag=0 -color_range tv out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bitstream filters leave the container colour fields alone
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: from MKV/MP4 input, ffmpeg copies the old container values (Matroska Colour elements, MP4 colr box), so ffprobe can keep showing the old tags. For an existing MKV, mkvpropedit fixes them in place. Remuxing with mkvmerge keeps the old values
how: `mkvpropedit out.mkv --edit track:v1 --set color-transfer-characteristics=1 --set color-primaries=1 --set color-matrix-coefficients=1` (needs mkvtoolnix, missing)

name: Output colour options behave differently by ffmpeg version
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: in ffmpeg 7.1 and later the encoder takes colour properties from the filtered frames: `-color_primaries`/`-color_trc` get overwritten, and `-colorspace`/`-color_range` can trigger an auto-inserted scaler that converts samples. Encode Wiki says to tag with setparams and convert with an explicit filter
how: in this repo's ffmpeg 6.1, `-colorspace 1 -color_primaries 1 -color_trc 1` did tag the output. For portable scripts, still use `setparams` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Tag options never move pixels
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: `-colorspace 1 -color_primaries 1 -color_trc 1` only add meta information. They do not transform the colour space of the video
how: pair the tags with a converting filter, e.g. `ffmpeg -i in.png -pix_fmt yuv420p -vf colorspace=all=bt709:iall=bt601-6-625:fast=1 -colorspace 1 -color_primaries 1 -color_trc 1 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: H.273 code points to remember
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: primaries 1 = BT.709/sRGB, 9 = BT.2020, 11 = DCI-P3 (DCI white), 12 = P3-D65/Display P3. Transfer 1 = BT.709, 13 = sRGB, 16 = PQ, 18 = HLG. Matrix 0 = GBR (RGB), 1 = BT.709, 5/6 = BT.601, 9 = BT.2020 NCL, 14 = ICtCp
how: use these numbers in h264_metadata/hevc_metadata.

name: "1-1-1" means a Rec.709 SDR master
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: QuickTime `colr` atom type `nclc` stores three indexes (primaries, transfer, matrix). MP4 `nclx` adds a full_range flag. 1-1-1 is the right tag for HD SDR pixels graded in Rec.709 and wrong for a P3 grade
how: check the three values with ffprobe before sending a MOV.

name: Transfer codes 1, 6, 14 and 15 are the same curve
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: BT.709, BT.601, BT.2020-10 and BT.2020-12 describe one curve. Use the one that matches the system. mpv displays all four with BT.1886
how: don't "fix" a 6 to a 1 expecting a visual change.

name: Pure-2.2 content can be tagged bt470m
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: sRGB (13) has a linear toe while many displays and much RGB content use a pure 2.2 power curve. If content was made for pure 2.2, tag transfer 4 (bt470m, "assumed display gamma 2.2")
how: `setparams=color_trc=bt470m` (option listed in setparams docs)

name: Tag checklist after every export
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: run the same ffprobe on source and output and compare. Then watch both side by side in a player that honours tags (mpv), looking at skin, saturated reds/greens and shadow detail
how: stream ffprobe from skill 801 plus frame ffprobe from 802 on both files.

name: Standalone x264/x265 pipes lose all colour info
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: Y4M carries no primaries, transfer or matrix, so pass `--colorprim/--transfer/--colormatrix/--range/--chromaloc` yourself. x265 4.3 ignores the Y4M full-range flag and tags limited
how: inside ffmpeg use `-x264-params colorprim=bt709:transfer=bt709:colormatrix=bt709:range=tv:chromaloc=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 signal-type presets
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: `--video-signal-type-preset` sets primaries, transfer, matrix, range and chroma location in one go (e.g. BT2100_HLG_YCC = bt2020 / arib-std-b67 / bt2020nc / limited / chromaloc 2). It overrides individual VUI options
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -x265-params "video-signal-type-preset=BT2100_HLG_YCC" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube standardises unclear SDR tags
section: Colour tags: read, keep, retag, convert
what: unspecified TRC → BT.709. Unknown matrix and primaries → BT.709. A 601/709 mix is made consistent by the matrix. Full range is converted to limited, BT.2020 without an HDR transfer is converted to BT.709 8-bit, and an RGB matrix upload is not recommended
how: upload SDR tagged 1-1-1 limited (`setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv`).

name: Luma is a weighted sum set by KR and KB
what: Y′ = KR·R′ + (1−KR−KB)·G′ + KB·B′. BT.709 uses KR 0.2126/KB 0.0722, BT.601 0.299/0.114, BT.2020 NCL 0.2627/0.0593. ffprobe reports the matrix as color_space
how: read `color_space` with ffprobe.

name: Luma is not luminance
what: luma (Y′) is a weighted sum of gamma-compressed R′G′B′. Relative luminance (Y) is a weighted sum of linear RGB. SMPTE EG 28 uses Y′ for luma and Y for luminance
how: remember signalstats YAVG is luma code values, not light.

name: A wrong matrix shifts saturated colours, not greys
what: decoding with the wrong matrix barely changes greys but moves reds, greens and skin. You often only see it next to the source
how: compare a skin crop of source vs encode with `hstack`.

name: Which tag mistakes you can see
what: wrong primaries (SMPTE 170M vs Rec.709) is almost undetectable. Wrong transfer (sRGB vs Rec.709) shows side by side. Wrong Y′CbCr encoding (601 vs 709) is easy to see
how: fix the matrix first when tags are in doubt.

name: PNG/RGB to video defaults to the BT.601 matrix
what: ffmpeg converts RGB input (PNG frames, screen captures) to YUV with BT.601 and leaves it untagged, and HD players then decode it as BT.709
how: `ffmpeg -i in.png -vf scale=out_color_matrix=bt709,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709 -c:v libx264 out.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24; on 6.1 the colorspace tag stayed unknown until `colorspace=bt709` was added to setparams)

name: Convert the matrix when SD becomes HD
what: upscaling a DVD to 1080p and tagging BT.709 without converting shifts greens and skin. zscale takes the input interpretation explicitly
how: `ffmpeg -i dvd.mkv -vf zscale=w=1440:h=1080:f=spline36:min=170m:pin=170m:tin=601:m=709:p=709:t=709 -c:v libx264 -crf 18 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24). For PAL use `min=470bg:pin=bt470bg`.

name: scale converts only the matrix
what: the built-in scale filter converts the matrix, so keep the source's primaries and transfer tags when you use it
how: `ffmpeg -i dvd.mkv -vf scale=1440:1080:in_color_matrix=bt601:out_color_matrix=bt709,setparams=color_primaries=smpte170m:color_trc=smpte170m -c:v libx264 -crf 18 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: colormatrix is the basic matrix filter
what: `colormatrix=src:dst` converts between bt709, fcc, bt601, bt470, bt470bg, smpte170m, smpte240m and bt2020. It does not set tags itself
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf colormatrix=bt601:bt709 -c:v libx264 out.mp4` then tag (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: colorspace filter: fast=1 equals colormatrix
what: `fast=1` skips gamma/primary correction (less CPU, mathematically incorrect). It gives output compatible with colormatrix
how: `colorspace=all=bt709:iall=bt601-6-625:fast=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: colorspace needs input tags or iall
what: the filter needs even frame size. If the input transfer/space/primaries/range are missing it logs an error and does not convert. Override with `iall`, `ispace`, `iprimaries`, `itrc`, `irange`
how: `colorspace=all=bt709:iall=bt601-6-625` for an untagged SD source.

name: colorspace can write 10-bit output
what: `format=` takes yuv420p/422p/444p in 8, 10 and 12 bit
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf colorspace=all=bt709:format=yuv420p10 -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: colorspace dithering and white-point adaptation
what: `dither=fsb` gives Floyd-Steinberg dithering. `wpadapt=bradford|vonkries|identity` sets white-point adaptation when primaries change
how: `colorspace=all=bt709:iall=bt2020:format=yuv420p:dither=fsb` and `colorspace=all=bt709:iall=bt2020:wpadapt=bradford` (both tested here 2026-10-24). `clipgamut=rgb` is in current docs but "Option not found" on 6.1.

name: Accurate swscale flags for colour conversion
what: the ffmpeg-tests author recommends the scale filter with `spline+accurate_rnd+full_chroma_int+full_chroma_inp`
how: `ffmpeg -i in.png -sws_flags spline+accurate_rnd+full_chroma_int+full_chroma_inp -vf scale=in_range=full:in_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv:out_color_matrix=bt709 -pix_fmt yuv444p10le -c:v libx264 -qp 0 -color_range tv -colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: swscale dither choice
what: `sws_dither` accepts auto (default), bayer, ed (error diffusion), a_dither and x_dither
how: `ffmpeg -i in10bit.mp4 -sws_dither ed -vf format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: BT.2020 C and NCL are different signals
what: bt2020nc (9) is normal for UHD SDR, HDR10 and HLG. bt2020c (10) needs different maths, so switching 9↔10 is never a fix. ICtCp (14) is a separate representation
how: leave 9 alone on phone/HDR files.

name: ICtCp basics
what: ICtCp (BT.2100) is RGB→LMS (3×3), then PQ or HLG nonlinearity, then another 3×3. I is intensity, CT blue-yellow, CP red-green. It is mostly used with PQ. BT.2408 prefers Y′CbCr for HLG and notes compatibility limits for ICtCp
how: treat `color_space=ictcp` files as special and don't retag them.

name: Range code-value table
what: 8-bit limited: luma 16–235, chroma 16–240. 10-bit limited: 64–940 / 64–960. Full: 0–255 / 0–1023. Neutral chroma is 128 (8-bit) and 512 (10-bit)
how: use 128/512 as the "no colour" target when reading UAVG/VAVG.

name: Deliver limited range
what: Blu-ray, UHD Blu-ray (incl. HDR), broadcast and streaming are limited range almost without exception. Full range turns up in screen recordings, some phone/webcam footage, JPEG-derived video and RGB sources
how: convert full-range phone/screen clips to limited for delivery (next skills).

name: Don't clamp a source for overshoot
what: values below 16 or above 235 can legitimately appear in limited-range video (camera/filter overshoot). Players clip them on display, but encoders and filters normally keep them
how: measure before deciding to legalise.

name: Rule out the player before fixing range
what: Encode Wiki: GPU drivers and TVs have their own range settings that produce the same washed-out or crushed symptoms as a file mix-up, so check the player/display first
how: compare the file's signalstats YMIN/YMAX with what the screen shows before re-encoding anything.

name: Prove the range from samples, not one frame
what: measure a scene that should hold black and white (credits). YMIN near 16 / YMAX near 235 means limited. 0 / 255 means full. A dim scene proves nothing
how: `ffmpeg -ss 00:10:00 -i in.mkv -frames:v 100 -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=-" -f null - | grep -E "YMIN|YMAX"` (pattern tested here 2026-10-24 with file= output)

name: Full→limited with scale needs format=yuv420p
what: ffmpeg decodes 8-bit full-range H.264/HEVC as legacy yuvj420p. Without `format=yuv420p`, scale silently does nothing
how: `ffmpeg -i full.mp4 -vf scale=out_range=limited,format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 -crf 18 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24: YMIN/YMAX went from 0/239 to about 13/218, but on 6.1 the range tag came out unknown)

name: Fix the unknown range tag on 6.1
what: here neither `setparams=range=tv` nor `-color_range tv` nor `-x264-params range=tv` tagged the converted file. A copy pass with h264_metadata did
how: `ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v h264_metadata=video_full_range_flag=0 -color_range tv out_tv.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24: ffprobe color_range=tv)

name: zscale converts range but may keep the pc tag
what: zscale=range=limited converts the samples but can leave the output tagged full range
how: `ffmpeg -i full.mp4 -vf zscale=rangein=full:range=limited,format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24), then retag as in 843.

name: yuvj formats are deprecated
what: yuvj420p is the legacy name for full-range 8-bit. ffmpeg developers have worked to remove YUVJ in favour of yuv420p plus a range tag
how: write full range as `format=yuv420p,setparams=range=pc` (tested here 2026-10-24; ffprobe still reported yuvj420p/pc on 6.1)

name: Matroska range numbers differ
what: Matroska's Range element uses 1 = broadcast (limited), 2 = full. The H.273 bitstream flag uses 0 = limited, 1 = full
how: mkvmerge `--color-range 0:1` means limited.

name: Narrow range keeps headroom, full range has none
what: BT.2100 narrow range keeps super-whites and sub-blacks for overshoots from resizing, filtering and compression, and clipping them adds distortion. BT.2408 says full range should not be used for HLG production/exchange. Full-range PQ only when all parties agree
how: keep HDR exports `range=tv`.

name: Legalise only with care
what: EBU R103 (2000): accept material when matrixed R, G, B lie within −5%…105% and luminance within −1%…103%. It warns that gamut "legalisers" can create artefacts more visible than the gamut errors
how: clip with `lutyuv="y='clip(val,16,235)':u='clip(val,16,240)':v='clip(val,16,240)'"` only when a spec demands it (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Out-of-gamut errors need area, not single pixels
what: R103 recommends flagging an error only when it covers more than 1% of the active picture, after a ~1 MHz low-pass to ignore transient overshoots
how: use signalstats BRNG (fraction of out-of-range pixels) per frame and judge against ~1% (BRNG read 0.0135 on testsrc2, tested here 2026-10-24).

name: limiter filter
what: limits pixel components to [min,max] per plane. `auto` uses the colourspace's signal levels for TV-range YUV
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf limiter=min=16:max=235:planes=1 -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: J:a:b notation
what: J = width of the reference region (usually 4), a = chroma samples in the first row, b = chroma changes between first and second row
how: yuv420p = 4:2:0, yuv422p = 4:2:2, yuv444p = 4:4:4 in ffmpeg names.

name: Bandwidth saving of subsampling
what: Matrox: 4:2:2 cuts overall image bandwidth by 33%, 4:2:0 by 50%
how: expect 4:2:0 for all delivery and 4:2:2 for ProRes intermediates.

name: Upsampling 4:2:0 to 4:4:4 recovers nothing
what: it only makes the file bigger. 4:4:4 helps for screen recordings, game UI and text overlays, where thin coloured edges smear at 4:2:0. Most hardware decoders and browsers expect 4:2:0
how: keep the source subsampling, and use 4:4:4 only for text-heavy screen captures.

name: Pixel format says nothing about colour meaning
what: a yuv420p10le file can be SDR BT.709, HDR10 or HLG. Primaries/transfer/matrix/range carry the meaning
how: never infer HDR from bit depth. Read `color_transfer`.

name: gbrp is planar RGB in G,B,R order
what: ffmpeg's gbrp stores planes as G, B, R. gbrpf32le is planar 32-bit float. A wrong depth/order/endianness in a raw pipe gives garbage colours
how: grade in RGB with `format=gbrp,...,format=yuv420p` (tested here 2026-10-24 with curves)

name: Chroma location values
what: AVChromaLocation: left = MPEG-2/4 4:2:0 and H.264 default. center = MPEG-1/JPEG. topleft = ITU-R 601, SMPTE 274M, MPEG-2 4:2:2. For HEVC BT.2020/BT.2100 (e.g. UHD Blu-ray) chroma is co-sited top-left
how: read `chroma_location` with ffprobe and keep it when re-encoding.

name: ITU guidance on ChromaLocType
what: H-Suppl.19: typical SD/HD (NCG) uses ChromaLocType 0, WCG/UHD uses 2 (co-sited). x265 presets for BT.2100 use `--chromaloc 2`
how: for HDR HEVC add `chromaloc=2` in -x265-params when the source is co-sited.

name: Set or convert chroma siting
what: the `-chroma_sample_location` codec option tags it. zscale `chromalin`/`chromal` converts
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -chroma_sample_location topleft -c:v libx264 out.mp4` and `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf zscale=chromalin=left:chromal=topleft,format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (both tested here 2026-10-24; ffprobe chroma_location=topleft)

name: Look at Y, U and V planes separately
what: extractplanes splits components into greyscale streams, useful to see chroma noise or blocking
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "extractplanes=y+u+v[y][u][v]" -map "[y]" -frames:v 1 y.png -map "[u]" -frames:v 1 u.png -map "[v]" -frames:v 1 v.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shift misregistered chroma
what: chromashift moves Cb/Cr horizontally/vertically (cbh, cbv, crh, crv; edge smear/warp)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf chromashift=cbh=2:crh=-2:edge=smear -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Reduce chroma noise only
what: chromanr averages chroma where the YUV difference is under `thres` (default 30) and leaves luma untouched
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf chromanr=thres=30:sizew=5:sizeh=5 -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Swapped U/V or planes
what: swapuv swaps U and V. shuffleplanes reorders planes (e.g. `0:2:1` swaps second and third)
how: `-vf swapuv` or `-vf shuffleplanes=0:2:1` (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Detect RGB/BGR and YUV swaps with test sources
what: rgbtestsrc should show red, green, blue stripes top to bottom. yuvtestsrc should show y, cb, cr stripes
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i rgbtestsrc=size=320x240 -frames:v 1 rgb.png` then push it through your chain and compare (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Remove chroma to check luma alone
what: lutyuv `u=128:v=128` turns video greyscale by neutralising chroma
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "lutyuv=u=128:v=128" -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rec.709 primaries and white
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: R 0.640/0.330, G 0.300/0.600, B 0.150/0.060, D65 white 0.3127/0.3290. sRGB uses the same primaries and white point
how: these are the `bt709` primaries in every ffmpeg option.

name: BT.709 OETF formula
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
how: an 18% grey gives V ≈ 0.409 (computed here with that formula, `python3 -c "print(1.099*0.18**0.45-0.099)"`, tested here 2026-10-24)

name: BT.709 never defined the display; BT.1886 does
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: BT.1886 (2011) is the reference EOTF for SDR flat panels: L = a·max(V+b,0)^2.4, with a and b from screen white Lw and black Lb. It is used for Rec.709 and Rec.2020 SDR
how: grade SDR on a gamma 2.4 reference, and export tagged bt709.

name: OETF, EOTF, OOTF
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: the camera applies an OETF (scene light → signal), the display an EOTF (signal → light), and the end-to-end relation is the OOTF. The two are not inverses because scene light differs from displayed light. "Gamma" is a loose word for these
how: always say which direction a curve or LUT goes.

name: Direction check: 0.5^2.4 vs 0.5^(1/2.4)
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: 0.5 decoded with 2.4 gives ~0.189 and encoded gives ~0.749. Those are opposite directions of one pair, not two contrast presets
how: if a "gamma" fix makes things far too dark or light, you applied the inverse.

name: sRGB piecewise curve
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
how: use these when converting sRGB PNG values to linear in Python.

name: sRGB EOTF: piecewise vs pure 2.2 is disputed
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: the IEC text's reference display reads like pure 2.2, but Jack Holm (IEC secretary) says the piecewise function is the EOTF. ACES 2.0 ships both outputs. Many sRGB/Display P3 devices measure as pure 2.2
how: expect small shadow differences between monitors, and don't chase them in the grade.

name: Rec.709 vs sRGB effective gamma
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: both are piecewise. sRGB's decoding is close to 2.2 overall, while Rec.709's overall encoding gamma is about 0.5 (decoding ~2.0)
how: an image made for sRGB web viewing and one graded on BT.1886 2.4 will not match exactly.

name: Rec.2020 gamut
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: primaries R 0.708/0.292, G 0.170/0.797, B 0.131/0.046 (D65). They lie on the spectral locus (630/532/467 nm). Coverage of CIE 1931: Rec.2020 75.8%, DCI-P3 53.6%, Rec.709 35.9%
how: `bt2020` primaries in zscale/setparams.

name: BT.2020 is a container, not the real gamut
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: most HDR is graded on a P3-D65 monitor and delivered in BT.2020. Tag the stream bt2020 and record P3 in the mastering metadata, not smpte432
how: keep `colorprim=bt2020` with a P3 `master-display` string.

name: BT.2020 does not mean HDR
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: UHD SDR also uses BT.2020 primaries. The transfer (smpte2084 or arib-std-b67) decides HDR
how: check `color_transfer`, not `color_primaries`.

name: P3 variants
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: DCI-P3: 2.6 gamma, 48 cd/m², DCI white 0.314/0.351 (~6300 K, slightly green). P3-D65 keeps the primaries with D65 white. Apple Display P3 = P3 primaries + D65 + sRGB curve, tagged smpte432 + iec61966-2-1
how: never tag Display P3 phone stills as smpte431.

name: P3 cannot be fully carried in positive Rec.2020
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: the P3 red lies very slightly outside the spectral locus, so 100% of P3 can't be encoded with positive Rec.2020 values
how: expect tiny red clipping in P3-limited masters in a 2020 container.

name: Retagging changes perceived saturation
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: tagging BT.709 pixels as bt2020 makes colours oversaturated, and the reverse looks dull. Wide → narrow gamut is a real conversion
how: convert with explicit in/out primaries, e.g. `zscale=p=709:m=709:t=709:tin=2020_10,format=yuv420p` for BT.2020 SDR (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: colorspace filter is not an HDR tone mapper
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: it converts matrix/primaries/trc, so use it for BT.2020 SDR → BT.709 SDR, not PQ/HLG → SDR
how: for HDR use the zscale+tonemap chain.

name: CIE plot of your pixels
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: ciescope overlays pixels on a CIE diagram with chosen gamut outlines (rec709, rec2020, dcip3 ...) and optional white point
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "format=rgb24,ciescope=system=rec709:cie=xyy:gamuts=rec709+rec2020+dcip3:showwhite=1" -frames:v 1 -update 1 cie.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Scene-referred vs display-referred
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: scene-referred signals represent light detected by the camera. Display-referred signals represent light on the grading monitor. They differ because the camera-to-display system is non-linear
how: log and HLG are scene-referred, PQ is display-referred: pick conversions accordingly.

name: Relative vs absolute signals
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: relative signals are ratios to the sensor peak (BT.601/709/2020, S-Log, LogC, HLG). An absolute signal gives each code a luminance in cd/m². PQ is the only absolute signal in wide use
how: a PQ code value means the same nits on every reference display.

name: SDR is about 5 stops without banding
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: BBC: 8-bit SDR TV has a displayed dynamic range of about 32:1 (5 stops) once banding is considered. A 10,000:1 HDR range needs about 700 just-noticeable levels, so 10-bit is necessary and 8 bits are inadequate
how: never deliver HDR in 8-bit.

name: Wide-gamut tag pitfall on YouTube HDR
section: Colour spaces and transfer functions (theory you need)
what: YouTube: mastering in P3 and tagging Rec.2020 primaries gives an oversaturated look with shifted hues. DCI-P3 delivery is not supported, so grade in Rec.2020 with PQ or HLG
how: convert P3 to 2020 values before tagging bt2020.

name: 10-bit gives four times the steps
what: 8-bit = 256 levels per channel, 10-bit = 1024, 12-bit = 4096. A sky across 20 codes in 8-bit gets 80 in 10-bit
how: do heavy grades on a 10-bit intermediate.

name: Encode 10-bit even from 8-bit sources
what: the encoder's prediction and quantisation keep more precision, so a 10-bit encode of an 8-bit source bands less at about the same bitrate
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -c:v libx264 -crf 18 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24). Check the target player supports 10-bit H.264.

name: Dither hides steps but restores nothing
what: dither spreads quantisation error into fine noise so contours are less visible. A dithered 8-bit image is still 8-bit
how: add dither only at the final bit-depth reduction (zscale `d=error_diffusion`).
refs: Why It Looks Like That, https://whyitlookslikethat.com/articles/tv-bit-depth-8-bit-vs-10-bit-banding-hdr, checked 2026-10-24

name: zscale dither on the way down
what: zscale `dither` takes none (default), ordered, random, error_diffusion
how: end an HDR→SDR chain with `zscale=t=709:m=709:r=limited:d=error_diffusion,format=yuv420p` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 8-bit PQ bands visibly
what: PQ and HLG need at least 10-bit samples. `-pix_fmt yuv420p` on a 10-bit HDR source keeps the tags but quantises PQ to 8 bits
how: keep `yuv420p10le` for any HDR output.

name: 8-bit SDR inside HDR limits up-mapping
what: BT.2408: up-mapping expands SDR highlights, and 8-bit resolution plus 8-bit compression limits how far before banding shows
how: prefer direct mapping of 8-bit phone clips into an HDR edit.

name: 10-bit is enough for HDR, 12-bit gives headroom
what: BT.2408: good HDR programmes can be made with 10-bit infrastructure and codecs at bitrates like SDR. 12-bit production systems give more headroom for later processing of PQ and HLG
how: keep HDR masters at least `yuv420p10le`, and consider 12-bit when heavy processing follows.

name: xvYCC uses the spare chroma codes
what: xvYCC keeps BT.709 primaries/white and luma 16–235, and uses chroma codes 1–15 and 241–254 for extended-gamut colour. It is always limited range
how: a clipping legaliser on chroma 16–240 throws such colours away, so don't clip camera files tagged xvYCC (`color_transfer=iec61966-2-4`).

name: Float RGB for precision
what: tonemap expects single-precision float. gbrpf32le carries out-of-range values between filters
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "format=gbrpf32le,exposure=exposure=0.3,format=yuv420p" -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Waveform with legal-range graticule in IRE
what: waveform `graticule=green|orange|invert` draws legal broadcast ranges. `scale=digital|millivolts|ire` sets the units
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "waveform=graticule=green:scale=ire:flags=numbers" -frames:v 1 -update 1 wf.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Waveform in millivolts
what: `scale=millivolts` for engineers who think in mV (PAL 100 IRE = 700 mV)
how: `-vf "waveform=graticule=orange:scale=millivolts"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Peak envelope over a whole clip
what: waveform/vectorscope `envelope=peak` holds min and max values over time, so out-of-range values show without watching every frame
how: `-vf "waveform=envelope=peak:graticule=green"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Overlay RGB waveform for neutrals
what: `display=overlay` superimposes the component graphs, which makes it easier to see if whites, greys and blacks that should be identical line up
how: `-vf "format=gbrp,waveform=display=overlay:components=7"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Waveform filters: flat, aflat, chroma
what: `filter=flat` shows luma and chroma combined, `aflat` the Cb–Cr difference, `chroma` only chroma, `color` the actual colour values
how: `-vf "waveform=filter=chroma:components=7"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Vectorscope with named targets and white point
what: vectorscope `graticule=color` with `flags=name+white` draws colour point names and the white target. `colorspace=601|709` picks the graticule
how: `-vf "vectorscope=mode=color4:envelope=peak:graticule=color:flags=name+white:colorspace=709"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Vectorscope of shadows or highlights only
what: `lthreshold`/`hthreshold` ignore pixels whose third component (luma) is outside the band (fractions of max), so you can see the cast of shadows and highlights separately
how: shadows `-vf "vectorscope=mode=color3:lthreshold=0:hthreshold=0.3"`, highlights `lthreshold=0.7:hthreshold=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Histogram parade, logarithmic
what: histogram `display_mode=parade` puts components side by side, and `levels_mode=logarithmic` shows sparse values
how: `-vf "histogram=display_mode=parade:levels_mode=logarithmic"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Histogram across time
what: thistogram keeps past histograms, so exposure drift or flicker over a shot shows as one picture
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "thistogram=display_mode=overlay:envelope=1:slide=picture" -update 1 th.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Read exact pixel numbers
what: datascope prints pixel values (hex or dec) for a region. pixscope shows sample values plus area statistics (minimum input 640x480)
how: `-vf "datascope=s=640x360:x=300:y=150:mode=color2:format=dec:axis=1"` and `-vf "scale=640:480,pixscope=x=0.5:y=0.5:w=7:h=7"` (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: signalstats percentiles and colour metrics
what: YLOW/YHIGH are the 10th/90th percentile luma. SATAVG/SATMAX are saturation, HUEMED/HUEAVG are hue, and Y/U/VBITDEPTH the plane depth. These are steadier than min/max
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=ss.txt" -frames:v 1 -f null -` then grep YLOW/YHIGH (tested here 2026-10-24: YLOW 41, YHIGH 210 on testsrc2)

name: Highlight out-of-broadcast-range pixels
what: `signalstats=out=brng:color=red` paints illegal pixels. `stat=brng` adds a BRNG value per frame
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "signalstats=out=brng:color=red" -frames:v 1 -update 1 brng.png` and `-vf "signalstats=stat=brng,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.BRNG:file=brng.txt"` (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One QC sheet: picture + waveform + vectorscope
what: Tek describes the waveform for luma/legal levels and the vectorscope for chroma. Stack them under the frame
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]split=3[a][b][c];[b]waveform=graticule=green:scale=ire,scale=640:360[w];[c]format=yuv444p,vectorscope=mode=color3:graticule=color,scale=360:360,pad=640:360[v];[a][w]vstack[top];[top][v]vstack" -frames:v 1 -update 1 panel.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Legal luma on a waveform
what: the brightest luma should not go past 100%, with occasional speculars allowed to about 105% depending on the broadcaster, and the darkest not below 0%. No digital format uses 7.5 IRE setup
how: read the IRE waveform from 894 against 0/100.

name: IRE, millivolts, code values
what: 100 IRE = 714 mV in NTSC, and PAL peaks at 700 mV. A code value, its full-range percentage and its legal-range IRE are three different numbers (code 95 = 9.29% full range = 3.5 IRE legal)
how: say which scale you mean, and use `waveform=scale=ire` for IRE.

name: 75% vs 100% bar targets
what: if 75% bars fall short of targets the scope is set for 100% bars, and vice versa. In SMPTE bars only the top two-thirds (75% bars) hit the standard targets
how: generate bars and check the chain: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i smptehdbars=size=1280x720 -vf "format=yuv444p,vectorscope=mode=color3:graticule=color:flags=name" -frames:v 1 bars_vs.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Test patterns ffmpeg can make
what: smptehdbars (SMPTE RP 219), pal75bars/pal100bars (EBU 75%/100%), colorchart (colour checker, presets reference or skintones), colorspectrum, allrgb/allyuv (4096x4096 every colour), haldclutsrc
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i colorchart=preset=skintones -frames:v 1 skin.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pseudocolor presets for false colour
what: pseudocolor has built-in LUTs incl. range1, range2, shadows, highlights, solar, nominal, preferred, total, heat, viridis
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf pseudocolor=preset=preferred -frames:v 1 -update 1 fc.png` (tested here 2026-10-24). The docs don't publish the band levels, so use it to spot regions, not to read IRE.

name: Paint only too-bright luma
what: the pseudocolor docs give an expression that turns luma above ymax into a gradient and leaves the rest
how: `-vf "pseudocolor='if(between(val,ymax,amax),lerp(ymin,ymax,(val-ymax)/(amax-ymax)),-1):if(between(val,ymax,amax),lerp(umax,umin,(val-ymax)/(amax-ymax)),-1):if(between(val,ymax,amax),lerp(vmin,vmax,(val-ymax)/(amax-ymax)),-1)'"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ARRI false-colour zones
what: ARRI ALEXA false colour: purple 0–2.5% black clipping, blue 2.5–4% just above black, green 38–42% = 18% grey, pink 52–56% = one stop over grey, yellow 97–99% just below clipping, red 99–100% clipping
how: read the matching IRE bands off `waveform=scale=ire` when no false colour monitor is around.

name: Zebras warn, they don't expose
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: Sony: zebra stripes show areas near overexposure at a set IRE (70–100). They are not recorded and do not control exposure
how: in post, use 905 (brng) or 912 for the same warning.

name: 70 IRE zebra on skin highlights
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: set zebra to 70 IRE and close the iris until only a stripe or two remain on a cheekbone or forehead. One trainer puts Caucasian skin highlights around 80 IRE, another "skin falls nicely between 75/85 IRE"
how: check face highlights on the IRE waveform near those values, don't force them.

name: Kodak grey card procedure
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: 18% grey with 3% black and 90% white patches. Shoot it before every major lighting setup to give post exposure and colour balance references. It reflects R, G, B equally
how: crop the card in post and read its numbers (918).

name: Grey cards must be spectrally flat
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: a grey card's flat reflectance spectrum keeps it the colour of its illuminant (no metamerism). DSC warns look-alike cards with a yellow cast give blue-biased images when normalised
how: trust only proper cards as neutral references.

name: Measure a card or neutral patch in ffmpeg
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: crop the patch and read YAVG/UAVG/VAVG. A neutral patch reads U and V at 128 (8-bit)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "crop=40:40:300:160,signalstats,metadata=mode=print:file=patch.txt" -frames:v 1 -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24: grey testsrc2 patch gave U 128, V 128)

name: 18% grey ≈ 41% in Rec.709
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: the Rec.709 OETF puts 18% grey at about 40.9% (video levels). DSC places 18% grey "usually around 40 IRE", and some DPs peg 45–50%. It is a choice
how: read the card on `waveform=scale=ire` and expect roughly 40–50% depending on the chosen placement.

name: Middle grey per log curve
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: colourist values for 18% grey: ARRI LogC3 .391, LogC4 .28, BMD Film Gen5 .466, Canon Log 2 .398, Canon Log 3 .343, DJI D-Log .399, RED Log3G10 .333, Panasonic V-Log .423, Sony S-Log3 .411
how: check a grey card on log footage at these levels before converting.

name: V-Log anatomy
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: V-Log maps 0% reflectance to 7.3% IRE, 18% to 42% and 90% to 61%, with ~5.5 stops above 100% IRE. Below 18% it behaves like Rec.709
how: a lifted black around 7% is normal on V-Log, so don't "fix" it before conversion.

name: Don't mix IRE tables between makers
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: Sony and Panasonic print legal-range IRE beside code values, while ARRI's LogC4 IRE column is full-range percent. S-Log3 grey is 10-bit code 420 = 41.06% full = 40.64% legal
how: convert codes yourself: legal% = (CV−64)/876.

name: Stops are doublings of linear light
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: one stop up doubles linear light, so grey 0.18 becomes 0.36, then 0.72
how: the ffmpeg `exposure` filter takes EV in −3…+3 (`exposure=exposure=0.5:black=0`, tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Remove exposure flicker
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: deflicker smooths frame luminance variations with a moving average (size 2–129, modes am/gm/hm/qm/cm/pm/median)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf deflicker=size=5:mode=pm -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Histogram equalisation only for degraded video
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: histeq is an automatic contrast filter meant only for degraded or poorly captured video. Limit `intensity` to avoid wash-out, and `antibanding` adds slight random variation
how: `-vf histeq=strength=0.2:intensity=0.21:antibanding=weak` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Auto levels with normalize
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: normalize stretches each channel's range to black..white. `smoothing` (frames) acts like camera auto-exposure to stop flicker. `independence=0` keeps hue, `1` removes casts. `strength` blends
how: `-vf normalize=blackpt=black:whitept=white:smoothing=50:independence=0:strength=0.5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: BT.2408 HDR line-up levels
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: 18% grey card: 26 cd/m², 38% PQ, 38% HLG. Greyscale chart 90%: 179 cd/m², 57% PQ, 73% HLG. HDR Reference White (100%, also Graphics White): 203 cd/m², 58% PQ, 75% HLG (PQ display, or a 1000 cd/m² HLG display)
how: put a 58% PQ / 75% HLG marker on your HDR waveform.

name: BT.2408 skin and grass ranges in HDR
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
how: check face levels on PQ/HLG grades against these.

name: Grey cards drift after grading
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: BT.2408: 18% grey is closest to skin and good for matching SDR/HDR cameras (not affected by an SDR knee), but artistic painting/grading moves it, so its level varies after looks are applied
how: use the grey card for technical matching before the look.

name: Comfortable HDR brightness
section: Exposure, middle grey and reference cards
what: NHK test: images whose average luminance was under 25% of display peak were not judged too bright. BBC: mean display luminance 5–80 cd/m² gave nearly no annoying brightness jumps, and up to 160 cd/m² is an extended creative range
how: keep scene averages of HDR edits inside that band, and watch cuts between bright and dark shots.

name: Grey world needs linear light
what: the grayworld filter corrects colour on the grey-world assumption and works in linear light, so linearise first
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf zscale=transfer=linear,grayworld,zscale=transfer=bt709,format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Grey edge / max edge illuminant estimate
what: greyedge estimates the illuminant from edges. The docs' Grey Edge example is `difford=1:minknorm=5:sigma=2`, and Max Edge is `minknorm=0`
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf greyedge=difford=1:minknorm=5:sigma=2 -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24; max edge also ran)

name: Auto white balance per frame with colorcorrect
what: colorcorrect (YUV) with `analyze=average|minmax|median` derives shadow/highlight balance each frame. `manual` uses rl/bl/rh/bh
how: `-vf colorcorrect=analyze=median` (tested here 2026-10-24; YAVG/UAVG/VAVG moved slightly on testsrc2)

name: Manual black/white spot balance
what: colorcorrect rl/bl set the red/blue shadow spot, rh/bh the highlight spot (−1…1), plus a saturation control (−3…3)
how: `-vf colorcorrect=rl=-0.05:bl=0.05:rh=0.03:bh=-0.03:saturation=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Independent normalize removes casts
what: normalize with `independence=1` (default) stretches channels separately, which shifts colour and can remove casts. `0` links them and preserves hue
how: `-vf normalize=blackpt=black:whitept=white:smoothing=50:independence=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gray vs white card for camera WB
what: Art Adams got better results white balancing from grey cards. He found the Canon 5D balanced better off a grey card than a white card, and he exposes white and grey references to about the same IRE. X-Rite says the 18% card is for exposure and a WB card for colour
how: if both exist in a shot, sample the grey one for 931.

name: Mireds measure temperature shifts
what: mired = 1,000,000 / K. Equal mired steps are closer to equal perceived differences than equal kelvin steps. A 5700 K → 3200 K correction is about −137 mireds (CTB). Negative-mired gels look blue/green, positive amber/red
how: `python3 -c "print(round(1e6/5700-1e6/3200))"` → −137 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Metameric failure under peaky lights
what: two materials can match under one light and not another. Most fluorescent lights have peaky spectra, so matches made under them may fail elsewhere
how: a mixed-light shot may not balance with one global correction, so use a secondary (qualifier/window section).

name: ColorChecker as a target
what: the 24-patch chart has six greys, six primaries/secondaries and natural colours (dark/light skin, blue sky, foliage), with reflectances that mimic natural objects. Pigments changed in Nov 2014, so old RGB tables don't fit new cards
how: generate a reference chart with `colorchart=preset=reference` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lift, gamma, gain, offset
what: Resolve: Lift targets shadows, Gamma midtones, Gain highlights, Offset affects the image uniformly. The master sliders under each wheel control YRGB of that range. Ranges overlap widely
how: ffmpeg filters whose docs describe the matching controls: `colorlevels` input black/white points, `lutyuv=y=gammaval(g)` for gamma, `colorbalance` for shadows/midtones/highlights colour.

name: Log wheels are for log data
what: Resolve's Log mode gives Shadow/Midtone/Highlight/Offset with narrower, adjustable ranges meant for log-encoded images. Offset/Printer Points adjust the signal in a linear, film-oriented way
how: when grading log in ffmpeg before conversion, prefer offset-style moves (colorlevels output levels) over gamma.

name: ASC CDL math
what: out = (in × slope + offset)^power per R, G, B, plus one saturation number (v1.2). Slope ≥ 0 (nominal 1), offset any (0), power > 0 (1)
how: bake a CDL into a cube with Python (identity loops, apply the formula) and use `lut3d=file=cdl.cube` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CDL values only mean something in a known space
what: ACESCentral: CDL parameters in ACES workflows are meaningful when made and read on ACEScc values. Wikipedia: calibrations, viewing devices and output transforms must match at both ends
how: send a CDL only with a note of the space it was made in.

name: Levels with colour preservation
what: colorlevels has `preserve=lum|max|avg|sum|nrm|pwr` so a levels move doesn't shift colour
how: `-vf colorlevels=rimin=0.039:gimin=0.039:bimin=0.039:rimax=0.96:gimax=0.96:bimax=0.96:preserve=lum` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Output levels to constrain range
what: colorlevels romin/romax (0–1) pick a constrained output range. The docs' "increase brightness" example is `romin=0.5:gomin=0.5:bomin=0.5`
how: `-vf colorlevels=romin=0.05:gomin=0.05:bomin=0.05:romax=0.95:gomax=0.95:bomax=0.95` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Monotonic curves avoid overshoot
what: curves uses natural cubic splines by default. `interp=pchip` guarantees monotonic transitions between points (no wiggle past a point)
how: `-vf "curves=interp=pchip:master='0/0 0.25/0.20 0.75/0.80 1/1'"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Master curve is a second pass
what: curves `master` is applied after r/g/b like a post LUT. `all` sets r, g and b together

name: Per-channel curve for a mid-tone cast
what: the docs' example lifts the blue midtone slightly with `curves=blue='0/0 0.5/0.58 1/1'`
how: use a per-channel mid point for a cast that sits only in the mids (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gamma on luma only
what: lutyuv `gammaval(g)` applies a power to luma between minval and maxval
how: `-vf "lutyuv=y=gammaval(0.8)"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Colour contrast between opposing pairs
what: colorcontrast sets red-cyan, green-magenta and blue-yellow contrast. Each needs a weight (`rcw` etc.) above 0, and `pl` preserves lightness
how: `-vf colorcontrast=rc=0.2:rcw=0.5:pl=0.5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Channel mixer with luminance preserved
what: colorchannelmixer `pc=lum|max|avg|sum|nrm|pwr` with amount `pa` keeps brightness while channels are remixed
how: `-vf colorchannelmixer=rr=1.1:bb=0.9:pc=lum:pa=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: vibrance filter options
what: intensity −2…2 (boost or alter), per-channel balance rbal/gbal/bbal, luma coefficients, and `alternate` (with negative intensity: shift colours instead of greying)
how: `-vf vibrance=intensity=0.3` and `-vf vibrance=intensity=-0.5:alternate=0` (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Saturation and contrast interact
what: Resolve's colorist guide puts balance first, and the Frame.io guide orders luma → chroma balance → saturation. Set luma before judging saturation
how: order the ffmpeg chain levels/curves → balance → `eq=saturation`.

name: Generic lut/lutrgb expressions
what: lutrgb/lutyuv compute a table from expressions using val, clipval, maxval, minval, negval, clip(), gammaval()
how: `-vf "format=gbrp,lutrgb=r='pow(clip((val/maxval)*1.05,0,1),1.0)*maxval',format=yuv420p"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Selective colour by purity
what: selectivecolor adjusts CMYK per colour range (reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks). `correction_method=relative|absolute` (default absolute). It reads Photoshop .asv files
how: `-vf "selectivecolor=correction_method=relative:greens=.5 0 -.33 0:blues=0 .27"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hue-vs curves as ffmpeg moves
what: Resolve's Hue vs Hue changes one hue to another (e.g. a too-cyan sky to blue), Hue vs Sat and Hue vs Lum change saturation/lightness of a hue
how: nearest ffmpeg tool is `huesaturation=hue=-10:colors=c+b:strength=1:lightness=1` (lightness=1 keeps lightness) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep one colour, grey the rest
what: colorhold (RGB) and hsvhold (HSV) turn everything except a chosen colour range grey, with similarity and blend
how: `-vf colorhold=color=red:similarity=0.3:blend=0.1` and `-vf hsvhold=hue=0:sat=0.7:val=0.5:similarity=0.3:blend=0.1` (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 1D vs 3D LUT
what: a 1D LUT is three independent curves (no cross-channel effects). A 3D LUT is indexed by R, G and B together and can represent any colour transform
how: use `lut1d` for pure tone/gamma, `lut3d` for colour.

name: Apply a 1D .cube
what: lut1d reads cube and csp 1D files with nearest/linear/cosine/cubic/spline interpolation
how: write `LUT_1D_SIZE 1024` + 1024 lines of "v v v", then `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf lut1d=file=g.cube:interp=cubic -c:v libx264 out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: lut3d file formats
what: 3dl (After Effects), cube (Iridas), dat (DaVinci), m3d (Pandora), csp (cineSpace). Interpolation nearest, trilinear, tetrahedral (default), pyramid, prism
how: `ffmpeg -hide_banner -h filter=lut3d` shows the default (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: .cube layout
what: optional TITLE, `LUT_3D_SIZE N` or `LUT_1D_SIZE N`, optional DOMAIN_MIN/MAX, then N³ RGB lines with red changing fastest
how: an identity 33-cube written with red in the innermost loop gave 88 dB PSNR through lut3d on a PNG, while blue-fastest gave 3.7 dB (tested here 2026-10-24). One site claims blue fastest, and the test shows that is wrong for ffmpeg.

name: LUT sizes and file weight
what: 17³ = 4,913 lines (~120 KB), 33³ = 35,937 (~900 KB), 65³ = 274,625 (~7 MB). Creative looks are usually 25 or 33, while camera conversion tables are often 65 so log shadows don't band
how: export conversions at 65 and looks at 33.

name: Tetrahedral beats trilinear per grid point
what: SMPTE review (BT.2100 PQ): tetrahedral interpolation outperformed others for SDR and HDR, matching trilinear quality with a LUT 20–25% smaller. For 10-bit SDR, >41³ trilinear or >31³ tetrahedral avoids artefacts
how: keep lut3d's default tetrahedral.

name: Camera Look File LUT rules (Canon)
what: Canon Look Files must be 17 or 33 grid .cube, built for full-range in and out
how: export 33-point full-range cubes for on-camera use.

name: Test a LUT pipeline with an identity cube
what: an identity LUT must change nothing, which proves the order and range handling
how: Python writes a 33³ identity (`for b: for g: for r:`), then `ffmpeg -i frame.png -vf lut3d=file=id33.cube:interp=tetrahedral -frames:v 1 out.png` and `ffmpeg -i frame.png -i out.png -lavfi psnr -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24: 88 dB)

name: Hald CLUT geometry
what: a Hald of level N is an N³×N³ pixel image holding an (N²)³ cube, e.g. level 8 = 512×512 = 64³. Square-image rules mean 17/33/65 cubes can't be written as Hald
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i haldclutsrc=8 -frames:v 1 hald.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bake any ffmpeg global grade into a LUT
what: run the identity Hald through the colour filters, then apply it with haldclut. Only global colour operations survive (no sharpening, denoise or local effects)
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i haldclutsrc=8 -vf "curves=preset=increase_contrast,colortemperature=temperature=5500" -frames:v 1 hald.png` then `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -i hald.png -filter_complex "[0][1]haldclut" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Convert a Hald PNG to .cube
what: the identity Hald holds every cube entry once in known order, so its pixels read row by row are the cube entries
how: Python/PIL: read hald.png pixels in order, write `LUT_3D_SIZE 64` and each pixel/255 as a line, then `lut3d=file=hald64.cube` (tested here 2026-10-24: 43.6 dB PSNR vs the haldclut result)

name: Animated CLUTs
what: haldclut accepts a video stream as the CLUT (`clut=all` default, `repeatlast=1` keeps the last one), so a grade can change over time
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i haldclutsrc=8 -vf "hue=H=2*PI*t:s=sin(2*PI*t)+1, curves=cross_process" -t 2 -c:v ffv1 clut.nut` then `-filter_complex "[0][1]haldclut"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube SDR down-conversion hint LUT
what: YouTube's HDR metadata tool can pack a .cube (Rec.2020 PQ → Rec.709 gamma 2.4, plus your primaries/curves/keys) as a hint for its automatic SDR version. Windows, blur keys and per-shot changes don't work
how: make one global LUT for the whole HDR video and give it to the tool.

name: Primary vs secondary
what: Frame.io: a primary correction changes every pixel. Resolve: a secondary isolates part of the image with a key (white = change, black = leave), from a qualifier, a Power Window or an external matte
how: in ffmpeg the key is the third input of `maskedmerge`.

name: maskedmerge semantics
what: mask value 0 keeps the first input, maximum (255) takes the second, in-between mixes, per plane
how: put mask, original and corrected all in gbrp so every plane gets the same weight: see 975 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: HSL qualifier = a colour key
what: the HSL qualifier keys any hue/sat/luma range (not just green/blue) from eyedropper samples. It is fastest for irregular subjects with a distinct colour, and needs no tracking
how: ffmpeg `hsvkey` (hue, sat, val, similarity, blend) makes the alpha. Pull it with `alphaextract`.

name: Matte finesse moves
what: Clean Black fills holes in the background, Clean White fills holes in the foreground, and Blur Radius/In-Out Ratio soften and push the edge. Key denoise reduces chattering over time. Heavy cleanup can kill soft edges and big blur can halo
how: soften the ffmpeg matte with `gblur=sigma=3..6`, and calm chatter with `tmix=frames=3` on the mask (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Qualifier secondary in one ffmpeg graph
what: key a hue range, invert to the wanted part, soften, and merge a corrected copy through the mask
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]split[a][b];[b]format=yuva444p,hsvkey=hue=0:sat=0.7:val=0.6:similarity=0.25:blend=0.1,alphaextract,negate,gblur=sigma=3,format=gbrp[m];[a]format=gbrp,split[o][g];[g]huesaturation=saturation=0.4[gr];[o][gr][m]maskedmerge,format=yuv420p" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Luma qualifier for range-specific colour
what: the LUM qualifier mode targets ranges of lightness. Colourists use it to change colour temperature in highlights or shadows only
how: ffmpeg `lumakey=threshold=1:tolerance=0.3:softness=0.1` → alphaextract → negate → maskedmerge with a `colortemperature` copy (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Power window shapes
what: Resolve offers linear, circle, polygon, curve and gradient windows, each with softness, invert and subtract. Windows give clean, precise edges for faces, car fronts and skies
how: draw a soft ellipse mask with geq: `nullsrc=s=640x360:d=2,geq=lum='255*clip(1.5-hypot((X-W/2)/(W*0.25),(Y-H/2)/(H*0.35)),0,1)',format=gray,format=gbrp` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gradient window = graduated filter
what: the gradient window works like a graduated filter, e.g. for a sky
how: mask `geq=lum='255*clip(Y/(H*0.5),0,1)'` merging a darker copy over the top half (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Windows must follow motion
what: Power Windows have to be animated or tracked to follow the subject
how: without a tracker in ffmpeg, move the geq mask with T: `geq=lum='255*clip(1.5-hypot((X-(W*0.3+T*100))/(W*0.2),(Y-H/2)/(H*0.3)),0,1)'` (tested here 2026-10-24); a real track needs a tracker (Missing tools)

name: Fix the grade first, isolate skin after
what: Noam Kroll: balance and match shots with one or two technical nodes first, then isolate elements like skin. Don't build the whole grade around skin and neglect everything else
how: run primaries on the whole clip, then a qualifier pass (975) for skin.

name: Window plus qualifier for skin
what: when a skin key also grabs similar background colours, a circular window limits it to the person
how: multiply the hsvkey matte by an ellipse geq mask (`blend=all_mode=multiply`) before maskedmerge. The blend step is not tested here.

name: Check the matte, then the picture
what: alternate matte view and normal view, since a perfect black-and-white mask doesn't guarantee an invisible correction. Diagnose leaks, noise, geometry or track drift first
how: render the mask branch alone (`-map` the `[m]` output) for a few frames and look at it.

name: Pick a technically sound hero shot
what: Frame.io: the hero should represent the scene (often a wide) and must not be badly exposed or cast. Match the others to it in a comparison view, scene by scene
