what: besides time alignment and choosing one mic per line, Audio Tool Kit suggests a high-pass on the lav so boom and lav overlap less in the low mids
how: `highpass=f=150` on the lav before any blend (value is a starting point, by ear)

name: Mid/side to pull a centred voice out of stereo
what: `stereotools` `mode=lr>ms` converts L/R to mid/side; `slev` lowers the side signal (e.g. wide ambience) while the centred voice stays
how: `stereotools=mode=lr>ms` or `stereotools=slev=0.3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: dialoguenhance builds a speech centre channel
what: it takes stereo and outputs 3.0 with an enhanced dialogue centre (FC), leaving FL/FR as input; `enhance` 0-3, `voice` detection 2-32. Our FC output was 1679 samples (35 ms) late vs the input
how: `dialoguenhance=enhance=2,pan=mono|c0=FC` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Why a gate fails on mic bleed
what: a gate opens from its own track's level, but bleed can be as loud as word starts and ends, so it opens late, cuts consonants or chatters, and during overlap both mics stay open
how: for two-host clips, cut bleed by hand or use a gain-sharing automixer

name: Gain-sharing automixers compare all mics
what: a Dugan-style automixer looks at all mic tracks together: the active mic stays open, quieter mics attenuate, overlaps can keep several open; with no one talking, the gains are set uniformly
how: needs an automixer plug-in (missing); not the same as spectral de-bleed

name: Edit bleed out by removing regions
what: with two people on separate close mics, removing each mic's region while the other person talks makes the speaker clearer; listen before deleting because quiet reactions or words may be in there
how: get each mic's speech regions from `silencedetect=m=1`, mute the rest with `volume=0:enable=...`

name: Bleed also causes phase problems
what: each mic hears a quieter, delayed copy of the other speakers, and that delayed bleed combines with the direct signal on another track into thin, hollow voices; EQ/compression on one host also reacts to the bleed
how: prevent with close mics; in the edit, mute bleed regions

name: Reduce bleed while recording
what: use dynamic mics close to the mouth, point each mic away from the other speakers; placement cuts bleed before any plug-in
how: brief clients before multi-person shoots

name: How much sync error is acceptable (EBU R37)
what: at any output for emission, sound should be no more than 40 ms before and no more than 60 ms after the picture; each production stage should stay within 5 ms early to 15 ms late
how: keep every processing step's added delay inside 15 ms or trim it out (see the latency lines)

name: When viewers notice (ITU-R BT.1359)
what: subjective tests put detectability at about +45 ms (sound early) to -125 ms (sound late) and acceptability at about +90 ms to -185 ms; the limit for late sound is wider than for early sound
how: when unsure, err toward audio slightly late rather than early

name: Film sync within half a frame
what: BT.1359 notes that for 24 fps film, ±half a frame (about ±22 ms) is an acceptable variation
how: at 24/25/30 fps, a one-frame slip (42/40/33 ms) is already near the limit; fix it

name: Most viewers notice at 2-3 frames
what: TV Technology: most viewers don't detect lip-sync error until about two or three frames, professionals may see one frame, and once noticed viewers become more sensitive to it
how: check talking-head sync at full speed after every audio replacement

name: Make a blip-and-flash sync test
what: EBU R37 describes measuring sync with a "flash" (one full frame of peak white) and a "blip" (1 kHz tone for the same duration). Build one, run it through the pipeline, and compare `silencedetect` vs `blackdetect` times; after `adelay=120` the blip read 2.12 s vs the flash at 2.00 s
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=black:s=320x180:r=25:d=4" -f lavfi -i "aevalsrc=if(between(t\,2\,2.04)\,0.5*sin(2*PI*1000*t)\,0):s=48000:d=4" -vf "geq=lum='if(between(T,2,2.039),235,16)':cb=128:cr=128" -c:v libx264 -c:a pcm_s16le test.mov`, then `ffmpeg -i out.mov -af silencedetect=n=-40dB:d=0.5 -vf blackdetect=d=0.5:pix_th=0.5 -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Audio filters shift sync: measure each one
what: measured output delay at 48 kHz: afftdn 1200 samples (25 ms), dialoguenhance 1679 (35 ms), arnndn 480 (10 ms), firequalizer 480 (10 ms); afwtdn, agate, speechnorm, adynamicequalizer about 0. afftdn + dialoguenhance together would already pass EBU's 15 ms per-stage limit
how: cross-correlate input vs output (`scipy.signal.correlate`) and trim with `atrim=start_sample=N,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sync two recordings by cross-correlation
what: the same idea PluralEyes uses (comparing audio content): correlate camera scratch audio with the recorder file; our test found a built-in 120 ms offset exactly (5760 samples)
how: `lag = argmax(abs(correlate(b, a, mode='full', method='fft'))) - (len(a)-1)` on the first ~10 s, then `adelay` or `atrim` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Move audio earlier by trimming its head
what: `adelay` can only delay; to make audio earlier cut the start with `atrim` (`start` in seconds or `start_sample`) and reset timestamps with `asetpts`
how: `ffmpeg -i late.wav -af "atrim=start_sample=5760,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS" out.wav` brought our 120 ms late copy to 0 lag (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shift only the audio input with -ss
what: put `-ss` before the audio file's `-i` and map video from the other input to skip the audio's first part
how: `ffmpeg -i v.mp4 -ss 0.12 -i late.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac -shortest out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Clap sync: match the spike to the frame
what: the editor lines up the waveform spike of the slate clap (or a hand clap/finger snap) with the frame where the sticks meet
how: find the clap time with `astats`/`silencedetect`, the frame by stepping through `ffmpeg -ss T -frames:v 1` stills

name: Resolve Auto Sync: timecode, waveform, in/out or markers
what: Resolve syncs dual-system audio by matching timecode to Broadcast WAVs, by waveform (needs camera audio), or by In/Out points or Markers placed on a known sync point; "Use channel number" Auto/Mix/specific channel avoids noisy channels; organise by day/scene to speed waveform sync
how: needs DaVinci Resolve (missing)

name: Keep the camera audio when syncing
what: Resolve's "Retain embedded audio" adds the synced channels on an extra track instead of replacing the camera audio, so both can be edited
how: locally keep the camera track as a second audio stream: `-map 0:a -map 1:a`

name: Premiere: synchronize before merging
what: Premiere's Merge Clips aligns from clip start unless you first use Clip > Synchronize (by clip start/end, timecode, numbered marker or audio); its Merge Clips dialog can also sync by audio
how: needs Adobe Premiere (missing)

name: Why automatic waveform sync fails
what: PluralEyes needs about 5-10 s of good audio per clip (3 s or less is a problem), cannot sync silent video, ignores clappers and timecode, and fails on discontinuous clips with dropped sound - trim those so each clip is one continuous recording
how: give the sync tool clean, continuous, long-enough clips

name: Sync good in the middle, off at the ends = drift
what: that pattern means the recorder's speed was not exact; PluralEyes detects it and writes drift-corrected new audio files
how: measure the offset at the start and the end; if they differ, correct the speed (next line)

name: Fix linear drift with rubberband or a re-stamped rate, not atempo
what: to slow a file by 0.1% we measured the lag at 3, 8 and 14 s: `rubberband=tempo=0.999` and `asetrate=47952,aresample=48000` both grew by about 1.0 ms per second as they should (3.7 -> 14.9 ms and 3.9 -> 15.1 ms), but `atempo=0.999` grew only about 0.57 ms per second and came out shorter (18.337 s). rubberband keeps pitch; the asetrate route changes pitch by the same 0.1%
how: tempo factor = current length / wanted length (below 1 makes it longer), then `ffmpeg -i rec.wav -af "rubberband=tempo=0.999" out.wav`; re-measure the end offset (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 0.1% pull-up/pull-down sample rates
what: 48.048 kHz is 0.1% above 48 kHz, the same 0.1% as 24 vs 23.98 fps; 48 kHz sound pulled down plays as 47.952 kHz to stay in sync with slowed video. Re-stamping the rate gives the 0.1% speed change: `asetrate=48048,aresample=48000` turned 18.34 s into 18.32 s
how: `ffmpeg -i in.wav -af "asetrate=48048,aresample=48000" out.wav` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: "F" stamped rates on Sound Devices recorders
what: if told to shoot 48.048 or 47.952 kHz, select the 'fake' stamped rates 48.048F or 47.952F unless pre-production says otherwise; some editors want 48.048 files stamped as 48 kHz
how: ask the post team which stamp they expect before a shoot

name: Drift causes and prevention
what: mixing 44.1 kHz with 48 kHz, variable frame rate footage and devices with independent clocks cause drift; set everything to 48 kHz and constant frame rate, and use timecode generators on multi-device shoots
how: check `ffprobe -show_entries stream=sample_rate,r_frame_rate,avg_frame_rate` on every source

name: Resample to timestamps with aresample async
what: `aresample=async=1000` stretches/squeezes samples (up to 1000 samples per second) to match the timestamps
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -af "aresample=async=1000" -c:v copy out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Jam-sync timecode
what: Tentacle devices can sync almost any camera or recorder with either a dedicated timecode input or at least one audio channel; Deity's TC-SL1 drifts less than 1 frame per 48 hours
how: on client shoots ask whether timecode was jammed; if so, sync by timecode, not waveform

name: Word anchors for drifting long recordings
what: WhisperSync transcribes both tracks with per-word timestamps and matches word anchors along the whole recording to follow clock drift that start-locked waveform matching misses
how: needs WhisperSync (missing); locally compare Whisper word times of both tracks at start and end to measure drift

name: Wild lines: re-record on set, camera off
what: actors repeat lines with the same mics and positions right after the take, without camera; editors line them up later; also used for off-screen voices
how: when a line is ruined on a client shoot, ask for a wild line before the setup is struck

name: Same mics as production, both boom and lav
what: use the exact make and model used on set (ask the location recordist) and record lav and boom simultaneously to choose later
how: note the production mics on every job

name: ADR mic placement
what: Thunderbird Sound: boom about 12-18 inches above the talent angled to the mouth (too far off in a poor room brings out resonances); lav on the shirt about 8 inches below the chin; the lav is often the better match to production
how: for owner VO pickups, copy the original mic distance

name: Record ADR at a higher rate if it will be stretched
what: heavy time-stretching makes 48 kHz audio grainy; record higher, process, then convert to the 48 kHz/24-bit delivery spec
how: `aresample=48000` after stretching; deliver `-c:a pcm_s24le -ar 48000`

name: Fit ADR length with rubberband
what: `rubberband` changes tempo and pitch independently, with `formant=preserved` and `pitchq=quality` options
how: `ffmpeg -i adr.wav -af "rubberband=tempo=1.08:formant=preserved:pitchq=quality" out.wav` (18.34 -> 16.98 s) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Match the performance level to the scene
what: a softly spoken ADR line in a noisy city scene never sounds convincing, however good the sync; deliver at the level the person would really use there
how: play the scene's background to the speaker before the take

name: Record every take, warm-ups included
what: natural performances often happen when the actor feels no pressure; keep recording past the "last" take
how: for owner VO sessions keep one continuous recording and cut later

name: Remove noisy clothes and jewellery before ADR
what: rustling fabrics, open zips and rattling jewellery ruin takes; a jewellery bowl on arrival helps
how: check before recording owner VO

name: Set ADR levels at both ends of the range
what: performances go from whisper to shout; check level at the top and bottom, e.g. by making the talent laugh to find the peak
how: leave headroom for the loudest cue

name: Sync ADR by matching waveforms
what: line the ADR waveform up with the production waveform, slide words or syllables that don't fall in sync, then listen and watch for lip sync
how: cut ADR into words with `atrim` at the peaks that match production

name: Use only the ADR you need
what: if noise covered only a syllable and a half, use just that frame or so of ADR instead of replacing the whole line, which can stick out
how: patch the syllable with a 5-20 ms crossfade

name: Place ADR in the room with an impulse-response reverb, in mono
what: Thunderbird Sound uses realistic IR-style reverbs (Altiverb, Revibe), in mono to match a mono boom; ffmpeg's `afir` convolves with any IR file (the docs' example applies reverb from a mono IR)
how: `ffmpeg -i adr.wav -i room_ir.wav -filter_complex "[0]asplit[d][w];[w][1]afir[wet];[d][wet]amix=inputs=2:weights='1 0.25':normalize=0" out.wav` (ran here with a synthetic IR) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Capture location impulse responses on the shoot
what: sound editors suggest recording IRs of locations during filming for ADR matching later, and recording exterior ADR outdoors rather than faking an exterior inside
how: a clap or balloon pop recorded at the shooting spot can serve as a rough IR for `afir`

name: Dirty up ADR that is too clean
what: Thunderbird Sound sometimes adds a little distortion or compression so studio ADR matches a gritty or over-compressed production lav
how: `acompressor` or `asoftclip` very lightly, A/B against production

name: Room tone under ADR
what: lay the production room tone under ADR so the background never breaks; find it at the head/tail of the take or an alternate take, Ambience Match as a fallback
how: `amix=inputs=2:normalize=0` with the scene's fill

name: Prep production around ADR so it can be undone
what: Semenoff prepares the surrounding production dialogue so the air doesn't drop out when the ADR line comes in, but in a way that the ADR fill can be muted if the mix goes back to production
how: keep ADR fill on its own file/track

name: Keep the untouched ADR copy
what: Semenoff sometimes changes pitch or EQ of ADR but always keeps the original for the mixer and adds reverb only temporarily to test a line
how: save `adr_raw.wav` next to any processed version

name: ADR usually needs more EQ than production
what: a film mixer notes ADR often carries more EQ than production dialogue because scenes may be dubbed in one go; a benefit is that ADR can be panned since no noise moves with it
how: budget EQ time for ADR lines

name: Match acoustics and perspective, not just words
what: the classic ADR mistake is dropping clean studio lines in without matching perspective (reverb, EQ), level and breaths, so they sound detached
how: EQ, IR reverb, level and room tone, then check in context

name: ADR cueing tools
what: cues should be prepared in a spotting session before ADR; EdiCue/EdiPrompt (Sounds in Sync) and 3Cue handle cue sheets, streamers and countdown beeps; Semenoff uses ADR Toolbox for cue databases
how: for small jobs, a cue list with timecode in/out and line text is enough

name: ADR is the answer when it must be truly clean
what: Larry Jordan: if you need an absolutely clean background, re-record in a studio with ADR; most of the time some background is wanted because it feels like the location
how: offer a re-record when the owner wants studio-clean speech from a noisy clip

name: Checkerboard dialogue by character
what: split the production clips line by line and move each character's lines to that character's own track, so each has its own volume, EQ and dynamics; add a production-effects (PFX) track for non-dialogue sounds the mics picked up
how: locally, one WAV per character (and one PFX WAV) built with `atrim`/`adelay`/`amix`

name: A/B tracks per mic and character
what: a track build checkerboards Jane's boom across two tracks (A/B), the Radio Voice boom across two more, and keeps each radio mic on its own track
how: alternate consecutive clips of the same mic between two tracks so fades and fills can overlap
refs: ebrary, "The dialogue editing track build", https://ebrary.net/294464/education/dialogue_editing_track_build, checked 2026-10-24

name: A live-action dialogue track template
what: Semenoff's standard: 10-12 PD (production dialogue), 4-6 PFX, 4-6 X tracks (production replaced by ADR), 2-6 Futz (speakers, radios), ADR tracks as needed, 16 loop-group tracks, kept in multiples of 8 for console fader banks
how: scale down for small jobs but keep the categories

name: Work tracks and junk tracks
what: Semenoff keeps 4-8 empty WORK tracks for temporary edits and inactive "Crap" tracks for clips he doesn't want to lose but that shouldn't feed the mix
how: in the scratchpad keep `work/` and `unused/` folders per job

name: Expand the editor's cut to all mics first
what: the dialogue assembly takes the AAF or audio EDL and expands the used takes to all microphones recorded, because picture usually cuts with the on-set mix track
how: ask clients for the original multi-channel recorder files, not just the camera mix

name: Watch everything before cutting
what: first watch the whole film/episode for pacing, scenes that need more work, and breaths/efforts to borrow
how: one full listen of the client's clip before any processing

name: Keep a muted unprocessed copy next to every NR clip
what: Semenoff's motto is "do no harm to the dialogue": if dialogue quality drops, the noise reduction went too far; he keeps the unprocessed version nearby, since the mixer can add more NR but going back is harder
how: always write `*_raw.wav` beside `*_nr.wav`

name: Background music on set is the hardest fix
what: Semenoff has no good fix for music playing on set when it is close in level to the dialogue; repo tests found the same: a song with a singer as background stays in any vocal stem
how: warn the owner early; try `clean_voice.py`, which removes only instrumental sound
refs: repo: CLAUDE.md "Voice and songs with words"

name: Classify noise first: steady or sudden
what: decide whether a noise is consistent (AC, fridge, crickets: whole-file tools like Dialogue Isolate) or intermittent (creaks, bumps: select and repair only those spots)
how: steady -> `afftdn`/`arnndn` on the clip; sudden -> patch the spot with room tone

name: What a dialogue editor does (and leaves to the mixer)
what: April Tucker's list: keep only usable/best mics, fades, crossfades and fills, remove pops, clicks, hums and thumps, repair dropouts, edit ADR and narration; broadband noise is addressed in mixing; volume automation is the mixer's job
how: in a client edit, do the cleanup pass before any loudness work

name: Ask before deleting volume automation
what: some re-recording mixers want the picture editor's volume automation kept in the AAF, so check with the mixer before stripping it
how: keep the editor's gain notes when re-cutting a client's timeline

name: Long fades let ambience come in naturally
what: Tucker's basic dialog edit uses long fade-ins and fade-outs so the ambience enters and leaves naturally where it is audible, fills holes with crossfades, and moves a bad mid-word edit
how: `afade=t=in:d=0.5` / `afade=t=out` on clip heads and tails with audible ambience

name: What Premiere's default AAF gives audio post
what: without adjusting settings Premiere often exports stereo as split mono pairs and gives no or too-short handles; on Windows, embedded AAFs over 2 GB fail, so use separate audio
how: when sending to an audio editor, set handles and separate audio

name: M&E needs split production effects
what: after the final mix the dialogue editor cuts all lines out for the M&E (music and effects) mix; production movement and PFX are lost unless they were split and filled during dialogue editing
how: keep PFX on its own file from the start

name: Cleanup first, enhancement second
what: Krotos frames dialogue editing as two phases: phase 1 cleanup (sync production audio, label and organise takes, rough comp of best performances), then enhancement; dialogue editing is distinct from mixing
how: don't EQ or level before the cleanup pass is done

name: Noise is "reduced", not "removed"
what: Larry Jordan: background noise and speech share frequencies, so removing too much damages the voice; aim to hear the speaker clearly while keeping the feeling of the location
how: stop de-noising when the voice starts to change

name: Resolve Voice Isolation amount
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: Larry Jordan finds the default 100 excessive, 70-80 natural for strong isolation, and used 25 on a noisy trade-show clip; use Voice Isolation or Dialogue Leveler's Background Reduction, not both, on one clip
how: needs DaVinci Resolve (missing; Voice Isolation is Studio only)

name: Resolve Dialogue Leveler (free and Studio)
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: it detects dialogue, rides down loud parts, lifts soft parts and lowers non-dialogue background; Larry Jordan prefers "Allow wider dynamics" and warns against settings that remove the noise completely so it pops in and out
how: needs DaVinci Resolve (missing)

name: Premiere Enhance Speech with Mix Amount
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: Essential Sound > Dialogue > Enhance runs the AI cleanup; the Mix Amount slider blends raw and enhanced audio so some natural background can return
how: needs Adobe Premiere (missing)

name: Audition Noise Reduction expectations
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: Audition's (Waveform Editor) Noise Reduction can typically raise signal-to-noise by 5-20 dB while keeping high quality; capture a noise print from a noise-only selection (Shift+P) first
how: needs Adobe Audition (missing)

name: Audition Adaptive Noise Reduction for changing noise
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: it removes variable broadband noise (background sounds, rumble, wind) and runs in real time, so it works in the Multitrack Effects Rack, unlike Noise Reduction
how: needs Adobe Audition (missing)

name: Audacity Noise Reduction controls
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: Noise Reduction (dB, default 6: use the lowest that works), Sensitivity (0-24, default 6), Frequency smoothing (bands, default 6; lower favours music, higher spoken word); time smoothing is fixed at 20 ms attack / 100 ms release
how: needs Audacity (missing, GPL)

name: Audacity "Residue" to hear the damage
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: Residue plays what would be removed; recognisable bits of speech in it mean Noise Reduction or Sensitivity is too high; artifacts like "tinkly bells" mean Sensitivity is too low or the profile isn't representative
how: the ffmpeg equivalent is `afftdn=om=n` or `arnndn=mix=-1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One noise type at a time
section: NLE and editor tools (when the owner has them)
what: if different noises sit in different places, Audacity advises profiling and reducing the first, then profiling the next; profiles must match the track's sample rate
how: in ffmpeg, process each section with its own `afftdn` profile via `asendcmd` sn start/stop

name: Learn the longest pure-noise stretch
what: RX Spectral De-noise works best with a profile from the longest noise-only selection (ideally a few seconds), often at the start/end or between words; a learned profile stays fixed, so Adaptive mode suits changing noise (traffic, waves)
how: same rule for `afftdn` sample-noise

name: Separate tonal and broadband reduction
what: RX Spectral De-noise splits noise into tonal (hum, buzz) and random (hiss) parts with separate Threshold/Reduction, e.g. remove an unpleasant buzz but leave harmless constant hiss
how: needs iZotope RX (missing); in ffmpeg combine `bandreject` for tones with light `afftdn`

name: Artifact Control: spectral subtraction vs gating
what: low values rely on spectral subtraction (more accurate, can sound chirpy/watery), high values on wide-band gating (fewer musical artifacts, but noise bursts after the signal drops)
how: needs iZotope RX (missing)

name: Voice De-noise: zero-latency adaptive gate
what: RX Voice De-noise is a 64-band psychoacoustic multiband gate; Adaptive mode follows a changing floor (set lower to avoid artifacts), Learn needs at least one second of pure noise, Dialogue mode reacts faster than Music, Surgical removes more than Gentle but can add musical noise
how: needs iZotope RX (missing)

name: clean_voice.py --fast only speeds up the voice stage
what: on an 18 s clip (speech + piano + noise) the MDX-Net Voc FT voice stage took 65 s, but the Mel-RoFormer denoise stage still took 248 s (5 min 26 s total); add `--no-denoise` for a quick preview
how: `/home/user/tools/venv/bin/python library/tools/clean_voice.py in.mp4 --out OUT --fast --no-denoise` for a preview, full run for delivery (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: clean_voice.py on a speech + piano + noise mix
what: the gap between speech and pause level went from 11 dB (input) to 46 dB after the voice stage and 48 dB in the final voice.wav, and the Whisper check in report.json kept every word
how: `clean_voice.py mix.wav --out OUT --fast --lang en`, then read `OUT/report.json` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: clean_voice.py writes a steady -16 LUFS voice
what: its final step is a 70 Hz high-pass and two-pass loudnorm in linear mode, because one-pass dynamic loudnorm made the cleaned voice pump inside sentences
how: read the comment above the loudnorm call in the script before changing its last stage

name: Separation models already on disk
what: /home/user/tools/sep-models holds BS-RoFormer (vocals), UVR-MDX-NET Voc FT (fast vocals), Mel-RoFormer denoise (aufr33) and UVR DeEcho-DeReverb; any of them can be run directly with `audio-separator -m FILE --model_file_dir /home/user/tools/sep-models`
how: `ls /home/user/tools/sep-models`, then `--single_stem Vocals` or `Instrumental` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Read -18 LUFS from the -18 dBFS alignment tone
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: EBU Tech 3341 says a 1 kHz stereo sine, in phase, peaking at -18 dBFS must read -18.0 LUFS; use it to check any meter chain
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "aevalsrc=exprs=0.125893*sin(2*PI*1000*t)|0.125893*sin(2*PI*1000*t):s=48000:d=20" -af ebur128=peak=true+sample:framelog=quiet -f null -` read I -18.0 LUFS, peak -18.0 dBFS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: EBU Mode test case 1 (-23 dBFS tone)
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Tech 3341 Table 1 case 1: 20 s stereo 1 kHz at -23 dBFS per channel must read M, S, I = -23.0 ±0.1 LUFS
how: same command with amplitude `0.070795` read I -23.0 LUFS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: EBU Mode gating test (case 5)
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Tech 3341 case 5: 20 s at -26 dBFS, 20.1 s at -20 dBFS, 20 s at -26 dBFS must integrate to -23.0 ±0.1 LUFS; it checks the relative gate
how: `aevalsrc=exprs=if(between(t\,20\,40.1)\,0.1\,0.050119)*sin(2*PI*1000*t)|...:d=60.1` into `ebur128` read I -23.0 LUFS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LRA test signals (Tech 3342)
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Tech 3342 cases: 20 s at -20 dBFS then 20 s at -30 dBFS must give LRA 10 ±1 LU; -40/-20 must give 20 ±1 LU
how: two-step `aevalsrc` tones (`if(lt(t\,20)\,0.1\,0.031623)` etc.) into `ebur128` read LRA 10.0 LU and 20.0 LU (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mono files read 3 dB low unless dual-mono
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: ebur128 and loudnorm have a dualmono option because a mono file meant for stereo playback measures perceptually wrong; ebur128's panlaw defaults to -3.01 dB
how: a mono 1 kHz tone at -18 dBFS read I -21.0 LUFS plain and -18.0 LUFS with `ebur128=framelog=quiet:dualmono=true` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ffmpeg's sine source is -18 dBFS by default
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Know your generator level before using it for alignment
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=f=1000:d=2 -af astats=measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=Peak_level -f null -` read peak -18.06 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LFE is left out of loudness
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: BS.1770 excludes the LFE channel of 5.1 from the loudness measurement (Tech 3343 §4.2); A/85 short-form measurement also excludes LFE
how: a 5.1 file with signal only in LFE read I -70.0 LUFS (nothing counted) in `ebur128` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Surround channels weigh +1.5 dB
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: BS.1770 weights the surround pair +1.5 dB, while the default downmix coefficient for them is -3 dB, a 4.5 dB loudness difference (Tech 3343 §7.1)
how: the same -20 dBFS tone read -23.0 LUFS in FL and -21.5 LUFS in a surround channel of a 5.1 file (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Silence barely moves Integrated, but LRA jumps
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Integrated loudness gates at -70 LUFS absolute and -10 LU relative; Tech 3342 warns that leading/trailing silence in short items can give misleadingly high LRA
how: adding 10 s of silence with `apad=pad_dur=10` moved I only -15.4 to -15.5 LUFS but LRA went 0.0 to 7.0 LU (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Relative gate is -10 LU, older meters used -8
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: R 128 revision August 2011 changed the relative gate from -8 to -10 LU; a meter on the old gate reads differently
how: check the meter's version before comparing numbers; ffmpeg `ebur128` prints its two thresholds (I threshold = I - 10 LU)

name: EBU +9 and +18 scales
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: EBU Mode meters offer +9 (-18 to +9 LU) by default and +18 (-36 to +18 LU) for wide-range programmes; 0 LU = -23 LUFS
how: `ebur128=video=1:meter=18` draws the +18 scale (rendered here to a 640x480 graph video) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Set the graph target for online work
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: ebur128's target option sets the 0 LU point of the visual meter; the docs note online material may prefer -16 LUFS
how: `-filter_complex "ebur128=video=1:meter=18:target=-16[v][a]" -map [v] -map [a]` made a graph video (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LRA needs about a minute
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: R 128 does not recommend LRA for programmes shorter than 1 minute; Tech 3341 says the first 60 s of LRA must be flagged as not yet stable
how: for a reel, judge Integrated, max short-term and true peak; ignore LRA

name: LRA = 10th to 95th percentile
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: LRA uses 3 s short-term values, gated at -70 LUFS and -20 LU relative, and takes the spread from the 10th to the 95th percentile, so one gunshot or a fade-out cannot set it
how: read `LRA low` and `LRA high` in the `ebur128` summary to see the two percentiles (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dump short-term loudness per 100 ms
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: ebur128 metadata=1 cuts audio into 100 ms frames carrying lavfi.r128.* keys; print them to find the loudest 3 s
how: `ebur128=metadata=1,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.r128.S:file=st.txt` wrote 60 values for 6 s; max S was -15.349 LUFS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Peak-to-Loudness Ratio
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: PLR = maximum true peak minus programme loudness, a measure of micro-dynamics (R 128 s2 glossary)
how: `ebur128=peak=true` on the test bed: TP -9.4 dBTP, I -15.4 LUFS, PLR 6.0 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: True peak needs an oversampling meter
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Tech 3343: a sample-peak meter cannot predict overs from sample-rate conversion or codecs; a 4x true-peak meter can under-read ~0.5 dB at 48 kHz, so leave 1 dB
how: always add `peak=true` to `ebur128` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Make an inter-sample-peak test file
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: A full-scale 12 kHz sine at 45 deg phase has samples at -3 dBFS but a reconstructed peak above 0 dBFS
how: `aevalsrc=exprs=sin(2*PI*12000*t+PI/4)|...:s=48000` saved as float WAV read sample peak -3.0 dBFS, true peak +0.6 dBTP (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Use a peak meter for alignment, not a loudness meter
section: Meter checks: prove the meter before trusting it
what: Tech 3343 §8.1: K-weighting makes loudness meters error-prone for alignment; EBU recommends a peak meter and 1 kHz at -18 dBFS
how: check the tone with `astats=measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=Peak_level` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: astats overall only
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: measure_perchannel=none plus a short measure_overall list keeps astats output to the numbers you need
how: `astats=measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=Peak_level+RMS_level+Crest_factor` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spot clipping with Flat_factor and Peak_count
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: Flat_factor is the run of identical samples at the peak; Peak_count counts times the signal hit min/max
how: the clean bed: Flat factor 0, Peak count 2; the same bed pushed +15 dB into s16 WAV: Flat factor 34.3, Peak count 69190 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Find DC offset
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: astats DC_offset shows mean displacement; dcshift docs say DC offset reduces headroom
how: `dcshift=shift=0.05` gave DC offset 0.0499; adding `highpass=f=10` brought it to -0.00004 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Per-half-second RMS log
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: astats metadata=1 with reset=1 writes lavfi.astats.* keys per frame; set frame size with asetnsamples
how: `asetnsamples=24000,astats=metadata=1:reset=1:measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=RMS_level,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level:file=rms.txt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: RMS peak and trough window
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: astats length sets the short window (default 50 ms) used for RMS_peak/RMS_trough
how: `astats=length=0.4:measure_overall=none:measure_perchannel=RMS_peak+RMS_trough` gave -17.07 / -19.11 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Crest factor per channel
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: Crest_factor is peak/RMS (not in dB) - low numbers mean squashed audio
how: `astats=measure_overall=none:measure_perchannel=Crest_factor+Dynamic_range+Noise_floor` gave 1.92 and 2.41 on the two channels (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: volumedetect histogram = safe boost
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: volumedetect reports mean/max and a histogram; per the docs, if max is -4 dB you can raise +4 dB without clipping
how: `-af volumedetect`: mean -17.1 dB, max -9.5 dB, so +9 dB is the sample-peak limit (true peak still to check) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ReplayGain scan
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: replaygain prints track_gain and track_peak at the end and passes audio unchanged
how: `-af replaygain` printed track_gain +1.92 dB, track_peak 0.336 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Phase value per frame
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: aphasemeter exports lavfi.aphasemeter.phase in [-1, 1]: -1 out of phase, 1 in phase
how: `aphasemeter=video=0,ametadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.aphasemeter.phase:file=ph.txt` (bed read 0.48) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Auto-detect mono stretches
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: aphasemeter phasing=1 logs mono and out-of-phase sequences longer than duration
how: `aphasemeter=video=0:phasing=1:duration=1:tolerance=0.001` on a dual-mono file logged mono_start 0 / mono_end 6 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Auto-detect out-of-phase stretches
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: angle (default 170 deg) sets the out-of-phase threshold
how: L = sine, R = -sine into `aphasemeter=video=0:phasing=1:duration=1:angle=170` logged out_phase_start 0 / end 5 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Read a correlation meter
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: +1 = dual mono, 0 = fully decorrelated/wide, steady readings below 0 = reduced mono compatibility; meters integrate ~600 ms
how: use the aphasemeter phase value as the correlation reading

name: Vectorscope video
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: avectorscope draws L/R as a Lissajous figure: vertical line = mono, horizontal = out of phase
how: `avectorscope=s=360x360:draw=line:scale=sqrt:zoom=1.5` rendered to MP4 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Burn a level meter onto a QA copy
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: showvolume turns levels into video; m=r for RMS, dm shows a max line
how: `[0:a]showvolume=r=30:w=320:h=12:m=r:dm=1[vol];[0:v][vol]overlay=0:H-h` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Windowed L/R correlation as audio
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: axcorrelate outputs a -1..1 signal per window; the docs example splits a stereo file first
how: `channelsplit,axcorrelate=size=1024:algo=fast` then astats (min -0.80 on the bed) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spectrum picture of the mix
section: astats, volumedetect and other level meters
what: showspectrumpic renders one image of the whole spectrum; mode=separate shows channels apart
how: `-lavfi showspectrumpic=s=800x400:mode=separate:color=intensity -frames:v 1 spec.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Alignment level stays -18 dBFS
what: Tech 3343 §8.1: the 1 kHz alignment tone for programme exchange stays at -18 dBFS; it reads -18 LUFS on a loudness meter if in both channels
how: make it with `aevalsrc=exprs=0.125893*sin(2*PI*1000*t)|0.125893*sin(2*PI*1000*t)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: A/85 -20 dBFS test tones
what: A/85 annex test signals: 1 kHz sine at -20 dBFS and 500 Hz-2 kHz band-limited pink noise at -20 dBFS for monitor setup
how: `aevalsrc=exprs=0.1*sin(2*PI*1000*t)` peak read -20 dBFS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gain staging targets
what: Sauce Mastering: mix peaks around -6 dBFS (-6 to -3) with nothing clipping; The Audio Owl: many set levels between -12 and -20 dBFS
how: trim each stem with `volume=-6dB` etc. and check `astats` Peak_level (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Write gains in dB
what: volume accepts dB: -6.0206dB halves the level (docs example)
how: `volume=-6.0206dB` took the bed peak from -9.5 to -15.5 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: dB to HyperFrames data-volume
what: data-volume and filter gains are linear; 10^(dB/20)

name: amix divides by the number of inputs
what: amix 'normalize' (default on) scales inputs instead of only summing; turn it off when you set levels yourself
how: voice+music: default amix RMS -20.9 dB, `amix=normalize=0` -14.9 dB (6 dB apart with 2 inputs) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: amix weights as faders
what: weights sets each input's gain (docs example: vocal 1, music 0.25, normalize=0)
how: `amix=inputs=2:weights='1 0.25':normalize=0:duration=first:dropout_transition=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stop the level jump when a stem ends
what: When an input ends, amix renormalizes over dropout_transition (default 2 s); with normalize=0 and dropout_transition=0 nothing rescales
how: `[v][1]amix=dropout_transition=0:normalize=0` with a voice that ends at 3 s (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: End the mix with the picture/voice
what: amix duration=first stops at the first input's length (longest is default)
how: put the voice or a picture-length bed first and use `duration=first` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bus graph with stem outputs
what: iZotope's video mix layout: group dialogue, B-roll, ambience, SFX, music into submasters so each gets bus processing
how: tested command (one graph, four outputs): `[D1][M1][E1]amix=inputs=3:normalize=0[mix]` with `asplit` copies mapped to dial.wav, mus.wav, fx.wav (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Deliver stems and M&E
what: Producers may ask for an M&E (everything but dialogue) and separate D/M/E stems; iZotope keeps a template with print tracks for all of them
how: print `[M][E]amix=normalize=0` as the M&E plus each stem from the same graph

name: Pan '<' renormalises
what: In pan, replacing '=' with '<' renormalises gains to a total of 1, avoiding clipping
how: stereo to mono: `pan=mono|c0=c0+c1` peak -5.6 dB, `pan=mono|c0<c0+c1` peak -11.6 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Null test two renders
what: Invert one copy (aeval -val) and sum with amix normalize=0: identical files cancel
how: `[1]aeval=-val(ch):c=same[i];[0][i]amix=normalize=0,astats=...Peak_level` read -inf for identical files, -16.2 dB RMS for a different one (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Float the whole graph
what: amix only works in float and auto-inserts aresample for integer inputs; aformat can set the format explicitly
how: `[0]aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:sample_rates=48000:channel_layouts=stereo[a];[a][1]amix=normalize=0` then `-c:a pcm_f32le` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Set foreground levels a little low
what: Tech 3343 §3.2: background sounds add to programme loudness, so set foreground (narrator) slightly below target and rise later if needed
how: set the voice bus, then check `ebur128` I before adding beds

name: Set the voice with the short-term meter
what: Tech 3343: the 3 s short-term window bridges word gaps and gives a stable voice reading
how: watch S in `ebur128` (or `gauge=shortterm` video) while trimming the voice (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fixed monitor gain, then mix by ear
what: Tech 3343: set anchor levels, fix the monitor gain and mix by ear; if you used to mix near -20 LUFS, raise the monitor 3 dB to land at -23
how: keep one playback volume for every session

name: Dialogue pass first
what: Production Expert: mix dialogue first close to target, then add music and effects around it
how: voice bus first, then beds; check with `ebur128`

name: Dub levels between lines
what: Netflix dubbing guide: keep lines and characters level, e.g. -14 dB regular dialogue, -6 dB for screams
how: check line peaks with `astats` Peak_level

name: Walla 10 dB under
what: Netflix dubbing premix: attenuate group walla by -10 dB so principal dialogue plays on top
how: `volume=-10dB` on the walla stem (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Calibrate the room with EBU pink noise
what: Tech 3343 §8.2: each speaker to 73 dBC SPL with 500-2000 Hz pink noise at -23 LUFS (mono), front pair within 0.5 dB
how: made the test noise: `anoisesrc=c=pink` + two 500 Hz highpass + two 2 kHz lowpass + `loudnorm=I=-23:TP=-9:LRA=1 -ar 48000` read I -23.0 LUFS (the EBU also hosts the file at tech.ebu.ch/loudness) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LFE +10 dB in-band
what: Tech 3343: LFE content plays back +10 dB relative to the same band in a main channel
how: remember this when judging an LFE send level

name: Compressor math
what: Docs: threshold -12 dB, signal -6 dB, ratio 2:1 -> -9 dB
how: a -6 dBFS steady sine through `acompressor=threshold=-12dB:ratio=2:knee=1:attack=1:release=50:detection=peak` measured -8.8 dB (knee/detector make it inexact) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Thresholds take dB
what: acompressor threshold is linear (default 0.125 = -18 dB) but ffmpeg accepts a dB suffix
how: `acompressor=threshold=-20dB:ratio=3:makeup=2dB` ran (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Attack lets short peaks through
what: Signals shorter than the attack time are left untouched
how: raise `attack` (default 20 ms) to keep transients (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Link stereo to the louder side
what: link=maximum makes the louder channel drive gain reduction (default average)
how: `acompressor=threshold=0.1:ratio=4:attack=10:release=200:link=maximum:detection=peak` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Soft knee
what: knee (1-8, default 2.83) rounds entry into compression
how: `acompressor=threshold=-18dB:ratio=3:knee=8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Parallel compression with mix
what: Parallel (New York) compression blends dry with a heavily compressed copy, raising soft parts and keeping transients (Wikipedia); acompressor's mix option blends inside the filter
how: `acompressor=threshold=-30dB:ratio=10:attack=5:release=100:makeup=6:mix=0.4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Parallel compression on an aux
what: Yamaha: put the compressor on an auxiliary return like a reverb and blend it with the dry track
how: tested command: `asplit[dry][wet];[wet]acompressor=threshold=-35dB:ratio=20:attack=1:release=60:makeup=10[c];[dry][c]amix=weights='1 0.35':normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Upward mode
what: mode=upward switches acompressor/agate direction (docs list upward/downward)
how: `acompressor=mode=upward:threshold=-30dB:ratio=2` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Don't crush for video
what: iZotope: for video mixes set compressors for no more than about -6 dB of compression; heavy compression raises the noise floor
how: compare `astats` RMS before/after to estimate reduction

name: Bus limiter gently
what: iZotope: on dialogue/music buses, no more than about -2 dB gain reduction from a maximizer-type limiter
how: `alimiter` on the bus, check Peak_level change

name: Change compressor settings mid-file
what: acompressor supports all options as commands; asendcmd sends them at set times
how: `asendcmd=c='3.0 acompressor threshold 0.05',acompressor=threshold=0.5:ratio=4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: compand 2:1 from -18 dB
what: Docs point lists for fixed ratios, e.g. 2:1 starting at -18 dB

name: compand soft limiter
what: Docs soft limiter curve

name: compand for noisy rooms
what: Docs example to make music with quiet and loud passages suit a noisy environment

name: compand predictive delay
what: delay about equal to attack/decay makes compand act predictively; volume=-90 avoids huge gain at the start for quiet audio
how: `compand=attacks=0.3:decays=0.8:points=-80/-80|-20/-20|0/-10:delay=0.3:volume=-90` (output kept the 6.000 s length) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spectral compressor
what: adrc applies a transfer expression per frequency power; docs example: -50 dB threshold, 1:6
how: `adrc=transfer='if(gt(p,-50),-50+(p-(-50))/6,p)':attack=50:release=100` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spectral limiter
what: adrc docs example: limit every frequency to -60 dB
how: `adrc=transfer='min(p,-60)':attack=2:release=10` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: dynaudnorm frame and window
what: dynaudnorm evens out quiet and loud sections without compressing inside each section; framelen (500 ms) and gausssize (31 frames) set how fast it adapts
how: `dynaudnorm=f=500:g=31:p=0.9:m=10` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: dynaudnorm small window acts like a compressor
what: Smaller gausssize = faster gain changes, more like a compressor; larger = more like plain normalization
how: `dynaudnorm=f=250:g=15:r=0.2:p=0.95` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: dynaudnorm: don't lift noise
what: maxgain (default 10) bounds gain in near-silent frames; threshold skips frames below a level so noise isn't amplified
how: `dynaudnorm=t=0.01:m=5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: dynaudnorm uneven channels
what: coupling=0 gains each channel independently; correctdc removes DC bias
how: `dynaudnorm=n=0:c=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: speechnorm presets
what: Docs presets from weak (e=3) to extreme (e=50) amplification
how: `speechnorm=e=6.25:r=0.00001:l=1` (moderate, slow) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gate a stem
what: agate reduces signal below threshold by range; range=0 makes it an expander
how: `agate=threshold=0.05:range=0.1:ratio=4:attack=5:release=200` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keyed gate
what: sidechaingate gates the first input from the second input's level
how: `[0][1]sidechaingate=threshold=0.1:range=0.05:attack=1:release=150` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: acrossover sums flat in level, not in phase
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: Docs: summing all acrossover bands back gives flat output
how: 3-band split summed with `amix=normalize=0`: RMS -17.105 vs original -17.102 dB, but a null against the original left -13.2 dB RMS (phase shift), so don't null-test crossovers (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Steeper crossover
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: order sets slope from 2nd (12 dB/oct) to 20th; default 4th
how: `acrossover=split=1500:order=8th[LOW][HIGH]` (docs example) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Band gains need a newer ffmpeg
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: The current docs list a gains option for acrossover
how: `acrossover=...:gains=` failed here ('Option not found', ffmpeg 6.1); use `volume` per band instead

name: Per-band compressors
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: Multiband compression = several compressors, each on one band from a crossover (iZotope)
how: tested command: `acrossover=split=120 5000[L][M][H]`, one `acompressor` per band, `amix=inputs=3:normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: mcompand
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: Multiband compand using 4th-order Linkwitz-Riley crossovers; args = attack,decay soft-knee points crossover per band, '|' between bands
how: 5-band `mcompand=args=...` with crossovers 100/400/1600/6400/22000 ran (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spectral ducking of music under VO
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: iZotope: compress only 1.5-4 kHz of the music, keyed from the dialogue bus, so the music keeps its energy when nobody talks; iZotope's surround tips also suggest dialogue-keyed multiband/dynamic EQ on music, FX and backgrounds
how: tested command: `[0]acrossover=split=1000 4000[L][M][H];[M][k]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.03:ratio=6:attack=10:release=250[md];[L][md][H]amix=inputs=3:normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Music EQ dip for VO
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: iZotope: making room for VO usually means turning down 1-4 kHz in the music (but it sounds muffled without VO)
how: `equalizer=f=2500:t=q:w=1:g=-4` on the music bus (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dialogue clarity band
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: iZotope: an adjustment between 2-5 kHz can help dialogue clarity in a dense mix
how: `equalizer=f=3000:t=q:w=1.4:g=2` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dynamic EQ on a harsh band
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: adynamicequalizer applies EQ only when the detection band crosses a threshold
how: ffmpeg 6.1 syntax: `adynamicequalizer=threshold=10:dfrequency=3000:dqfactor=2:tfrequency=3000:tqfactor=2:mode=cut:ratio=2:range=6:attack=5:release=100` (newer docs name the modes cutabove/cutbelow etc.) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Listen to the detection band
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: mode=listen outputs only the isolated detection signal
how: `adynamicequalizer=dfrequency=200:dqfactor=1.5:mode=listen` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dynamic low shelf
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: dftype/tftype choose detection (bandpass, lowpass, highpass, peak) and target (bell, lowshelf, highshelf)
how: `adynamicequalizer=threshold=20:dfrequency=100:dftype=lowpass:tfrequency=120:tftype=lowshelf:mode=cut:range=6` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Peaking EQ widths
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: equalizer width_type h, q, o (octave), s, k
how: `equalizer=f=250:t=o:w=1:g=-4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Parallel EQ
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: equalizer mix (0-1) blends filtered with dry
how: `equalizer=f=3000:t=q:w=1:g=6:m=0.5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Automate an EQ band
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: equalizer supports frequency/width/gain/mix commands
how: `asendcmd=c='3.0 equalizer gain -9',equalizer=f=300:t=q:w=1:g=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shelves
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: bass/lowshelf and treble/highshelf: gain about -20..+20, beware clipping on boosts

name: Tilt the whole mix
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: tiltshelf boosts lows and cuts highs (or the reverse) around a centre (default 3000 Hz)
how: `tiltshelf=g=-2:f=1500` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: FIR EQ from points
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: firequalizer gain_entry draws an arbitrary curve (docs custom example)
how: `firequalizer=gain_entry='entry(100,0);entry(400,-4);entry(1000,-6);entry(2000,0)'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Zero-phase FIR
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: firequalizer zero_phase compensates its delay
how: `firequalizer=delay=0.1:fixed=on:zero_phase=on` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Steep rumble cut
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: asubcut gives a steeper roll-off than highpass (cutoff 2-200 Hz, order up to 20)
how: `asubcut=cutoff=25:order=10` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Ultrasonic cut
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: Spotify: inaudible high frequencies can make the loudness algorithm overestimate loudness (BS.1770 has no lowpass); asupercut cuts above 20 kHz
how: `asupercut=cutoff=20000:order=10` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sub boost
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: asubboost boosts subwoofer frequencies (cutoff 50-900 Hz)
how: `asubboost=boost=2:cutoff=90:slope=0.5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Exciter
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: aexciter adds harmonics above freq (2-12 kHz) instead of EQ-boosting highs
how: `aexciter=amount=1:drive=6:freq=6000` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: High-pass guitars against bass
section: Multiband and EQ for the mix
what: SOS: in mono checks, high-pass wide guitars ~12 dB/oct at 140-150 Hz so they don't smear the bass
how: `highpass=f=150:p=2` on the guitar/music stem (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: alimiter auto-levels by default
what: alimiter 'level' (auto level, default on) normalizes output back to 0 dB
how: limit=0.25: default output peak 0.0 dB; `alimiter=limit=0.25:level=disabled` -12.04 dB. Always set level=disabled for a ceiling (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: alimiter limit is linear or dB
what: limit default 1; attack 5 ms, release 50 ms by default
how: `alimiter=limit=-2dB:level=disabled` and `limit=0.891` both ran (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Compensate the lookahead delay
what: latency=1 compensates the attack-length lookahead and flushes at EOF
how: `alimiter=limit=0.5:attack=5:latency=1:level=disabled` kept a 6.000 s file at 6.000 s (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Upsample before alimiter
what: Docs recommend 2x-4x upsampling before alimiter depending on settings
how: limit 0.891 at 48 kHz gave TP -0.9 dBTP; with `aresample=192000,alimiter=...,aresample=48000` TP -1.0 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ASC release
what: asc releases to an average reduction when reduction is always needed; asc_level 0-1
how: `alimiter=limit=0.7:attack=3:release=80:asc=1:asc_level=0.5:level=disabled` peak -3.1 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lossy encode raises peaks
what: FabFilter: AAC/MP3 conversion can expose inter-sample peaks; R 128 says permitted TP may be lower for data reduction
how: a WAV limited at 0 dBFS (TP +0.1) read TP +1.5 dBTP after AAC 128k and +1.6 after AAC 96k (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: -2 dBTP before the encoder
what: Tech 3344: pass the signal through an end-stage limiter at -2 dBTP before the encoder; lower it for low bitrates
how: `aresample=192000,alimiter=limit=-2dB:level=disabled:latency=1,aresample=48000` then AAC 128k read TP -1.6 dBTP (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: -2 dBTP for MP2 and AC-3
what: Tech 3343: recommended max TP for MPEG-1 Layer 2 and Dolby AC-3 is -2 dBTP
how: use `limit=-2dB` for those

name: -3 dBTP with bitrate compression
what: EBU QC item 0084B: where bitrate compression is used -3 dBTP may apply; SOS argues for below -3 dBTP before MP3/AAC
how: `alimiter=limit=-3dB:level=disabled` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Psychoacoustic clipper
what: apsyclip clips with psychoacoustic shaping; adaptive 0-1, iterations 1-20
how: +10 dB into `apsyclip=clip=0.7:adaptive=0.5:iterations=10` gave peak -2.9 dB, RMS -7.7 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hear what the clipper removes
what: apsyclip diff=1 outputs only the difference
how: `apsyclip=clip=0.7:diff=1` gave RMS -25.3 dB of removed signal (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Soft clip with oversampling
what: asoftclip types hard, tanh, atan, cubic, exp, alg, quintic, sin, erf; oversample option
how: `asoftclip=type=tanh:threshold=0.7:oversample=4` peak -5.7 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spotify Loud mode limiter
what: In Loud (-11 LUFS) Spotify applies a limiter at -1 dB sample, 5 ms attack, 100 ms decay
how: know that quiet dynamic masters get limited in Loud mode

name: loudnorm outputs 192 kHz
what: Dynamic loudnorm upsamples to 192 kHz for true peak; set the output rate
how: without `-ar` the WAV was 192000 Hz; with `-ar 48000` 48000 Hz (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Check which mode loudnorm used
what: linear mode reverts to dynamic if target LRA < source LRA or the gain would break TP; print_format=json shows normalization_type
how: a linear pass asking I=-5 from -15.4 LUFS reported "normalization_type" : "dynamic" (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: loudnorm offset
what: offset gain is applied before the true-peak limiter
how: `loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1:offset=0.5:print_format=summary` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: loudnorm dual_mono
what: dual_mono compensates mono files meant for stereo playback
how: `loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1:dual_mono=true:print_format=summary` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Static gain is the cleanest fix
what: Tech 3343: in post, measure the whole programme and apply one static gain offset to reach target
how: I -15.4 LUFS, `volume=4.1dB` -> -11.3 LUFS exactly; TP rose -9.4 -> -5.3, so check TP after (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Only turn down quiet-on-purpose pieces
what: Tech 3343 §9.1: for intentionally quiet items, perform only negative gain corrections so they pass unharmed
how: if measured I is below target and quiet is intended, skip positive `volume`

name: Loudness Offset / Low Loudness Flag
what: Tech 3343 §6.1.1: metadata keeps the real programme loudness; 'Loudness Offset' marks a deliberate distance from target, -99.9 = Low Loudness Flag
how: note the intended offset in delivery notes

name: Don't trust incoming dialnorm
what: Tech 3343 §6.3: dialnorm -27 (Dolby default) or -31 (lowest) suggests unchecked metadata; re-measure external sources
how: re-measure with `ebur128` on ingest (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Symphony rule for multi-part items
what: AES TD1004: normalise multi-part programmes by the loudest part's gain and apply it to all parts
how: measure each part, use one `volume` value for all

name: The docs sidechain example makes 4 channels
what: The sidechaincompress docs example ends with amerge, which stacks channels
how: with stereo music+voice the docs graph wrote 4 channels; replacing amerge with `amix=normalize=0` wrote 2 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Boost a quiet key
what: level_sc (sidechain gain) changes what the detector hears without changing the voice in the mix
how: `sidechaincompress=threshold=0.05:ratio=4:level_sc=4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Partial ducking
what: sidechaincompress mix blends compressed and dry
how: `sidechaincompress=threshold=0.03:ratio=20:mix=0.6` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Duck the reverb, not just the music
what: SOS: put a compressor after the reverb keyed from the dry source so reverb sits back during words and blooms in pauses; mixanalog suggests the same for vocals
how: tested command: `[send]aecho=0.8:0.9:120|240:0.4|0.3[wet];[wet][key]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.05:ratio=8:attack=5:release=400[wd];[dry][wd]amix=normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Kick-keyed pumping
what: Wikipedia: in EDM, synths are side-chained to the kick so they compress only when the beat hits
how: tested command: `[music][clicks]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.1:ratio=10:attack=1:release=300` with a 0.5 s click track (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Drawn volume automation
what: volume with eval=frame evaluates per frame (docs fade example)
how: `volume='if(between(t,2,4),0.3,1)':eval=frame` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Ramp automation
what: Docs: fade volume after time 10 over 5 s with an expression
how: `volume='if(lt(t,2),1,max(1-(t-2)/2,0.25))':eval=frame` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Timed volume commands
what: asendcmd sends 'volume' commands at given times
how: `asendcmd=c='2.0 volume volume 0.3;4.0 volume volume 1.0',volume=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Interpolated command ramps
what: asendcmd [expr] flag with TI (0..1 across the interval) builds ramps
how: `asendcmd=c='1.0-3.0 [expr] volume volume 1-0.7*TI',volume=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fade curves
what: afade has many curves (tri, qsin, hsin, esin, log, exp, ...)
how: `afade=t=out:st=3:d=3:curve=exp` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fade to a level, not silence
what: afade silence/unity set the end gains, so a fade can dip to 0.25
how: `afade=t=out:st=3:d=1:curve=qsin:silence=0.25` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Clip gain at the end of a line
what: iZotope: many speakers fade at the end of phrases; raise clip gain gradually toward the end instead of more compression
how: `volume='if(gt(t,3),1+0.3*(t-3)/3,1)':eval=frame` (ramp +30% over the last 3 s) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mono-fold loss in LU
what: Fold to mono and compare loudness; Mastering The Mix: if the level drops noticeably or elements vanish, it's too wide
how: bed: stereo I -15.4, `pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0+0.5*c1` + `ebur128=dualmono=true` -16.5 LUFS (1.1 LU loss) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Measure side vs mid
what: Mid = common to both channels, side = difference (Mastering The Mix); stereotools converts L/R to M/S
how: `stereotools=mode=lr>ms,pan=mono|c0=c1,astats=...RMS_level` side -23.9 dB vs mid -18.1 dB (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: M/S round trip is lossless
what: stereotools modes lr>ms and ms>lr
how: `stereotools=mode=lr>ms,stereotools=mode=ms>lr` nulled to -inf against the original (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Narrow or widen with side level
what: stereotools slev sets side level (default 1)
how: `stereotools=slev=0.5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: extrastereo m values
what: m=0 mono, 1 unchanged, -1 swaps channels, default 2.5 widens
how: `extrastereo=m=0` then aphasemeter detected mono for the whole 6 s (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bass mono below 100-150 Hz
what: Mastering The Mix: keep sub and bass centred below roughly 100-150 Hz, width in mids/highs
how: tested command: `acrossover=split=120:order=4th[lo][hi];[lo]pan=stereo|c0=0.5*c0+0.5*c1|c1=0.5*c0+0.5*c1[lom];[lom][hi]amix=normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Check mono after every width move
what: Mastering The Mix: fold to mono each time you add width and check weight and centre
how: repeat the mono-fold loudness check after each change (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Haas on mono costs level in mono
what: haas gives a mono signal direction/width (default delays 2.05/2.12 ms)
how: mono voice -16.8 LUFS; after `haas` folded back to mono -19.6 LUFS (2.8 LU lost) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: stereowiden
what: Suppresses common signal and cross-delays L/R; crossfeed=1 cancels all common signal
how: `stereowiden=delay=20:feedback=0.3:crossfeed=0.3:drymix=0.8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pseudo-stereo by decorrelation
what: adecorrelate applies decorrelation stages (1-16, default 6)
how: `adecorrelate=stages=6:seed=1` ran on dual mono, but aphasemeter still read phase 1.0 at the end, so measure before relying on it (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Balance with power law
what: stereotools balance_out with bmode power = equal power -6..+6 dB
how: `stereotools=balance_out=0.3:bmode_out=power` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pan the mid
what: stereotools mpan pans the middle signal
how: `stereotools=mpan=-0.3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pan laws
what: 0 dB law: centre not attenuated; -6 dB: same level anywhere but weaker in a dense centre; -3 dB is the compromise
how: for a mono source in ffmpeg write the gains yourself, e.g. -3 dB centre `pan=stereo|c0=0.7071*c0|c1=0.7071*c0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pan law doesn't fix mono balance
what: SOS: in a mono sum, panned sounds always get quieter relative to centre; changing the pan law has no bearing on that
how: fix with level/EQ, check by folding to mono

name: LCR panning
what: SOS: pan each mono source hard left, hard right or centre only; separation should come from EQ, ducking or arrangement, not panning
how: `pan=stereo|c0=c0|c1=0*c0` for hard left (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Swap or copy channels
what: pan remaps exactly with gains of 0/1 ('Pure channel mapping')
how: `pan="stereo|c0=c1|c1=c0"` swaps; `pan=stereo|c0=c1|c1=c1` copies right to both (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Split channels to inspect
what: channelsplit sends each channel to its own stream
how: `channelsplit=channel_layout=stereo[L][R]` -map each (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Headphone crossfeed check
what: crossfeed blends L/R lows for more speaker-like headphone listening
how: `crossfeed=strength=0.4:range=0.5` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: bs2b is in this build
what: Bauer stereo-to-binaural; profiles default, cmoy, jmeier
how: `bs2b=profile=cmoy` ran here (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Upmix stereo to 5.1
what: surround filter upmixes (default out 5.1); Tech 3343: an upmix should never replace a discrete mix, and must be re-measured
how: `surround=chl_out=5.1` gave 6 ch 5.1; the upmix read -17.3 LUFS from a -15.4 LUFS source (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Downmixes change loudness
what: Tech 3343: downmix loudness depends on method, coefficients, content and correlation; measure and gain-correct
how: that upmix through `-ac 2` read -22.7 LUFS, far below the original stereo (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: BS.775 default coefficients
what: Tech 3343: without reliable metadata start from L/R 0 dB, C/Ls/Rs -3 dB
how: `pan=stereo|FL=FL+0.7071*FC+0.7071*BL|FR=FR+0.7071*FC+0.7071*BR` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Downmix levels in the resampler
what: swr options clev/slev (dB) and lfe_mix_level set downmix levels
how: `aresample=clev=-3:slev=-3:ocl=stereo` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Prefer Lo/Ro
what: EBU recommends Lo/Ro as the default downmix metadata; Lt/Rt is less predictable in loudness
how: use plain matrix downmix (as above)

name: 5.0 when no LFE is needed
what: Tech 3343: one way to avoid LFE problems is not to use it (5.0) when no extra low headroom is needed
how: deliver `5.0` layout unless the mix needs LFE

name: Stem placement for a quick 5.1
what: iZotope starting point: dialogue 100% centre; Foley front L/R; hard FX front L/R + 50% LFE; ambience 50/50 front/rear; music 75% front, 25% rear
how: build with `pan=5.1|...` per stem

name: Measure dialogue in the centre
what: R 128 s4: for 5.1 the centre channel is the speech track for manual checks; for stereo the complete mix
how: `channelsplit=channel_layout=5.1:channels=FC[c];[c]ebur128` (a -20 dBFS tone in FC read -23.0 LUFS) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix AAC channel order
what: Docs: remap a 5.1 WAV wrongly in AAC native order
how: `channelmap=1|2|0|5|3|4:5.1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Virtual bass to 2.1
what: virtualbass outputs 2.1 with a synthesized LFE
how: `virtualbass=cutoff=200:strength=2` output layout 2.1 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Reverb on a send, 100% wet
what: SOS: a wet/dry knob on an insert turns the dry sound down as you add reverb; LordReverb: sends at 100% wet so all tracks share one space
how: tested command: `asplit[d][s]` -> wet chain -> `[d][w]amix=weights='1 0.25':normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Abbey Road reverb filters
what: SOS: high-pass the reverb ~200 Hz, 12-18 dB/oct, and low-pass ~10 kHz
how: `highpass=f=200,lowpass=f=10000` on the send (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pre-delay by source
what: iZotope: pre-delay 20-80 ms on vocals, 40-100 ms on guitar, 5-50 ms on drums
how: `adelay=25:all=1` before the reverb on the send (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Filtered echoes into reverb
what: SOS: a repeating delay with lows rolled off ~300 Hz and highs above ~1.2 kHz recedes nicely
how: tested command: `aecho=0.8:0.9:300|600:0.4|0.3,highpass=f=300,lowpass=f=1200` on a send (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: aecho doubling
what: Docs: aecho=0.8:0.88:60:0.4 sounds like twice as many instruments

name: aecho mountains
what: Docs: 1000 ms (and 1800 ms) delays sound like open-air mountains; 6 ms sounds metallic/robot

name: Convolution reverb with afir
what: afir convolves the first input with an IR stream (docs: mono IR as second input)
how: `ffmpeg -i voice.wav -i ir.wav -lavfi afir conv.wav` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Synthetic IR for tests
what: No real IR here; a decaying noise burst works as a test IR
how: `anoisesrc=c=white:a=0.5:r=48000:d=1.6:s=7` + `afade=t=out:st=0:d=1.6:curve=exp,lowpass=f=8000` -> ir.wav (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: afir dry/wet
what: dry sets input gain, wet the output gain
how: `afir=dry=10:wet=10` inside the send graph (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Switch IRs
what: nbirs inputs switchable with ir (runtime command)
how: `[s][i0][i1]afir=nbirs=2:ir=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: irnorm/irgain need newer ffmpeg
what: Current docs list irnorm, irlink, irgain
how: `afir=irnorm=-1:irgain=0.1` failed in ffmpeg 6.1 ('Option not found')

name: IR length limit
what: maxir default 30 s, range 0.1-60 s
how: `afir=maxir=60` for long halls (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Chorus
what: Docs: typical delays 40-60 ms; two-delay example

name: Align two mics by distance
what: compensationdelay delays by mm/cm/m (temp-corrected); ~30 cm between mics can cause antiphase
how: `compensationdelay=cm=30:wet=1:dry=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mono reverb panned opposite
what: SOS: send a hard-panned mono source to a mono reverb/delay panned to the other side so it isn't a sore thumb
how: tested command: `asplit[d][s];[s]aecho=0.8:0.9:80:0.5,pan=stereo|c1=c0[w];[d]pan=stereo|c0=c0[dl];[dl][w]amix=normalize=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: EBU R 128 target and tolerances
what: -23.0 LUFS; ±0.2 LU QC measurement tolerance; ±1.0 LU only where target isn't practical (live); TP max -1 dBTP in production (±0.3 dB)
how: `ebur128=peak=true` on the final file (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: R 128 measures the whole mix
what: Measure the programme in its entirety, not just speech or music
how: run `ebur128` on the full mix, all channels (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Short-form: max short-term -18 LUFS
what: R 128 s1: adverts/promos (up to ~2 min) at -23.0 LUFS, max short-term -18.0 LUFS (+5 LU), TP -1 dBTP, no LRA
how: check max of `lavfi.r128.S` from `ebur128=metadata=1` (per-100 ms dump as in the metering section) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Short-form momentary option was removed
what: Klangfreund: R 128 s1 v1 allowed max momentary -15 LUFS as alternative; v2 (2016) removed it, keeping max short-term +5 LU
how: measure short-term, not momentary, for spots

name: Streaming broadcast content (s2)
what: R 128 s2: stream unchanged at -23 LUFS; if the broadcaster wants control for mobiles, interim distribution level -20 to -16 LUFS
how: make a separate streaming master with `volume` + true-peak limiter

name: Cinematic content: LDR <= 5 LU
what: R 128 s4: Loudness-to-Dialogue Ratio (PL - DL) should not exceed 5 LU; within 5 LU don't adapt; don't push LDR to 0
how: measure PL on the mix and DL on the dialogue stem with `ebur128`; LDR = PL - DL (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Anchor normalisation cap
what: R 128 s4: dialogue-anchored normalisation up to -23 LUFS; with LDR <= 5 LU PL can reach -18 LUFS max
how: static `volume` so DL sits at target, then limit

name: When to anchor
what: Tech 3343 §4.1: optionally use an anchor signal when LRA > ~20 LU or PL-DL > 5 LU
how: check LRA in `ebur128` summary first (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Comfort zone +3/-5 LU
what: Tech 3343 §9: listeners accept about +3/-5 LU around target; Production Expert uses it as a short-term guide
how: keep short-term within -20..-28 LUFS for a -23 mix

name: Meter green zones
what: Production Expert: momentary ±3 LU, short-term ±2 LU, integrated ±1 LU green zones around target
how: read M/S/I from `ebur128` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sports: commentary a bit under
what: Tech 3343: keep commentators around -24 LUFS so crowd reactions have room
how: level the commentary bus to about -24 short-term

name: Shows: audience can be the anchor
what: Tech 3343: in entertainment shows, balance the audience around target and let the presenter move above/below
how: pick the anchor stem before levelling

name: Don't build loudness sausage
what: Tech 3343: overly aggressive loudness processing ruins contrast; compliant content should bypass loudness processors
how: don't run `dynaudnorm`/`loudnorm` dynamic on a compliant mix

name: Live: tame packages beforehand
what: Production Expert: measure pre-recorded packages and play them a little lower to keep a live show near target
how: pre-measure inserts with `ebur128`

name: ATSC A/85: -24 LKFS, below -2 dBTP
what: For content without metadata: target -24 LKFS, ±2 dB measurement variation expected but don't aim high or low; TP below -2 dBTP
how: `ebur128=peak=true`; LKFS = LUFS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: A/85 long-form: measure typical dialog
what: Measure a representative section of normal dialog (not shouting/whispering) and record it as Dialog Level
how: cut a dialog-only section and run `ebur128` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: A/85 short-form: all channels
what: Commercials: measure all channels (LFE excluded) and all elements over the whole spot
how: `ebur128` on the full spot (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: A/85 has a 2026 revision
what: ATSC lists A/85:2026-07 as current (approved 8 July 2026), also covering streaming
how: check the current version before delivering US TV

name: CALM Act
what: FCC rules (effective Dec 13, 2012) require commercials to have the same average volume as programs, via ATSC A/85
how: mix spots to the program target

name: dialnorm meaning
what: AC-3 dialnorm = |Dialog Level| (1-31); the decoder reduces gain by the difference between -31 and dialnorm
how: set dialnorm to the measured value if encoding AC-3

name: US networks may measure full mix
what: TV Tech: long-form is anchored on voice with dialnorm to match, but some networks measure long-form across all channels
how: ask which method the network uses

name: Australia OP-59
what: OP-59: -24 LKFS target with true peak -2 dBTP; the integrating meter is for the finished product, not for mixing
how: `ebur128=peak=true`
refs: Free TV Australia OP-59 FAQ, https://www.freetv.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/OP-59-Part-1-Advisory-Note-to-Advertising-Agencies-and-Production-Facilities-Frequently-Asked-Questions.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Japan ARIB TR-B32
what: ARIB TR-B32: operational guidelines for average loudness and true peak of all digital TV programmes and CMs
how: get the current spec from ARIB before delivery

name: Italy AGCOM
what: Vojvoda's table: Italian TV -24 LUFS (±0.5 LU), -2 dBTP (AGCOM 219/09/CSP)
how: use as the delivery check; measure the file with `ebur128=peak=true` (the source gives no ffmpeg step)

name: Loudness metadata in BWF
what: Tech 3343: Programme Loudness, LRA, max TP, max momentary and max short-term can be stored in the BWF BEXT chunk / ADM; IEC 62760 lists integratedLoudness, loudnessRange, maxTruePeak, maxMomentary
how: ffmpeg wav muxer `-write_bext 1` adds a BEXT chunk (ran here); loudness fields themselves were not verified (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spotify: -14 at playback, not on upload
section: Loudness specs: streaming, social and OTT
what: Spotify measures at upload and applies gain at playback; audio isn't processed beforehand; albums normalised as a whole
how: use as the delivery check; measure the file with `ebur128=peak=true` (the source gives no ffmpeg step)

name: Tested master chain

how: `highpass=f=30,acompressor=threshold=-18dB:ratio=2:attack=30:release=250,equalizer=f=3000:t=q:w=1:g=1,aresample=192000,alimiter=limit=-2dB:level=disabled:latency=1,aresample=48000` -> I -18.0 LUFS, TP -8.2 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Freesound CC0-only search
what: Freesound mixes licences; to get sounds that need no credit, filter the search to CC0
how: on freesound.org use the licence filter on the results page (right-hand side), or the URL filter `f=license:"Creative Commons 0"` (a CC0-only search showed 41,474 results); download, then still record the page URL in `library/README.md`.

name: Freesound has several licences, not one
what: each uploader picks one of three licences (plus a retired fourth), and what you may do depends on it, so check every sound's own page
how: read the licence line on each sound page before download; keep only CC0 for the owner's no-credit rule.

name: Kenney UI and interface packs (CC0)
what: Kenney's "51 UI sound effects" (5 clicks, 2 mouse clicks, 6 rollovers, 38 switches, WAV, organic) and "Interface Sounds" (100 OGG files, normalized volume: clicks, snaps, minimize/maximize, confirmations) are CC0; credit is "not mandatory"
how: download from the OpenGameArt pages, convert OGG to WAV with `ffmpeg -i x.ogg x.wav`, add to `library/sfx/` with the source URL.

name: Kenney audio categories
what: kenney.nl lists audio packs: Casino, Sci-fi, Interface, Impact, Voiceover (Fighter), Voiceover, Music Jingles, RPG, Digital and UI audio
how: pick the pack by category on kenney.nl/assets/category:Audio, then confirm the licence on the pack page.

name: OpenGameArt "100 CC0 SFX" packs
what: rubberduck's packs are CC0: pack 1 (bells, dishes, door squeaks/closes, explosion, glass, gong, hits, keys, machine loops, metal, paper, plops, shots, slams, splash, springs, switches...), pack 2 (air flowing, doors, footsteps, glass, hits, ambient/machine/construction/highway/water loops, metal, stones, switches, thunder, wood) and "50 CC0 Sci-Fi SFX" (beeps, explosions, loops, retro beeps/laser, rocket, teleport, terminal sounds)
how: download the zip from each page; note the pack name in `library/README.md`.

name: OpenGameArt CC0 collection page
what: "CC0 Sound Effects" (OwlishMedia) collects packs with attribution not required (8-bit pack, time slow, machine shutting down, 20 rustles of dry leaves, casino sounds, monster voices...)
how: browse the collection, open each pack and confirm "CC0" on that pack's own page before use.

name: BVKER "Footsteps" foley library (CC0)
what: 700+ WAV files of footsteps, ambience and one-shots under CC0, no credit needed
how: download from the BVKER page; sort by surface into `library/sfx/foley/`.

name: Lots of Sounds (CC0)
what: a CC0 library (14,077 sounds in the search snapshot, "12,000+" on the page, MP3) with soundboard and REST API; browsing is free but downloading needs an account sign-in, and API access is a paid Pro plan
how: use only manual downloads after sign-in; do not script the API.

name: ZapSplat's CC0 category
what: ZapSplat labels some sounds "CC0 1.0 Universal": copy, modify, distribute, even commercially, without permission; patent/trademark/publicity rights are not affected
how: only take ZapSplat files whose page shows the CC0 licence type.

name: Sonniss GDC bundles (royalty-free, no credit, not CC0)
