what: a tween with no ease uses `power1.out`; at half time it is already 75% of the way
how: check with `gsap.parseEase('power1.out')(0.5)` -> 0.75; set your own default with `gsap.defaults({ease:'power2.out'})` or `gsap.timeline({defaults:{ease:'expo.out', duration:0.8}})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Power ladder: pick strength by number
what: power1..power4 (= quad, cubic, quart, quint) get steeper: at 50% time the .out versions read 0.75 / 0.875 / 0.938 / 0.969
how: `gsap.parseEase('power3.out')(0.5)` to compare (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: expo.out = almost there immediately
what: expo.out reaches ~50% of the distance in the first 10% of the time and 97.7% at half time, the long tail HyperFrames recommends for arrivals
how: `tl.from(title,{y:60,opacity:0,duration:0.9,ease:'expo.out'},t)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: circ.out for a firm, round stop
what: circ.out sits between power2 and power3 at mid-time (0.866)
how: `ease:'circ.out'` when power2 is too soft and power3 too strong (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: sine.inOut for gentle drifts and loops
what: sine.inOut is symmetric (exactly 0.5 at mid-time); HyperFrames eases camera moves both ways
how: `ease:'sine.inOut'` on a slow background drift (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ease 'none' for constant motion
what: `none` (linear) keeps speed constant: right for spins, tickers, progress bars and scrolling credits
how: `tl.to(strip,{xPercent:-50,duration:8,ease:'none'},0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: back.out overshoot amount
what: back.out(1.7) peaks 10% past the target; back.out(3) peaks 25% past
how: `ease:'back.out(1.4)'` on badges/pills; raise the number for more overshoot; never on opacity or colour (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: elastic.out amplitude and period
what: elastic.out(amplitude, period): elastic.out(1,0.3) overshoots to 1.37, elastic.out(1,0.5) only to 1.20, so a larger period means a calmer spring
how: `ease:'elastic.out(1,0.5)'` for a premium spring, `elastic.out(1,0.3)` for a cartoon one (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: bounce.out never overshoots
what: bounce.out bounces against the end value and never exceeds 1 (max 1.0 measured)
how: `gsap.from(word,{y:-300,duration:1.2,ease:'bounce.out'})` for drop-in letters (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: steps(n) for frame-by-frame or digital looks
what: `steps(5)` jumps in 5 equal increments (x to 100 gave 0,20,60,100 at progress .1,.3,.5,.99)
how: `tl.to(caret,{opacity:0,duration:0.5,ease:'steps(1)',repeat:7,yoyo:true})` for a hard blink, or `steps(12)` for stop-motion (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: expoScale for zooms that look linear
what: scale animated linearly appears to slow down; `expoScale(start,end)` bends the curve so the zoom feels even (scale 1->2 sits at 1.414 at half time instead of 1.5); start/end must be non-zero
how: `tl.fromTo(bg,{scale:1},{scale:2,duration:4,ease:'expoScale(1,2)'})`; add a third arg to bend another ease: `expoScale(0.5,3,power2.inOut)` (needs EasePack) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SlowMo: fly in, read, fly out in one tween
what: `slow(linearRatio, power, yoyoMode)` decelerates, moves linearly, then accelerates; default 0.7/0.7, so 70% of the time is steady pace for reading
how: `tl.fromTo(line,{x:-900},{x:900,duration:4,ease:'slow(0.7,0.7)'})` (needs EasePack) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SlowMo yoyoMode for the matching fade
what: with yoyoMode true the ease goes 0 -> 1 -> 0, so an opacity tween with the same duration fades in during the ease-in and out during the ease-out of the SlowMo move
how: `tl.from(line,{opacity:0,duration:4,ease:'slow(0.7,0.7,true)'},'<')`; measured values 0, .889, 1, .889, 0 at 0/.1/.5/.9/1 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: RoughEase for jitter and glitch moves
what: `rough({strength, points, template, taper, randomize, clamp})` wanders around a template ease; `clamp:true` keeps it inside start/end; `taper:'out'` calms it toward the end; it always ends on the target
how: `ease:'rough({strength:2,points:30,template:none.out,taper:out,randomize:false,clamp:true})'` (EasePack); randomize:false gives an even zig-zag that is the same every load (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Ease the whole stagger, not just each item
what: the stagger object has its own `ease` that spaces the start times; `'power2'` starts with big gaps that tighten (distribute with power2 gave 0, .578, .875, .984, 1)
how: `stagger:{amount:0.6, ease:'power2'}` so the first items spread out and the last ones bunch up (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CustomEase from a cubic-bezier string
what: CustomEase accepts the 4-number `cubic-bezier` format, so any curve from a design spec or cubic-bezier.com can drive GSAP
how: `CustomEase.create('m3emph', '.05,.7,.1,1'); tl.to(el,{y:0,ease:'m3emph'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CustomEase from SVG path data
what: any SVG path built from M/C/S/L/Z commands becomes an ease (normalized internally); create it once and reference by name

name: Draw the ease to check it
what: `CustomEase.getSVGData(ease,{width,height,path})` returns/fills SVG path data of any ease, built-in or custom, for a visual check
how: `CustomEase.getSVGData('power2.out',{width:500,height:400,path:'#ease'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CustomBounce with synced squash
what: CustomBounce.create(id,{strength, endAtStart, squash, squashID}) makes the bounce ease plus an `id-squash` ease for scaleX/scaleY that sticks at each impact
how: `CustomBounce.create('drop',{strength:0.7,squash:3}); tl.from(el,{y:-400,duration:2,ease:'drop'},0).to(el,{scaleX:1.3,scaleY:0.7,duration:2,ease:'drop-squash',transformOrigin:'50% 100%'},0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CustomBounce endAtStart for a hop
what: with `endAtStart:true` the ease returns to the start value (measured 0 at the end): sit, leap, bounce back down to rest
how: `CustomBounce.create('hopb',{strength:0.6,endAtStart:true}); tl.to(logo,{y:-120,duration:1.4,ease:'hopb'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CustomWiggle for shakes that end at rest
what: a wiggle ease goes to the value and back the same amount the other way, ending where it began (measured end 0, min -0.98); strength is the tween value, frequency is `wiggles`
how: `CustomWiggle.create('shake',{wiggles:8,type:'easeOut'}); tl.to(word,{rotation:8,duration:0.6,ease:'shake'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: M3 emphasizedDecelerate as a CustomEase
section: Material 3 motion tokens as GSAP eases
what: the Material spec's emphasizedDecelerate curve is Cubic(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1.0)
how: `CustomEase.create('m3EmphDecel','.05,.7,.1,1'); tl.from(card,{y:80,duration:0.5,ease:'m3EmphDecel'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Flutter API (Material spec): Easing class, https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Easing-class.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: M3 emphasizedAccelerate as a CustomEase
section: Material 3 motion tokens as GSAP eases
what: emphasizedAccelerate is Cubic(0.3, 0.0, 0.8, 0.15)
how: `CustomEase.create('m3EmphAccel','.3,0,.8,.15')`
refs: Flutter API (Material spec): Easing class, https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Easing-class.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: M3 standard curve family
section: Material 3 motion tokens as GSAP eases
what: standard Cubic(0.2,0,0,1), standardDecelerate Cubic(0,0,0,1), standardAccelerate Cubic(0.3,0,1,1)
how: `CustomEase.create('m3Std','.2,0,0,1')` when a demo should move like Material UI
refs: Flutter API (Material spec): Easing class, https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Easing-class.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: M3 duration scale
section: Material 3 motion tokens as GSAP eases
how: take tween durations from this one ladder instead of ad-hoc numbers, e.g. `duration:0.3` (medium2)
refs: Flutter API (Material spec): Durations class, https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Durations-class.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: each vs amount
what: `each` is the gap between starts (5 items, each 0.1, duration 1 -> total 1.4 s); `amount` is the total spread split among all items (amount 1 -> 2.0 s total regardless of count)
how: use `stagger:{amount:0.5}` when the item count changes but the beat length must not (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Negative stagger runs backwards
what: a negative number makes the last element start first
how: `stagger:-0.06` for right-to-left letter reveals (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stagger from center or edges
what: `from:'center'` starts in the middle and spreads out; `'edges'` starts at both ends and meets in the middle; also 'start','end','random' or an index
how: `stagger:{each:0.05, from:'center'}` for a title that blooms from its middle (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Grid staggers
what: with `grid:[rows,cols]` (or 'auto') the delay follows 2D distance from `from`; `axis:'x'|'y'` limits it to one axis; `from:[0.5,0.5]` is the centre, `[1,0]` the top-right corner
how: `stagger:{each:0.04, grid:[3,8], from:'center'}` on a tile/letter wall (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Function stagger for custom rhythm
what: a function `(index,target,list)` returns each item's total delay from the start (not from the previous one)
how: `stagger:(i)=>i*i*0.04` for an accelerating cascade; 5 items with i*i*0.1 gave a 2.6 s tween (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Repeat inside the stagger object
what: repeat/yoyo/callbacks inside the stagger object apply per element; at top level they repeat the whole group after all finish
how: `stagger:{each:0.1, repeat:3, yoyo:true}`; in HyperFrames keep repeats finite: `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(duration/cycle)-1)`

name: utils.distribute for any property
what: distribute() is the engine behind advanced staggers and spreads any value by index/grid with base, amount/each, from, grid, axis and ease
how: `scale: gsap.utils.distribute({base:0.5, amount:0.5, from:'center'})` gave 1, .75, .5, .75, 1 across 5 items (edges big, centre small) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stagger spacing by role
what: letters about a frame apart, words 60-120 ms, list items 40-80 ms (registry stagger-cascade cites observed steps of 0.04-0.08 s, 0.14-0.18 s for deliberate item reveals)
how: `stagger:1/30` for letters at 30 fps, `0.08` for words
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/stagger-cascade.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add stagger-cascade`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Position parameter '<' and '>'
what: `'<'` = start of the previous animation, `'>'` = its end; `'>0.5'` is half a second after it ends (measured starts 0, 0, 1.5)

name: Percent offsets in the position parameter
what: `'<25%'` = 25% into the previous animation; `'-=25%'` overlaps by 25% of the inserted animation's duration (measured 0, 0.5, 1.5)
how: `tl.to(word2,{...},'<30%')` for 30%-done overlap between titles (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Labels as beat markers
what: `addLabel('hit',2)` then `'hit+=0.5'` places tweens relative to a named moment
how: label each music hit: `tl.addLabel('drop', beatTimes[8])`; then `tl.from(title,{...},'drop')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Absolute times for HyperFrames
what: HyperFrames places tweens at absolute seconds and wants start states in `fromTo`, not CSS
how: `tl.fromTo('#t',{opacity:0},{opacity:1,duration:0.4},2.4)`

name: Percentage keyframes
what: keyframes `{'0%':{},'50%':{},'100%':{}}` inside one `to()`; default ease between keyframes is power1.inOut, change with `easeEach`, ease the whole block with `ease`
how: `tl.to(ball,{keyframes:{'0%':{y:0},'50%':{y:-200},'100%':{y:0}, easeEach:'sine.inOut'},duration:1})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Array keyframes
what: `keyframes:{x:[0,100,50]}` spreads values evenly over the duration; arrays need not have the same length

name: Object keyframes with gaps
what: an array of vars objects runs like chained to() tweens; `delay` creates gaps or overlaps (two 1 s steps with delay 0.5 -> 2.5 s)
how: `keyframes:[{x:100,duration:1},{y:100,duration:1,delay:0.5}]` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: from() renders immediately
what: from()/fromTo() default to immediateRender:true, so a from() placed after a to() on the same property can jump at frame 0
how: prefer `fromTo` for every state that matters, or set `immediateRender:false` on the later from()
refs: GSAP: Common GSAP mistakes, https://gsap.com/resources/mistakes, checked 2026-10-24

name: Set initial transforms with GSAP too
what: GSAP can't read units or rotation reliably back from computed matrices, so initial transforms should be set by GSAP
how: `gsap.set(el,{xPercent:-50,yPercent:-50,x:960,y:540})` before building tweens
refs: GSAP: Common GSAP mistakes, https://gsap.com/resources/mistakes, checked 2026-10-24

name: Combine xPercent with x
what: xPercent/yPercent stack with pixel x/y, e.g. centre an element on a point
how: `gsap.set(dot,{xPercent:-50,yPercent:-50,x:300,y:200})` -> `translate(-50%,-50%) translate(300px,200px)` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: GSAP: Common GSAP mistakes, https://gsap.com/resources/mistakes, checked 2026-10-24

name: Finite yoyo length
what: totalDuration includes repeats and repeatDelay: 1 s, repeat 3, yoyo, repeatDelay 0.2 -> 4.6 s
how: compute `repeat` from the clip length so the loop ends inside it (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Reusable named effects
what: `gsap.registerEffect({name, effect, defaults, extendTimeline:true})` turns a recipe into `tl.fadeUp(target,config,position)`
how: `gsap.registerEffect({name:'fadeUp',effect:(t,c)=>gsap.fromTo(t,{y:c.y,opacity:0},{y:0,opacity:1,duration:c.duration}),defaults:{y:40,duration:0.5},extendTimeline:true}); tl.fadeUp('#t',{y:20},0.3)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Snap a tween to increments
what: `snap:{x:20}` snaps every in-between value (live) to multiples of 20; an array snaps to the nearest listed value; `{values,radius}` only snaps within a radius

name: Counter by tweening textContent
what: tweening an element's `textContent` with `snap:{textContent:1}` counts in whole numbers (0->1000 linear showed 333 at 33.3%)
how: `tl.to('#n',{textContent:2500,snap:{textContent:1},duration:1.4,ease:'power2.out'},t)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Formatted counter via onUpdate
what: drive a plain object and write the formatted number in onUpdate; HyperFrames says to drive charts/counters from a tween's onUpdate and use tabular figures, count-up 1.2-1.6 s
how: `const c={v:0}; tl.to(c,{v:10000,duration:1.5,ease:'power2.out',onUpdate:()=>el.textContent=Math.round(c.v).toLocaleString('en-US')},t)` (showed 8,750 at half time); CSS `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Wrap values with a modifier
what: modifiers intercept each applied value: `modifiers:{x:gsap.utils.wrap(0,100)}` keeps x looping 0-100 (x 250 became 50)
how: seamless marquee: `tl.to(items,{x:'+=1000',duration:8,ease:'none',modifiers:{x:gsap.utils.unitize(x=>parseFloat(x)%1000)}})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: interpolate colours and strings
what: `gsap.utils.interpolate('red','blue',0.5)` -> rgba(128,0,128,1); works on numbers, colours, complex strings, arrays and objects
how: inside a seek-driven onUpdate: `el.style.color = gsap.utils.interpolate('#ffffff','#ffcc00',p)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: mapRange for scroll-to-value mapping
how: map a beat index or timeline progress to a property in canvas/onUpdate code (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: wrap / wrapYoyo for cycling palettes
what: `wrap(['red','green','yellow'],5)` -> 'yellow'; `wrapYoyo(0,10,12)` -> 8
how: `backgroundColor:(i)=>gsap.utils.wrap(palette,i)` for per-letter colours (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: splitColor for colour maths
what: `splitColor('red')` -> [255,0,0]; with true -> HSL [0,100,50]
how: derive a tinted accent: lighten L in HSL then rebuild the hsl() string (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: utils.random is unseeded
what: `gsap.utils.random(min,max,snap,true)` returns a reusable random function, but it is not seeded; HyperFrames wants a seeded PRNG (mulberry32)
how: precompute scatter positions with a seeded PRNG into an array, then `x:(i)=>table[i].x`

name: Tween CSS variables
what: GSAP animates CSS custom properties (a colour var went to rgba(128,0,128,1) at half way)
how: `tl.to(root,{'--accent':'#ffcc00',duration:0.4},t)` so every element using var(--accent) changes together (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Split only what you animate
what: SplitText.create(target,{type}) returns `.lines`, `.words`, `.chars`; the default type splits all three, which costs more nodes
how: `const s = SplitText.create('#title',{type:'words'})` for word animation; check what you got with `s.lines.length`, `s.words.length`, `s.chars.length` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: mask:'lines' for clean rise-in reveals
what: mask wraps each line (or word/char) in an extra element with `overflow: clip`, exposed as `split.masks`, classes get `-mask` appended
how: `const s=SplitText.create('#t',{type:'lines,words',mask:'lines'}); tl.from(s.lines,{yPercent:100,duration:0.6,ease:'expo.out',stagger:0.12},0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Masked lines can clip descenders
what: with line-height 1.05 at 96 px, `hyperframes check` reported `text_box_overflow`: the split words extend ~9 px below their masked line box, and the mask clips whatever sits outside it
how: give split headlines `line-height: 1.15` or more (or a little padding-bottom) before masking; re-run `npx hyperframes check --json` and look for `text_box_overflow` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Only one mask type
what: mask can be 'lines', 'words' or 'chars', not a combination
how: for char reveals inside word masks use two SplitText passes or mask the words and animate chars

name: Auto-numbered classes with ++
what: `charsClass:'char++'` gives `char char3` on the third char; same for wordsClass/linesClass
how: target one letter in CSS/GSAP: `.char3{color:var(--accent)}` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: propIndex writes CSS index variables
what: `propIndex:true` puts `--word: 3` (etc.) on each piece, usable for CSS calc() offsets
how: `.word{transform:translateY(calc(var(--word)*4px))}` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Default wrappers are inline-block divs
what: SplitText wraps pieces in `div` with `display:inline-block` (transforms work); `tag:'span'` makes plain inline spans where rotation/scale do not render
how: keep the default tag when you rotate or scale letters; HyperFrames notes transforms on `<span>` need inline-block (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Built-in aria
what: by default the split element gets `aria-label` with its text and every piece `aria-hidden=true`
how: keep `aria:'auto'`; use `aria:'hidden'` or `'none'` only with a screen-reader duplicate (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Split after fonts load
what: splitting before web fonts load misplaces lines; either wait for `document.fonts.ready` or use `autoSplit:true` with animations created in `onSplit()`
how: in HyperFrames build inside `document.fonts.ready.then(()=>{ ...split...; window.__timelines['main']=tl; })` — registering at the end of the async build is allowed

name: onSplit returns the animation
what: with autoSplit, return the tween from onSplit so SplitText reverts it and restores its totalTime on each re-split
how: `SplitText.create(el,{type:'lines',autoSplit:true,onSplit:s=>gsap.from(s.lines,{yPercent:100,stagger:0.1})})`

name: Kerning shift fix
what: putting each character in its own element can lose kerning so letters shift; fix with CSS
how: `font-kerning:none; text-rendering:optimizeSpeed;` on the split element

name: smartWrap for chars-only splits
what: splitting chars alone can break words across lines; `smartWrap:true` wraps words in nowrap spans
how: `SplitText.create(el,{type:'chars',smartWrap:true})`

name: Custom word delimiter
what: `wordDelimiter` splits on another character (e.g. zero-width joiner) or a RegExp with `{delimiter, replaceWith}`; a hashtag with ZWJ split into 3 words
how: `SplitText.create(el,{type:'words',wordDelimiter:String.fromCharCode(8205)})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: revert() restores the original HTML
what: `split.revert()` returns innerHTML exactly to the original (verified equal)
how: revert after a reveal finishes if many nodes slow the render (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Avoid text-wrap: balance on split text
what: text-wrap: balance interferes with splitting; SplitText does not work on SVG `<text>`
how: remove `text-wrap:balance` from elements you split

name: 3D line flip-up
what: the SplitText docs demo flips lines up in 3D: rotationX -100, transformOrigin '50% 50% -160px', opacity 0, stagger 0.25 with a perspective on the parent
how: `gsap.set(el,{perspective:500}); tl.from(s.lines,{rotationX:-100,transformOrigin:'50% 50% -160px',opacity:0,duration:0.8,ease:'power3',stagger:0.25})`

name: Chars fly in from the side
what: docs demo: chars from x:150, opacity 0, duration 0.7, ease 'power4', stagger 0.04
how: `tl.from(s.chars,{x:150,opacity:0,duration:0.7,ease:'power4',stagger:0.04},t)`

name: Words drop with random rotation
what: docs demo: words from y:-100, opacity 0, rotation 'random(-80,80)', ease 'back', stagger 0.15 — but 'random()' strings are unseeded
how: replace `'random(-80,80)'` with a seeded table `rotation:(i)=>rot[i]`

name: TextPlugin typewriter
what: `text:'...'` replaces an element's text one character at a time over the tween; rewinding restores the old text (at 50% of 'ABCDEFGHIJ' it showed 'ABCDE')
how: `tl.to('#line',{text:'Season two starts Friday',duration:1.6,ease:'none'},t)` — use `ease:'none'` for an even typing rate (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Word-by-word typing
what: `text:{value, delimiter:' '}` reveals whole words (50% of 4 words showed 'one two')
how: `tl.to(el,{text:{value:'one two three four',delimiter:' '},duration:1,ease:'none'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Typing speed instead of duration
what: `speed` (1 slow ... 20 fast) sets duration from the number of changes: 0.05/speed*changes (10 chars at speed 1 = 0.5 s)
how: `text:{value:str, speed:4}` so long and short lines type at the same rate (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Type from the right
what: `rtl:true` introduces text right-to-left (30% of 'ABCDEFGHIJ' showed 'HIJ')
how: use for right-aligned numbers or RTL layouts (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Only animate what changed
what: `type:'diff'` skips identical characters between old and new strings, so an edit types only the changed part
how: `tl.to(el,{text:{value:'Price: $49',type:'diff'},duration:0.5})` when only the end changes

name: Style old and new text differently
what: `newClass`/`oldClass` wrap the incoming/outgoing text in spans with those classes
how: `text:{value:'Saved',newClass:'accent',oldClass:'muted'}`

name: Keep width while replacing
what: `padSpace:true` pads with non-breaking spaces when new text is shorter so the line doesn't collapse; `preserveSpaces:true` keeps extra spaces
how: `text:{value:'OK',padSpace:true}`

name: Blinking caret with steps
what: a caret that blinks hard on/off is an opacity yoyo with `steps(1)`, count kept finite
how: `tl.to('#caret',{opacity:0,duration:0.5,ease:'steps(1)',repeat:5,yoyo:true},t)`

name: ScrambleText decode reveal
what: `scrambleText:{text, chars, revealDelay, speed}` shows random characters then resolves left to right (50% showed 'HELLO WOXXX' with chars 'XO')
how: `tl.to('#code',{scrambleText:{text:'SEASON 02',chars:'01',revealDelay:0.3},duration:1.2,ease:'none'},0.3)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Scramble character sets
what: chars can be 'upperCase' (default), 'lowerCase', 'upperAndLowerCase' or any custom string like '0123456789' or 'XO'
how: digits-only scramble for a price or score: `chars:'0123456789'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hold the scramble before revealing
what: `revealDelay` keeps the text fully scrambled for that many seconds first
how: `scrambleText:{text:'123456',chars:'0123456789',revealDelay:0.5}` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Scramble refresh speed and direction
what: `speed` (default 1, lower = slower changes), `rightToLeft:true`, `delimiter:' '` for word-by-word, `tweenLength` (default true) grows/shrinks length gradually
how: `scrambleText:{text:t, speed:0.3, rightToLeft:true}`

name: DrawSVG stroke reveal
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `drawSVG` animates the visible stroke segment via stroke-dasharray/dashoffset on path, line, polyline, polygon, rect, ellipse; it needs a stroke set, and never touches fill
how: `tl.fromTo('#line',{drawSVG:'0%'},{drawSVG:'100%',duration:1.2,ease:'power2.inOut'},t)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Draw from the middle outward
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: drawSVG describes the visible segment: from '50% 50%' to '0% 100%' grows from the centre both ways
how: `tl.fromTo(path,{drawSVG:'50% 50%'},{drawSVG:'0% 100%',duration:1})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Travelling dash
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: keep the segment size and move it: '0 5%' -> '95% 100%'
how: `tl.fromTo(path,{drawSVG:'0 5%'},{drawSVG:'95% 100%',duration:1.5,ease:'none'})` for a comet on a route

name: Staggered multi-stroke draw
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: draw many strokes in sequence with a stagger
how: `tl.from('.draw-me',{drawSVG:0,duration:1,stagger:0.1},t)` for a line-art logo

name: Split multi-segment paths before drawing
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: a path with several M commands draws badly; GSAP's helper splits it into one path per segment, then time each by its length for even speed
how: use the docs helper with `MotionPathPlugin.getRawPath()`; duration per segment = total * len/totalLength

name: Measure stroke length
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `DrawSVGPlugin.getLength(el)` returns the stroke length (a test arc measured 420.4)
how: base durations on length so strokes draw at one speed (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hand-made draw-on without plugins
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: registry items draw strokes with a getTotalLength dash: set dasharray and dashoffset to the measured length and tween dashoffset to 0 (never the pathLength attribute, never non-scaling-stroke on a dashed path)
how: `const L=p.getTotalLength(); gsap.set(p,{strokeDasharray:L,strokeDashoffset:L}); tl.fromTo(p,{strokeDashoffset:L},{strokeDashoffset:0,duration:0.6},t)`
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/marker-highlight.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add marker-highlight`, checked 2026-10-24
repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/titlecard-lockup.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add titlecard-lockup`, checked 2026-10-24

name: MorphSVG between unlike shapes
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: morphSVG animates a path's d to another shape even when point counts differ, converting to cubic beziers and adding points as needed; the original is stored in `data-original`
how: `tl.to('#shape',{morphSVG:'#star',duration:0.8,ease:'power3.inOut'},t)`; morph back with `morphSVG:'#shape'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Convert primitives before morphing
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `MorphSVGPlugin.convertToPath('circle, rect, ellipse, line, polygon, polyline')` swaps each in place for an identical path keeping its id
how: call once at build time, then morph the new paths (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix twisting morphs with shapeIndex
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: shapeIndex offsets which start point maps to the end shape's first point (negative reverses); `findShapeIndex()` previews options during development
how: `morphSVG:{shape:'#b', shapeIndex:3}` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rotational morph type
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `type:'rotational'` interpolates angle and length of points instead of x/y, often more natural and kink-free; adjust `origin` ('50% 50%' default)
how: `morphSVG:{shape:'#b', type:'rotational', origin:'20% 60%'}` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Segment matching with map
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: for multi-segment paths, `map:'size'` (default), `'position'` or `'complexity'` decides which pieces pair up; if none works, split into separate paths
how: `morphSVG:{shape:'#b', map:'position'}`

name: smooth and curveMode for cleaner morphs
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `smooth: 80|'auto'|{points,redraw,persist}` adds evenly spaced anchors; `curveMode:true` interpolates handle angle/length to avoid mid-morph kinks
how: `morphSVG:{shape:'#b', smooth:{points:'auto', redraw:false}}`

name: Icon state morph without the plugin
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: if both paths have the same command structure and point count, GSAP can tween `d` directly (registry icon-morph-beat does this for mic->check, play->check, lock->unlock)
how: `npx hyperframes add icon-morph-beat` or `tl.to(path,{attr:{d:endD},duration:0.4})` with matched paths (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/icon-morph-beat.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add icon-morph-beat`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Follow an SVG path
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `motionPath:{path:'#route', align:'#route', alignOrigin:[0.5,0.5], autoRotate:true}` moves the element exactly on the path regardless of nested transforms and turns it along the tangent
how: `tl.to('#dot',{motionPath:{path:'#line',align:'#line',alignOrigin:[0.5,0.5],autoRotate:true},duration:1.5,ease:'power1.inOut'},t)`; check flagged a `rotation_pivot_drift` warning for the moving dot — expected for a path follower (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Curve through points
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: an array of {x,y} plots a smooth curve through them (current position added at the start); `curviness` 0 = straight, 1 default, 2 curvier; `type:'cubic'` reads anchor/control/control/anchor
how: `motionPath:{path:[{x:100,y:50},{x:200,y:0},{x:300,y:100}],autoRotate:true}` (ended at 300,100); add `curviness:2` for rounder bends (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Travel only part of a path
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `start`/`end` (0-1, can be negative or above 1 to wrap; end<start goes backwards)
how: `motionPath:{path:'#p',start:0,end:0.5}` (stopped at the arc's apex) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: autoRotate offset
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: autoRotate can be a number of degrees added to the path angle (autoRotate:90 adds 90 degrees)
how: `autoRotate:90`

name: Smooth any property list
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: motionPath with objects of other props (e.g. scale, rotation) smooths velocity through those values
how: `motionPath:{path:[{scale:1.3},{scale:0.2},{scale:1}],curviness:2}`

name: Sample a point on a path
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `getRawPath` + `cacheRawPathMeasurements` + `getPositionOnPath(raw,progress,true)` gives x,y,angle at any progress — useful in a seek-driven onUpdate (apex of the test arc: 200,25, angle 0)
how: `const rp=MotionPathPlugin.getRawPath('#p'); MotionPathPlugin.cacheRawPathMeasurements(rp); const pt=MotionPathPlugin.getPositionOnPath(rp,p,true)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Path following without a plugin
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: registry offset-path-traveler tweens one progress value and samples the SVG path for position and tangent in onUpdate, so seeks are exact
how: `npx hyperframes add offset-path-traveler`; its `path` variable takes SVG data in a 1000x500 viewBox (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/offset-path-traveler.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add offset-path-traveler`, checked 2026-10-24

name: CSS offset-path
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: offset-path (with offset-distance, offset-rotate, offset-anchor) moves an element along a path(), basic shape, ray() or url(#svgShape); offset-rotate defaults to auto (faces path direction), 'reverse' = auto 180deg
how: `#chip{offset-path:path('M0,100 C200,0 400,200 600,100');offset-rotate:auto}` then `tl.fromTo('#chip',{offsetDistance:'0%'},{offsetDistance:'100%',duration:2})`

name: svgOrigin for shared pivots
section: SVG: draw-on, morph and motion paths
what: `svgOrigin:'250 100'` rotates SVG elements around a point in the SVG's global coordinates (recorded in data-svg-origin); use either svgOrigin or transformOrigin
how: `tl.to('.spoke',{rotation:360,svgOrigin:'300 200',duration:2,ease:'none'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: clip-path inset wipe
what: GSAP tweens clip-path strings: inset(0% 100% 0% 0%) -> inset(0% 0% 0% 0%) wipes in from the left (50% showed inset(0% 50% 0% 0%))
how: `tl.fromTo(title,{clipPath:'inset(0% 100% 0% 0%)'},{clipPath:'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)',duration:0.6,ease:'power3.out'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: clip-path circle iris
what: circle(0% at x y) -> circle(75% at x y) opens an iris (half way = 37.5%)
how: `tl.fromTo(next,{clipPath:'circle(0% at 50% 50%)'},{clipPath:'circle(75% at 50% 50%)',duration:0.15})` — HyperFrames 'iris from the click' (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mask/crop on an inner wrapper
what: HyperFrames: crop or mask reveals tween clip-path or a mask on an inner wrapper so media source time is untouched
how: wrap the `<video>` in a div and tween the div's clipPath

name: mask-image gradient reveal
what: mask-image takes images incl. CSS gradients; mode is alpha by default; local file:// mask images render transparent black (use gradients or served files)
how: `.reveal{mask-image:linear-gradient(90deg,#000 var(--p),transparent calc(var(--p) + 10%))}` and tween `--p` from '0%' to '100%'

name: Video or gradient inside letters
what: background-clip:text paints the background only where text is; keep contrast readable
how: `h1{background:linear-gradient(90deg,#ff5a36,#ffcc00);background-clip:text;-webkit-background-clip:text;color:transparent}` then tween backgroundPosition

name: Animated gradient position
what: GSAP tweens backgroundPosition strings (0%->100% was 50% at half)
how: `tl.fromTo(h1,{backgroundPosition:'0% 50%'},{backgroundPosition:'100% 50%',duration:2,ease:'none'})` with `background-size:200% 100%` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Outline text
what: -webkit-text-stroke sets stroke width and colour of glyphs
how: `.outline{color:transparent;-webkit-text-stroke:3px #fff}` for a hollow title, fill it later by tweening `color`

name: Blur-in titles
what: GSAP tweens filter strings (blur 8px->0 was blur(4px) at half); HyperFrames per-word recipe: blur(6px)->0 with opacity 0->1 in 0.13 s, words 0.067 s apart
how: `tl.fromTo(s.words,{filter:'blur(6px)',opacity:0},{filter:'blur(0px)',opacity:1,duration:0.13,stagger:0.067},t)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Variable-font axis animation
what: font-variation-settings takes 4-letter axes ('wght','wdth','slnt'...) and overrides font-weight; GSAP interpolated "wght" 100->900 to 500 at half
how: load a variable font, then `tl.fromTo(el,{fontVariationSettings:"'wght' 200"},{fontVariationSettings:"'wght' 900",duration:1.4})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: transformPerspective per element
what: `transformPerspective:500` puts perspective() inside that element's transform (output `perspective(500px) rotateX(45deg)`); lower = stronger distortion, ~200-1000 typical
how: `gsap.set(card,{transformPerspective:600}); tl.from(card,{rotationY:-70,duration:0.8})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shared perspective on the parent
what: set `perspective` on the container so children share one vanishing point
how: `gsap.set('#stage',{perspective:900})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: perspective-origin moves the vanishing point
what: perspective-origin on the parent sets where the viewer looks; perspective applies to children, unlike the perspective() function on the element itself
how: `#stage{perspective:900px;perspective-origin:50% 20%}`

name: Things behind the viewer are not drawn
what: parts with z greater than the perspective distance are not drawn; perspective creates a stacking context
how: keep z moves smaller than the perspective value

name: preserve-3d on every non-leaf level
what: transform-style is not inherited, so each nested container needs preserve-3d; some properties (e.g. paint containment) force flattening
how: `.scene,.group{transform-style:preserve-3d}`; also keep mix-blend-mode/opacity<1/filter off preserve-3d containers

name: backface-visibility for card flips
what: backface-visibility:hidden hides an element when turned away (3D only)
how: two faces, back `rotateY(180deg)`, both `backface-visibility:hidden`; tween the parent `rotationY:180`

name: 3D transform origin behind the element
what: transformOrigin accepts a third (z) value, e.g. rotate around a point 400px back
how: `gsap.set(word,{transformOrigin:'50% 50% -400'})` then rotationY for an orbiting word

name: GSAP transform order
what: GSAP always applies translation, then scale, rotationX, rotationY, skew, rotation, whatever order you write them
how: write `{x,scale,rotation}` freely; use shorthand props, not transform strings

name: Directional rotation suffixes
what: `_short`, `_cw`, `_ccw` pick the rotation direction (170 -> '-170_short' passed through 180, i.e. the 20-degree way)
how: `rotation:'-170_short'` for dials and needles (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: autoAlpha instead of opacity
what: autoAlpha sets visibility:hidden at 0 and inherit otherwise
how: `tl.to(inner,{autoAlpha:0})` on an inner element, never on a `.clip` element (HyperFrames lists visibility tweened on a .clip as a cause of blank scenes) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: clearProps after a move
what: clearProps removes inline props at the end; clearing any transform part clears the whole transform
how: `tl.set(el,{clearProps:'transform'})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Physics2D throws and arcs
what: `physics2D:{velocity, angle, gravity|acceleration+accelerationAngle, friction}` computes x/y from time (300 px/s at -60 deg, gravity 400 over 1 s ended at 150,-59.8); eases are ignored; it reversed exactly on re-seek
how: `tl.to(chip,{physics2D:{velocity:600,angle:-70,gravity:900},duration:1.2},t)` for confetti/sparks with seeded per-item velocity/angle tables (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Friction for drifting stops
what: friction 0-1 slows the object (start ~0.02)
how: `physics2D:{velocity:400,angle:-30,friction:0.08}`

name: PhysicsProps for any number
what: physicsProps gives any property its own velocity/acceleration/friction (a:{velocity:100,acceleration:-50} for 2 s ended at 100)
how: `tl.to(o,{physicsProps:{rot:{velocity:720,friction:0.1}},duration:2,onUpdate:()=>gsap.set(el,{rotation:o.rot})})` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Simulate once, look up by time
what: HyperFrames 3D/generative rule: simulate particles/physics once at load into arrays, then read state at t; seed every random choice
how: build a table `pos[frame][i]` then draw from `e.detail.time` in the hf-seek listener

name: Centre text with text_w/text_h
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: x and y are expressions; text_w/text_h are the rendered text size
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Title':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Ticker crawl right-to-left
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: x as a function of t scrolls a line; the docs example puts it on the last row with y=h-line_h
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='BREAKING NEWS':fontsize=40:fontcolor=white:y=h-line_h-10:x=w-150*t" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Credits roll from a text file
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: textfile + y=h-speed*t scrolls a block upward; line_spacing adds pixels between lines; textfile avoids escaping trouble
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:textfile=credits.txt:fontsize=30:fontcolor=white:line_spacing=12:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=h-60*t" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Eased rise-in with pow()
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: write the ease into the y expression: cubic ease-out over 0.6 s from 80 px below
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Rise':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2+80*pow(1-min(t/0.6\,1)\,3)" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Eased slide-in from off-screen
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: an if() on t switches from the eased move to the resting position
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Slide in':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:y=(h-text_h)/2:x='if(lt(t\,0.8)\,-text_w+(w/2+text_w/2)*(1-pow(1-t/0.8\,3))\,(w-text_w)/2)'" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fade text with the alpha expression
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: alpha takes an expression 0-1 (default 1)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Fade':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40:alpha='min(t/0.5\,1)'" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fade in and out in one expression
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: nest if() to ramp up, hold, ramp down
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='InOut':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40:alpha='if(lt(t\,0.5)\,t/0.5\,if(gt(t\,2.5)\,(3-t)/0.5\,1))'" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Show text in a time window
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: timeline `enable` limits when the filter draws
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Window':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40:enable='between(t\,1\,2)'" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Blink text
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: the docs pattern enable=lt(mod(t,3),1) shows 1 s of every 3; here 0.5 of every 1 s
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='blink':fontsize=40:fontcolor=white:x=100:y=100:enable=lt(mod(t\,1)\,0.5)" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Number count-up with eif
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: %{eif:expr:d} prints an expression as an integer; clamp with min() so it stops at the target
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='%{eif\:min(t*400\,1000)\:d}':fontsize=80:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Zero-padded counter
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: the third eif argument pads with zeros to that many places
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='%{eif\:t*10\:d\:4}':fontsize=80:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Running timecode
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: %{pts:hms} prints HH:MM:SS.mmm of each frame; %{n} prints the frame number
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='%{pts\:hms}':fontsize=40:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Outline and drop shadow on drawtext
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: borderw/bordercolor draw an outline; shadowx/shadowy/shadowcolor add an offset shadow
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Outline':fontsize=70:fontcolor=white:borderw=4:bordercolor=black:shadowx=4:shadowy=4:shadowcolor=black@0.6:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Box padding per side
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: boxborderw takes 1-4 values separated by | (top|right|bottom|left like CSS)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Boxed':fontsize=50:fontcolor=white:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.6:boxborderw=10|40:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fixed box size with aligned text
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: boxw/boxh set the box size and text_align places text inside it; on our ffmpeg 6.1 build 'MC' failed but 'M+C' and 'middle+center' worked
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Align':fontsize=50:fontcolor=white:box=1:boxw=400:boxh=100:text_align=M+C:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Baseline alignment of separate texts
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: y_align=baseline puts the first line's baseline at y; the older trick is y=Y+fontsize-max_glyph_a
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='DOG':fontsize=24:fontcolor=white:x=10:y=20+24-max_glyph_a,drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='cow':fontsize=24:fontcolor=white:x=80:y=20+24-max_glyph_a" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Animated font size
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: fontsize accepts an expression, e.g. a 1 s zoom from 20 to 60
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Zoom':fontsize='20+40*min(t\,1)':fontcolor=white:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Colour fade with fontcolor_expr
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: fontcolor_expr is expanded like text, so %{eif:...:x:2} can write the hex alpha byte
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text=Pulse:fontsize=60:fontcolor_expr='ffcc00%{eif\:clip(255*t/2\,0\,255)\:x\:2}':x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Change text mid-clip with sendcmd
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: drawtext accepts `reinit` (and x, y, alpha, fontsize, colours, box...) as commands at given times
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "sendcmd=c='1.0 drawtext reinit fontsize=80\:fontcolor=yellow',drawtext=fontfile=...:text='Cmd':fontsize=40:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Typewriter by chained drawtext enables
section: Kinetic text straight in ffmpeg (drawtext expressions)
what: drawtext has no substring function, so stack one drawtext per growing prefix, each with enable=gte(t,start) (tested with two steps; generate the chain with a script for long lines)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='T':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40:enable=gte(t\,0.2),drawtext=fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf:text='Ty':fontsize=60:fontcolor=white:x=40:y=40:enable=gte(t\,0.4)" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Search the registry before hand-building
what: about 450 blocks and components are installable as editable source; the catalog search is local and English-indexed
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "kinetic type" --json`, `--type component`, `--tag typography`; then `npx hyperframes add <name> --json` (178 text/data/motion items installed cleanly here) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Component vs block wiring
what: a component installs to compositions/components/<name>.html and is merged into your scene (markup, style, script, timeline calls); a block installs to compositions/<name>.html and is mounted with data-composition-src
how: read the item's header comment first, then copy its parts; run `npx hyperframes lint` after wiring (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Variables instead of edits
what: registry items read `data-composition-variables`, fall back to defaults on bad values, and can be set per mount
how: `npx hyperframes add count-up --vars '{"end":2500,"suffix":""}'` writes `data-variable-values` on the host

name: IN / HOLD / OUT envelopes
what: registry primitives use fixed IN and OUT phases with an elastic HOLD and are never time-scaled; if the mount is shorter, IN and OUT compress together
how: size the mount's `data-duration` to at least IN_BASE+OUT_BASE from the header so the move isn't compressed

how: `npx hyperframes add particle-text-dissolve --json`; set `text`, `direction` in|out, `density` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/particle-text-dissolve.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add particle-text-dissolve`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Registry `particle-image-reveal`
what: seeded particles converge while an image reveals beneath (ltr wipe or centre iris); image via `<template data-slot="particle-image-reveal-image">`
how: `npx hyperframes add particle-image-reveal --json` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/particle-image-reveal.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add particle-image-reveal`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Registry `parallax-zoom`
what: centre card scales up to fill the frame while siblings parallax outward; drive --pz-progress 0 -> 1 (defaults focus scale 6, push 900px)
how: `npx hyperframes add parallax-zoom --json` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/parallax-zoom.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add parallax-zoom`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Registry `parallax-unzoom`
what: reverse of parallax-zoom: focus card shrinks from full frame as siblings parallax in to form a grid; drive --pu-progress
how: `npx hyperframes add parallax-unzoom --json` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/parallax-unzoom.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add parallax-unzoom`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Registry `spring-pop`
what: badge pops from scale 0.9 past full size with back.out(overshoot, default 1.7) and settles at 1 in 0.6 s
how: `npx hyperframes add spring-pop --json` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/spring-pop.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add spring-pop`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Registry `stagger-cascade`
what: grid of tiles fades and travels into place with one evenly spaced stagger (20-150 ms, default 60); exit uses power2.in
how: `npx hyperframes add stagger-cascade --json` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo registry: header comment of `compositions/components/stagger-cascade.html` installed by `npx hyperframes add stagger-cascade`, checked 2026-10-24

name: Land titles dead still
what: a landed title doesn't keep sliding or scaling; motion moves to the next element, the camera or the world
how: end every title tween with a plain hold; if a client says 'the titles move', remove drift

name: Vary title entrances within a film
what: HyperFrames lists per-word blur-in, grey-to-ink per word, whole-line blur, per-letter for a name, title behind the subject and a slot-machine word roll — never fade+slide-up on every title
how: rotate entrances: blur-in for line 1, `kinetic-type-swap` for line 2, `per-word-rise` for line 3

name: Hold time per line
what: a line to be read holds about 0.5 s + 0.3 s per word; the film's last line at least 2 s; then exit with a 0.13-0.25 s blur-out/fade
how: for 6 words hold ~2.3 s before the exit tween

name: Exits shorter than entrances
what: exits are 40-50% shorter than entrances; the next element starts when the previous is 30-50% done
how: entrance 0.6 s -> exit 0.3 s; next tween at `'<40%'`

name: Client says 'too fast' or 'feels like slides'
what: HyperFrames fixes: 'too fast' -> slow every zoom and pan to 0.7x of its speed, nothing else; 'feels like slides' -> enter the next scene through an object on screen and cut a move mid-flight
how: multiply only camera/zoom tween durations by 1/0.7; for slide-feel use `text-match-cut` or a zoom-through

name: Fit text to a width in HyperFrames (fitTextFontSize)
what: `window.__hyperframes.fitTextFontSize(text,{fontFamily,fontWeight,maxWidth})` returns a fontSize that fits
how: call it once in the build before splitting the text

name: Assert motion with a sidecar
what: a `<name>.motion.json` makes `check` verify appearsBy, before, staysInFrame and keepsMoving on the seeked timeline
how: `{"assertions":[{"kind":"appearsBy","selector":"#headline","bySec":0.5}]}` then `npx hyperframes check --json`

name: Inspect a move's curve
what: `npx hyperframes keyframes --json --selector '#id'` lists property, time, value, ease; `--shot motion.png` draws samples along the path
how: run it on a title after writing its tweens

name: Opt-in motion blur for fast type
what: `data-motion-blur="on"` on the root smears fast 2D movers in preview and render (~1.7x render time); off with WebGL, backface flips or root opacity
how: add the attribute, then `npx hyperframes check` and look for `motion_blur_off`

name: Beat-grid timing for kinetic type
what: frames per beat = fps*60/BPM; compute each beat from its index and round, never add a rounded beat repeatedly (drift)
how: `const t=i=>Math.round(i*30*60/bpm)/30` for word hit times

name: SRT to WebVTT in one command
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: ffmpeg picks the WebVTT muxer from the `.vtt` extension and writes the `WEBVTT` header, keeping `<i>`/`<b>`
how: `ffmpeg -i s.srt s.vtt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: WebVTT back to SRT
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: the reverse conversion works the same way when a platform wants SRT
how: `ffmpeg -i s.vtt s.srt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SRT to ASS keeps basic markup
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: on conversion ffmpeg turned `<i>` into `{\i1}`, `<b>` into `{\b1}`, `<font color="#ff0000">` into `{\c&HFF&}` (ASS colours are BGR) and kept an inline `{\an8}`
how: `ffmpeg -i s.srt s.ass`, then style the `.ass` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Aegisub manual: ASS Override Tags, https://aegisub.org/docs/latest/ass_tags/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Fix the header ffmpeg writes into a converted ASS
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: ffmpeg's generated ASS had `PlayResX: 384`, `PlayResY: 288`, `Fontsize 16` and no LayoutRes; the libass guide says new files should set PlayRes and LayoutRes to the video's display size
how: after `ffmpeg -i in.srt out.ass`, edit `[Script Info]` to `PlayResX: 1920` `PlayResY: 1080` `LayoutResX: 1920` `LayoutResY: 1080` and scale Fontsize to match (tested here 2026-10-24, header observed)
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: ASS back to SRT
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: ffmpeg converts `\i1`/`\b1`/`\c` back to `<i>`/`<b>`/`<font color>`, but a position tag like `{\an8}` stays in the text as a brace block
how: `ffmpeg -i s.ass s.srt` and check the result for leftover `{...}` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LRC lyrics file from an SRT
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: ffmpeg's LRC muxer takes a subrip/text stream and writes `[mm:ss.xx]` lines, but it copied `<i>`/`<font>` tags into the LRC, so strip markup first; 6.1.1 has no `precision` option (the current docs list one for newer builds)
how: `ffmpeg -i lyrics.srt lyrics.lrc` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: TTML/DFXP from an SRT
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: ffmpeg 6.1 has a TTML muxer/encoder; its output sets `ttp:cellResolution="384 288"` and a bottom `Default` region in Arial
how: `ffmpeg -i s.srt s.ttml` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube SBV to SRT
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: YouTube's SubViewer `.sbv` uses `0:00:00.500,0:00:01.500` times with no counter; ffmpeg reads it when the subviewer demuxer is forced
how: `ffmpeg -f subviewer -i captions.sbv captions.srt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Don't try to make SCC from SRT in ffmpeg
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: the SCC format only carries EIA-608 data; ffmpeg 6.1.1 refused `-i s.srt s.scc` ("Output file does not contain any stream")
how: deliver SRT/VTT instead, or use a dedicated 608 tool (needs a 608 encoder (missing)) (tested here 2026-10-24, failure confirmed)

name: YouTube's basic formats are plain
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: for SRT and SBV YouTube supports only basic files: no style markup is recognised and the file must be plain UTF-8
how: for YouTube uploads export SRT with `pysubs2 --clean` (removes styling) and save UTF-8 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube advanced formats
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: YouTube's WebVTT support handles positioning but only `<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>` styling; TTML is partial (iTT supported), SAMI/RealText take simple markup without positioning, and SCC is the preferred broadcast format
how: if a YouTube caption must sit at the top, upload a `.vtt` with a `line:0` cue setting rather than an SRT

name: A UTF-8 BOM doesn't break ffmpeg
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: an SRT starting with the BOM bytes `EF BB BF` converted cleanly
how: `ffmpeg -i bom.srt bom.vtt` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide (BOM advice for ASS), https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Read a sloppy SRT
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: an SRT with no cue numbers and `.` instead of `,` before the milliseconds parsed when the format was forced, and was written back as a clean numbered SRT
how: `ffmpeg -f srt -i loose.srt clean.srt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Legacy Arabic/Urdu code page to UTF-8
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: `sub_charenc` sets the input subtitle character encoding; a Windows-1256 SRT came out byte-identical to the UTF-8 original (apart from a final newline)
how: `ffmpeg -sub_charenc CP1256 -i old.srt fixed.srt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Burn a legacy-encoded file without converting
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: the `subtitles` filter's `charenc` option; the CP1256 burn was pixel-identical (same md5) to the UTF-8 burn
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "subtitles=old.srt:charenc=CP1256" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shift a whole subtitle file with -itsoffset
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: the offset is added to the input timestamps; a cue at 0.500 s became 2.000 s with `-itsoffset 1.5` and no re-typing
how: `ffmpeg -itsoffset 1.5 -i s.srt -c copy shifted.srt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ffmpeg loses every cue after a WebVTT STYLE block
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: a `.vtt` with a `STYLE` block produced an empty output in ffmpeg 6.1.1, while the same file loaded fully in pysubs2; a `NOTE` block alone was fine
how: convert styled VTT with `python3 -m pysubs2 --to srt in.vtt` instead of ffmpeg (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ffmpeg drops WebVTT cue settings
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: `line:0 position:20% align:start` disappeared on a VTT to VTT copy and on VTT to ASS; `<v Bob>` and `<c.loud>` tags were stripped to plain text
how: keep positioned VTT as the master file; to burn it, re-create the position as `{\an7\pos(x,y)}` in ASS (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: List the subtitle tracks in a file
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: ffprobe can print each subtitle stream's index, codec and language tag
how: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams s -show_entries stream=index,codec_name:stream_tags=language -of csv=p=0 in.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Extract one subtitle track
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: map the subtitle stream by type index and give an `.srt` name
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0:s:1 urdu.srt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Drop all subtitle tracks
section: Formats: convert and repair caption files
what: `-sn` as an output option disables subtitle mapping, so a client copy carries no stray tracks
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0 -sn -c copy clean.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: pysubs2 basics
what: pure-Python, MIT library that reads SRT, ASS/SSA, MicroDVD, MPL2, TMP, WebVTT, TTML and SAMI into an ASS-based model; times are int milliseconds
how: `pip install --target <scratch>/pylib pysubs2` then `subs = pysubs2.load("s.srt"); subs.save("s.ass")` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Retime by a constant
what: `SSAFile.shift()` takes h/m/s/ms or frames+fps; negative times are treated as zero on export
how: `subs.shift(s=1.5)` moved 0.5 s to 2.0 s (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix subs made for another frame rate
what: `transform_framerate(in_fps, out_fps)` rescales all times
how: `subs.transform_framerate(25, 23.976)` moved 500 ms to 521 ms (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Times from frames
what: `pysubs2.make_time(frames=50, fps=25)` returns 2000 ms; `pysubs2.time.ms_to_frames(1000, 30)` returns 30
how: use these in timing scripts instead of hand maths (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Text without tags
what: `SSAEvent.plaintext` hides override tags and turns `\N` into newlines (writing to it throws tags away)
how: `[e.plaintext for e in subs]` gave `Hello world, this is line one` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One model, many outputs
what: `to_string()`/`save()` write vtt, ass, json, tmp, mpl2, ttml and (with `fps=`) microdvd from the same object
how: `subs.to_string("ttml")` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pass unknown encodings through untouched
what: `errors="surrogateescape"` lets you retime or convert a non-UTF-8 file without knowing its encoding; a CP1256 file kept its exact Arabic bytes
how: `subs = pysubs2.load("old.srt", errors="surrogateescape"); subs.save("old_fixed.srt", errors="surrogateescape")` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sort events by time
what: `SSAFile.sort()` orders events chronologically (events compare by time)
how: after appending cues out of order, `subs.sort()` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Strip drawings and karaoke junk
what: `remove_miscellaneous_events()` removed a `{\p1}` drawing event (4 events to 3); the CLI `--clean` does the same and strips styling for non-SSA output
how: `python3 -m pysubs2 --to srt --clean in.ass` kept only the text line (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rename a style safely
what: `rename_style(old, new)` also fixes every event that points to it
how: `subs.rename_style("top", "English")` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Batch convert and shift from the shell
what: the pysubs2 CLI converts with `--to` and retimes with `--shift`/`--shift-back` ("1m30s", "0.5s"), writing to `-o DIR`
how: `python3 -m pysubs2 --to vtt *.srt -o out/` and `python3 -m pysubs2 --shift 0.5s s.srt -o shifted/` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bilingual subtitles, top and bottom
what: pysubs2's own example puts one language in a `BOTTOM_CENTER` style and the other in a `TOP_CENTER` style in one ASS file
how: load `ur.srt` and `en.srt`, set `subs.styles = {"bottom": SSAStyle(fontname="Noto Nastaliq Urdu", alignment=Alignment.BOTTOM_CENTER), "top": SSAStyle(alignment=Alignment.TOP_CENTER)}`, append events with `e.style`, `subs.save("bi.ass")` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Soft subs in MP4 must be mov_text
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: MP4 takes the 3GPP timed-text codec; add a language tag so players label the track
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -i s.srt -map 0 -map 1 -c copy -c:s mov_text -metadata:s:s:0 language=urd out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: What mov_text keeps
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: extracting back from MP4 kept `<i>` and `<b>` but lost the font colour and the `{\an8}` position
how: keep coloured/positioned captions as ASS (burn them) or MKV, not MP4 soft subs (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Two languages in one MKV, choose the default
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: set language per track and move the default flag; ffmpeg's own example clears `s:0` and sets `s:1` default
how: `ffmpeg -i v.mp4 -i en.srt -i ur.srt -map 0 -map 1 -map 2 -c copy -c:s srt -metadata:s:s:0 language=eng -metadata:s:s:1 language=urd -disposition:s:0 0 -disposition:s:1 default out.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Flag a forced-narrative track
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: forced subtitles carry only the on-screen-text/foreign-dialogue lines; mark the track `forced` and give it a title
how: `-disposition:s:0 forced -metadata:s:s:0 title="Forced narrative"` (ffprobe showed forced=1) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Attach the fonts inside the MKV
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: the libass guide says every font a script uses must exist and be attached to the release; Matroska needs a mimetype tag on the attachment
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0 -c copy -attach NotoNastaliqUrdu.ttf -metadata:s:t mimetype=application/x-truetype-font out.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Pull fonts out of someone's MKV
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: `-dump_attachment:t ""` writes every attachment under its stored filename
how: `ffmpeg -dump_attachment:t "" -i in.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Burn a track that lives inside the video file
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: the `subtitles` filter can read from a container; `si` picks the subtitle stream
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mkv -vf "subtitles=in.mkv:si=1:fontsdir=fonts" out.mp4` (also worked on an MP4's mov_text track) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: HLS with a WebVTT subtitle rendition
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: the HLS muxer can segment a text stream as WebVTT and add `#EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=SUBTITLES` to the master playlist; `language:` in the var_stream_map adds `LANGUAGE=`. In 6.1.1 the `sname:` key from the current docs was rejected
how: `ffmpeg -i v.mp4 -i s.srt -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 1 -c:v copy -c:a copy -c:s webvtt -f hls -hls_time 1 -var_stream_map "v:0,a:0,s:0,sgroup:subs,language:eng" -master_pl_name master.m3u8 h_%v.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Check HLS WebVTT segments for X-TIMESTAMP-MAP
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: Apple requires WebVTT segments to carry an X-TIMESTAMP-MAP header; ffmpeg 6.1.1's segments had none and a cue at 0.500 s was written as 0.567 s
how: `grep -L X-TIMESTAMP-MAP *.vtt` before delivering to Apple devices (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Apple: which caption formats
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: Apple devices take CEA-608/708 captions, WebVTT subtitles and IMSC1 (text profile) subtitles; subtitles must be WebVTT text files or IMSC1 in fMP4, and the subtitle playlist must cover the whole programme
how: for an HLS delivery pick WebVTT unless the client asks for IMSC1

name: Apple: mark SDH tracks
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: a subtitle track meant for deaf/hard-of-hearing viewers must have `CHARACTERISTICS="public.accessibility.transcribes-spoken-dialog,public.accessibility.describes-music-and-sound"`, `AUTOSELECT=YES` and a LANGUAGE attribute
how: edit the `#EXT-X-MEDIA` line of `master.m3u8` after ffmpeg writes it

name: Apple: forced plus full subs
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: if a language has forced and regular subtitles, the regular track must contain both; forced tracks should be AUTOSELECT=YES; and if a clean (no burnt text) version exists, forced subtitles should be used instead of burnt-in text
how: build the full track as forced lines + dialogue lines merged with `subs.sort()`

name: Apple: codec strings
section: Soft subtitle tracks in MP4, MKV and HLS
what: use `stpp.ttml.im1t` for IMSC1 subtitles; `wvtt` may be used for WebVTT in the CODECS attribute
how: add it to `#EXT-X-STREAM-INF` CODECS when the player needs it

name: Prefer the `ass` filter for burning ASS
what: it is the subtitles filter without the libavcodec/libavformat conversion, limited to ASS files, and it is the one that exposes `shaping` in ffmpeg 6.1.1 (`ffmpeg -h filter=subtitles` lists no shaping option)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "ass=caps.ass:fontsdir=library/fonts" -c:a copy out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: The `subtitles` filter broke Hindi and Urdu here
what: with ffmpeg 6.1.1, `subtitles=` rendered Devanagari with broken conjuncts (visible halant in नमस्ते, क्ष split) and Noto Nastaliq Urdu as empty boxes, even for an `.ass` input; the same text through `ass=` was correct
how: never burn Urdu/Hindi with `subtitles=`; convert first (next skill) (tested here 2026-10-24, frames inspected)

name: SRT in Urdu/Hindi: convert, then burn with `ass`
what: converting the SRT to ASS and rendering with the `ass` filter gave correct conjuncts
how: `ffmpeg -i h.srt h.ass` → set Fontname (e.g. Noto Sans Devanagari) and PlayRes → `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "ass=h.ass:fontsdir=fonts" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Force complex shaping for scripts that need it
what: `shaping=complex` uses OpenType substitution and positioning and is required for Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari and Thai; `simple` only substitutes. On the same Hindi line `simple` and `complex` produced different frames, and only `complex`/`auto` joined the conjuncts
how: `-vf "ass=hi.ass:fontsdir=fonts:shaping=complex"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Use repo fonts without installing them
what: `fontsdir` adds a folder of fonts to what the font provider already has
how: `-vf "ass=caps.ass:fontsdir=/home/user/new-startup/library/fonts"` rendered Kalam and Rozha One (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Prove which font file libass picked
what: at `-v verbose` the filter logs `fontselect: (Noto Nastaliq Urdu, 400, 0) -> NotoNastaliqUrdu-Regular`; a silent fallback font is the usual cause of tofu
how: `ffmpeg -v verbose -i in.mp4 -vf "ass=u.ass:fontsdir=fonts" -frames:v 1 -f null - 2>&1 | grep fontselect` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: original_size only matters when the aspect changes
what: the docs say it is needed to scale fonts correctly if the aspect ratio was changed; on a same-aspect 640x360 to 1280x720 burn it made no difference (identical frames)
how: `subtitles=s.srt:original_size=640x360` only after anamorphic or aspect changes (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Input seeking shifts burned subtitles
what: with `-ss 1` before `-i`, timestamps restart at 0 and the filter shows the wrong cues (a cue at 0.5-1.5 s vanished from the first second). Shift the clock for the filter and back
how: `ffmpeg -ss 1 -i in.mp4 -vf "setpts=PTS+1/TB,subtitles=s.srt,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS" out.mp4` showed the cue correctly (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Transparent caption layer for compositing
what: render captions onto a fully transparent canvas with `alpha=1` and keep alpha in the codec (qtrle wrote argb)
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:r=30:d=10,format=rgba" -vf "ass=caps.ass:alpha=1" -c:v qtrle caps.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Caption-only or lyric video
what: burn the ASS onto a colour source and add the audio
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=black:s=1080x1920:r=30:d=11 -i voice.flac -vf "ass=caps.ass" -shortest -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac lyric.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Darken the caption band before burning
what: a filled semi-transparent `drawbox` under the text (CLAUDE.md: put captions over a darker lower part of the frame)
how: `-vf "drawbox=x=0:y=ih*0.7:w=iw:h=ih*0.3:color=black@0.5:t=fill,subtitles=s.srt"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: force_style colours carry alpha
what: `force_style` takes ASS `KEY=VALUE` pairs; the docs' example `PrimaryColour=&HCCFF0000` is 80% transparent blue (AABBGGRR)
how: `subtitles=s.srt:force_style='Fontname=DejaVu Serif,PrimaryColour=&HCCFF0000'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Find the cuts to time captions against
what: `scdet` logs `lavfi.scd.time` at each scene change; a red/blue cut at 1.3 s (24 fps) was found at 1.33333 s. Feed these times to the shot-change rules below
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "scdet=threshold=10,metadata=print:key=lavfi.scd.time" -f null - 2>&1 | grep scd.time` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Snap caption edges to cuts like Aegisub's keyframe snapping
what: Aegisub moves a line start onto a keyframe when it is within a threshold, and an end to the frame before the keyframe; its post-processor applies lead-in/out first, then joins adjacent lines, then snaps
how: in Python, for each cut time `c` from scdet: if `0 <= c - start < 0.5` set `start = c`; if `0 <= c - end < 0.5` set `end = c - 2/fps`

name: drawtext is fine for Arabic Naskh, not for Urdu Nastaliq or Hindi
what: `text_shaping` (needs FriBidi) reverses RTL text and joins Arabic letters: Noto Naskh Arabic came out joined and right-to-left, but Noto Nastaliq Urdu showed boxes and Devanagari conjuncts broke
how: use drawtext only for Latin/Naskh text; burn Urdu and Hindi with the `ass` filter (tested here 2026-10-24, frames inspected)

name: Put caption text in a file
what: drawtext's text needs up to four levels of escaping; `textfile` avoids that and must be UTF-8
how: `printf 'مرحبا 123' > line.txt` then `drawtext=fontfile=NotoNaskhArabic.ttf:textfile=line.txt:fontsize=36:fontcolor=white:x=(w-tw)/2:y=h-120` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Live-updating caption from a file
what: `reload=N` re-reads the textfile every N frames; update the file atomically or it may be read half-written
how: `drawtext=fontfile=DejaVuSans.ttf:textfile=live.txt:reload=1:fontsize=30:fontcolor=white:x=20:y=20` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Time a drawtext line with `enable`
what: timeline editing evaluates `enable` per frame (with `t` in seconds); outside the window the frame passes unchanged
how: `drawtext=...:text='Timed line':enable='between(t,1,2)'` showed the text at 1.5 s and not at 0.5 s (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Change the words mid-clip with sendcmd
what: drawtext's `reinit` command re-sets options (text, fontsize...) at a given time
how: a command file `1.0 drawtext reinit text=Second;` with `-vf "sendcmd=f=cmds.txt,drawtext=fontfile=DejaVuSans.ttf:text=First:fontsize=30:fontcolor=white:x=20:y=300"` switched the text at 1 s (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Asymmetric box padding
what: `boxborderw` takes 1-4 values; `8|24` pads 8 px top/bottom and 24 px left/right for a wide caption pill
how: `drawtext=...:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.7:boxborderw=8|24` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fixed caption box with centred lines
what: `boxw`/`boxh` fix the box size and `text_align` places the text inside it; in 6.1.1 the flags are joined with `+` (`M+C`), the docs' `MC` form was rejected
how: `drawtext=...:textfile=two.txt:box=1:boxw=500:boxh=100:text_align=M+C:line_spacing=8:x=(w-500)/2:y=h-130` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: fix_bounds pulls text back on screen, within limits
what: with `fix_bounds=1` text placed off the bottom-right moved up and left into the frame, but a line wider than the frame still overflowed
how: add `:fix_bounds=1`, and still wrap long lines yourself (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Minimum header for a portable ASS
what: `ScriptType: v4.00+` is required; the guide also wants `ScaledBorderAndShadow`, `YCbCr Matrix`, `PlayResX/Y` and `LayoutResX/Y`, sections in order with `[Events]` last, UTF-8 (BOM recommended)
how: start every file from the guide's example header (`ScaledBorderAndShadow: yes`, `YCbCr Matrix: None`, PlayRes = LayoutRes = video size); every test file here used it (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: ScaledBorderAndShadow: yes, always
what: the guide says `no` has no benefit and only exists for backward compatibility; with `yes` border and shadow sizes are in script pixels
how: keep `ScaledBorderAndShadow: yes` in `[Script Info]`
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24
Aegisub manual: Resolution and Matrix, https://aegisub.org/docs/latest/resolution_and_matrix/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Set YCbCr Matrix to match the video
what: for BT.601/BT.709 video set exactly `TV.709` (or `TV.601`, `PC.*` for full range), otherwise `None`; a missing header is read as TV.601, which mangles colours on modern HD video in VSFilter-style renderers
how: for normal phone/YouTube HD footage use `YCbCr Matrix: TV.709` (or `None`)
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24
Aegisub manual: Resolution and Matrix, https://aegisub.org/docs/latest/resolution_and_matrix/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Script resolution is a coordinate system
what: font sizes, margins, `\pos`, clips and drawings are in PlayRes units, independent of the video size; it only needs the same aspect as the video (1280x720 is fine for 1920x1080, 1440x1080 is not)
how: author vertical reels at `PlayResX: 1080 PlayResY: 1920` so numbers equal pixels
refs: Aegisub manual: Resolution and Matrix, https://aegisub.org/docs/latest/resolution_and_matrix/, checked 2026-10-24

name: LayoutRes keeps blur and 3D rotation consistent
what: `\blur`, the 3D-rotation focal length and text widths scale with Layout Resolution; set it so the file renders the same at any size, with the same aspect as PlayRes
how: `LayoutResX`/`LayoutResY` = display size of the source video
refs: Aegisub manual: Resolution and Matrix, https://aegisub.org/docs/latest/resolution_and_matrix/, checked 2026-10-24
libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Pick the wrap mode
what: 0 balances line lengths (top wider), 1 fills the first line then breaks, 2 never wraps (only `\N`/`\n` break). Rendered: `\q0` and `\q1` broke the same 60-character line at different words, `\q2` ran off both edges
how: global `WrapStyle: 0` for dialogue, `{\q2}` plus manual `\N` for styled social captions (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Aegisub manual: ASS Override Tags, https://aegisub.org/docs/latest/ass_tags/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Don't use wrap mode 3
what: VSFilter's mode 3 (bottom line wider) is unsupported in libass and treated as 0; the guide says use `\q2` with explicit `\N` for a specific break shape
how: for a bottom-heavy two-liner write the break yourself: `{\q2}Short top\Nlonger bottom line`
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Style line rules
what: booleans are `-1`/`0`, colours are `&HAABBGGRR` (alpha 00 opaque, FF invisible), `Encoding` must be `1` (see the libass RTL exception below), Fontname ≤ 31 characters, Fontsize ≤ 511 (scale with tags instead)
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: No letter Spacing on Urdu/Hindi styles
what: the guide says Spacing is not advisable with scripts that depend on complex shaping
how: keep `Spacing` 0 and no `\fsp` on Nastaliq/Devanagari styles
refs: libass wiki: ASS File Format Guide, https://github.com/libass/libass/wiki/ASS-File-Format-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Event times are h:mm:ss.cc
what: exactly two digits for minutes, seconds and centiseconds; start is inclusive and end exclusive
how: write times with a helper such as `f"{h}:{m:02d}:{s:02d}.{cs:02d}"` (used by the generators below) (tested here 2026-10-24)
