what: in Natron's Merge an input with only RGB has alpha treated as one, so the output is fully opaque; non-zero RGB with zero alpha is not valid premultiplied RGBA
how: add `format=yuva420p` and a real matte before a merge that should stay transparent.

name: VP9 WebM with alpha
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: libvpx-vp9 accepts yuva420p; ffprobe shows the stream as yuv420p with tag alpha_mode=1
how: `-vf "chromakey=...,format=yuva420p" -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 30 out.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Decode WebM alpha with libvpx
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: the native vp9 decoder drops the alpha (a frame came out rgb24); forcing the libvpx decoder before -i keeps it (rgba)
how: `ffmpeg -c:v libvpx-vp9 -i cut.webm -frames:v 1 f.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP8 WebM alpha
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: libvpx (VP8) also takes yuva420p
how: `-c:v libvpx -b:v 1M -auto-alt-ref 0` with `format=yuva420p` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lossless alpha masters
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: QuickTime Animation (qtrle, argb) and FFV1 (yuva444p and others) store alpha losslessly; PNG/TIFF are the common alpha image formats
how: `format=argb -c:v qtrle out.mov`, `format=yuva444p -c:v ffv1 out.mkv` (ffprobe `yuva444p`), or `format=rgba out_%03d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Ignore alpha on decode
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: the decoder option skip_alpha=1 disables alpha processing
how: `ffmpeg -skip_alpha 1 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -i cut.webm ...` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Check that a file really has alpha
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: an alpha stream shows an alpha pix_fmt (yuva*, rgba, argb, gbrap)
how: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=pix_fmt -of csv=p=0 file` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: GIF has only 1-bit transparency
section: Alpha in files: codecs and checks
what: GIF marks one palette entry transparent; HEVC alpha is browser-limited to Safari in the Wikipedia table; magenta #FF00FF is sometimes used as 1-bit 'magic pink'
how: GIF: `split[a][b];[a]palettegen=reserve_transparent=1[p];[b][p]paletteuse=alpha_threshold=128` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rebuild a transparent WebM from rembg masks
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: extract frames, make a mask per frame with one session, then rebuild a transparent WebM with alphamerge
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf fps=5 rf/f_%03d.png` -> masks `rf/m_%03d.png` -> `ffmpeg -framerate 5 -i rf/f_%03d.png -framerate 5 -i rf/m_%03d.png -filter_complex "[1:v]format=gray[m];[0:v][m]alphamerge,format=yuva420p" -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 32 cut.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: rembg b streams raw frames from ffmpeg
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: the `b` subcommand reads RGB24 frames from stdin: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -an -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 pipe:1 | rembg b 1280 720 -o out-%03u.png`; width/height must match
how: the rembg CLI in /home/user/tools/venv fails to start here (missing python module `watchdog`), so use the Python API until it is installed.

name: Temporally smooth a per-frame mask
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: per-frame masks flicker; average neighbouring mask frames before applying them
how: `tmix=frames=3` on the mask video before alphamerge (the repo's bg_blur.py smooths its rembg mask over time).

name: GrabCut from a rectangle
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: draw a rectangle fully around the subject; outside is sure background, inside unknown; GMMs and a graph min-cut label pixels; run ~5 iterations with GC_INIT_WITH_RECT, then map mask 0/2 to background and 1/3 to foreground
how: `cv2.grabCut(img,mask,(x,y,w,h),bgd,fgd,5,cv2.GC_INIT_WITH_RECT); m2=np.where((mask==2)|(mask==0),0,1)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: GrabCut touch-ups
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: mark wrong areas in the mask as sure foreground (1) or background (0) and rerun with GC_INIT_WITH_MASK; hard labels do not change
how: `mask[60:80,100:120]=cv2.GC_FGD; cv2.grabCut(img,mask,None,bgd,fgd,3,cv2.GC_INIT_WITH_MASK)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: GrabCut result as a soft PNG cutout
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: turn the GrabCut labels into an alpha channel, blur it slightly, and write a BGRA PNG for HyperFrames or ffmpeg
how: `a=np.where((m==1)|(m==3),255,0).astype(np.uint8); a=cv2.GaussianBlur(a,(5,5),0); rgba[:,:,3]=a; cv2.imwrite('cut.png',rgba)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Background subtraction for a locked camera
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: MOG2 makes a foreground mask by subtracting a background model, for static cameras; defaults history=500, varThreshold=16, detectShadows=True
how: `bs=cv2.createBackgroundSubtractorMOG2(history=500,varThreshold=16,detectShadows=True); m=bs.apply(frame)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Strip MOG2 shadows
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: with shadows on, the mask is 0 background, 255 foreground and 127 (default shadow value) for shadows; shadow threshold 0.5 means a pixel more than twice darker is not shadow
how: `_,fg=cv2.threshold(m,200,255,cv2.THRESH_BINARY)` keeps only 255 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Freeze the background model
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: learningRate 0 stops updating the model, 1 reinitialises from the last frame, negative picks automatically; getBackgroundImage() returns the learned plate
how: `bs.apply(frame, learningRate=0); plate=bs.getBackgroundImage()` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: KNN background subtractor
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: KNN uses dist2Threshold (default 400) on squared distance; detectShadows can be turned off for speed
how: `cv2.createBackgroundSubtractorKNN(history=500,dist2Threshold=400.0,detectShadows=False)` gave a pure 0/255 mask (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: HSV range mask with inRange
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: convert BGR to HSV and threshold a hue window; OpenCV hue runs 0-179
how: `hsv=cv2.cvtColor(img,cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV); m=cv2.inRange(hsv,(h-10,100,50),(h+10,255,255))` (green screen sampled at hue 70) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Clean a mask with opening and closing
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: opening (erode then dilate) removes specks, closing (dilate then erode) fills small holes
how: `k=cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE,(5,5)); cv2.morphologyEx(m,cv2.MORPH_OPEN,k)` then MORPH_CLOSE (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Otsu threshold for a quick luma matte
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: Otsu picks the threshold automatically from a bimodal histogram; blur first to reduce noise
how: `g=cv2.GaussianBlur(g,(5,5),0); t,th=cv2.threshold(g,0,255,cv2.THRESH_BINARY+cv2.THRESH_OTSU)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep only the largest blob
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: find external contours and fill the biggest one to drop stray islands from a key
how: `cs,_=cv2.findContours(fg,cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL,cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE); c=max(cs,key=cv2.contourArea); cv2.drawContours(m,[c],-1,255,cv2.FILLED)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Histogram backprojection mask
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: build a hue-saturation histogram of a sample region and back-project it to find similar pixels anywhere
how: `hist=cv2.calcHist([roi],[0,1],None,[180,256],[0,180,0,256]); cv2.normalize(...); cv2.calcBackProject([hsv],[0,1],hist,[0,180,0,256],1)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Watershed with markers
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: threshold, find sure background (dilate) and sure foreground (distance transform), label markers, and let watershed split touching objects
how: as in the tutorial: `dt=cv2.distanceTransform(th,cv2.DIST_L2,5)` ... `cv2.watershed(img,markers)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: segments prominent people close to the camera (under 2 m); model 0 'general' runs on 256x256, model 1 'landscape' on 144x256 and is faster; output mask matches the input size; the example thresholds at 0.1 and suggests a joint bilateral filter for edges
how: needs mediapipe (missing here); the legacy solution was upgraded to the Image Segmenter in 2023.

name: Smooth a mask edge with a bilateral filter
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: OpenCV's plain bilateralFilter runs on a mask; the joint (guided by the image) version is in opencv-contrib ximgproc, which this build does not have
how: `cv2.bilateralFilter(mask,9,75,75)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fade a cutout through a wrapper
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: the HyperFrames runtime forces opacity 1 on a timed clip, so fade a cutout by animating an untimed wrapper div
how:
`
` and tween `#cutwrap` opacity.

name: Freeze-frame cutout recipe
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: extract the exact frame, remove its background, then add `freeze-frame-dressing`; inspect the matte on light and dark plates and reject missing fingers or halos
how: `ffmpeg -ss <s> -i src.mp4 -frames:v 1 freeze.png; npx hyperframes remove-background freeze.png -o freeze-cutout.png --json; npx hyperframes add freeze-frame-dressing --no-clipboard`

name: Roto drives effects, not only cutouts
section: Rotoscoping and segmentation on CPU (rembg, GrabCut, OpenCV)
what: in VFX rotoscoping means hand-making a matte; it also prepares garbage mattes for other keys and can guide an effect such as a glow (the original lightsaber glow was drawn from a matte of the prop)
how: use a GrabCut/rembg mask as the region for a glow (see Glow section) instead of only cutting out.

name: Tracks are 2D paths of features
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: a feature is a point the tracker can lock onto (bright/dark spots, edges, corners); followed through frames it becomes a series of 2D coordinates, a track, usable for 2D motion tracking or for solving 3D. Template matching with NCC score is a common method
how: think of every tracker output here as one (x, y) per frame, saved to CSV/JSON in the scratchpad.

name: One point is never enough for a camera solve
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: each tracked point narrows the possible camera parameters; many tracks plus a known focal length make the 3D solve tractable; errors call for statistical methods (bundle adjustment)
how: for 3D camera solves use a dedicated solver (Blender, missing here); this repo stays with 2D tracks.

name: Stabilize, match-move, remove or add jitter
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: a tracker's output can stabilise the plate, match-move another image to the track, remove jitter (smooth high frequencies) or add jitter (apply the shake to another image)
how: choose the mode first; in ffmpeg vid.stab stabilises, `invert=1` reverses the transforms.

name: Reference frame and fitting error
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: the reference frame is where the exported transform is identity; the fitting error (px) per frame flags a poor model choice (Natron warns at 1 px by default); a robust model drops points that do not fit
how: pick the frame where the insert is placed as reference; print per-frame reprojection error from findHomography inliers.

name: MIL tracker (built into OpenCV)
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: TrackerMIL trains an online classifier to separate object from background; init(frame, box) then update(frame) returns (ok, box). ok False may mean the target is really out of sight, not a failure
how: `t=cv2.TrackerMIL_create(); t.init(f0,(x,y,w,h)); ok,bb=t.update(f)` (OpenCV 5.0.0 in the venv) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: MIL parameters
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: Params: samplerInitInRadius 3, samplerSearchWinSize 25, featureSetNumFeatures 250, samplerTrackMaxPosNum 100000, samplerTrackMaxNegNum 65 (defaults read here)
how: `p=cv2.TrackerMIL_Params(); p.samplerSearchWinSize=40; cv2.TrackerMIL_create(p)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: DNN trackers need model files
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: TrackerNano needs backbone.onnx + neckhead.onnx (~1.9 MB total), TrackerVit needs vitTracker.onnx (~767 KB), DaSiamRPN three nets; GOTURN does not handle occlusion
how: default param file names read here: Nano ('backbone.onnx','neckhead.onnx'), Vit ('vitTracker.onnx'); models are missing (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CSRT/KCF are not in this OpenCV
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: the venv's OpenCV 5.0.0 has no TrackerCSRT/TrackerKCF and no cv2.legacy (they live in opencv-contrib); only MIL, Nano, Vit, DaSiamRPN exist
how: `hasattr(cv2,'TrackerCSRT_create')` was False (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Template match a point track
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: matchTemplate slides a patch over the frame; with TM_CCOEFF_NORMED the best match is the maximum from minMaxLoc; colour templates work and give one result channel
how: `r=cv2.matchTemplate(frame,tpl,cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED); _,score,_,loc=cv2.minMaxLoc(r)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shi-Tomasi corners to track
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: goodFeaturesToTrack finds corners that track well (smooth areas suffer from the aperture problem); maxCorners caps work, qualityLevel rejects weak corners, minDistance spreads them
how: `cv2.goodFeaturesToTrack(gray,maxCorners=200,qualityLevel=0.01,minDistance=30,blockSize=3)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lucas-Kanade with status filtering
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: calcOpticalFlowPyrLK tracks sparse points (defaults winSize 21x21, maxLevel 3); keep only points with status 1, because a returned coordinate is not automatically valid
how: `p1,st,err=cv2.calcOpticalFlowPyrLK(prev,cur,p0,None,winSize=(21,21),maxLevel=3); v=st.reshape(-1)==1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dense flow: DIS presets
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: DISOpticalFlow has ULTRAFAST, FAST (default) and MEDIUM presets; even the slowest is fast
how: `cv2.DISOpticalFlow_create(cv2.DISOPTICAL_FLOW_PRESET_FAST).calc(a,b,None)` returned a HxWx2 flow (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dense flow: Farneback
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: Gunnar Farneback's dense optical flow is the other built-in dense method
how: `cv2.calcOpticalFlowFarneback(a,b,None,0.5,3,15,3,5,1.2,0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ECC alignment for one patch or frame
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: findTransformECC aligns by intensity (area-based) with translation, euclidean, affine (default) or homography models; it needs a rough initial warp for big moves and throws if it does not converge; the multi-scale version is more stable
how: `cc,W=cv2.findTransformECC(a,b,np.eye(2,3,dtype=np.float32),cv2.MOTION_TRANSLATION,(cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_EPS|cv2.TERM_CRITERIA_COUNT,50,1e-4),None,5)` (cc 0.964 here) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CamShift / meanShift colour tracking
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: meanShift moves a window to the mass centre of a back-projection (size fixed); CamShift also adapts size and rotation and returns a rotated rect; pre-filtering the back-projection helps
how: hue histogram of the box -> `calcBackProject` -> `cv2.CamShift(dst,win,crit)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Kalman-smooth a noisy track
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: OpenCV has a KalmanFilter class (predict/correct) for smoothing measured positions
how: constant-velocity `cv2.KalmanFilter(4,2)`, `predict()` then `correct(measured_xy)` per frame (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Drive an ffmpeg overlay from a track
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: overlay supports x and y as commands, so a sendcmd file of per-time positions moves an overlay along a track; sendcmd must sit in a chain before the overlay
how: `[0:v]sendcmd=f=track.cmd[b];[b][fg]overlay@ov=x=0:y=0[v]` with lines like `0.5 overlay@ov x 60, overlay@ov y 30;` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Write the sendcmd file from a tracker
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: turn tracker boxes into timed overlay commands (time = frame/fps)
how: MIL boxes -> `f"{i/30:.4f} overlay@ov x {x}, overlay@ov y {y};"` per frame (29 lines written here) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Overlay position by expression
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: overlay x/y expressions see t, n, W, H, w, h and are evaluated per frame by default; an invalid expression puts the overlay off screen. The docs' slide-in: x='if(gte(t,2), -w+(t-2)*20, NAN)'
how: `overlay=x='if(gte(t,0.5),-w+(t-0.5)*300,NAN)':y=40` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Time-limit an overlay
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: the timeline `enable` option shows an overlay only between two times
how: `overlay=enable='between(t,0.5,1.5)'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Line up overlay timestamps
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: overlay takes frames in timestamp order, so inputs that start at different times should go through setpts=PTS-STARTPTS
how: `[1:v]setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,chromakey=...[fg];[b][fg]overlay=shortest=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: What happens when the overlay ends
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: eof_action repeat (default) holds the last overlay frame, endall stops both, pass shows the main input again
how: `[1:v]trim=0:1,...[fg];[0:v][fg]overlay=eof_action=pass` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Invert the transforms
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: invert=1 applies the transforms reversed, the building block for 'add jitter' (move an element with the measured shake)
how: `vidstabtransform=input=tr.trf:invert=1:smoothing=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Limits of a global 2D stabiliser
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: one global affine cannot align different depths (parallax), rolling shutter needs a spatially varying model, a big moving subject biases the estimate, blur/low texture loses corners, and a centred moving average needs future frames (use a causal filter for live)
how: check inlier ratios and cap implausible transforms before trusting the result.

name: Blender Stabilize 2D sampling
section: Tracking: points, objects and stabilised overlays
what: Stabilize 2D can invert the stabilisation and choose Nearest (pixel steps, jitter in motion), Bilinear, Bicubic or Anisotropic sampling
how: prefer bilinear or bicubic interpolation for photographic footage in any stabiliser.

name: perspective: corner-pin an insert
what: with sense=destination the corners of the source go to the given points, which pins a replacement image into a screen; give the insert alpha so the rest stays transparent for overlay
how: `[1:v]scale=320:180,format=yuva420p,perspective=x0=180:y0=40:x1=290:y1=30:x2=185:y2=120:x3=300:y3=135:sense=destination[w];[0:v][w]overlay` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Animated corner pin by expression
what: perspective coordinates can use W, H, in and on (frame counts) when eval=frame, for a simple animated pin
how: `perspective=x0='20*on/60':y0=0:x1=W:y1=0:x2=0:y2=H:x3=W:y3=H:sense=destination:eval=frame` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Homography from feature matches
what: match SIFT features with FLANN and Lowe's ratio test (0.7), require at least 10 good matches, then findHomography with RANSAC (5.0) and perspectiveTransform the object corners; at least four correct points are needed and RANSAC returns an inlier mask
how: as in the tutorial: `M,mask=cv2.findHomography(src,dst,cv2.RANSAC,5.0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: OpenCV tutorial Feature Matching + Homography, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencv/opencv/4.x/doc/py_tutorials/py_feature2d/py_feature_homography/py_feature_homography.markdown, checked 2026-10-24

name: ORB for a free, fast matcher
what: ORB is a free alternative to SIFT/SURF; match its binary descriptors with BFMatcher NORM_HAMMING (crossCheck=True) before findHomography
how: `orb=cv2.ORB_create(nfeatures=1000)` ... `cv2.BFMatcher(cv2.NORM_HAMMING,crossCheck=True)` (138 of 145 matches were inliers on a synthetic warp) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Warp an insert into four tracked corners
what: getPerspectiveTransform maps the insert's corners to the screen corners; warp the insert and a white mask with the same matrix, feather the mask a little, and mix
how: `M=cv2.getPerspectiveTransform(src,dst); warped=cv2.warpPerspective(ins,M,(w,h)); mask=cv2.warpPerspective(white,M,(w,h))` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CornerPin point count sets the model
what: CornerPin is a translation with 1 point enabled, a similarity with 2, affine with 3, homography with all 4
how: when only two corners are trackable, fit a similarity (estimateAffinePartial2D) instead of a homography.

name: Full-frame to screen move
what: to fly an image from full frame onto a billboard, combine Transform and CornerPin and animate both Amount values 0 -> 1; CornerPin alone interpolates corners linearly, which can shrink and swell unrealistically when rotating
how: in HyperFrames, animate scale/position of a wrapper first and finish on the pinned corners.

name: CornerPin vs Transform export
what: exported to a CornerPin, four or more tracks keep more information and are more stable than a Transform
how: store all four corner tracks per frame, not only a centre.

name: Plane track mask vs image output
what: Blender's Plane Track Deform outputs the warped image and a Plane mask; using the warped image moves and skews it, using the original with the Plane mask only shows the part inside the mask
how: decide which you need: a pinned insert (warp) or a window onto a fixed image (mask).

name: Motion blur on a planar insert
what: Plane Track Deform can add motion blur from the plane's motion (samples, shutter in frames; samples from the next frame only, so the blur leads slightly)
how: ffmpeg's perspective filter has no motion-blur option (its options are the corners, interpolation, sense and eval), so compare the insert with the plate's own blur in snapshots.

name: Blur only a tracked region
what: feedback crops a region to its second output, lets you filter it, and puts it back on the frame; the docs blur a 100x100 corner with gblur
how: `[0:v][fbin]feedback=x=100:y=40:w=100:h=80[out][fbout];[fbout]gblur=sigma=8[fbin]` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Variable blur by a matte
what: varblur blurs by a second stream that sets the radius per pixel (min_r 0, max_r default 8)
how: `[a][r]varblur=max_r=12` with a negated matte as the radius map (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Phone-screen and device blocks
what: HyperFrames has device scenes instead of tracking real footage: `filmed-screen` (scene filmed off a screen with perspective and DOF), `device-frame-stage`, `multi-device-splay`, `yt-screen-warp` (makes footage read as playing on a physical display)
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "screen replacement device mockup"` then `npx hyperframes add filmed-screen`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: delogo only for part of the clip
what: the docs show a time-limited delogo: split, trim the delogo branch, and overlay it back with eof_action=pass; the timeline enable option is simpler
how: `split[m][d];[d]trim=start=0.5:end=1.5,delogo=...[dl];[m][dl]overlay=eof_action=pass` or `delogo=...:enable='between(t,0.5,1.5)'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: OpenCV inpaint: Telea vs Navier-Stokes
what: cv2.inpaint fills masked pixels from the boundary inward (INPAINT_TELEA, fast marching) or by continuing isophotes (INPAINT_NS); the mask is 8-bit, non-zero = fill; usable on stills or video frames
how: `cv2.inpaint(frame,mask,3,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Seamless clone modes
what: seamlessClone blends a source region into a destination: NORMAL_CLONE keeps the source look, MIXED_CLONE mixes source structure with destination texture (good with loose selections), MONOCHROME_TRANSFER swaps textures; *_WIDE variants use the whole mask area
how: `cv2.seamlessClone(src,dst,mask,(cx,cy),cv2.NORMAL_CLONE)`; all six flags exist in this OpenCV 5.0.0 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Poisson local edits
what: illuminationChange (alpha, beta 0-2; defaults 0.2/0.4) relights a masked area or reduces specular glare, colorChange multiplies channels (0.5-2.5) inside a mask, textureFlattening washes out texture
how: `cv2.illuminationChange(img,mask,alpha=0.2,beta=0.4)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Clean plate from a temporal median
what: tmedian picks the median of successive frames (radius up to 127; percentile 0 = min, 1 = max), so moving things drop out of a locked shot
how: `tmedian=radius=15` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fill garbage at the frame edge
what: fillborders fills N pixels at each border without changing size (smear, mirror and other modes)
how: `fillborders=left=4:right=4:top=2:bottom=2:mode=smear` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Colour-key a clean blue sky and feather it
what: for a sky that is a fairly even colour, sample it and colorkey it, then soften only the matte
how: `[0:v]colorkey=0xF0F4FF:0.08:0.05,format=yuva444p,split[c][a];[a]alphaextract,gblur=sigma=1[m];[c][m]alphamerge[k];[1:v][k]overlay` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Invert a luma matte when needed
what: a luma key of a white background gives the opposite matte of what you want; invert it (Blender uses a Color Ramp) or swap the inputs of the mix
how: `alphaextract,negate` before alphamerge, or swap main/overlay inputs.

name: Glare controls to copy
what: Blender's Glare node: threshold (minimum luminance that glows), smoothness (gradual transition), clamp maximum (consistent bloom over varied highlights), strength, saturation and tint, size (1 = whole image); types bloom, fog glow (more physical, slower), streaks, ghosts, simple star, sun beams, kernel
how: in ffmpeg the same parts are a highlight cut (`lutyuv=y='if(gt(val,200),val,16)'`), a big `gblur` and a `blend=all_mode=screen` back over the frame.

name: Nuke Glow controls
what: Glow brightens bright areas with a blur: tolerance (low threshold), saturation, effect only, a box (fastest) or gaussian (smoothest) filter, quality by downscale, and a mask
how: 'effect only' means rendering only the blurred-highlight branch and compositing it later.

name: ffmpeg blend mode 'glow'
what: blend has a mode named glow among about 40 modes (addition, screen, lighten, softlight, vividlight...); the first input is the top layer
how: `[g][a]blend=all_mode=glow` with a blurred copy as top (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Blend opacity
what: all_opacity (or c0_opacity...) sets how much of the blend mode applies, only together with a mode
how: `blend=all_mode=screen:all_opacity=0.6` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Light wrap controls (Nuke)
what: LightWrap spills background light onto the foreground's edges; apply it to the foreground before the merge. Diffuse (default 15) spread and Intensity are balanced together; FGBlur 1 sets matte blur, BGBlur 0 background blur, Highlight Merge plus gives a glow; options: wrap only, disable luminance-based wrap, constant colour, enable glow
how: start with Diffuse low, raise Intensity, then return to Diffuse.

name: Light wrap in ffmpeg
what: blurred background inside a thin band just inside the matte edge, laid over the composite
how: edge = matte x blurred inverted matte; wrap = blurred bg with that alpha: `[fa]alphaextract,split[m1][m2];[m1]negate,gblur=sigma=6[inv];[m2][inv]blend=all_mode=multiply[edge];[0:v]format=yuv444p,gblur=sigma=10[bgb];[bgb][edge]alphamerge[wrap];[base][fg]overlay[comp];[comp][wrap]overlay` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Use background luminance on edges
what: IBK/PIK can let the new background affect edge colour and brightness (use bkg luminance/chroma), which also hides fringing; grade the bg input up or down just before it to tune
how: ffmpeg's keyers have no such option; the tested light-wrap command above is the nearest stand-in here.

name: Glow from a roto shape
what: a matte can guide a glow: the lightsaber blades were roto'd from sticks, enlarged and glowed
how: dilate + heavy gblur the matte, tint it, and screen it over the plate.

name: Screen or Add for light on black
what: for elements that emit light shot on a dark background (fire), a Screen or Add mix beats a key
how: `[1:v][0:v]blend=all_mode=addition` or screen in gbrp (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Screen in RGB for fire
what: screen fire over a plate in RGB planes so the mode works on R, G, B, then convert back for delivery
how: `[0:v]format=gbrp[b];[1:v]format=gbrp[f];[f][b]blend=all_mode=screen,format=yuv420p` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: What a lens flare is
what: light scattered inside the lens (internal reflections, forward scatter) causes visible artefacts, often aperture-shaped (6 blades -> hexagons), in a row across the image, plus veiling glare that lowers contrast and saturation; flares move with the camera relative to the light and fade as it points away
how: place flare elements on a line through the light and the frame centre, and lower contrast slightly while the flare is strong.

name: Anamorphic flare streaks
what: anamorphic lenses make horizontal line flares, common with car headlights at night and part of the 'film look'
how: tested stand-in (look not judged): a horizontal directional blur of the highlights, screened back: `[b]dblur=angle=0:radius=40[s];[a][s]blend=all_mode=screen` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cheap flare = textures on a line
what: game-style flares draw starburst, ring and disc textures over the image and move them as the light moves; adding a flare implies an unedited photo, but overuse is criticised (Abrams admitted his were overdone)
how: one soft disc at the light with a geq gaussian: `geq=lum='255*gauss((X/W-0.7)*12)*gauss((Y/H-0.3)*12)/gauss(0)/gauss(0)'`, screened over the plate (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Flare elements as donuts
what: Nuke's Flare is a donut with inner, middle and outer radii, ring and inner colours (equal colours make discs), chroma spread (red out, blue in), edge flattening for polygonal flares, and repeat flares randomised along the centre-to-light line; 'offset' places a flare between centre (0) and light (1)
how: a ring in ffmpeg: `geq=lum='clip(255*exp(-pow((hypot(X-220,Y-50)-18)/5,2)),0,255)'` screened over the plate (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Ghosts mirrored through the centre
what: reposition flare elements along the imaginary line between the light position and the image centre
how: a second, dimmer disc at centre - (light - centre) x 0.6 in the same geq expression (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Flare visibility mask
what: a visibility mask limits the flare (white = full, black = off) and is blurred by a radius, so the flare dims when the light goes behind something
how: multiply the flare layer by a matte of the light source before the screen blend.

name: HyperFrames flare and light blocks
what: the registry has `lens-flare` (WebGPU star burst and rainbow halo), `vfx-anamorphic-flare` (points with long blue-violet streaks), `godrays`, `sun-burst`, `light-edge`, `light-sweep-pass`, `light-leak` and `organic-light-leak-overlay`
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "lens flare"`, then `npx hyperframes add lens-flare`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Ripple distortion with displace
what: displace moves pixels by two map streams (x and y; 128 = no move); the docs build ripple and wave maps with geq sine expressions; edge blank/smear (default)/wrap/mirror
how: `[0][1][2]displace` with `nullsrc,lutrgb=128:128:128` and a geq sine map (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Heat-haze and distortion blocks
what: for distortion transitions the registry has `thermal-distortion` (heat haze), `ripple-waves`, `swirl-vortex` and `transitions-distortion`
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "heat distortion"`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Particle system basics
what: particle systems simulate fuzzy phenomena (fire, smoke, sparks, snow, dust) with many small sprites: an emitter sets spawn rate and initial velocity, a simulation stage ages and moves particles and removes them past their lifetime, a render stage draws each (often a camera-facing quad)
how: give each spark a birth time, velocity and lifetime; fade it out before it dies.

name: Seek-safe particles in HyperFrames
what: HyperFrames particle blocks are seeded and deterministic: `confetti`, `particle-image-reveal`, `particle-text-dissolve`, `caption-particle-burst`, `snow`, `starfield`, `falling-lines`
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query particles`, then `npx hyperframes add snow`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Embers background from the repo
what: ember_background.py writes the FireCraft dark ember scene: 36 seeded rising embers plus glow, as a HyperFrames composition
how: `python3 library/tools/ember_background.py embers.html` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Floating hearts and bokeh from the repo
what: floating_hearts.py writes a deterministic hearts + bokeh overlay scene with duration, count, an optional end burst and canvas size
how: `python3 library/tools/floating_hearts.py hearts.html --duration 6 --count 12 --width 1080 --height 1920` printed 'wrote hearts.html: 12 hearts, 16 bokeh, 6s' (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stock fire/smoke shot on black
what: stock explosions, smoke and debris are normally shot on a dark background; separate them by luminance, or for light-emitting elements use Screen/Add
how: `[1:v]lumakey=threshold=0:tolerance=0.08:softness=0.3[f];[0:v][f]overlay` for smoke; screen for flames (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: No fire or smoke block in the registry
what: catalog searches for 'smoke', 'flame' and 'sparks embers' returned nothing, so use stock CC0 footage or the ember tool
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query smoke` (empty) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Generated gradients and life sources
what: the gradients source makes moving linear/radial/circular/spiral/square gradients (2-8 colours, speed); life makes a cellular automaton pattern with life/death colours
how: `-f lavfi -i "gradients=s=320x180:c0=0x0b1a40:c1=0xff8a3d:type=radial:speed=0.02:d=2"`; `life=s=320x180:mold=10:ratio=0.1:...` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Grain and film-look blocks
what: `grain-overlay` (CSS keyframes) and `grain-field` are the registry's texture overlays
how: `npx hyperframes add grain-overlay`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Blend modes off the 3D world
what: mix-blend-mode, opacity < 1 and filters on a preserve-3d container flatten the 3D world; put blend modes only in separate 2D overlay compositions above it
how: fire or flare layers with `mix-blend-mode: screen` live in their own 2D overlay composition.

name: mix-blend-mode works inside a stacking context
what: mix-blend-mode blends an element with what is behind it in the same stacking context; `isolation: isolate` on a parent stops it blending with the page background
how: wrap a flare + plate pair in a div with `isolation:isolate` when the blend should not reach other layers.

name: plus-lighter for clean crossfades
what: plus-lighter blends with the plus-lighter compositing operator and prevents the brightness dip when two overlapping elements fade in opposite directions
how: `mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter` on both layers of a dissolve.

name: mask-image alpha vs luminance
what: mask-image hides parts of an element by the mask's alpha; with mask-mode luminance (default for SVG <mask>) the luminance times alpha is used, so white shows and black hides
how: use a PNG matte from rembg/GrabCut as `mask-image: url(matte.png)` with `mask-mode: luminance` for a grey matte.

name: clip-path for hard shapes
what: clip-path creates a clipping region: inside shows, outside hides; shapes include inset(), circle(), polygon()
how: animate a `polygon()` for a simple garbage-matte style reveal.

name: drop-shadow follows the cutout
what: filter: drop-shadow() draws a blurred, offset copy of the image's alpha mask below it, conforming to the shape, unlike box-shadow's rectangle; inset and spread are not allowed
how: `filter: drop-shadow(0 12px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.45))` on a transparent cutout to seat it in the plate.

name: backdrop-filter needs transparency
what: backdrop-filter blurs or shifts the area behind an element and is only visible if the element or its background is (partly) transparent
how: glass over bright footage needs a dark scrim and a dark base like rgba(15,16,22,.78) with blur(22px).

name: Light text on bright walls
what: light text on a bright wall fails contrast; use a deep colour with a light glow or caption over the darker lower frame with a gradient veil
how: `#6e0c20` with a soft glow, or a bottom gradient veil.

name: Gradients band on dark grounds
what: full-screen linear gradients on dark grounds band under H.264; use a radial gradient, a solid, or a solid plus a local glow
how: choose a radial glow behind a keyed subject on a dark plate.

name: Blur only the colour before keying
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: Blender's Keying pre-process blurs only colour (luminosity intact) to cut colour noise, and it affects the matte only, not the result image
how: key a copy whose U/V planes are blurred, apply the matte to the original: `[k]format=yuv444p,gblur=sigma=2:planes=6,chromakey=0x00b140:0.12:0.05,format=yuva444p,alphaextract[m];[o][m]alphamerge` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: IBK screen range
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: lower IBK's screen range until it stops changing the background; if too much noise remains in the backing, degrain before pulling the key; this may also harden matte edges
how: in ffmpeg, denoise the key branch (`hqdn3d`) rather than raising similarity.

name: IBK luminance match
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: luminance match adds a luminance factor that captures transparent foreground areas brighter than the background and can firm up alpha in light areas; pushed too far it eats foreground blacks
how: watch the darkest foreground parts in the matte when you add any luma term to a key.

name: IBK autolevels for supersaturated colours
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: autolevels removes hard edges from strongly saturated foreground colours (a red subject on blue gives a magenta transition); keep yellow/cyan/magenta boxes for real foreground colours
how: in the numpy PIK, check saturated edges separately before trusting a single weight setting.

name: Alpha bias for an impure screen
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: when the screen colour is not pure (strong global cast), PIK/Keylight's Alpha Bias normalises colours by a grey-reference colour before computing alpha; pick it from the foreground area that went transparent. Despill Bias (often skin or hair colour) can be set separately
how: divide A and B by the bias colour in the numpy PIK before the alpha formula.

name: Keylight screen gain
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: Screen Gain sets how much screen colour is removed to make the matte; increasing it keys more
how: the closest knob in ffmpeg's chromakey is similarity: raise it in small steps.

name: Inside-mask replace colour
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: when an inside mask raises alpha, Keylight can leave the despilled image (None), bring back the original pixel (Source) or add a replace colour (Hard Color, or Soft Color which keeps the original luminance)
how: after a core matte, check the patched area does not show the screen colour.

name: Acceptance and suppression angles
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: Natron's ChromaKeyer suppresses foreground colours only inside the acceptance angle (default 120); inside the suppression angle (default 40, at most a third of acceptance) chrominance is zeroed against noise; Key Lift raises fewer background pixels, Key Gain lowered classifies more
how: the angle model is Keith Jack's; ffmpeg's chromakey uses a similarity distance instead.

name: Pick an output mode on purpose
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: keyers can output Intermediate (source colour + key, for multipass), Premultiplied, Unpremultiplied, or a Composite over the background; a premultiplied result must be merged with a premultiplied over
how: ffmpeg: straight alpha from chromakey, `premultiply=inplace=1` for premultiplied, `overlay` for the composite.

name: PIKColor clean-plate workflow
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: feed PIKColor the same (denoised) screen as PIK's PFg, then while watching PIK's alpha lower darks.g (green screen) until the garbage area changes, and back off one step; give both nodes the same inside mask
how: the numpy equivalent is building the plate from screen-only pixels before the PIK formula.

name: Key and despill as two jobs
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: separating matte generation from spill correction gives more control: the key's alpha merges the despilled foreground over the new background
how: branch: `split[a][b]`, alpha from `[a]chromakey...alphaextract`, colour from `[b]despill`, then `alphamerge`.

name: Why per-pixel colour is not enough
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: good keyers use more than the pixel's colour: its position, neighbours, reference images, a statistical colour model and user masks; another family finds a 2D path between foreground and background (active contours)
how: add garbage/core mattes and a clean plate before pushing similarity further.

name: Angle-based chroma key controls
section: More keying controls worth knowing (Keylight, IBK, PIK, ChromaKeyer)
what: Blender's Chroma Key: Minimum is a colour-wheel angle of tolerance, Maximum sets what counts as pure background, Falloff softens the edge
how: these map to the idea of similarity (tolerance) and blend (falloff) in ffmpeg's chromakey.

name: Fade a keyed layer by its alpha
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: Blender's Alpha Over fade-in animates the Factor 0 -> 1; in ffmpeg the fade filter's alpha=1 fades only the alpha channel
how: `[1:v]chromakey=0x00b140:0.12:0.05,fade=t=in:st=0:d=1:alpha=1[fg];[0:v][fg]overlay` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Grain extract and grain merge
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: grain-extract is B - A + 0.5 and grain-merge B + A - 0.5, a way to lift texture from one plate and lay it on another; ffmpeg's blend has both modes
how: `[1:v][0:v]blend=all_mode=grainextract` and `blend=all_mode=grainmerge` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Graduated blend between two plates
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: blend expressions mix two layers by position; the docs' linear transition is A*(X/W)+B*(1-X/W). A vertical version blends a sky plate into the ground plate
how: `[0:v][1:v]blend=all_expr='A*(Y/H)+B*(1-Y/H)'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Soft radial matte
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: the geq docs build a radial gradient with gauss(); use it as a soft round matte for maskedmerge
how: `nullsrc=s=320x180:d=2,geq=lum='255*gauss((X/W-0.5)*3)*gauss((Y/H-0.5)*3)/gauss(0)/gauss(0)',format=gray` then `[a][b][m]maskedmerge` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Transparent colour layer
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: the overlay docs add a translucent colour layer with color=red@.3 at the main input's size, a quick way to tint a plate toward the foreground's light
how: `color=color=0x203060@0.3:size=320x180:d=2[over];[0:v][over]overlay` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Premultiply by a separate matte
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: premultiply can use the first plane of a second stream as alpha (same size and pixel format)
how: `[0:v]format=yuv444p[c];[1:v]format=yuv444p[m];[c][m]premultiply` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Clone a person with a locked-off split
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: in-camera multiple exposure records one part of the frame at a time (Buster Keaton played nine people at once); the actions must match. With a locked camera, two takes and a split do the same
how: `[1:v]crop=160:180:0:0[l];[0:v][l]overlay=x=0:y=0` (left half of take B over take A) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Static split matte for a set extension
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: a static matte has the same shape every frame (actors in front of a store, a city above the roof: one mask above the roofline, one below); a travelling matte changes per frame
how: soft horizontal split: `geq=lum='if(lt(Y,80),255,0)',format=gray,gblur=sigma=3` as the maskedmerge mask (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pull the alpha plane with extractplanes
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: extractplanes accepts 'a', so it can pull alpha as a grey stream like alphaextract
how: `format=rgba,extractplanes=a` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Chain overlays in cascade
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: the overlay docs build a 2x2 layout by chaining overlays, each adding one layer to the previous result (test the speed of long chains)

name: Float EXR for pre-rendered plates
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: Nuke recommends EXR for a pre-rendered IBKColor plate because 8-bit formats lose colour information; ffmpeg can write EXR
how: `ffmpeg -i plate.png -vf format=gbrapf32le -c:v exr plate.exr` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Where seamlessClone puts the patch
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: p is where the centre of the source is placed in the destination; an empty mask means all-non-zero; the result has the destination's size and type
how: `cv2.seamlessClone(src,dst,mask,(160,90),cv2.NORMAL_CLONE)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Tracker trade-offs from the refresh
section: More compositing building blocks in ffmpeg
what: MIL updates a classifier online and reduces small box errors, but wrong self-updates can drift and full occlusion or moves beyond the search window are hard; NanoTrack keeps a fixed template and searches locally; a returned box is not proof of accuracy
how: re-initialise MIL on a fresh box after occlusions and check boxes against frames.

name: Retroreflective screen with an LED ring
what: a retroreflective curtain lit only by a ring of LEDs around the lens needs no big screen lights or rigging (practical since blue and green LEDs)
how: an option for small rooms where two softboxes do not fit.

name: Give the talent a monitor
what: weather presenters use a field monitor beside the screen to see where their hands are, or a faint image projected onto the screen
how: show the presenter the composite on a laptop when they must point at inserted graphics.

name: Patterned backdrop for difference mattes
what: a background with a repeating pattern avoids many difference-matte problems and is less sensitive to wardrobe colour than a solid backdrop
how: when no green screen exists, shoot a patterned wall plus a clean plate.

name: Extend the set beyond the screen
what: compositing software can take the screen colour at the backing's edges and extend it to fill the frame, so subjects in a small area can sit in a large virtual vista
how: treat everything outside the screen as garbage: black it out in the matte (drawbox on the matte) so the new plate shows there.

name: Shade the lens against stray flare
what: a light just outside the frame causes washed-out haze; a lens hood, a gobo or barn doors on the light, or a filter reduce it
how: flag lights that hit the lens on owner shoots; add flares later on purpose instead.

name: Match a handheld plate with camera-shake
what: the registry's `camera-shake` gives procedural handheld, telephoto and rig shake for any wrapper (nine measured profiles, seek-safe), useful when a still or keyed layer must sit in a handheld plate
how: `npx hyperframes add camera-shake`, then apply it to the wrapper that holds the composite.
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Feathered spotlight mask block
what: `yt-feather-highlight` dims the frame except a feathered ellipse whose position and size are CSS variables, so a helper can glide it between targets
how: `npx hyperframes add yt-feather-highlight`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Mask-reveal blocks
what: `svg-mask-reveal` reveals media through an editable SVG wordmark mask; `texture-mask-text` uses CSS luminance masks (66 masks from ambientCG maps) to cut holes in letters
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "mask reveal"`
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: Real aperture bokeh pull
what: `rack-focus` pulls focus from a near to a far subject with hard-edged aperture bokeh on the defocused one
how: `npx hyperframes add rack-focus` when a composite needs a focus shift.
refs: repo: npx hyperframes catalog v0.8.191, checked 2026-10-24

name: SAM point prompts in rembg
what: the sam model takes prompts through extra JSON, e.g. a foreground point: `-x '{"sam_prompt": [{"type": "point", "data": [724, 740], "label": 1}]}'`
how: needs the sam encoder/decoder download (missing here) and a working rembg CLI.

name: rembg on OpenCV frames
what: remove() also accepts a NumPy array (as cv2.imread gives), so frames read with cv2.VideoCapture go straight in; the result is a 4-channel array
how: `out=remove(frame, session=new_session("u2netp"))` returned shape (180, 320, 4) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Propagate GrabCut through a clip
what: GrabCut accepts a mask initialisation (GC_INIT_WITH_MASK), so the previous frame's labels can seed the next frame as probable foreground/background
how: `m=np.where((m==1)|(m==3),cv2.GC_PR_FGD,cv2.GC_PR_BGD).astype(np.uint8); cv2.grabCut(f,m,None,bgd,fgd,2,cv2.GC_INIT_WITH_MASK)`; on the synthetic clip the foreground shrank from 10000 to 5899 px in four frames, so check every few frames (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Evaluate a static overlay position once
what: eval=init evaluates x/y only at init (or when a command arrives); t and n are NAN then, so use it only for fixed positions
how: `overlay=x=W-w-10:y=H-h-10:eval=init` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stop showing the last overlay frame
what: repeatlast (default on) extends the last frame of the secondary input past its end; repeatlast=0 lets it disappear
how: `[1:v]trim=0:1,...[fg];[0:v][fg]overlay=repeatlast=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: alphamerge inside one -vf chain with movie
what: the alphamerge docs read the matte with the movie source inside the filtergraph: `movie=in_alpha.mkv [alpha]; [in][alpha] alphamerge [out]`
how: `-vf "movie=matte.mp4,format=gray[alpha];[in][alpha]alphamerge,format=yuva420p"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Smooth a track before it drives anything
what: Natron's Tracker can smooth translation, rotation and scale by averaging N frames and uses a 10-frame jitter period for remove/add jitter; an edge-padded moving average does the same on a tracked CSV
how: `np.convolve(np.pad(c,(r,r),'edge'),np.ones(2*r+1)/(2*r+1),'same')[r:-r]` (as in the stabiliser test) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Filter flare ghosts
what: photographic filters can add flare, especially ghosts of bright lights; drop the filter, use a better one, or stop down
how: for night shoots with practical lights, take filters off the lens.

name: VitTrack's score tells you when the track is lost
what: the opencv_zoo VitTrack model returns confidence values during tracking, and the score drops sharply when the target is lost, while NanoTrack returns about 0.9 in any situation
how: needs vitTracker.onnx (missing); with it, `t=cv2.TrackerVit_create(p)` and read `t.getTrackingScore()` per frame.

name: CapCut speed limits in ffmpeg terms
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: CapCut's Normal speed slider runs 0.1x to 100x; its Curve (velocity) graph runs from 0.1x (bottom) to 10x (top)
how: speed s = `setpts=PTS/s`; 0.1x: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "trim=0:0.3,setpts=10*(PTS-STARTPTS)" -an out.mp4`; trim first so a 10x slow-down doesn't make a huge file (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: "Keep Pitch" = atempo, chained past 2x
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: CapCut's Keep Pitch keeps the voice pitch when speeding up; ffmpeg's atempo does the same, accepts 0.5-100, but above 2 it skips samples, so chain instances
how: 4x with pitch kept: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]setpts=PTS/4[v];[0:a]atempo=2,atempo=2[a]" -map "[v]" -map "[a]" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Name the CapCut curve preset the client means
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: CapCut's Speed > Curve templates are Montage, Hero, Bullet, Jump Cut, Flash In and Flash Out (plus Custom), and each can be opened with Edit to adjust
how: when a client says "Hero curve" or "Bullet", ask for a reference clip or rebuild it as a fast-slow-fast segment list (next skill) and show them; don't guess the preset's shape from its name.

name: Custom velocity curve as a segment list
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: in CapCut's Custom curve, dragging a point sideways sets how long the effect lasts and up/down sets the pace (top speeds up, bottom slows down)
how: write the curve as (start, end, speed) rows and concat: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]trim=0:0.6,setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/3[a];[0:v]trim=0.6:1.0,setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)*2[b];[0:v]trim=1.0:2,setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/3[c];[a][b][c]concat=n=3:v=1:a=0,fps=30" out.mp4` (3x, 0.5x, 3x) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: "Smooth slow mo" only where the clip is slow
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: CapCut's custom curve has a "Smooth slow mo" checkbox for the point you want to emphasise
how: interpolate only the slow segment: in the segment list above make the middle row `setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)*3,minterpolate=fps=30:mi_mode=mci`; the fast rows need no interpolation (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CapCut "Style > Velocity" presets are effect + music
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: the mobile Style > Velocity presets (flash, retro zoom, fade blur, blur shake, rainbow...) wait to detect music before applying
how: our equivalent is beat times first (`npx hyperframes beats`, file `beats/<audio>.json`), then one effect per beat (flash, zoom punch, blur pulse, hue cycle: see the beat section); we can't reproduce CapCut's exact presets, only the idea.

name: Velocity points sit on the music
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: CapCut's own tip for syncing a velocity edit: add the track first, then place the curve's points where the speed should change, on the music
how: take the segment boundaries of the segment-list skill from the beat file (beat index × 60/BPM, rounded per index, never accumulated)

name: VN and InShot have the same tool
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: VN offers speed "presets or advanced curve-based speed ramps"; InShot offers speed control, "speed ramping" and "smooth slow-mo"
how: a VN/InShot speed-ramp brief is the same job as a CapCut curve: build it with the segment list and minterpolate for the slow part.
refs: VN on the App Store, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/vn-video-editor/id1343581380, checked 2026-10-24
InShot on the App Store, https://apps.apple.com/in/app/inshot-ai-video-editor/id997362197, checked 2026-10-24

name: Forward, back, forward (time-remap rewind)
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: AE time remapping can play a walk forward, a few frames backward ("the person retreats"), then forward again
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]trim=0:1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a];[0:v]trim=0.6:1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,reverse[b];[0:v]trim=0.6:2,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[c];[a][b][c]concat=n=3:v=1:a=0" out.mp4` (reverse only the short middle piece: reverse buffers it in memory) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Time-stretching and time-remapping", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/time-stretching-time-remapping.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Read a speed graph: height is speed
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: in AE's speed graph level lines are constant speed and higher means faster; in the motion path, wider dot spacing means faster and Hold keys show no dots
how: to see a GSAP ease as a speed graph, sample its slope: `const e=gsap.parseEase('power3.out'); speed_i=(e((i+1)/10)-e(i/10))*10` gave 3.44 2.47 1.70 ... 0.00 (fast start, dead stop) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Alight curve axes: slope = speed
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: in Alight Motion's curve editor the X axis is project time, Y is the remapped animation time, the slope is the speed (steeper = faster), and there is one curve per pair of keyframes (keyframes − 1)
how: read a client's Alight screenshot the same way as a GSAP ease graph; in GSAP give each segment its own ease (separate tweens or per-keyframe eases).
refs: Alight Motion Help "Animation Easing Curves", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536934703889-Animation-Easing-Curves, checked 2026-10-24

name: "Paste Curve to All Keyframes" = timeline defaults
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: Alight can paste one easing curve onto every keyframe pair of a property
how: GSAP `gsap.timeline({defaults:{ease:'power2.inOut',duration:1}})` pushes the ease into every child tween (child values still override); checked: x at 25% progress = 6.25 = power2.inOut(0.25)×100 (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Alight Motion Help "Animation Easing Curves", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536934703889-Animation-Easing-Curves, checked 2026-10-24

name: Alight "Cyclic" easing = wrapYoyo
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: Alight's Cyclic easing repeats the progression between the two key values, back and forth or one way
how: for a value (or a frame index) that ping-pongs inside a span use `gsap.utils.wrapYoyo(0,3,i)` → 0,1,2,3,2,1,0,1,2 for i=0..8; plain cycling is `gsap.utils.wrap` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Alight Motion Help "Animation Easing Curves", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536934703889-Animation-Easing-Curves, checked 2026-10-24

name: AE linear() = mapRange + clamp
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: AE `linear(t, tMin, tMax, value1, value2)` maps t into a value range (e.g. `linear(time, 0, 6, 20, 80)`) and holds at the ends
how: `gsap.utils.clamp(20,80,gsap.utils.mapRange(0,6,20,80,t))` → 50 at t=3, 80 at t=9; mapRange alone does not clamp (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: AE ease() = parseEase + interpolate
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: AE `ease(t, tMin, tMax, value1, value2)` is the eased version of linear()
how: `const e=gsap.parseEase('sine.inOut'); v=gsap.utils.interpolate(v1,v2,e(clamp(0,1,(t-tMin)/(tMax-tMin))))` → 0, 50, 100 at t=0,1,2 for 0..2 s (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: AE posterizeTime(fps) for one property
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: `posterizeTime(1); random()` updates a property only once per second while the comp runs at full rate
how: in a GSAP/HyperFrames driver quantise the time you feed the formula: `tq=Math.floor(t*8)/8` (8 updates a second: 0.01→0, 0.13→0.125, 0.26→0.25) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Velocity-matched hard cut
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: registry `cut-the-curve`: the outgoing subject accelerates with power4.in, the cut happens at peak velocity, and the incoming subject continues the same direction with power4.out
how: `npx hyperframes add cut-the-curve`, or by hand: last tween of shot A `ease:'power4.in'`, first tween of shot B `ease:'power4.out'`, same direction, cut between them.

name: Beat-driven ramp + freeze + cut block
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: registry block `beat-freeze-cut` is "a beat-driven speed ramp, freeze-frame hit, and hard-cut sequence for music-led promos and montages"
how: `npx hyperframes add beat-freeze-cut` and point its beats at the music's beat file instead of rebuilding the sequence.

name: Whip rail that overshoots and snaps
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: registry `velocity-throw-snap`: a five-shot rail whips past on a fast decaying curve, overshoots and snaps the hero shot to centre
how: `npx hyperframes add velocity-throw-snap` for a "which one is it" product/feature pick.

name: "Never fully lands" arrival
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: registry `extended-keyframe`: an element covers most of its move in the first fifth of the duration, creeps the rest to the last frame, exits along its arrival vector and carries shutter blur
how: `npx hyperframes add extended-keyframe` (it also exports the ease alone for any tween).

name: Full-frame whip with matched speed
section: Velocity edits and speed curves (CapCut, VN, InShot, AE, Alight)
what: registry `whip-pan-cut`: scene A whips off with capped directional blur while B enters the same way at matched velocity on a speed-ramp profile; both ride one strip so seam velocity is exact
how: `npx hyperframes add whip-pan-cut`, fill its before/after slots.

name: AE wiggle(freq, amp) as a crop shake
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: `wiggle(freq, amp)` shakes a property about freq times a second by about amp units; CapCut's Camera Shake has the same two controls (intensity, speed)
how: overscan, then move the crop window with sines at roughly freq Hz: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "scale=704:396,crop=640:360:'32+20*sin(2*PI*5*t)':'18+12*sin(2*PI*4.3*t+1)'" out.mp4` (two different frequencies so x and y never line up) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Overscan = twice the shake amplitude
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: crop's x must stay between 0 and in_w−out_w, so a ±A px shake needs A px of extra picture on each side
how: scale up by 2A first (640→704 for ±32, 360→396 for ±18) and centre the crop at x=A, y=A; registry `camera-shake` solves this per frame including rotation (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/camera-shake.html` (`npx hyperframes add camera-shake`), checked 2026-10-24

name: The ffmpeg doc shake zooms 2x
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: the crop docs' "trembling" and "erratic camera" examples crop to in_w/2 × in_h/2 and swing across the remaining half
how: the doc line `crop=in_w/2:in_h/2:(in_w-out_w)/2+((in_w-out_w)/2)*sin(t*10):(in_h-out_h)/2+((in_h-out_h)/2)*sin(t*13),scale=640:360` works but doubles the zoom and swings ±25% of the frame: for a subtle shake use the small-overscan form above (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: wiggle octaves = summed harmonics
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: `wiggle(5, 20, 3, .5)` adds two finer layers at 10 and 20 Hz with 10 and 5 px; amp_mult near 1 keeps detail, near 0 removes it
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Shake on one axis only
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: the AE example `w = wiggle(freq,amp); [value[0], w[1]]` wiggles only y
how: keep x fixed: `scale=704:396,crop=640:360:32:'18+16*sin(2*PI*3*t)'` (bass-drop bounce, footsteps) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Uniform scale wiggle
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: the AE example `v = wiggle(5, 10); [v[0], v[0]]` wiggles scale by the same amount on both axes
how: zoompan on video with d=1: `zoompan=z='1.06+0.03*sin(2*PI*5*it)':d=1:x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':s=640x360:fps=30` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Stepped jitter (posterizeTime + wiggle / Alight Random Jitter)
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: AE posterizeTime lowers a property's update rate; Alight's Random Jitter "jumps the layer randomly back and forth", unlike Random Displacement, which moves "smoothly but randomly"
how: hold each offset for 1/8 s with a hashed floor: `crop=640:360:'32+20*sin(floor(t*8)*12.9898)':'18+12*sin(floor(t*8)*78.233)'` after `scale=704:396` (deterministic, re-renders identically) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Shake only for a window
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: CapCut's Basic > Shake is added as an effect clip whose duration you drag
how: gate the amplitude with between(): `crop=640:360:'32+24*between(t,0.5,1.2)*sin(2*PI*9*t)':'18+14*between(t,0.5,1.2)*sin(2*PI*7*t)'` after `scale=704:396` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Shake that ramps up (or dies out)
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: Alight's Oscillate tip: keyframe Magnitude from or to zero to make a shake transition
how: multiply the amplitude by an envelope: in `min(1,t/0.5)` (up over 0.5 s) or out `exp(-8*(t-T0))`; tested `crop=640:360:'32+25*min(1,t/0.5)*sin(2*PI*8*t)':18` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hit shake that decays on every beat
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: a FlexClip CapCut tutorial shakes on the beat points of the music
how: restart a decaying shake at each beat (0.5 s = 120 BPM): `crop=640:360:'32+30*exp(-8*mod(t,0.5))*sin(2*PI*14*t)':'18+18*exp(-8*mod(t,0.5))*sin(2*PI*11*t)'` after `scale=704:396` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Beat bounce: down on one beat, up on the next
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: FlexClip's manual CapCut shake: zoom in, keyframe the clip down on the first beat and up on the second, repeat in pairs
how: `crop=640:360:32:'18+14*(1-2*mod(floor(t/0.5),2))'` after `scale=704:396` (hard jumps each 0.5 s beat); in GSAP the same is `tl.set(wrapper,{y:±14},beatTime)` per beat (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Alight Oscillate in numbers
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: Oscillate moves the layer back and forth: Angle 0º = horizontal (right first), 90º = vertical (down first); Frequency in Hz (1 = back home after exactly 1 s); Magnitude = max distance in px (default 25 at 45º, 2 Hz)

name: Triangle-wave oscillation = zig-zag
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: Oscillate's Triangle wave moves at constant speed with an abrupt reversal; Alight suggests it perpendicular to a move for zig-zag motion
how: triangle of period 0.5 s: `crop=640:360:'32+25*(2*abs(2*(2*t-floor(2*t+0.5)))-1)':18` after `scale=704:396`; in GSAP a finite `repeat:N, yoyo:true, ease:'none'` (HyperFrames forbids `repeat: -1`) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Swing (rotation shake) from the rotate docs
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: Alight Swing "rotates the layer back and forth"; ffmpeg's rotate docs give the oscillation form A*sin(2*PI/T*t)
how: overscan so corners never show: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "scale=736:414,rotate=0.04*sin(2*PI*1.5*t),crop=640:360" out.mp4` (±0.04 rad ≈ 2.3°) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spin with no black corners
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: rotate's doc example `rotate=2*PI*t:ow='min(iw,ih)/sqrt(2)':oh=ow:c=none` shrinks the output so no background shows (Alight Spin = constant spin)
how: with libx264/yuv420p the doc's size is odd (254.5 px) and the encoder refuses it; round to even: `rotate=2*PI*t/4:ow='trunc(min(iw,ih)/sqrt(2)/2)*2':oh=ow:c=none` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stabilise first, then add the shake you want
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: Miracamp's CapCut advice: stabilise to remove unwanted shake, then add a controlled shake for style; CapCut's stabiliser zooms in slightly
how: `vidstabdetect=result=tr.trf` pass, then `vidstabtransform=input=tr.trf:smoothing=10,scale=704:396,crop=640:360:'32+15*sin(2*PI*6*t)':'18+9*sin(2*PI*5*t)'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Yoyo shake legs must be whole frames
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: the repo's core-GSAP shake is a short tween with repeat + yoyo (GSAP's "rough" ease isn't in core)
how: `tl.to(wrap,{x:8,duration:0.04,repeat:7,yoyo:true,ease:'none'})` ends exactly at rest (x=0 after the odd repeat count), but at 30 fps a 0.04 s leg aliases (sampled x per frame: 0, 6.7, 2.7, 4.0, 5.3...): use leg durations that are whole frames (1/30 s) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: camera-shake: nine measured profiles
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: registry component `camera-shake` gives handheld (normal, wide-angle, telephoto; mild/strong/extreme) and rig (6D shake "engine buzz", 6D wobble) profiles with an intensity multiplier 0-3 and a frequency multiplier 0.1-4
how: `npx hyperframes add camera-shake`, wrap the shot in `.camera-shake-frame > .camera-shake-rig`, then `cameraShake(tl, "#shot", { profile: "handheld-tele-mild", duration: 8 })`
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/camera-shake.html` (`npx hyperframes add camera-shake`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Long lens = smaller angular shake
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: camera-shake's profile table: wide-angle carries 12° on X where telephoto carries 4°, "because a long lens magnifies angular jitter"; keep the 3x ratio
how: pick the profile from the shot's look (wide vlog vs zoomed-in), not by taste; a hand-written shake on a tight shot needs less amplitude.
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/camera-shake.html` (`npx hyperframes add camera-shake`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Seek-safe shake: drive it from a property setter
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: camera-shake computes every value as a closed form of t and runs it from a setter on a tweened driver object, because GSAP suppresses onUpdate on seek() and the shake would freeze on frame 0
how: `tl.to(driver,{t:dur,duration:dur,ease:'none'})` with `driver` defining `set t(v){ applyShake(v) }`; no accumulators, no unseeded random
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/camera-shake.html` (`npx hyperframes add camera-shake`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Depth layers make a shake read as a camera
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: inside the camera-shake rig, layers can carry `data-cs-z="-800"` to sit at a depth, so they parallax instead of sliding flat
how: split a still or a cutout scene into 2-3 layers with different data-cs-z values before shaking.
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/camera-shake.html` (`npx hyperframes add camera-shake`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Three-frame landing shake
section: Shake presets (AE wiggle, CapCut Shake, Alight Oscillate/Jitter)
what: registry `headline-slam`: a heavy headline scales down into frame, lands with a deterministic three-frame shake, holds with subtle drift, whips up on exit
how: `npx hyperframes add headline-slam` for impact titles instead of a long wiggle.

name: AE Glow = threshold, radius, intensity
what: Glow brightens pixels above Glow Threshold, spreads them by Glow Radius (px) and scales by Glow Intensity
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]format=gbrp,split[o][g];[g]lutrgb=r='if(gt(val,180),val,0)':g='if(gt(val,180),val,0)':b='if(gt(val,180),val,0)',gblur=sigma=15[gl];[o][gl]blend=all_mode=screen" out.mp4` (threshold in the lutrgb, radius = sigma, intensity = add `colorlevels`/a second screen pass) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Horizontal-only glow (anamorphic streak)
what: AE Glow Dimensions can be horizontal, vertical or both
how: gblur has separate sigma (horizontal) and sigmaV: `...lutrgb=...(gt(val,200)...),gblur=sigma=40:sigmaV=0.5[gl];[o][gl]blend=all_mode=screen` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Glow in float so it doesn't clip
what: AE notes glows look brighter and more real in 32-bpc because the high range keeps glow values from clipping
how: run the glow branch in float: `[0:v]format=gbrpf32le,split[o][g];[g]gblur=sigma=15[gl];[o][gl]blend=all_mode=addition:all_opacity=0.6,format=yuv420p` (blend accepted gbrpf32le here) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Glow behind a cutout or text (backlight)
what: AE Glow's Composite Original "Behind" puts the glow behind the image; glows based on alpha make brightness only at the edges
how: in HyperFrames put CSS `filter: drop-shadow(0 0 18px #ffd27a)` on the cutout/text: drop-shadow is a blurred copy of the element's alpha mask drawn below it (stack two for a stronger halo)

name: Alight Light Glow numbers
what: Light Glow glows pixels above a luminance threshold (default 0.7), Diffusion = softness (default 0.25), Intensity 1 = light areas don't get brighter, they only spill into darker neighbours
how: threshold 0.7 ≈ lutrgb `gt(val,178)`; keep the screen blend at 1 pass for "intensity 1", add passes only when they ask for blown highlights.

name: Dark Glow (Alight)
what: Dark Glow makes dark blooms from pixels under a luminance threshold (default 0.3)
how: invert, glow the (now bright) darks, invert back: `[0:v]format=gbrp,negate,split[o][g];[g]lutrgb=...gt(val,180)...,gblur=sigma=15[gl];[o][gl]blend=all_mode=screen,negate` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Edge Glow (Alight)
what: Edge Glow "detects edges in a photo or video and creates a glow around them" (Threshold up = fewer edges)
how: `[0:v]format=gbrp,split[o][e];[e]edgedetect=low=0.1:high=0.3:mode=colormix,gblur=sigma=6[g];[o][g]blend=all_mode=screen`; raise edgedetect low/high for fewer edges (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Soft Glow contrast squeezes glow out of the darks
what: Alight Soft Glow's Contrast raises the light/dark contrast of the blurred copy before blending, so dark areas stop glowing
how: add `eq=contrast=1.6` to the blurred branch: `[g]gblur=sigma=20,eq=contrast=1.6[gl];[o][gl]blend=all_mode=softlight` (tested command; blend mode is our choice) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Glow is not a default
what: the HyperFrames spec bans glow, bloom, neon, lens flares and glowing orbs "by default"
how: add glow only when the brief or the shot calls for it (a neon sign, a night scene, "glow wala text"), never as decoration on every title.

name: Neon lower third
what: registry `lt-neon-border`: two arcs of light travel a rounded panel's edge and snap corner to corner with a soft three-layer bloom
how: `npx hyperframes add lt-neon-border` for a gaming/night-event name strap.

name: Neon caption style
what: registry `caption-neon-glow` (cyan and magenta glow with keyword accent colours) and `caption-neon-accent` (multi-colour neon accents with wiggle drift)
how: `npx hyperframes add caption-neon-glow` for gaming captions instead of hand-stacking text-shadows.

name: Alight RGB Split = rgbashift with opposite offsets
what: RGB Split keeps one channel fixed and shifts the other two in opposite directions
how: keep green, push red left and blue right: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "rgbashift=rh=-8:bh=8" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: rgbashift edge mode on ffmpeg 6.1 is "wrap", not "warp"
what: the current docs list edge = smear, default or warp; this container's 6.1 accepts only smear (default) and wrap (`ffmpeg -h filter=rgbashift`)
how: `rgbashift=rh=-30:bv=20:edge=wrap` makes pixels pushed off one side reappear on the other (a harder glitch than smear) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Animate the split with sendcmd
what: rgbashift supports all its options as commands, so a split can jump on and off at set times
how: `-vf "sendcmd=c='0.5 rgbashift rh -20, rgbashift bh 20; 0.7 rgbashift rh 0, rgbashift bh 0',rgbashift"`; inside one interval separate commands with commas and don't repeat the time (writing the time again fails to parse) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Shift Channels = channel swap
what: Shift Channels replaces R, G, B (and alpha) with values taken from other channels
how: swap red and blue: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "colorchannelmixer=rr=0:rb=1:bb=0:br=1" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Invert one channel (AE Invert / Alight Invert)
what: AE Invert can invert RGB, a single Red/Green/Blue channel, HLS or YIQ channels; Alight's Invert flips R, G or B independently
how: negate takes components, but r/g/b only work on RGB input: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "format=rgb24,negate=components=r" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Glitch only in short windows
