what: CapCut's glitch effects are dragged onto the clip for a chosen duration
how: most ffmpeg filters take `enable`: `-vf "rgbashift=rh=-16:bh=16:enable='between(t,0.5,0.7)+between(t,1.5,1.7)',shufflepixels=m=block:w=40:h=20:enable='between(t,0.55,0.65)'"`; `ffmpeg -h filter=NAME` prints "support for timeline" when enable works (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: RGB-split wipe
what: registry `chromatic-aberration-wipe`: a fast slide wipe with RGB channel split on the peak frames; its Aberration control multiplies the red/cyan split (0 removes it)
how: `npx hyperframes add chromatic-aberration-wipe`

name: Glitch caption style
what: registry `caption-glitch-rgb`: RGB chromatic aberration with a CRT scanline overlay, as a caption style
how: `npx hyperframes add caption-glitch-rgb` for tech/cyber captions.

name: Scan band reveal
what: registry `scan-band`: a diagonal distortion band sweeps once across a wordmark, showing clipped red and cyan offsets only inside the band
how: `npx hyperframes add scan-band` for a logo sting with a single glitch pass.

name: Chromatic radial split shader
what: registry block `chromatic-radial-split` is a shader transition with a chromatic-aberration radial split
how: `npx hyperframes add chromatic-radial-split` between two scenes.

name: Block shuffle (Alight Tile Shift look)
what: shufflepixels reorders pixels in horizontal, vertical or block mode with a block size and seed; Alight's Tile Shift shifts the contents of grid tiles randomly
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "shufflepixels=m=block:w=32:h=32:s=3" out.mp4` (keep it to a few frames with enable) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: shufflepixels "inverse" didn't undo the shuffle here
what: the docs say the seed lets you reverse a shuffle with the same parameters and direction=inverse
how: on 6.1 a forward+inverse pair with the same seed in one graph did not restore the picture (lossless check, max difference 231): don't plan a "glitch in, glitch back out" on that; animate enable instead. (tested here 2026-10-24)  NOTE 2026-10-24: #5414 (file 21) tested inverse bit-exact when the block size divides the frame size (8x8 on 640x360; 16x16 did not) — use that.

name: Swap two rectangles on some frames
what: swaprect swaps two w×h rectangles; its expressions are evaluated once per frame
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "swaprect=w=200:h=40:x1=0:y1=60:x2=300:y2=220:enable='lt(mod(n,10),2)'" out.mp4` (2 frames out of every 10) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Nervous frame order
what: `random` flushes cached frames out in random order (cache 2-512, default 30), inspired by frei0r "nervous"; no frame is dropped
how: `-vf "random=frames=6:seed=7"`: a small cache keeps the jumble local; set seed for repeatable renders (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Two-frame swap stutter
what: shuffleframes remaps frame indexes; the doc example `shuffleframes=0 2 1` swaps the 2nd and 3rd frame of every three
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "shuffleframes=0 2 1" out.mp4` for a subtle broken-playback twitch (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Noise: colour vs mono
what: AE Noise with "Use Color Noise" adds different random values to R, G and B; otherwise the same value goes to all channels
how: colour: `noise=alls=25:allf=t+u` (t = changes every frame, u = uniform); mono: noise only on the luma plane `noise=c0s=30:c0f=t` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Noise and Grain effects", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/apply-effects-and-animation-presets/list-of-effects/noise-grain-effects.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Alight Block Noise
what: Block Noise multiplies random rectangular noise blocks (Size default 20, Strength 0-1 default 0.25) into the layer
how: make low-res noise and scale it up with nearest neighbour, then multiply at 0.25: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=32x18:r=30,geq=lum='random(1)*255':cb=128:cr=128,scale=640:360:flags=neighbor" -filter_complex "[0:v]format=yuv444p[a];[1:v]format=yuv444p[b];[a][b]blend=all_mode=multiply:all_opacity=0.25:shortest=1" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Line tear with a displacement map
what: displace moves pixels by a second (x) and third (y) input; the repo's VHS Playback treatment keeps its line tear (digitalGlitchLineTear) at 0.04-0.1
how: an x-map that is 128 everywhere except a moving band: `-f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=640x360:r=30,geq=lum='128+if(between(Y,100+50*sin(T*7),130+50*sin(T*7)),60,0)':cb=128:cr=128"` plus a flat 128 y-map, then `[0:v][x][y]displace=edge=wrap` (escape the commas inside -i as `\,`) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Datamosh step 1: prepare a moshable file
what: datamoshing needs few I-frames and no B-frames (moshy's `prep` converts to "no B-Frames ... as few I-Frames as possible")
how: `ffmpeg -i a.mp4 -i b.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0" -c:v libx264 -bf 0 -g 1000 -sc_threshold 0 -force_key_frames 0,2 mosh_src.mp4` (2 = the cut; this gave exactly 2 keyframes) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Datamosh step 2: drop the keyframe at the cut
what: the noise bitstream filter can drop packets by expression; datamosh-cli's remove-keyframes does the same idea (keeps the first keyframe) so one scene's pixels leak into the next
how: `ffmpeg -i mosh_src.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v "noise=drop='key*gt(pts*tb\,1)'" mosh_raw.mkv` (119 of 120 packets kept, 1 keyframe left); measured: a frame 0.5 s after the cut differed 14 levels from the last frame of A but 56 from the clean frame of B (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Datamosh step 3: bake it
what: moshy's "Bake" re-encodes the corruption as real video so it survives upload and further edits
how: `ffmpeg -i mosh_raw.mkv -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p mosh_baked.mp4`; check the baked file's length (4.03 s here, both shots kept) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Datamosh only between the two shots you choose
what: a mosh happens where a keyframe is removed, so control the cut points, not the whole file
how: force keyframes only at the cuts you want to mosh (`-force_key_frames 2,5.5`) and use `drop='key*between(pts*tb\,1.9\,2.1)'` to drop just one; other cuts stay clean

name: Registry `glitch` shader block
what: registry block `glitch` is a shader transition with digital glitch artifacts
how: `npx hyperframes add glitch` when a CapCut-style "glitch transition" is wanted between two HyperFrames scenes; for footage-only edits use the ffmpeg windows above.

name: Effect only inside a box (feedback)
what: feedback sends a crop of the frame to a second output, lets you filter it, and lays it back on top; the docs pixelize a region this way
how: `-vf "[in][fin]feedback=x=200:y=100:w=200:h=120[out][fout];[fout]pixelize=w=16:h=16[fin]"` (any filter in place of pixelize) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Copy Background = adjustment layer = backdrop-filter
what: Alight's Copy Background turns a layer into an adjustment layer: effects apply only to the background under its shape
how: in HyperFrames give a transparent element `backdrop-filter: blur(8px) hue-rotate(90deg)`: it filters what is painted behind it, up to the nearest backdrop root (an element with clip-path or mask is one)

name: Flash safety check after strobes and glitches
what: photosensitivity reduces flashes for viewers with epilepsy (frames default 30, threshold default 1, lower = stricter)
how: `ffmpeg -i strobe.mp4 -vf "photosensitivity=f=20:t=1" safe.mp4`; on a 0.5 s white strobe it cut the largest frame-to-frame mean jump from 128 to 28 levels: run it on any client piece with strobes (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Time-difference ghost (AE Time Difference)
what: Time Difference compares a layer with a time-offset copy (e.g. 3/30 s); with Absolute Difference, unchanged areas go black and changes glow
how: `-filter_complex "[0:v]split[a][b];[b]setpts=PTS+3/30/TB[d];[a][d]blend=all_mode=difference:shortest=1"`; frame-to-frame version: `tblend=all_mode=difference` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Exaggerate small motion
what: amplify boosts differences between a pixel and the same pixel in nearby frames (radius 1-63, factor, threshold)
how: `-vf "amplify=radius=2:factor=10:threshold=50"` makes moving edges flare while still areas stay; a glitchy "energy" pass for dance/sport clips (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pixel sorting, the original algorithm
what: Kim Asendorf's ASDF Pixel Sort walks every column and then every row, finds runs of pixels past a threshold, and sorts each run by colour value; modes are 0 white, 1 black, 2 bright, 3 dark
how: `python3 pixelsort.py in.png out.png 127` (our numpy port of mode 2, scratchpad `sk2_12/t/py/pixelsort.py`): on a testsrc2 frame it changed 87% of pixels (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pixel sort thresholds
what: the original defaults: brightValue 127 and darkValue 223 (Processing brightness 0-255), whiteValue −12345678 and blackValue −3456789 (packed RGB ints, 0 = white, −16581375 = black)
how: raise the bright threshold to sort only highlights (sky, lights), lower it to smear more of the frame; brightness() is the HSB max of R, G, B (color(0,126,255) → 255)

name: Pixel sort on video
what: the sort is per image, so video means frames out, sort, frames in
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -t 0.2 d/f%04d.png`, run the script on each PNG, `ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i d/f%04d.png -pix_fmt yuv420p out.mp4` (script `sk2_12/t/py/pixelsort_video.sh`): about 0.35 s per 640x360 frame here, so sort only the beat or the hero shot (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Glitch vocabulary from CapCut's own guide
what: CapCut's glitch article lists RGB split from channel manipulation, a wave filter for a classic glitch, pixel sorting and datamoshing as glitch looks, and describes glitches as pixelation, artifacts, flicker and abrupt jumps
how: when a client asks for "glitch", offer these named looks (rgbashift, displace wave, pixel sort, datamosh, pixelize, strobe) and agree on one or two.

name: Scanlines with geq
section: VHS and screen bits (mechanics only; the full VHS look is file 03)
what: every other line darker
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "format=yuv444p,geq=lum='lum(X,Y)*(0.75+0.25*mod(Y,2))':cb='cb(X,Y)':cr='cr(X,Y)'" out.mp4` (slow: geq runs per pixel; tested command, no claim on the look) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Camcorder REC overlay
section: VHS and screen bits (mechanics only; the full VHS look is file 03)
what: registry block `camcorder-hud`: REC, battery, editable date and a timeline-driven counter for creator-camera treatments; InShot's effect list includes a "Retro DV" look
how: `npx hyperframes add camcorder-hud` over the footage instead of drawing a HUD by hand.
refs: InShot on the App Store, https://apps.apple.com/in/app/inshot-ai-video-editor/id997362197, checked 2026-10-24

name: Footage on a physical screen
section: VHS and screen bits (mechanics only; the full VHS look is file 03)
what: registry `yt-screen-warp`: grid, scanline, vignette and sheen overlay plus a 3D-warp wrapper class so footage reads as playing on a display
how: `npx hyperframes add yt-screen-warp` for "TV/monitor" inserts.

name: No radial blur filter in this ffmpeg
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: an `rblur` radial/circular blur filter was proposed on ffmpeg-devel in 2020, and its first version was criticised as aliased; this container's 6.1 has no rblur (`ffmpeg -filters`)
how: for a zoom/spin blur use a HyperFrames shader block (`cinematic-zoom`) or the stacking approximations below.  (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Zoom streaks = scale + blend overlapping frames
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: Alight's Zoom Streaks "creates radial streaks by scaling the layer around a point and blending together overlapping pixels"
how: literally that: zoom a little every frame and average the last frames: `ffmpeg -loop 1 -i still.png -vf "zoompan=z='1+0.01*on':d=1:x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':s=640x360:fps=30,tmix=frames=8" -t 1 -pix_fmt yuv420p out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spin streaks = rotate + blend overlapping frames
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: Alight's Spin Streaks spins the layer around a point and blends the overlapping pixels
how: `ffmpeg -loop 1 -i still.png -vf "rotate=0.08*t*30*PI/180*10,tmix=frames=6" -t 1 -pix_fmt yuv420p out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Radial Blur (Zoom) approximated on a still
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: AE Radial Blur Zoom blurs outward from a centre "simulating a zooming camera" (Spin blurs in arcs)
how: average copies scaled 1.00/1.03/1.06/1.09 and centre-cropped: `[0:v]format=gbrp,split=4[a][b][c][d];[b]scale=iw*1.03:-2,crop=640:360[b2];...[a][b2]blend=all_mode=average[ab];[c2][d2]blend=all_mode=average[cd];[ab][cd]blend=all_mode=average` (tested command only; the look was not judged) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Blur and Sharpen effects", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/apply-effects-and-animation-presets/list-of-effects/blur-sharpen-effects.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: AE Radial Blur (Spin) approximated
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: same idea with rotation
how: copies at `rotate=0.02`, `0.04`, `0.06` rad averaged with blend=average as above (tested command only) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Blur and Sharpen effects", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/apply-effects-and-animation-presets/list-of-effects/blur-sharpen-effects.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Directional blur at an angle
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: AE Directional Blur gives "the illusion of motion" and blurs equally to both sides; Alight Directional Blur's 0º is horizontal
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "dblur=angle=0:radius=20" out.mp4` (dblur default angle is 45, radius 5); horizontal-only gaussian alternative `gblur=sigma=12:sigmaV=0.01` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Blur and Sharpen effects", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/apply-effects-and-animation-presets/list-of-effects/blur-sharpen-effects.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Linear streaks
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: Alight's Linear Streaks slides the layer at an angle and blends overlapping pixels
how: on a still or a graphic use `dblur=angle=A:radius=R` at the streak angle; for moving footage use the motion-blur recipes below.

name: Registry zoom-blur shader blocks
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: registry block `cinematic-zoom` is a "shader transition with dramatic zoom blur"; `zoom-through-transition` zooms through a focal card into the next scene
how: `npx hyperframes add cinematic-zoom` (or `zoom-through-transition`) instead of approximating radial blur in ffmpeg.

name: Whip-pan shader
section: Zoom blur, spin blur, directional blur
what: registry block `whip-pan` is a shader transition simulating a fast camera whip pan
how: `npx hyperframes add whip-pan` for HyperFrames scenes; registry `whip-pan-cut` when both sides are layouts you control.

name: Shutter angle → exposure
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: AE: 90° on 24 fps footage = 1/96 s (25% of 1/24 s); 1° ≈ no blur, 720° = heavy; exposure = angle / (360 × fps)
how: in ffmpeg supersample then average the frames inside the shutter: 4x sub-frames and 180° = 2 of 4: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "minterpolate=fps=120:mi_mode=blend,tmix=frames=2:weights='1 1',fps=30" out.mp4` (moving square: 60 px wide → 68 px smear) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pixel Motion Blur = motion vectors
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: AE's Pixel Motion Blur analyses footage and synthesises blur from motion vectors (Shutter Samples = quality)
how: use motion-compensated sub-frames before averaging: `-vf "minterpolate=fps=120:mi_mode=mci,tmix=frames=4,fps=30"` (360° here); slow, so trim first (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Blur real footage without changing its speed
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: AE's Timewarp note: set Speed 100, enable motion blur in the effect and use manual shutter controls to add blur without retiming
how: the minterpolate + tmix + fps chain above keeps duration and frame rate; it only adds blur.

name: Layer motion blur doesn't blur what's inside the footage
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: AE's layer Motion Blur only blurs layer animation; for live action at a very different frame rate use frame blending instead
how: HyperFrames' blur (`data-hf-motion-blur` / `data-motion-blur`) smears DOM elements along their tweens; motion inside a `<video>` needs the ffmpeg pre-pass above, done before the clip goes in.
refs: Adobe AE Help "Assorted animation tools" (motion blur), https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/assorted-animation-tools.html, checked 2026-10-24
HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/motion-blur.html` (`npx hyperframes add motion-blur`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Centre the blur on the frame with shutter phase
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: AE's shutter phase offsets when the shutter opens; it helps when a blurred object seems to lag behind. HyperFrames' motion-blur snippet defaults to angle 720 and phase −360, which integrates [t − 1/fps, t + 1/fps]
how: for a blur centred on the frame time set phase = −angle/2 (the snippet's 720/−360 is that rule; 180° → −90°)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Assorted animation tools" (motion blur), https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/assorted-animation-tools.html, checked 2026-10-24
HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/motion-blur.html` (`npx hyperframes add motion-blur`), checked 2026-10-24

name: HyperFrames motion-blur snippet
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: registry `motion-blur`: put `data-hf-motion-blur` on any element the timeline animates; it seeks the timeline to sub-frame times across the shutter window and stacks copies at 1/N opacity with `mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter` in an isolated group (without isolation a light background blows out to white)
how: `npx hyperframes add motion-blur`, then set shutterAngle/shutterPhase/samplesPerFrame per element
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/motion-blur.html` (`npx hyperframes add motion-blur`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Render-time motion blur switches itself off
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: `data-motion-blur="on"` on the composition root blurs fast 2D movers, but it turns off with a WebGL canvas, a 3D flip using backface-visibility, a root transform or opacity, or an HDR render; it costs about 1.7x render time
how: after adding it run `hyperframes check`; the `motion_blur_off` warning names the cause

name: Blur depends on the frame rate
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: Alight's Motion Blur measures how far the layer moved since the previous frame, so the amount changes with the project frame rate
how: when a 30 fps edit is re-rendered at 60, re-check blur: in ffmpeg the shutter is a fraction of the frame (sub-frames × angle/360), so recompute the tmix frame count for the new fps.

name: Abrupt starts give wrong blur
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: Alight: an animation that starts or stops abruptly makes too much or too little blur; ease in/out, or put the keyframes at or beyond the layer's ends
how: in GSAP give blurred moves an eased start/end, or start the tween before the scene's data-start so it is already moving when the scene appears.

name: Hand-made blur peak on a fast move
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: HyperFrames motion defaults: a fast move takes 0.3-0.6 s and carries blur on its own ease, peaking at the fastest frame, 6-12 px on text, 15-20 px full-frame, horizontal-only on a horizontal move
how: for horizontal-only blur use an SVG `<feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="12 0">` filter (two numbers = x and y deviation; 0 on one axis blurs only the other) and tween stdDeviation up and back with the move

name: Speed-adaptive streak
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: registry `echo-smear` records each element's real trajectory and trails time-offset copies in proportion to its speed, combined by brightest pixel, so fast moves smear and slow ones stay sharp
how: `npx hyperframes add echo-smear` when an AE-style smear is wanted rather than an even shutter blur.

name: Shutter-blurred word slam
section: Motion blur (AE shutter, Pixel Motion Blur, Alight Motion Blur)
what: registry `shutter-slam` throws one word through six single-property beats (two translate slams, a scale punch, a full turn on each axis) under integrated shutter blur, on easing measured from an AE export
how: `npx hyperframes add shutter-slam`

name: AE Echo decay = geometric tmix weights
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: Echo combines the current frame with Number of Echoes earlier frames; each echo's opacity is Decay × the previous one (Decay 0.5 → 1/2, 1/4...)
how: 3 echoes, decay 0.5: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "tmix=frames=4:weights='1 0.5 0.25 0.125'" out.mp4` (moving 60 px square → 80 px visible trail) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Echo "Add" blows out to white
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: AE warns the Add operator overloads into white streaks if Starting Intensity is high
how: tmix with scale=1 is a plain sum: `tmix=frames=4:weights='1 1 1 1':scale=1` lifted the dark background to grey and turned 90 columns pure white; leave scale unset (auto = divide by the weight sum) unless you want that burn (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Echo "Minimum" = dark trails
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: AE's Minimum operator keeps the darkest pixel of all echoes
how: lagfun keeps bright pixels and lets them decay ("makes short flashes of light appear longer"), so invert around it for dark trails: `-vf "negate,lagfun=decay=0.9,negate"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Echo a moving layer: apply it after the move
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: AE Echo doesn't echo motion made by moving the layer; precompose and echo the precomp
how: in ffmpeg put tmix after the overlay that moves the element: `[0][1]overlay=x='mod(t*300\,560)':y=140:shortest=1,tmix=frames=5:weights='1 0.6 0.36 0.22 0.13'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Alight Echo Keyframes → echo-trail
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: Echo Keyframes copies the layer as it was at other times: Seconds = how far the most distant echo is (negative = future), Count = echoes in between (Seconds 1, Count 2 → echoes at 0.5 s and 1 s), Alpha fades them
how: registry `echo-trail` draws N ghosts at t − i×delta (echoes 2-6, delta 0.03-0.3 s): set delta = Seconds/Count
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/echo-trail.html` (`npx hyperframes add echo-trail`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Slit-scan with AE Time Displacement
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: Time Displacement replaces each pixel with the same pixel at another time: displacement (s) = max × (2 × (lum − 128)/256) from a grey map; a gradient map gives the classic slit-scan
how: `python3 slitscan.py in.mp4 out.mp4 0.5` (numpy port with a vertical-gradient map, scratchpad `sk2_12/t/py/slitscan.py`) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Slit-scan reveal in HyperFrames
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: registry `slit-scan-reveal`: each row of the frame samples the subject at a row-dependent time offset, smearing the arrival until the offsets collapse to zero and the mark holds
how: `npx hyperframes add slit-scan-reveal` for a logo arrival in the Time Displacement style.

name: Choppy frame rate on one layer only
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: AE Posterize Time locks a layer to its own frame rate ("sometimes called Strobe"); Alight's Time Quantization makes time pass in steps "just for this layer"
how: step only a region: `-filter_complex "[0:v]split[bg][fg];[fg]crop=320:180:160:90,fps=8,fps=30[c];[bg][c]overlay=160:90:shortest=1"` (in HyperFrames: a separate `<video>` or element with stepped time) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stutter: repeat a few frames
section: Echo and trails (AE Echo, Alight Echo Keyframes)
what: AE time-remapping can play a few frames backward and forward; the loop filter repeats a frame range
how: `-vf "loop=loop=3:size=5:start=20,setpts=N/30/TB"` repeats frames 20-24 three extra times (rebuild timestamps after loop) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Time-stretching and time-remapping", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/time-stretching-time-remapping.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: AE Mirror: left onto right
what: Mirror splits the image on a line and reflects one side onto the other; Reflection Angle 0° reflects left onto right, 90° top onto bottom
how: 0°: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]crop=iw/2:ih:0:0,split[l][r];[r]hflip[rf];[l][rf]hstack" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Mirror: top onto bottom
what: the 90° case
how: `-filter_complex "[0:v]crop=iw:ih/2:0:0,split[t][b];[b]vflip[bf];[t][bf]vstack"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Four-way kaleidoscope (quad mirror)
what: the RoughDraft ffmpeg wrapper's QuadMirror mirrors the upper-left quarter into all four quadrants with crop, flips and stacks; Alight's Kaleidoscope makes "symmetric radial reflections" (more than four: no single ffmpeg filter for that)
how: `-filter_complex "[0:v]crop=iw/2:ih/2:0:0,split=4[a][b][c][d];[b]hflip[b2];[c]vflip[c2];[d]hflip,vflip[d2];[a][b2]hstack[top];[c2][d2]hstack[bot];[top][bot]vstack"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Motion Tile with Mirror Edges
what: Motion Tile repeats the image across the output; Mirror Edges flips adjacent tiles into mirror images
how: 3x3 with flipped neighbours: `[0:v]scale=320:180,split=9[a]...[i];[b]hflip[b2];[d]vflip[d2];[e]hflip,vflip[e2];[f]vflip[f2];[h]hflip[h2];[a][b2][c][d2][e2][f2][g][h2][i]xstack=inputs=9:layout=0_0|w0_0|w0+w1_0|0_h0|w0_h0|w0+w1_h0|0_h0+h1|w0_h0+h1|w0+w1_h0+h1` (960x540 out) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Alight Mirror = overlay a mirrored copy
what: Alight's Mirror overlays the layer with a mirrored copy of itself, with alpha and blend mode control (not a hard split like AE's)
how: `-filter_complex "[0:v]split[a][b];[b]hflip[f];[a][f]blend=all_mode=lighten:all_opacity=0.5"` (any blend mode; opacity = the copy's alpha) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Offset = wrap-around pan (looping background)
what: Offset pans the image; what leaves one side comes back on the other, e.g. a looping background
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "scroll=h=0.01" out.mp4` (h = fraction of width per frame, −1..1); measured: at 0.5 s the frame equalled the source rolled 96 px (15 frames × 0.01 × 640) with wrap (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Grid Repeat needs even tile sizes
what: Alight's Grid Repeat makes copies of the layer in a grid
how: `-filter_complex "[0:v]scale=212:120,split=9[a][b][c][d][e][f][g][h][i];[a][b][c][d][e][f][g][h][i]xstack=inputs=9:grid=3x3"`; with 213 px tiles the 639 px-wide result failed in libx264 (yuv420p needs even sizes) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mirror side-fill for vertical media
what: registry block `yt-vertical-fill` fills a widescreen frame with portrait media using blurred-scale, mirror or copy side fills (images inside the block; keep live footage in the host)
how: `npx hyperframes add yt-vertical-fill` and pick the mirror fill when the blurred fill looks muddy.

name: AE Mosaic block count → pixelize size
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: Mosaic fills the layer with solid rectangles, set as a count of horizontal/vertical blocks; pixelize sets the block size in px (default 16, mode avg/min/max)
how: blocks from a count: w = width / horizontal blocks (640/26 ≈ 24): `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "pixelize=w=24:h=24" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mosaic as a transition
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: AE suggests animating Mosaic for a transition; pixelize takes all options as commands
how: `-vf "sendcmd=c='0.0 pixelize w 4, pixelize h 4; 0.5 pixelize w 16, pixelize h 16; 1.0 pixelize w 48, pixelize h 48',pixelize"`; between two clips the built-in `xfade=transition=pixelize:duration=0.5:offset=1` also works (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sharp (sampled) pixels vs averaged blocks
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: AE Mosaic's Sharp Colors takes each tile's colour from its centre pixel instead of the average; Alight Pixelate samples at pixel centres, Alight Mosaic averages
how: averaged = `pixelize`; sampled = nearest-neighbour down and up: `-vf "scale=iw/16:ih/16:flags=neighbor,scale=iw*16:ih*16:flags=neighbor"` (which pixel neighbour picks is the scaler's choice, not guaranteed the centre) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mosaic a face or a number plate
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: AE notes Mosaic is useful for obscuring faces
how: pixelize only the box with feedback: `-vf "[in][fin]feedback=x=200:y=100:w=200:h=120[out][fout];[fout]pixelize=w=16:h=16[fin]"`; for a moving face the box must follow it (track first) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Magnifier: nearest vs linear sampling
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: Alight's Magnify Background magnifies what is behind the layer; Sampling Nearest gives hard square pixels, Linear blends neighbours for a softer zoom
how: `-filter_complex "[0:v]split[a][b];[b]crop=120:120:260:120,scale=240:240:flags=neighbor[m];[a][m]overlay=200:60"`; use `flags=bilinear` for the soft version (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Posterize = levels per channel
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: Posterize maps each channel to the nearest of N tonal levels (2 levels = 2 tones per channel)
how: 4 levels: `-vf "format=rgb24,lutrgb=r='floor(val/64)*85':g='floor(val/64)*85':b='floor(val/64)*85'"` (Alight Posterize "decreases the number of steps" the same way) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Posterize to N best colours
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: elbg posterizes with the ELBG algorithm: codebook_length = number of distinct output colours, picked per image
how: `-vf "elbg=l=8:s=1"` gives an 8-colour poster look that follows each frame's palette; set seed for repeatable renders (slow: test on 1 s) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE / Alight Threshold
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: Threshold turns pixels lighter than the level white and darker ones black
how: `-vf "lutyuv=y='if(gt(val,128),255,0)':u=128:v=128"` (u/v at 128 removes colour) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Find Edges look
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: by default Find Edges draws dark lines on white; Invert gives bright lines on black. ffmpeg edgedetect (Canny) draws white wires on black
how: AE default look = `-vf "edgedetect=low=0.1:high=0.4,negate"`; AE "Invert" look = edgedetect alone (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cartoon: drop the frame rate first
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: AE's Cartoon tip: lower the frame rate (Posterize Time) before cartooning, because cartoons have lower frame rates; edgedetect's colormix mode "mixes the colors to create a paint/cartoon effect"
how: `-vf "fps=12,edgedetect=mode=colormix:high=0,fps=30"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Emboss
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: the convolution docs include an emboss kernel

name: Painterly median
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: AE Median: small radius reduces noise, a high radius "gives an image a painterly appearance"
how: `-vf "median=radius=6"` (1-127; radiusV for a different vertical size) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Noise and Grain effects", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/apply-effects-and-animation-presets/list-of-effects/noise-grain-effects.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Block dissolve between scenes
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: AE Block Dissolve makes a layer disappear in random blocks; registry `grid-pixelate-wipe` dissolves the screen into a grid of squares that fade with staggered timing
how: `npx hyperframes add grid-pixelate-wipe` between scenes

name: Halftone field
section: Mosaic, pixelate, posterize and other stylize effects
what: Alight's Halftone Dots replaces tones with dots (Amount = dots across, default 100; Angle default 45º); registry `halftone-field` is a WebGL halftone light field of dots tracking a flowing noise field
how: for a halftone background use `npx hyperframes add halftone-field`; there is no halftone filter in ffmpeg 6.1 (`ffmpeg -filters`).

name: Bulge / pinch with lenscorrection
what: AE Bulge pushes an area toward or away from the viewer; ffmpeg lenscorrection remaps radius by r_src = r_tgt × (1 + k1(r/r0)² + k2(r/r0)⁴), k1/k2 in −1..1
how: one sign swells the centre, the other pinches it: `-vf "lenscorrection=k1=-0.5:k2=0.1:i=bilinear"` and `lenscorrection=k1=0.5:i=bilinear` (i=bilinear avoids the default nearest's jaggies; check which sign gives bulge on a frame) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Wave Warp / ripple = the displace doc example
what: the displace docs give a ripple from two map inputs (128 = no move)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=640x360:r=30,lutrgb=128:128:128" -f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=640x360:r=30,geq='r=128+30*sin(2*PI*X/400+T):g=128+30*sin(2*PI*X/400+T):b=128+30*sin(2*PI*X/400+T)'" -lavfi "[0][1][2]displace" out.mp4` (30 = wave height, 400 = wavelength px, T term = speed) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Turbulent Displace with moving maps
what: AE Turbulent Displace uses fractal noise to warp (flowing water, funhouse mirrors, flags); displace accepts any grey maps, and edge=mirror fills pixels from outside with mirrored ones
how: two slowly moving sine-product maps: x-map `geq=lum='128+40*sin(X/37+T*3)*cos(Y/23-T*2)':cb=128:cr=128`, y-map with other constants, then `[0:v][x][y]displace=edge=mirror` (tested command only) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Turbulent displace in HyperFrames (SVG)
what: feTurbulence makes Perlin-noise textures and feDisplacementMap moves pixels by P(x + scale·(XC − 0.5), y + scale·(YC − 0.5))
how: `<filter id="t"><feTurbulence baseFrequency="0.01" numOctaves="2"/><feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" scale="30" xChannelSelector="R" yChannelSelector="G"/></filter>` on an element; tween the scale attribute from GSAP for a wobble-in

name: Twirl / Swirl with geq
what: AE Twirl rotates more in the centre than at the edges (whirlpool at extremes); Alight Swirl rotates by distance from a centre
how: on a still, rotate each pixel by 2×(1 − r/180) rad: `-vf "format=gray,geq=lum='p(W/2+(X-W/2)*cos(2*(1-min(1,hypot(X-W/2,Y-H/2)/180)))-(Y-H/2)*sin(2*(1-min(1,hypot(X-W/2,Y-H/2)/180))),H/2+(X-W/2)*sin(2*(1-min(1,hypot(X-W/2,Y-H/2)/180)))+(Y-H/2)*cos(2*(1-min(1,hypot(X-W/2,Y-H/2)/180))))'"` (gray only; colour needs the same for cb/cr; tested command only) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Faux-3D tilt of a flat clip
what: perspective moves the four corners; sense=destination sends the source corners to the given points
how: keystone the top inward: `-vf "perspective=x0=60:y0=0:x1=W-60:y1=0:x2=0:y2=H:x3=W:y3=H:sense=destination"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Animated tilt needs eval=frame
what: perspective evaluates its corner expressions once unless eval=frame
how: `-vf "perspective=x0='40*sin(on/10)':y0=0:x1='W-40*sin(on/10)':y1=0:x2=0:y2=H:x3=W:y3=H:sense=destination:eval=frame"` (rocking card) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Distortion transition showcases
what: registry blocks `transitions-distortion` (warp and distortion transitions), `cross-warp-morph`, `domain-warp-dissolve` and `gravitational-lens` (shader transitions)
how: `npx hyperframes catalog --tag transition` and preview these before hand-building a warp transition.

name: CapCut cutout = remove-background here
what: CapCut: Cutout > Remove Background, then Feather to soften the edge and put a new background on the layer below
how: `npx hyperframes remove-background` makes a transparent video; first run downloads 168 MB and it runs about 2 fps at 1080p on CPU; it drops mic arms and flickers on held objects, so check the matte

name: Freeze one frame for a set time
what: CapCut's Freeze halts a frame to emphasise a subject
how: frame 30 held for 1 s: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "trim=start_frame=30:end_frame=31,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=1" freeze.mp4`, then cut it in at that point (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Freeze in place with freezeframes
what: freezeframes replaces frames first..last with one frame from a second input
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]freezeframes=first=30:last=45:replace=30" out.mp4` (keeps the clip length, unlike tpad) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Freeze + cutout dressing
what: registry block `freeze-frame-dressing`: timeline-driven paper, tape and flash dressing for a freeze-frame or background-removed subject
how: freeze the frame, cut the subject out with remove-background, then `npx hyperframes add freeze-frame-dressing` around it

name: Sticker outline on a cutout (InShot "stroke")
what: InShot lists AI effects "Clone, stroke, auto-blur"; CSS drop-shadow follows the alpha shape but does not allow a spread value
how: fake a solid outline by chaining zero-blur shadows: `filter: drop-shadow(3px 0 0 #fff) drop-shadow(-3px 0 0 #fff) drop-shadow(0 3px 0 #fff) drop-shadow(0 -3px 0 #fff)` on the cutout
refs: InShot on the App Store, https://apps.apple.com/in/app/inshot-ai-video-editor/id997362197, checked 2026-10-24

name: Cinemagraph from a clip
what: registry block `cinemagraph`: a still frame with one living region, drawn from the seek time with a period that divides the duration so it loops seamlessly
how: ffmpeg version: still + live window: `ffmpeg -loop 1 -i still.png -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[1:v]crop=200:120:220:120[live];[0:v][live]overlay=220:120:shortest=1" -pix_fmt yuv420p out.mp4` (still taken from the same clip) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE camera Zoom = CSS perspective
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: AE: a layer at the Zoom distance appears full size, at twice the distance half as tall and wide; Alight's Zoom Distance is the distance at which a project-sized layer fills the screen; CSS perspective is the distance from the viewer to the z=0 plane
how: set `perspective` on the scene to the AE/Alight zoom value in px and place layers with translateZ (negative = farther/smaller)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Cameras, lights, and points of interest", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/cameras-lights-points-interest.html, checked 2026-10-24
Alight Motion Help "Camera Objects Guide", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536993608977-Camera-Objects-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Orbit, Track XY, Track Z as wrapper moves
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: AE's camera tools orbit around the point of interest, track horizontally/vertically, or move along the line to the point of interest; a two-node camera orients toward its point of interest
how: one rig wrapper per camera: orbit = rotateY/rotateX on a wrapper whose transform-origin is the point of interest, Track XY = x/y on the wrapper, Track Z = translateZ
refs: Adobe AE Help "Cameras, lights, and points of interest", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/cameras-lights-points-interest.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Things behind the camera vanish
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: CSS: parts of 3D elements behind the viewer (z greater than the perspective value) are not drawn; the repo's voxel film found Chrome drops a whole face once any part passes behind the camera
how: keep camera moves short of passing layers, and tile big floors into small quads

name: Effects on a 3D container flatten it
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: repo learning: mix-blend-mode, opacity < 1 or a filter on a preserve-3d container flattens the 3D world (pitch stops working, the ground vanishes)
how: glow, blur and blend go on separate 2D overlay compositions above the 3D world, not on its container

name: Dolly zoom (vertigo)
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: registry block `camera-dolly-zoom`: the camera tracks while the field of view changes the opposite way, solved per frame from d × tan(FOV/2) = const; it needs content at two or more depths
how: `npx hyperframes add camera-dolly-zoom` and give it layered (translateZ) content; a flat element gains nothing

name: Focus follows the subject
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: AE locks focus to the point of interest with `length(position, pointOfInterest)` on Focus Distance; Alight's Focus Blur blurs layers outside Focus Distance ± Depth of Field
how: registry block `rack-focus` (real aperture bokeh, needs two clearly separated depths) or component `focus-rack` (blur, dim, scale between two cards)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Cameras, lights, and points of interest", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/cameras-lights-points-interest.html, checked 2026-10-24
Alight Motion Help "Camera Objects Guide", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536993608977-Camera-Objects-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Fog by distance
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: Alight camera Fog: layers nearer than Near Distance are clear, between Near and Far partly hidden, beyond Far fully covered
how: in CSS set each depth layer's opacity (or a fog-coloured overlay) from its distance with `gsap.utils.mapRange(near, far, 1, 0, dist)`, clamped; registry `gallery-tunnel` already fades its far end into fog
refs: Alight Motion Help "Camera Objects Guide", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536993608977-Camera-Objects-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Camera rig with depth
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: registry component `camera-rig-depth-stack`: a 3D camera-rig card stack with depth, parallax and focus shift
how: `npx hyperframes add camera-rig-depth-stack` for "3D zoom" style photo/card intros instead of a flat Ken Burns.

name: 3D zoom and tilt helpers for any wrapper
section: 3D camera (AE camera, Alight Camera Objects) in CSS/HyperFrames
what: registry `yt-camera-move`: zoom, slide and 3D tilt-pan helpers for a video, include or card wrapper, with cubic-easing defaults and an edge-defocus pulse overlay
how: `npx hyperframes add yt-camera-move` for creator-style punch-ins with a 3D tilt.

name: AE Strobe Light: period and duration
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Strobe Light fires every Strobe Period seconds for Strobe Duration seconds (e.g. every 5 s for 0.1 s)
how: white strobe every 0.5 s for 2 frames: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawbox=c=white:t=fill:enable='lt(mod(t,0.5),0.067)'" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Strobe colour and Blend With Original
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Strobe Light has a Strobe Color and a Blend With Original amount (100% = no visible effect)
how: colour with alpha in drawbox: `drawbox=c=white@0.5:t=fill:enable='lt(mod(t,0.5),0.067)'` (0.5 = half-strength flash) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Strobe "Operates On Color Only" (invert flashes)
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Strobe Light can apply an operator to the colours on each strobe instead of making the layer transparent, e.g. invert at intervals
how: `-vf "negate=enable='lt(mod(t,0.5),0.1)'"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Random strobe probability, repeatable
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Strobe Light's Random Strobe Probability is the chance per frame
how: use a hash of the frame number so renders repeat: `-vf "negate=enable='lt(mod(sin(n*12.9898)*43758.5453,1),0.2)'"` → 11 of 60 frames flashed (target 20%) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Alight Blink
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Blink alternates the layer between visible and invisible; Frequency 0-16 cycles/s (default 2); use cases: a REC dot, a crossing signal, an unset clock
how: `-filter_complex "[0][1]overlay=20:20:shortest=1:enable='lt(mod(t*2,1),0.5)'"` (input 1 = the REC dot); in GSAP use `tl.set(dot,{visibility:...})` at each half-cycle (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Flicker without randomness
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Alight Flicker randomly adjusts opacity; the repo's film-memory treatment forbids randomness, infinite keyframes, timers and onUpdate: flicker is a gentle exposure pulse (−0.03..0.03 in sine.inOut segments of 0.45-0.8 s), not a flash
how: ffmpeg deterministic flicker: `-vf "eq=brightness='0.06*sin(2*PI*7*t)*sin(2*PI*3.1*t)':eval=frame"` (eval=frame is required for t to change) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pulse Opacity (sine or triangle)
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Alight's Pulse Opacity pulses opacity on a sine or triangle wave
how: 1 Hz sine pulse toward white at most 30%: `-filter_complex "[0][1]blend=all_expr='A*(1-0.3*(0.5-0.5*cos(2*PI*T)))+B*0.3*(0.5-0.5*cos(2*PI*T))':shortest=1"` (input 1 = a white color source); in GSAP a finite `repeat:N, yoyo:true` (never `repeat: -1` in HyperFrames) with `sine.inOut` (sine) or `none` (triangle) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pulse Size
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: Alight's Pulse Size grows and shrinks the layer on a sine or triangle wave
how: `-vf "zoompan=z='1.05-0.05*cos(2*PI*1*it)':d=1:x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':s=640x360:fps=30"` (1.00↔1.10 once a second) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Flash on a list of hits
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: for flashes on chosen beats instead of a fixed period
how: sum between() windows: `-vf "eq=brightness=0.4:enable='between(t,0.47,0.53)+between(t,1.27,1.33)'"` (generate the list from the beat file) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Camera-flash cut overlay
section: Flicker and strobe (AE Strobe Light, Alight Blink/Flicker/Pulse)
what: registry block `editorial-flash-overlay`: finite neutral-warm light layers for a seek-safe camera-flash cut or social reveal; `flash-through-white` is a shader white-flash crossfade
how: `npx hyperframes add editorial-flash-overlay` at the cut instead of a plain white div.

name: Beat file for the music
what: `npx hyperframes beats` needs a local music `<audio>` marked `data-timeline-role="music"` (or an id containing music, bgm or soundtrack), decodes it with ffmpeg and writes `beats/<audio-path>.json`; with no steady beat it fails and writes nothing
how: mark the track, run it, read the JSON before placing any beat effect

name: Don't trust beats on calm music
what: on calm music the tracker invents a metronome, often at double tempo; `beats` reports bpmConfidence
how: on calm stretches place effects on phrase and energy changes from `npx hyperframes audio --only sections,onsets,moments --json`, and give footage one slow push (1.0 → 1.08) instead of beat effects

name: Land the effect on the hit
what: HyperFrames film rules: a move that must land on a hit starts 40-190 ms early, a reaction starts 0-45 ms after, and the hit itself is a 0 ms `tl.set` ("easing a hit kills it")
how: flash/RGB split/zoom punch: `tl.set(el,{...},beatTime)` exactly on the beat, decay after it; a slide into the hit starts ~0.1 s before

name: Beat sync is for music, not voice
what: CapCut's beat-sync workflow is for music timing and "not designed to sync voice snippets to beats"; HyperFrames: in narrated pieces the voice is the clock
how: apply beat effects only on music-only stretches; under narration time effects to words

name: Spend the strong beats on the key moments
what: CapCut's beat-detection guide: big actions on strong beats, camera changes on secondary beats, titles or slow motion on breaks; beat drop = stronger transition, steady groove = steady cut pace, breakdown = longer hold
how: tag each beat in the JSON as strong/secondary/break first, then assign effect strength by tag instead of hitting every beat the same

name: Per-beat effects from a command file
what: sendcmd reads timed commands from a file
how: write lines like `0.50 rgbashift rh -24, rgbashift bh 24;` and `0.60 rgbashift rh 0, rgbashift bh 0;` from the beat JSON, then `-vf "sendcmd=f=beats.cmd,rgbashift"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Decaying zoom punch on every beat
how: zoompan restarts an exponential decay each beat (0.5 s here): `-vf "zoompan=z='1+0.12*exp(-10*mod(it,0.5))':d=1:x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':s=640x360:fps=30"`; zoompan's doc example `z='if(between(in_time,0,1),2,1)'` is the hard version (2x for one second) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Blur pulse on the beat via sendcmd expressions
what: sendcmd's [expr] flag evaluates the argument with T (time), TS, TE, TI
how: put it in a file to avoid shell escaping: `0.0-2.0 [expr] gblur sigma 12*exp(-8*mod(T\,0.5));` then `-vf "sendcmd=f=blur.cmd,gblur"` (inline in `c=` the comma split the command and failed); measured detail rose from 0.87 at the beat to 1.19 a quarter-second later (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hue cycle ("rainbow")
what: CapCut's velocity presets include "rainbow"; hue's doc example rotates hue with time
how: `-vf "hue=H=2*PI*t"` (one full turn a second); doc variant `hue="H=2*PI*t: s=sin(2*PI*t)+1"` also swings saturation (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Music-hit sting
what: registry `beat-accent`: impact flash, micro scale-pulse and small shake on one hit; the impact lands 0.25 s into its unscaled IN, and intensity 0.5-2 scales pulse, flash and shake together
how: `npx hyperframes add beat-accent`, start it 0.25 s before the beat
refs: HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/beat-accent.html` (`npx hyperframes add beat-accent`), checked 2026-10-24

name: Background that pulses on the beat
what: registry `beat-pulse-background`: an accent backdrop pulses glow intensity and saturation on a supplied deterministic beat grid
how: `npx hyperframes add beat-pulse-background` and feed it the beats JSON times

name: AE Linear Wipe = xfade wipe
section: AE transitions and loops in ffmpeg/GSAP
what: AE Linear Wipe wipes the layer in a direction (Wipe Angle 90° = left to right)
how: `ffmpeg -i a.mp4 -i b.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition=wipeleft:duration=0.5:offset=1" out.mp4`; pick wipeleft/wiperight/wipeup/wipedown (and wipetl...) by eye for the direction (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Radial Wipe = xfade radial
section: AE transitions and loops in ffmpeg/GSAP
what: AE Radial Wipe reveals the layer below with a wipe that circles a point (Start Angle 0° = top)
how: `xfade=transition=radial:duration=0.5:offset=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Iris Wipe = xfade circleopen
section: AE transitions and loops in ffmpeg/GSAP
what: AE Iris Wipe reveals the underlying layer radially and is animated by its radius
how: `xfade=transition=circleopen:duration=0.5:offset=1` (circleclose for the reverse) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Blur crossfade
section: AE transitions and loops in ffmpeg/GSAP
what: xfade has an `hblur` transition; registry `transitions-blur` shows blur-based scene transitions
how: `xfade=transition=hblur:duration=0.5:offset=1` for footage; the registry showcase for HyperFrames scenes (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE loopOut("offset") in GSAP: explicit tweens
section: AE transitions and loops in ffmpeg/GSAP
what: loopOut "offset" repeats a segment and adds the start-to-end change on each cycle (a staircase that keeps climbing). GSAP's `repeatRefresh` re-records relative values each repeat, but it is state-dependent: frame-stepped it gave 100/200/300, yet a direct seek from 0 to 2.5 s gave 350 instead of 250
how: for seek-safe renders build the cycles as separate tweens (`x:100`, `x:200`, `x:300` back to back → 250 at 2.5 s) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Expression language reference", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: RGB split on any HyperFrames element (SVG filter)
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: feColorMatrix can isolate one channel and feOffset shifts a filter result by dx/dy
how: filter with three matrices (R only, G only, B only), `feOffset dx="-8"` on red and `dx="8"` on blue, recombined with two `feBlend mode="screen"`, applied as `filter:url(#rgbsplit)`; a white box rendered red | yellow | white | cyan | blue fringes in headless Chromium (`color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"`) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cross-dissolve without the mid-fade dip
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: MDN: plus-lighter blending is useful for cross-fades and prevents unwanted blinking when two overlaid elements animate opacity in opposite directions
how: give both layers `mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter` inside an `isolation:isolate` wrapper; measured in Chromium: two white layers at 50% gave 192 with normal blending, 255 with plus-lighter (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hue cycle on an element (CSS hue-rotate)
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: CSS filters include hue-rotate(); the ffmpeg hue cycle has a CSS twin for graphics and text
how: drive `filter:hue-rotate(Xdeg)` from the seek-safe setter (X = 360 × t); note it is not a pure hue swap: pure red at 120° rendered (0,113,0), a darker green (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fast per-frame writes: quickSetter + pipe
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: gsap.quickSetter is an optimised replacement for repeated gsap.set() calls on the same property (GSAP quotes 50-250% faster) and can sit at the end of a `gsap.utils.pipe()` after clamping or snapping
how: inside a shake/flicker setter: `const setX=gsap.quickSetter(rig,'x','px'); setX(value)`; use plain gsap.set when speed doesn't matter

name: Pixel-stepped (retro) motion with snap
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: gsap.utils.snap(increment, value) snaps to the nearest increment (snap(10, 23.5) = 20)
how: for a chunky 8-bit move, snap the value in the setter: `setX(gsap.utils.snap(8, x))`; together with stepped time (posterizeTime skill) it gives low-frame-rate, low-resolution motion

name: Coloured glow (AE Glow Colors)
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: AE Glow can use the original colours or A & B colours for the glow
how: tint the glow branch before the blur: `...lutrgb=...(gt(val,180))...,colorchannelmixer=rr=1:gg=0.55:bb=0.15,gblur=sigma=18[gl];[o][gl]blend=all_mode=screen` (warm glow; tested command) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Timewarp's no-pulse half speed
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: AE Timewarp at Speed 50 makes new frames a quarter and three quarters of the way between originals and leaves the originals out, to avoid a pulse on every other frame
how: interpolate 4x and keep only those positions: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "minterpolate=fps=120:mi_mode=mci,select='eq(mod(n,4),1)+eq(mod(n,4),3)',setpts=N/30/TB" -r 30 out.mp4` → 2 s clip became 3.87 s at 30 fps (50%) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Exaggerated motion blur
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: AE: 720° shutter gives a large amount of blur; Alight's Motion Blur Tune (0-4) can be raised to exaggerate motion
how: in HyperFrames raise the element's shutterAngle above 360 (the snippet's default is already 720) or in ffmpeg average more sub-frames (tmix frames > sub-frame factor)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Assorted animation tools" (motion blur), https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/assorted-animation-tools.html, checked 2026-10-24
HyperFrames registry source `compositions/components/motion-blur.html` (`npx hyperframes add motion-blur`), checked 2026-10-24

name: A camera "zoom" without scale
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: Alight camera objects have no scale property; pinching changes view angle and zoom distance, and Alight advises moving the camera's Z to feel depth between layers
how: in a CSS 3D rig, push the world (or camera wrapper) along translateZ for a depth zoom; scaling the wrapper zooms everything equally and kills the parallax
refs: Alight Motion Help "Camera Objects Guide", https://support.alightmotion.com/hc/en-us/articles/10536993608977-Camera-Objects-Guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Coloured flash on every beat (FlexClip "trigger warning")
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: FlexClip's CapCut recipe splits an overlay on each beat, fades each piece out and sets its colour and opacity
how: decaying red flash every 0.5 s: `-f lavfi -i "color=c=red:s=640x360:r=30" -filter_complex "[0][1]blend=all_expr='A*(1-0.6*exp(-10*mod(T,0.5)))+B*0.6*exp(-10*mod(T,0.5))':shortest=1"` → mean RGB 200/51/50 on the beat, 126/124/120 a quarter-second later (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Skew = shear
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: AE's Transform effect has Skew and Skew Axis; ffmpeg shear takes shx/shy factors −2..2 and supports them as commands
how: `-vf "shear=shx=0.3:c=black"`; for a skew whip on a cut: `-vf "sendcmd=c='0.9 shear shx 0.4; 1.0 shear shx 0.2; 1.1 shear shx 0',shear"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AE Camera Lens Blur "Blur Map" = varblur
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: AE's Camera Lens Blur can take a control layer as a blur map; ffmpeg varblur blurs by radius read from a second stream of the same size (min_r/max_r)
how: tilt-shift-style map (sharp middle row band, blur toward top and bottom): `-f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=640x360:r=30,geq=lum='255*abs(Y-180)/180':cb=128:cr=128,format=gray" -filter_complex "[0:v]format=yuv444p[a];[1:v]format=yuv444p[m];[a][m]varblur=max_r=12:shortest=1"` (tested command only) (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Adobe AE Help "Blur and Sharpen effects", https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/apply-effects-and-animation-presets/list-of-effects/blur-sharpen-effects.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Colour pop (Alight Spot Color)
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: Alight's Spot Color keeps one colour and desaturates the rest; ffmpeg colorhold removes colour from everything except one RGB colour (similarity 0.01 = exact, 1 = all; blend keeps some colour)
how: `-vf "format=rgb24,colorhold=color=red:similarity=0.3:blend=0.1"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gooey / metaball effect = blur + threshold
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: registry `gooey-split` makes its goo with an SVG blur-and-threshold filter, `ink-bleed-reveal` uses a "gooey blur-plus-threshold filter", and `morph-text` uses SVG threshold + blur
how: `npx hyperframes add gooey-split` (or ink-bleed-reveal / morph-text) and reuse its filter instead of writing one

name: Lens flare
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: AE lists a Lens Flare generate effect and Alight a (members-only) Lens Flare; registry block `lens-flare` is a WebGPU star burst with a faint rainbow halo that shimmers on black
how: `npx hyperframes add lens-flare`, composite it with screen blending over the shot; spec.md bans flares by default, so only when asked
refs: Alight Motion Effect Guide index, https://guide.alightmotion.com/effects/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Phosphor trail (CRT persistence)
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: registry `oscilloscope-trace` sweeps a CRT beam across a graticule with closed-form phosphor persistence; in ffmpeg the same "bright things fade slowly" is lagfun
how: `npx hyperframes add oscilloscope-trace` for a retro data beat; for footage `lagfun=decay=0.95` (a moving white square left a 360 px trail over 1 s) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hologram look
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: registry `hologram`: a pale blue holographic orb with scan rings and flicker (WebGPU)
how: `npx hyperframes add hologram` for a sci-fi insert rather than stacking scanlines, flicker and glow by hand.

name: Shutter and iris transitions
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: registry `transitions-mechanical` shows mechanical shutter and iris transitions (AE's Iris Wipe family)
how: preview it with `npx hyperframes add transitions-mechanical` before building an iris by hand.

name: Title with an RGB fringe that settles
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: registry `yt-prism-title`: blur-focus entrance, a red/blue fringe that settles then breathes, on a transparent root
how: `npx hyperframes add yt-prism-title` for a creator title with a gentle RGB split.

name: Light-based transitions showcase
section: More translations (CSS/SVG in HyperFrames, extra ffmpeg filters, registry blocks)
what: registry `transitions-light` (glow and flash transitions), `transitions-scale` (scale and zoom) and `transitions-3d` (3D flip and rotate)
how: run them as a menu for the client before choosing; match the transition to the effect family already in the edit.

name: Read this build's vid.stab defaults, not the web page
what: the online docs give smoothing 10, mincontrast 0.3, relative 0 and optalgo gauss, but the 6.1 build here reports smoothing 15, mincontrast 0.25, relative 1 and a default optalgo called `opt` (global optimization). Tune from the real defaults
how: `ffmpeg -hide_banner -h filter=vidstabtransform` and `ffmpeg -hide_banner -h filter=vidstabdetect` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep accuracy at or above shakiness
what: the 6.1 help text describes accuracy as ">=shakiness" (1 low, 15 high/slow); shakiness 1 means little shake, 10 strong shake or a quick camera. For a violently shaken clip set both high
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabdetect=shakiness=10:accuracy=15:result=s10.trf -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Faster first pass for a quick preview
what: accuracy is the slow knob (15 = high, slow) and stepsize sets the search step before the 1-pixel refinement around the minimum; lowering accuracy and raising stepsize trades precision for speed. Use it to judge a clip, then re-run at full accuracy for the deliverable
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabdetect=shakiness=5:accuracy=9:stepsize=12:result=fast.trf -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lower mincontrast for flat, low-texture shots
what: measurement fields whose contrast is below mincontrast are discarded, so sky, walls or night footage may leave too few fields; lower it (6.1 default 0.25) so more fields count
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabdetect=mincontrast=0.15:result=mc.trf -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: See what the detector measured
what: `show=1` or `show=2` draws the measurement fields and transforms into the output, so you can see whether it locked on the background or on a moving subject. Write it to a real file (not null)
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabdetect=show=1:result=show.trf -t 1 show1.mp4` (also `show=2`) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Virtual tripod: lock a near-static shot to one frame
what: set `tripod=N` (1-based reference frame) in pass 1 and `tripod=1` in pass 2; motion is then measured against that frame and the view is held still. Frames before the reference are not stabilized (still zoomed/cropped) and the view snaps to the reference pose there, so pick an early reference
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabdetect=tripod=1:result=tri.trf -f null -` then `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabtransform=tripod=1:input=tri.trf -an tri.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: smoothing=0 simulates a static camera
what: smoothing is the half-window (value*2+1 frames) of the low-pass on camera motion; 0 is the special case "static camera" without needing tripod mode
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:smoothing=0 sm0.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bigger smoothing = floatier camera, slower pans
what: a larger value gives a smoother video but limits how fast the camera may accelerate in pans and tilts; smoothing=30 uses 61 frames. Use high values on walking shots, low values when the operator pans on purpose
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:smoothing=30,unsharp=5:5:0.8:3:3:0.4 sm30.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pick the camera-path algorithm
what: 6.1 offers `opt` (global optimization, default here), `gauss` (Gaussian low-pass) and `avg` (simple averaging). If the default path looks wrong on a shot, render the other two and compare side by side
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:optalgo=gauss:smoothing=10` / `optalgo=avg` / `optalgo=opt` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cap the correction with maxshift and maxangle
what: maxshift limits translation in pixels and maxangle limits rotation in radians (degrees*PI/180); -1 means no limit. Capping stops one bad measurement from throwing the frame far off
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:maxshift=20:maxangle=0.05` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Smooth position only, leave rotation alone
what: Final Cut's SmoothCam has separate Translation, Rotation and Scale smoothing; vid.stab has one smoothing value, but maxangle=0 allows no rotation correction, so only position is stabilized
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:maxangle=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Border fill: previous-frame vs black
what: `crop=keep` (default) fills the moving borders with image from the previous frame, `crop=black` fills them black; with `optzoom=0` you see the borders and can judge how far the frame really moves
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:crop=black:optzoom=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Zoom modes: static, adaptive, manual
what: `optzoom=1` (default) picks one static zoom so only very strong moves show borders; `optzoom=2` zooms adaptively so no borders show, limited per frame by `zoomspeed` (0-5 %, default 0.25); `zoom=` adds a fixed percentage on top (negative zooms out)
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:optzoom=2:zoomspeed=0.5`; `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:zoom=-5:optzoom=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bicubic interpolation for the final render
what: interpol is no / linear (horizontal only) / bilinear (default) / bicubic (cubic in both directions, slow). Preview bilinear, render bicubic
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:interpol=bicubic` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Absolute vs relative transforms
what: `relative=1` (the 6.1 default) treats transforms as relative to the previous frame, `relative=0` as absolute. Tripod mode is equivalent to relative=0:smoothing=0
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:relative=0` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: invert=1 flips the stored transforms
what: the option only inverts the transforms read from the file. Running a clean clip through another clip's inverted, relative transforms ran here, but whether it reproduces that clip's shake was not checked by eye, so look at frames before using it as a "borrowed shake"
how: `ffmpeg -i clean.mp4 -vf vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:invert=1:relative=1:smoothing=0:optzoom=0 -an inv.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dump the per-frame global motion with debug=1
what: pass 2 with debug=1 writes `global_motions.trf` in the working folder: one data line per frame `time x y alpha zoom extra` (x/y in pixels, alpha in radians), each followed by a comment line. Use it to find the shakiest seconds
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:debug=1 -f null - && head -4 global_motions.trf` (tested here 2026-10-24: frame 2 read `0 35.107748 17.861798 -0.035629 -0.128952 0`)

name: Feed vid.stab your own camera path
what: vidstabtransform also accepts the global_motions format as input (the time column is ignored, frames are taken in file order), which is the supported way to apply a path you computed or edited yourself, e.g. in numpy
how: edit global_motions.trf, then `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf vidstabtransform=input=global_motions.trf -an own.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24 with the unedited dump)

name: This build writes text .trf files, and fileformat is missing
what: the current vid.stab doc says ffmpeg always gets the binary encoding, but libvidstab 1.1.0 here wrote a text file starting `VID.STAB 1` with `Frame N (List ...)` lines, and `fileformat=ascii` failed with "Option not found". Text means you can read the fields with grep
how: `head -c 300 s10.trf` (tested here 2026-10-24); the reader auto-detects either encoding

name: A .trf belongs to one resolution
what: every value in the file is in pixels of the analysed frame and the frame size is not stored, so detecting on a downscaled copy and transforming the full-size clip does not work unless you rescale the values yourself. Detect at the size you transform
how: run both passes on the same `-vf` chain and size

name: Drop duplicated frames before stabilizing
what: duplicates (e.g. 25 fps stored as 30 fps) are measured as exactly zero motion and show up as a regular jerk; drop them with mpdecimate in both passes (or work at the true rate)
how: `ffmpeg -i dup.mp4 -vf mpdecimate,vidstabdetect=result=dd.trf -f null -` then `ffmpeg -i dup.mp4 -vf mpdecimate,vidstabtransform=input=dd.trf -fps_mode vfr dd.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Convert 10-bit 4:2:2 to 8-bit 4:2:0 first
what: the README warns that 10-bit 4:2:2 input gives chroma shift and colour bleeding; add `format=yuv420p` at the start of both passes
how: `ffmpeg -i t422.mp4 -vf format=yuv420p,vidstabdetect=result=t422.trf -f null -` then `ffmpeg -i t422.mp4 -vf format=yuv420p,vidstabtransform=input=t422.trf out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hyperlapse: drop frames first, then stabilize, in both passes
what: any filter that changes the number, order or rate of frames (fps, minterpolate, select, framestep, trim, -r) must run before vidstabdetect too, or the transforms stop lining up ("not enough transforms found"). For a hyperlapse from walking video, framestep before both passes
how: `ffmpeg -i walk.mp4 -vf "framestep=3,vidstabdetect=shakiness=8:result=hl.trf" -f null -` then `ffmpeg -i walk.mp4 -vf "framestep=3,vidstabtransform=input=hl.trf:smoothing=10,unsharp=5:5:0.8:3:3:0.4,setpts=N/(30*TB)" -r 30 -an hyper.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Judge stabilization side by side
what: put the original and the result next to each other (LearnOpenCV's stabilizer writes a "Before and After" hconcat) and watch both; on a vertical deliverable stack them
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -i stab.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]hstack" -t 2 sbs.mp4` (or `vstack`) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Newer vid.stab has an L1-optimal "dolly/crane" path
what: the current README describes an L1-optimal camera path (Grundmann et al., CVPR 2011) made of static, linear and parabolic segments, steered by zoom/optzoom (crop budget) and smoothing. The 6.1 build here lists only opt/gauss/avg, so don't assume it has the L1 path; it would need a newer libvidstab build
how: check `ffmpeg -h filter=vidstabtransform` for the available optalgo values (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Black bars after stabilizing: three fixes
what: Final Cut's guide gives three ways to lose the black edges a big move causes: lower the smoothing values, cut out the shakiest stretch, or crop the edges. In ffmpeg: lower `smoothing`, trim with -ss/-t in both passes, or leave `optzoom=1`/`2` on
how: `vidstabtransform=input=s10.trf:optalgo=gauss:smoothing=10` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Tell deshake where the static background is
what: `x:y:w:h` limits the motion search to a rectangle (same meaning as drawbox), so a person walking through the frame is not mistaken for camera motion; -1 means the full frame. Draw the box first to check it
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=200:h=150:color=red -frames:v 1 box.png`, then `-vf deshake=x=0:y=0:w=200:h=150` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Raise deshake's search range for big jolts
what: rx/ry set the maximum movement searched in x and y, 0-64 px, default 16; a shake bigger than that is not found
how: `-vf deshake=rx=64:ry=64` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Choose how deshake fills the edges
what: edge = blank (zeros), original (original image), clamp (extruded edge pixels) or mirror (default). Mirror hides gaps on texture but can show mirrored objects; clamp smears the last row
how: `-vf deshake=edge=clamp` / `edge=blank` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: deshake blocksize, contrast and search speed
what: blocksize (4-128, default 8) is the motion-search block; only blocks whose darkest-to-lightest difference exceeds `contrast` (1-255, default 125) are used; `search=less` is a less exhaustive, faster search than the default exhaustive one. Lower contrast on flat footage
how: `-vf deshake=blocksize=16:contrast=60`; `-vf deshake=search=less` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Log deshake's motion search
what: `filename=` writes a per-frame log with columns Ori/Avg/Fin for x, y, angle and zoom, so you can see the raw and the corrected motion
how: `ffmpeg -i shaky.mp4 -vf deshake=filename=deshake.log -f null - && head -3 deshake.log` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: deshake_opencl needs an OpenCL device (none here)
what: the feature-point OpenCL stabilizer offers tripod, smooth_strength (0-1, 0 = adaptive), smooth_window_multiplier (window = fps x value, default 2.0) and adaptive_crop. This container has no OpenCL device (`-init_hw_device opencl` failed with "No such device"), so use vid.stab
how: needs an OpenCL GPU (missing)

name: OpenCV point-feature stabilizer as a second opinion
what: LearnOpenCV's script tracks Shi-Tomasi corners (maxCorners 200, qualityLevel 0.01, minDistance 30) with Lucas-Kanade flow, fits `estimateAffinePartial2D` per frame pair, integrates the trajectory, smooths it and warps each frame; it writes a before/after video
how: copy the script into its own folder, then `/home/user/tools/venv/bin/python -I vs.py --input shaky.mp4 --output-dir out --output-name out.mp4 --smoothing-radius 15 --no-display --validate` (tested here 2026-10-24: "VALIDATION PASSED: 89 frames, 1280x360, mean tracked points 28.26")

name: Moving-average radius = how much intent survives
what: the script's default radius 50 is a 101-frame window (50 each side) chosen to remove high-frequency shake while keeping slower intentional camera motion; it smooths x, y and angle separately and pads the ends with edge values. Smaller radius keeps more of the operator's moves
how: `--smoothing-radius 15` for short handheld clips (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hide warp wedges with a 4% centre scale
what: the script's `fix_border` scales each stabilized frame by 1.04 around its centre to hide most of the empty wedges the warp leaves. In ffmpeg the same idea is a small scale-up then crop back to size
how: in Python `cv2.warpAffine(frame, cv2.getRotationMatrix2D((w/2,h/2),0,1.04),(w,h))` (part of the tested run above)

name: Fall back to the last good transform
what: when a frame pair has fewer than 3 tracked points or a non-finite result, the script reuses the previous transform instead of failing; copy that guard into any custom tracker or reframe script
how: see `estimate_transforms()` in the script (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gyro stabilization for action-cam footage
what: Gyroflow stabilizes from the gyroscope (and optionally accelerometer) data that GoPro (HERO 5+), Sony, Insta360, DJI and others record, with rolling-shutter correction, adaptive zoom, horizon levelling and lens profiles; it also works with already-HyperSmoothed GoPro clips (HERO 8+). For a client's action-cam file, ask for the original file with metadata intact
how: needs Gyroflow (missing; GPLv3)

name: Phone footage can be gyro-stabilized too
what: for cameras without a built-in gyro, Gyroflow reads logs from phone apps such as Sensor Logger (iOS/Android) or a separate logger; its "additional 3D rotation" option is noted as useful for framing vertical videos
how: needs Gyroflow (missing) plus a gyro log recorded during the shoot

name: Pans and zooms: smoothing; static shots: tripod
what: Final Cut's InertiaCam is for footage with camera moves such as pans and zooms (one Smoothing slider) and may offer Tripod Mode after analysis; SmoothCam smooths translation, rotation and scale separately. In ffmpeg: a moderate `smoothing` for moving shots, `tripod` for locked-off shots
how: see 3446 and 3448 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: The retime quality ladder
section: Slow motion quality: interpolation and blending
what: Final Cut's Video Quality menu is the clearest map of the options: Fast (Floor) duplicates frames or rounds down, Fast (Nearest Frame) reduces artifacts but may stutter, Good (Frame Blending) blends neighbouring frames, Better (Optical Flow) draws new frames from pixel motion, Best (Machine Learning) uses bidirectional ML optical flow with better occlusion handling. Apple's tip: try frame blending first, go to optical flow or ML only if you see artifacts. ffmpeg's matching steps: `minterpolate=mi_mode=dup`, `mi_mode=blend`, `mi_mode=mci`; ML needs RIFE (missing)
how: `-vf minterpolate=fps=60:mi_mode=dup`, `...:mi_mode=blend`, `...:mi_mode=mci` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: minterpolate defaults to mci in 6.1
section: Slow motion quality: interpolation and blending
what: the 6.1 help shows mi_mode default mci, mc_mode obmc, me_mode bilat, me epzs, mb_size 16, search_param 32, scd fdiff, scd_threshold 10. A bare `minterpolate=fps=60` therefore already runs the slow motion-compensated mode
how: `ffmpeg -hide_banner -h filter=minterpolate` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bidirectional motion estimation
section: Slow motion quality: interpolation and blending
what: me_mode `bidir` estimates vectors for each source frame forwards and backwards, while the default `bilat` estimates them directly for the interpolated frame; try bidir when bilat warps a shot
how: `-vf minterpolate=fps=60:mi_mode=mci:mc_mode=aobmc:me_mode=bidir:vsbmc=1` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pick the motion search algorithm
section: Slow motion quality: interpolation and blending
what: `me` accepts esa (exhaustive), tss, tdls, ntss, fss, ds, hexbs, epzs (default) and umh (uneven multi-hexagon). esa is the brute-force search; test it on a short troublesome stretch only
how: `-vf minterpolate=fps=60:mi_mode=mci:me=esa` / `me=umh` (tested here 2026-10-24 on 1 s clips)

name: Smaller blocks and search window
