what: Shorts made with remixed content are attributed to the original (audio source on the Sound page, video source linked in the Shorts player), which YouTube calls a chance for new viewers to discover you
how: make long FireCraft videos remix-friendly: a clean 1-5 s signature moment and a reusable original sound

name: Remix "Cut" = 1-5 s sample
section: YouTube Shorts rules that shape the edit
what: Cut samples a 1-5 second segment (audio + video); Sound samples up to 90 s of audio (some videos only 30 s); Green Screen uses a video as background
how: for a reaction Short, open the source video in the YouTube app > Share > Remix > Cut, then add our commentary

name: Shorts templates spread a format
section: YouTube Shorts rules that shape the edit
what: any Short can be used as a template (Remix > Use this template) and others drop their clips in
how: when a FireCraft Short format works, it is available to others as a template via Remix > Use this template

name: Non-original Shorts earn nothing
section: YouTube Shorts rules that shape the edit
what: ineligible Shorts views include unedited clips of others' movies/TV, re-uploads of other creators' content, and compilations with no original content added
how: every Short we cut must add original edit/voice/commentary; never just re-post someone's clip

name: Music in a Short cuts the pool, not your share
section: YouTube Shorts rules that shape the edit
what: Shorts revenue with 1 licensed track sends half the associated revenue to the Creator Pool (2 tracks: one third); creators keep 45% of their allocation, and their allocation itself isn't reduced by music use
how: for monetized Shorts, our own/CC0 music keeps the pool larger; licensed partner music doesn't change the creator's 45%

name: Front-load the title, branding last
what: viewers may see only part of a title, so keep it short, put the most important words first and save episode numbers and branding for the end
how: "Lifesteal heart steal trick | FireCraft S2 Ep 3", not "FireCraft S2 Ep 3: ..."

name: Searchable vs intriguing title
what: searchable titles say exactly what to expect (reach searchers); intriguing titles spark curiosity for viewers not hunting that topic
how: tutorials/server-join guides get searchable titles; event/drama videos get intriguing ones

name: Description: the first lines are the preview
what: viewers see only the first lines before "Show more"/"more", so describe the video there; the rest can hold channel info; max 5,000 characters
how: line 1 = what the video is + the key word; links and credits below

name: 1-2 main words in title AND description
what: identify 1-2 main words that describe the video and feature them prominently in both; search terms are matched with the description text
how: e.g. "Minecraft lifesteal server" in title and first description line

name: Unique description per video
what: each video should have a unique description to be found in search and stand out from similar videos; a default description can auto-fill channel info
how: set Settings > Upload defaults description to the server links/credits, then write a fresh top paragraph each time

name: Description formatting and bullets
what: descriptions support bold, italic and strikethrough; start a line with "*", "+" or "-" and a space for a bullet list
how: list chapters/links as bullets for readability

name: Pretend to search for your own video
what: YouTube suggests checking the "How viewers find" search terms and adding missing words a searcher would type
how: compare the search-terms card with the description and add the missing ones in natural sentences

name: Check the description on every surface
what: check how the description appears in search results, on the watch page and on mobile, so the important info shows
how: open the video on a phone after publishing and read the visible two lines

name: What the system watches
section: YouTube recommendation signals and diagnosing drops
what: when recommended, does the viewer click, ignore, or press "not interested"; then do they stay (AVD and average % viewed are both ranking signals); then did they enjoy it (likes, post-watch surveys)
how: an edit must win all three: packaging (click), retention (stay), payoff (like/satisfaction)

name: No favoured format
section: YouTube recommendation signals and diagnosing drops
what: YouTube says its system has no opinion about the type of video and doesn't favour a format; ranking is performance plus personalisation
how: pick format by what the audience watches, not by rumours of algorithm preferences

name: Three external factors: topic, competition, seasonality
section: YouTube recommendation signals and diagnosing drops
what: reach depends on topic interest worldwide, competition with all channels, and seasonal swings (holidays, school)
how: plan launch videos (e.g. a new season) outside exam weeks and big holidays for the audience's country

name: Watch-time drop checklist
section: YouTube recommendation signals and diagnosing drops
what: check recent changes in topic, editing style, thumbnail design, on-screen talent, cadence, output or length; check topic appeal in Google Trends; see if new or returning viewers fell
how: falling casual/regular = content less appealing to fans; falling new = less broad appeal

name: Change one thing at a time
section: YouTube recommendation signals and diagnosing drops
what: YouTube advises not making too many changes at once so a rise or drop can be attributed
how: when testing a new edit style, keep thumbnail style and length the same for those uploads

name: Topic ageing
section: YouTube recommendation signals and diagnosing drops
what: YouTube's example: a gaming creator still playing Among Us may decline more than those playing new releases
how: check Google Trends for "minecraft lifesteal" before promising growth from a topic

name: Pick a goal per upload
what: revenue-focused (advertiser-friendly, high-CPM topics), subscriber-growth (introduce the brand, give a reason to return) or reach-focused (accessible, mass appeal)
how: tag each planned FireCraft video with one goal and edit accordingly (reach = accessible, mass-appeal angle)

name: Weigh cost and time per format
what: compare production cost to views and revenue (RPM) and time to produce; choose between low-frequency high-production and high-frequency easy content
how: keep a short note per edit in library/research of hours spent vs views

name: Fill gaps between uploads
what: keep interaction between videos with Shorts, live and Posts-tab polls without overwhelming the audience; batch-film and schedule uploads
how: cut 2-3 Shorts from each long edit to post in the gap days

name: Plan around dates
what: build holidays, game releases, movie premieres, collabs and your own breaks into the schedule
how: time FireCraft season launches with Minecraft update news

name: Collab test: would one viewer watch both?
what: choose collaborators by aligned audience, growth potential and personality, not just subscriber count
how: use "Channels your audience watches" to shortlist, then ask "would their viewer immediately watch ours?"

name: Cross-promote a collab both ways
what: upload two different videos (one per channel), link with cards and mentions, use a verbal CTA, mention the channel in titles/descriptions
how: add a card at the moment the guest is introduced plus an end-screen Channel element

name: Prepare the channel for collab traffic
what: ask viewers to subscribe at the end, put best/most relevant videos in the top channel section and have a channel trailer
how: cut a channel trailer from the season promo before a collab goes live

name: Both AVD and % viewed matter
what: YouTube says the algorithm uses both absolute (AVD) and relative (% viewed) watch time, and encourages making videos the appropriate length for the content
how: don't pad a 4-minute idea to 10 minutes for AVD, and don't cut a strong 12-minute story just to raise % viewed

name: Bucket videos, review 90 days
what: group content by format/series/style, audience, topic longevity and cost; compare the groups over a wide range such as 90 days and check whether one viral video skews a group's average
how: Advanced mode groups "promo", "tutorial", "event"; 90-day range; look at median-like episodes, not the outlier

name: Repeatable format over one-offs
what: YouTube recommends a repeatable format for long-term viewership and warns not to judge the next upload against a viral hit; trend audiences may not be your fanbase
how: turn the FireCraft launch video into a template (video/ folder) and reuse its structure per season

name: Mostly non-subscribers? add a subscribe CTA
what: YouTube's example creator with a mostly non-subscriber audience refocused the format and added a subscribe call to action, then grew
how: if "Watch time from subscribers" is low, put a short subscribe line right after the payoff, not in the intro

name: Compare new formats only with the same format
what: when trying a new format, compare videos of the same format because audience behaviour differs across formats
how: judge the first FireCraft live-stream highlights against other highlight videos, not against Shorts

name: Trends tab: top searches and breakout videos
what: Studio Analytics > Trends shows top searches from your audience (last 28 days), breakout videos from similar creators, and recent related videos
how: check Trends before scripting; borrow the topic, never the footage

name: Content gaps for Shorts
what: the Trends tab lists Shorts search terms where viewers find no results, no exact match, or only old/low-quality results
how: make a Short that exactly answers one content-gap term and use that term in its title

name: Audience interest levels
what: Trends search shows audience interest from very low to very high, based on videos watched over 1,000 times per week in the last 28 days
how: prefer ideas rated high for your audience when choosing between two scripts

name: Use retention dips to learn editing
what: YouTube's editing tips say dips mean viewers skip or leave, and suggest studying how editing kept viewers in your top videos; jump cuts can hide filler lines
how: compare the cut rhythm (shots per minute) of the best vs worst video with `ffmpeg -i v.mp4 -vf "select='gt(scene,0.3)',showinfo" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -c pts_time` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Plan B-roll for teasers while shooting
what: YouTube's editing tips: think about the open, close and key moments during writing, and ask whether you need extra footage for B-roll, trailers or teasers
how: for FireCraft recordings, capture extra clean B-roll per session for hooks, trailers and Shorts

name: Lock exposure and focus on phone shoots
what: YouTube's mobile tips: shoot horizontally for 16:9, use the rear camera, lock exposure and focus, turn off notifications
how: pass this checklist to the owner before a phone shoot

name: Keep a consistent channel look
what: consistent backgrounds, clothing and design elements help viewers recognise your content; branding should be clear, consistent and simple
how: reuse one caption style, one title font and one colour accent across all FireCraft videos

name: Image posts: 1:1, up to 10 images, 16 MB
what: image/GIF posts take up to 10 images, JPG/PNG/GIF/WEBP, size up to 16 MB; 1:1 is suggested because that's how the feed shows them
how: export a square teaser still from the edit: `ffmpeg -ss 5 -i promo.mp4 -frames:v 1 -vf "crop='min(iw,ih)':'min(iw,ih)',scale=1080:1080" post.jpg` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Tease with a GIF of the best moment
what: YouTube's posts tips suggest teasing an upcoming video with a GIF of its best moment
how: `ffmpeg -ss 12 -t 3 -i promo.mp4 -vf "fps=12,scale=480:-1:flags=lanczos,split[a][b];[a]palettegen[p];[b][p]paletteuse" tease.gif` (tested here 2026-10-24) then post it before release

name: Poll limits
what: text polls: up to 4 answers of 65 characters; image polls: up to 4 images with 36-character captions; text posts can't be combined with polls
how: "Next video: PvP guide / base tour / heart economy / event recap?" (each under 65 chars)

name: Quiz posts and in-video quizzes
what: post quizzes: up to 4 answers (80 chars, 30 with an image), one correct answer, optional 500-char explanation; Studio can add up to 10 timed quizzes to a video, which can't be edited after saving
how: add a quiz at a key moment of a tutorial; double-check text before saving

name: Schedule posts and @mention channels
what: posts can be scheduled (date, time, time zone) and @handle mentions may notify that channel; there is a 24-hour posting limit
how: schedule a teaser post for the morning of a Premiere and mention the collab partner

name: Posts travel beyond the Posts tab
what: posts can appear on Home and Subscriptions feeds, image posts also in the Shorts feed, and subscribers may get a notification; a post about a video already in a viewer's feed might not show again
how: post about a video a few days after release (new angle/still), not the same hour

name: Engage with other creators' posts
what: YouTube says engaging with other creators' posts may increase the chance of your viewers seeing those posts across YouTube
how: like/comment on collab partners' posts during a joint launch week

name: Move the Posts shelf up
what: the Posts shelf sits at the bottom of the channel Home tab by default; drag it up in Customization > Home tab > Layout
how: move it up during launch weeks so polls are seen

name: Schedule a Premiere 24 h ahead
what: scheduling at least 24 hours early lets viewers worldwide see the thumbnail in Subscriptions; each Premiere has its own shareable landing page and URL
how: share the watch-page URL on Discord/website as soon as it's scheduled

name: Reminder timing
what: viewers who press "notify me" get a notification about 30 minutes before and another at the start
how: pin a comment on the watch page asking for reminders

name: Premiere limits
what: Shorts can't be Premieres; 360/VR180 or output above 1080p isn't supported; viewers can rewind but not skip ahead; the countdown isn't part of the saved video
how: render the launch video at 1080p for a Premiere; keep 4K masters for later re-upload only if needed

name: Countdown starts 2 minutes before
what: a live countdown video plays for two minutes before the Premiere; theme and length are chosen in "Set up Premiere"
how: don't put anything important in a pre-roll of your own; the countdown already covers the wait

name: Premiere trailer: 15 s-3 min
what: a trailer can play on the watch page before the Premiere (channels with over 1,000 subscribers and no strikes); 15 s to 3 min, same aspect ratio/resolution as the main video, not a previously premiered video
how: cut a 15 s-3 min trailer from the master with the same 1920x1080 settings

name: Premiere ads are pre-roll only
what: during a Premiere only pre-roll ads run, no mid- or post-rolls; afterwards upload-default ad settings apply
how: no need to design mid-roll breaks for the Premiere itself

name: Host the chat to hold viewers
what: YouTube suggests adding talking points, fun facts and behind-the-scenes, asking fans to guess what happens next, and using the post-show chat to direct viewers to another video or stream
how: prepare chat lines (facts, behind-the-scenes, "guess what happens next") timed to the edit's beats

name: Live to Premiere to live
what: YouTube suggests sending viewers from a live stream to a Premiere (Live Redirect) and setting the Premiere as the channel trailer
how: go live shortly before the season Premiere and redirect

name: Stagger end-screen elements
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: elements show together by default; YouTube recommends timing them to appear at different times and adding a CTA for each
how: in Studio Editor drag each element's start; in the edit, point to each slot as it appears ("yeh dekho...")

name: "Best for viewer" end-screen video
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: a video element can show your most recent upload, let YouTube pick the best one for each viewer, or a chosen video/playlist (public or unlisted, any channel)
how: use one "best for viewer" plus one fixed next-episode element

name: End screens suppress watermark and card teasers
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: during the end screen, card teasers and the video watermark are hidden; end screens don't show for made-for-kids videos, in YouTube Music/Kids apps, mobile web (except iPad), 360 video; viewers can hide them
how: also say the next video verbally; don't rely on the element alone

name: Custom end-screen image ≥300x300
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: for a custom image YouTube recommends at least 300 x 300 px
how: `ffmpeg -i logo.png -vf "scale=600:600:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=600:600:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=0x00000000" -frames:v 1 es_logo.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Channel-level end-screen reports
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: channel analytics have "Top end screen element types" and "Top videos by end screen" cards
how: once several videos have end screens, compare video vs playlist vs subscribe elements and keep the best type

name: Cards are a desktop feature shown below the description
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: cards show for viewers on computers, appear below the description, can be scrolled; a teaser shows at your chosen time
how: don't build a mobile-first Short's CTA around a card

name: Channel cards need message + teaser
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: message and teaser text are required for channel cards; use them to thank a channel that helped
how: add a channel card at the timestamp where a collaborator appears

name: Cards vanish with a Content ID campaign
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: cards won't show if the video is claimed by Content ID with a content-owner campaign; videos with cards don't show a call-to-action overlay
how: another reason to use only CC0/our music in FireCraft edits

name: Auto chapters can be turned off
section: End screens and cards: beyond the basics
what: automatic chapters are on by default for new uploads; manual timestamps override them; opt out per video (Show more) or for all uploads in Settings > Upload defaults > Advanced; channels with active strikes get no chapters
how: write our own chapter list (below) so wording is ours

name: Three ranking factor groups
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: TikTok ranks by user interactions (likes, shares, comments, watching in full or skipping), content information (sounds, hashtags, view count, country published) and user information (language, location, device); for most users interactions, including time spent watching, weigh most
how: optimise the edit for watch-in-full: cut dead air, end on the payoff

name: TikTok search weighs match to the query
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: for search results, content information (how well the content matches the search term, hashtags, the sound) generally weighs most
how: say and caption the exact search phrase ("Minecraft lifesteal server") and use it in the description for search-led TikToks

name: No two posts in a row from one creator
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: TikTok generally won't recommend two posts in a row from the same creator in Friends/Following, and typically doesn't recommend content already seen
how: every post must stand alone; don't split one idea into "part 1/part 2" expecting back-to-back delivery

name: Popular videos get a safety review
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: TikTok's safety teams may review content as it rises in popularity; content not meeting For You feed eligibility standards isn't recommended there
how: read the "FYF Ineligible" sections of the Community Guidelines before posting edgy content

name: Low views ≠ rule broken
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: TikTok says ineligible videos can still be found via search or the profile, low views don't necessarily mean a rule was broken, and analytics show if a video was made ineligible for recommendation
how: check the post's analytics for an ineligibility notice before re-editing

name: Hook in 3 seconds, TikTok's own three tactics
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: Creator Academy: hook within the first 3 seconds by asking a question you'll answer, setting a timer or putting the time in the title, or opening with a quick tease of the end result; the first thing seen should be different, original or attention-grabbing
how: open FireCraft reels with a quick tease of the end result (the kill/win), then go to the start

name: Snip the boring parts
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: Creator Academy advises fast-paced storytelling, quick cuts and trimming boring parts to raise watch time
how: cut silences with the CLAUDE.md "shorten pauses" approach before adding effects

name: Read drop-off in watch time
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: Creator Academy suggests starting with "watch time" in the Content tab and looking at the drop-off point: where and why viewers leave; an unusually long average watch time should inform the next video
how: note the drop-off second and look at that frame of the render

name: Landscape without fake bars
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: TikTok's Full Screen mode shows a "view full screen" button on horizontal uploads; Creator Academy says no black margins are needed, as long as the video is truly landscape with no text in the margins
how: post 16:9 renders as-is; never burn captions into letterbox bars

name: Creator Rewards metrics
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: the Additional Reward depends on average watch time, retention rate (viewers staying after 30, 40, 50, 60 or 90 s), completion rate and search value
how: for 1 min+ TikToks plan a re-hook just before 30 s and 60 s

name: Creator Rewards eligibility
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: original content over 1 minute, at least 1,000 For You views, not a Duet/Stitch/Photo Mode/ad, 1080p or higher; the account needs 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in 30 days, in listed countries only (US, UK, Germany, Japan, South Korea, France, Mexico, Brazil)
how: export 1080x1920 masters; Pakistan isn't in that list, so for the owner this is informational

name: 1 min+ content grows
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: TikTok says users spend 50% of their time on longer content and watch time of 1 min+ content was 5x higher than short videos in the last 6 months
how: besides the short cut, make a version over 1 minute of strong FireCraft stories

name: Teach step by step with text
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: Creator Academy lists formats that get shared: solve a problem, bust a myth, share a hack, elevate the everyday, respond to a comment, and step-by-step lessons with text for context
how: a "how to join FireCraft" step-by-step with numbered on-screen text

name: Pick a niche and a mission statement
section: TikTok: how the For You feed ranks, and what that means for the edit
what: Creator Academy tip 1: avoid general interests, focus on a niche, write a mission statement and check each upload against it
how: FireCraft = "Minecraft lifesteal stories"; check each cut against that line

name: TikTok Studio web upload limits
what: web uploads must be MP4 or WebM, 720x1280 or higher, up to 30 minutes, under 10 GB; you can set caption, cover, Duet/Stitch permissions and run a sound copyright check before posting (Creator Academy pages mention uploads up to 60 minutes on TikTok.com/TikTok Studio, so the limits differ by page)
how: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=width,height:format=duration,size -of compact in.mp4` then upload; tick the copyright check (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Run TikTok's sound copyright check
what: Studio can auto-check sound copyright on every new post, or once per upload, so you can edit before posting
how: turn on "Video sound copyright check" in TikTok Studio settings

name: Let advertisers use your post
what: TikTok Studio settings include "Ad settings: You can allow advertisers to use your post in their ads"
how: turn it on for FireCraft promo posts if partners may want to run them as ads

name: Business accounts: commercial music only
what: Business accounts can't use music not licensed for commercial use (also for effect templates); Promote needs original or commercial-use sounds
how: for the FireCraft (business) account use our own/CC0 music or TikTok's Commercial Music Library

name: Adding a TikTok sound replaces all audio
what: once you change the music, all previous background music and voices are replaced
how: never add an app sound over our mixed render with voice; post our mix as original sound

name: Photo posts: up to 35 photos
what: a TikTok photo post takes up to 35 photos, with sound, text and stickers
how: export stills of a build tour as a photo post (note: Photo Mode posts don't qualify for Creator Rewards)

name: Privacy setting carries over
what: a new TikTok post keeps the previous post's privacy setting (e.g. "Only you")
how: after a private test upload, check privacy before posting the real one

name: Web upload posts the whole file
what: uploading from a browser uploads the entire video; to trim length you must use the app
how: trim in our pipeline first (`ffmpeg -ss A -to B -i in.mp4 -c copy out.mp4`)

name: One speed per clip in TikTok's editor
what: the in-app editor allows Normal or Curve speed, one speed option per clip
how: do speed ramps in ffmpeg/HyperFrames before upload

name: Stitch/Duet control = "Allow reuse of content"
what: one setting per post controls Stitch, Duet, stickers and adding to Stories; account must be public; deleting associated Stitches also deletes your original
how: keep reuse ON for promo clips so others can Stitch them

name: Add Yours prompts
what: an Add Yours sticker posts a prompt anyone can answer; responders' posts notify the creator; the button can't be removed after publishing
how: use a prompt like "Apna best Minecraft base dikhao" on a FireCraft post

name: TikTok playlists
what: creators (where available) group public posts into playlists watched in sequence; a post can be in one playlist only; newest added plays first unless reordered
how: put a multi-part FireCraft story in one playlist and reorder to episode order

name: Creator Search Insights: content gaps
what: shows topics people search on TikTok, with filters like Content gap and Searches by followers (over 1,000 followers), plus search analytics for your posts
how: search "Creator Search Insights" in the app, pick a gap topic, make the post

name: Comment insights
what: AI-summarised comment topics show frequent discussions, audience suggestions and questions (18+, not everywhere)
how: turn the top question topic into the next video's hook

name: TikTok analytics need time
what: analytics exist only for videos posted after enabling them, take 1-2 days to update; follower activity is in local time, everything else in UTC
how: convert UTC peaks to Pakistan time (+5) before scheduling

name: Trending vs Inspiration feeds in TikTok Studio
what: Trending is non-personalised by region and topic; Inspiration is tailored and shows performance insights on others' posts
how: scan Trending (region: Pakistan, topic: games) before planning a reel

name: Promote results aren't guaranteed
what: Promote packs give estimates from past performance; Promote needs a public post with original/commercial sound; you can't delete a post while its promotion is active
how: promote only a finished cut you won't need to replace

name: Reposts reach friends' For You
what: Repost shares a post to your friends' and community's For You feeds, labelled with your name
how: ask server staff to repost launch clips rather than re-upload them

name: Reels' top predictions
what: Instagram says the most important Reels predictions are how likely you are to reshare, watch all the way through, like, and go to the audio page; it also surveys viewers on whether a reel was worth their time
how: build reels to be watched to the end (payoff in the last second) and shareable (one clear idea)

name: What makes a reel less visible
what: Instagram aims to make less visible low-resolution or watermarked reels, muted reels, reels with borders, majority-text reels, and reels already posted on Instagram
how: export clean 1080x1920 without another app's watermark, no letterbox bars, with sound, and never re-post an old reel as new

name: Watermark notifications
what: Instagram is experimenting with notifying creators when a reel's reach may be limited due to a watermark
how: render from our master, never re-upload a downloaded TikTok file to Instagram

name: Feed's five key predictions
what: in Feed, Instagram most closely predicts whether you'll spend a few seconds on a post, comment, like, share, and tap the profile photo
how: for feed videos, the first frame must stop the scroll for a few seconds (title on screen at 0 s)

name: Explore leans on post popularity
what: in Explore, popularity signals (how many and how quickly people like, comment, share, save) matter much more than in Feed or Stories; key predicted actions are likes, saves and shares
how: give Explore-bound posts a save reason (tips, a checklist)

name: Recommendation Guidelines limit reach
what: content allowed on Instagram but against its Recommendation Guidelines (e.g. people fighting, tobacco/vaping, pharmaceutical drugs) isn't recommended in Explore/Reels/Search; repeat offenders lose recommendation eligibility for a period
how: check Account Status before blaming the edit when reach drops

name: No paid-reach suppression
what: Instagram states it does not suppress content to push people to buy ads
how: fix packaging/retention before spending on boosts

name: Explore: 95%-watch and 5-second predictions
what: Meta's Explore system card lists predictions such as "how likely you are to watch more than 95% of a video" (signal: how many people watched over 95%) and "spend more than five seconds viewing a post"; candidates go 1500 → 100 → final list
how: keep Explore-targeted clips short enough to be finished; remove trailing outro seconds

name: Feed: carousel swipe and DM-share signals
what: the Instagram Feed system card predicts swiping through a whole carousel and sharing in a DM; DM-share signals include whether the post is informative (news, reviews, tutorials, how-tos) and created within 90 days
how: make tutorial carousels from video stills for DM-share reach

name: Feed ranks about 500 posts
what: the Feed system gathers followed accounts' posts, a light model picks about 700, then about 500 get a relevance score, with a balanced mix of content types
how: post the format your followers engage with most; feed balances types anyway

name: Facebook Reels: watch length is predicted from completions
what: Facebook's Reels card predicts how long you'll watch a reel using how many times others watched it to completion, views, your recent interactions and the author; reel length is an input signal; a light model picks about 10-100 reels
how: completion rate matters on Facebook too: trim the end so the payoff is the last frame

name: Facebook Reels can come from Instagram
what: Facebook Reels may include cross-app recommended content from Instagram
how: a reel posted on Instagram can also reach Facebook Reels viewers

name: Facebook Feed video ad: 4:5 at 1440x1800
what: Meta's Ads Guide recommends 4:5, 1440x1800, MP4/MOV/GIF, H.264, square pixels, fixed frame rate, progressive, stereo AAC 128 kbps+, no edit lists; duration 1 s-241 min, max 4 GB; primary text 50-150 chars, headline 27
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -vf "crop=ih*4/5:ih,scale=1440:1800" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 128k -ac 2 -movflags +faststart fb45.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Awareness objective hides the ad footer
what: with Awareness (or reach/2-second-view/impression/post-engagement goals) the headline, description and CTA button aren't shown on Facebook Feed on mobile
how: burn the CTA (e.g. www.firecraft.fun) into the video's last seconds for such campaigns

name: LinkedIn organic video limits
what: 75 KB-5 GB, 3 s (desktop) / 2 s (mobile) to 15 min, 256x144 to 4096x2304, aspect 1:2.4 to 2.4:1, 10-60 fps, 192 kbps-30 Mbps; ProRes may upload but won't process; keep edges free of key text/logos
how: upload the H.264 MP4 master; check with `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height,r_frame_rate,bit_rate -of compact master.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LinkedIn video ads: 4:5 recommended
what: vertical 4:5 (720x900, max 1080x1350) is LinkedIn's recommended ad ratio; also 16:9 (1920x1080), 1:1, 9:16; MP4, H.264 or VP8, under 30 fps, AAC, 75 KB-500 MB, 3 s-30 min, 15-30 s recommended
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -vf "crop=ih*4/5:ih,scale=1080:1350" -r 25 -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 128k li45.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: LinkedIn ads loop to 30 s
what: LinkedIn video ads under 30 s loop until at least 30 s of playback (10 s plays 3 times, 20 s twice); over 30 s plays once
how: for a 10-15 s LinkedIn ad make the last frame flow into the first, since it will repeat

name: LinkedIn ad captions: plain SRT
what: LinkedIn ad captions must be SRT, text only (no font colours); headline up to 70 chars to avoid truncation, intro text 150; more than four emojis can get an ad rejected
how: export our Whisper captions as plain .srt for LinkedIn ads

name: Pinterest video file and length limits
what: Pinterest video (standard width): MP4/MOV/M4V, H.264 or H.265, up to 2 GB, 4 s-15 min (ads recommended 6-15 s), aspect between 1:2 and 1.91:1, square or vertical 2:3, 4:5, 9:16 recommended
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -vf "crop=ih*2/3:ih,scale=1000:1500" -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac pin23.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pinterest titles: first 40 chars show
what: titles up to 100 characters, the first 40 may show in feeds; descriptions (up to 800) don't show in feed but are used for relevance
how: put the key phrase in the first 40 characters and write a real description

name: Pinterest creative basics
what: Pinterest's creative guide: plan for a vertical 2:3 canvas, keep the logo/brand clearly visible without overtaking the ad, concise messaging and a specific CTA on every asset
how: add a small logo bug and a URL end card to Pinterest cuts

name: TikTok in-feed ad specs
what: vertical 9:16 ≥540x960 recommended (16:9 ≥960x540, 1:1 ≥640x640), mp4/mov/mpeg/3gp/avi, up to 10 min, ≤500 MB, bitrate ≥516 kbps; ad captions up to 4 lines, white fixed font, no links/@/hashtags; safe-zone files depend on caption length
how: use the vertical master; download TikTok's safe-zone zip and overlay it on a snapshot to check

name: Relative watch time for short, absolute for long
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: YouTube: broadly, relative watch time (% viewed) matters more for short videos and absolute watch time (AVD) more for longer videos
how: for a 60 s Short aim for near-full completion; for a 12-min video judge minutes watched, not %

name: Title/thumbnail change re-ranks only through viewer behaviour
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: changing title or thumbnail can bring more views because viewers react differently, not because the change itself re-ranks; "don't change what's working"
how: only swap packaging on a video with weak CTR, never on one that is climbing

name: Packaging to avoid
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: YouTube lists titles/thumbnails that are deceiving/clickbaity, shocking, disgusting, gratuitously violent, indecent, or loud (ALL CAPS or "!!!!!"); these turn viewers away and can get content removed
how: check every title against this list before upload

name: Tags are not important
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: tags mainly correct common misspellings (YouTube vs U Tube)
how: add 2-3 misspelling tags ("firecraft smp", "fire craft") and spend the time on title/description instead

name: Search ranks by match and engagement, not views
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: search ranking uses how well title, description and video content match the search, and which videos drive the most engagement for it; results aren't a most-viewed list
how: say the searched words in the video too (content match), not only in text fields

name: Unlisted first, public later is fine
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: flipping an unlisted upload to public doesn't hurt performance; what matters is viewers' response after publishing
how: upload unlisted, check on phone, then publish

name: Publish time and cadence myths
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: publish time isn't known to affect long-term performance (it matters for Live and Premieres); growth isn't correlated with time between uploads; breaks showed no correlation with view changes
how: schedule for early viewers if you like, but don't rush an edit to hit a weekday

name: Channel location doesn't target viewers
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: location settings aren't used for recommendations
how: reach Pakistani/Indian viewers with language and topic, not a location setting

name: Monetisation status doesn't affect discovery
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: the system doesn't know which videos monetise; violent/graphic content may be recommended less because of the content itself
how: no need to fear "limited ads" as a reach penalty; watch the content

name: When an old video takes off
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: reasons YouTube lists: topic rising, new viewers binging, more viewers accepting the recommendation, or a new episode sending people back
how: when an old FireCraft video spikes, make a follow-up quickly and link it with a card/end screen

name: Viral spike that doesn't return
section: YouTube discovery myths and facts (official FAQ)
what: one listed cause of falling Home/Suggested traffic: a viral video whose viewers didn't come back
how: after a viral hit, judge the next uploads against typical retention, not against the hit

name: Appeal → engagement → satisfaction funnel
what: YouTube's Content-tab tips frame a video as a funnel: appeal (CTR), engagement (did they watch: views), satisfaction (AVD and returning)
how: diagnose the weakest stage first: low CTR = packaging, low AVD = edit

name: Above-typical intro = 50% at 30 s
what: a typical intro is about 30 s; videos with 50% or more of the audience still watching after 30 s appear in the "above typical intros" list; grey area on the chart = typical retention of your last 10 similar-length videos
how: use 50% at 0:30 as the bar for long FireCraft edits

name: Search-heavy traffic? widen sources
what: YouTube: if YouTube search is the top source, viewers come looking for you; think how to grow other sources like external to expand reach
how: share each upload's link on the FireCraft website and Discord to add external traffic

name: Pin a comment that works
what: pin your own comment to clarify something, ask a specific question, tease a moment or easter egg, or thank viewers; hearting a comment may notify the viewer
how: pin a timestamped tease ("4:12 pe dekho kya hua") on every upload

name: Filter comments for questions
what: comment filters include subscriber status, member status, commenter subscriber count, comments containing questions, and response status
how: answer question-comments first; turn the best into a Short reply

name: Signature welcome or sign-off
what: YouTube suggests a signature welcome or sign-off, memes, catchphrases or inside jokes to build channel branding and belonging
how: keep one short FireCraft sign-off line/sting for all videos

name: Put the schedule where fans see it
what: tell fans when to come back by adding your schedule to the banner, channel trailer and videos, and warn them in advance of changes
how: add "New video har Friday" to the end card if a fixed day is chosen

name: Explain the bell
what: YouTube suggests explaining that the bell sends notifications for uploads and lives; fans choose all, none or personalised
how: one short bell line at a natural moment, not at 0 s

name: Community space: welcome post in week one
what: for YouTube Communities, create a welcome post within the first week, announce it everywhere, and post weekly conversation starters/polls
how: use the season launch week for the welcome post

name: Pivot gradually, judge in months
what: YouTube's pivot tips: define success beyond views (subscribers, new/casual/regular), pivot gradually mixing old content, prepare several videos ahead, announce the change, and expect months not weeks
how: if FireCraft videos shift style, keep one old-style video per few uploads

name: Ask for the like inside the Short
what: YouTube's Shorts tips: something as simple as asking "If you liked the Short, give it a like and comment" helps; consider universal-appeal topics when stuck
how: a 1-line on-screen ask near the end

name: Auto-dub needs clear, not-too-fast speech
what: automatic dubbing skips videos over 120 min, with no/little speech or only music, unsupported or undetected language, speech too fast, or copyrighted content; Hindi can be dubbed into English and Bengali
how: set the video language correctly (Hindi) and keep narration at a natural pace so auto-dubs can reach English viewers

name: Review dubs before publishing
what: Settings > Channel > Advanced > Automatic dubbing: allow it and choose "Manually review dubs before publishing"
how: turn on manual review so a bad dub of a FireCraft name doesn't go live

name: Playlist analytics: views from playlist
what: playlist analytics aggregate Overview/Content/Audience/Revenue; "views from playlist" and playlist watch time include others' videos in the playlist, while total views don't
how: compare "views from playlist" across season playlists to see which one people binge

name: Shorts "Get feedback" before upload
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: in the YouTube app's Short details screen a "Get feedback" button gives an analysis of the video's hook, pacing and more
how: after rendering, open the Short in the app's upload flow and tap Get feedback before publishing

name: YouTube caps Short uploads at 1080p, title 100 chars
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: Shorts can be uploaded at a maximum resolution of 1080p; the Short title is max 100 characters
how: render Shorts at 1080x1920; no 4K Short masters

name: Shorts thumbnail: app only, a frame of the video
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: you pick a frame (optionally with text/filters) as the Short's thumbnail before or after upload, only in the YouTube app, not in Studio (per this page; other YouTube pages may differ); edits can't be undone step by step
how: design one strong frame inside the Short (title card frame) so it can be chosen as the thumbnail

name: Batch-upload Shorts from Studio
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: Studio accepts up to 15 short videos at a time (each up to 3 min, square or vertical); complete details via EDIT DRAFT before publishing
how: batch-upload the 2-3 Shorts cut from each long edit as drafts, then schedule them

name: Shorts drafts live on the phone
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: Shorts drafts are saved to the device, not the channel; deleting the app or changing phones loses them
how: keep our rendered files in the scratchpad/handoff until the Short is published

name: Shorts views vs engaged views (since 31 Mar 2025)
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: a Shorts view counts every start or replay with no minimum watch time; the older metric is now "Engaged views", used for comparing Shorts and for YPP/revenue
how: compare Shorts edits by engaged views, never by raw views

name: YPP through Shorts
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: to join the YouTube Partner Program with Shorts you need 1,000 subscribers and 10 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days; subscribers gained from Shorts count toward Creator Awards milestones
how: track qualified Shorts views over rolling 90 days in Analytics before applying

name: Where Shorts are found
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: the Shorts feed, search (including most smart TVs/consoles), Home, the channel homepage, Subscriptions and notifications
how: give Shorts searchable titles too, since search is one of the entry points

name: Mid-rolls need 8+ minutes and natural breaks
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: mid-roll ads are possible on monetized videos 8 minutes or longer; manual slots at natural breakpoints (an audio pause or visual transition) are more likely to serve; slots unlikely to serve show red
how: when a long FireCraft video is monetised, leave a short beat (pause/transition) at chapter boundaries and place slots there

name: Automatic ad slots stack on manual ones
section: YouTube Shorts upload details and long-video ad breaks
what: automatic mid-roll slots are added on top of manual slots by default (uncheck "Automatic ad slots" to stop); YouTube says mid-rolls may not suit some content, e.g. meditation
how: for an emotional/cinematic edit, turn automatic slots off and place only at chapter breaks

name: Dashes and zeros = data thresholds
what: reports may be limited when metrics don't meet a threshold; totals can differ from the sum of rows; extending the range past 30 days or removing filters helps; no demographics for private/unlisted videos
how: read small-channel geography/demographics over ranges longer than 30 days, without extra filters

name: One-off search terms don't show
what: search terms and external URLs that drive little traffic may not appear in traffic reports
how: don't assume a keyword failed because it's missing from the list

name: No universal "good" CTR
what: YouTube says there's no single most important metric and no universal good CTR benchmark; define your own growth goals and zoom out at least 90 days, with year-over-year comparison for seasonality
how: set a FireCraft goal (e.g. monthly audience) and review it every 90 days

name: New uploads are entry points
what: the Overview pairs views with a timeline of published videos; publishing is often correlated with view growth as each video is a new entry point
how: check the Overview timeline after each upload to see the bump each one gives

name: Sort the Content list by AVD
what: YouTube suggests sorting by impressions to see reach potential and by average view duration to see what keeps viewers; then compare top vs low performers for shared themes, editing styles or thumbnails
how: sort by AVD, note the editing style of the top 3

name: Don't compare across formats
what: long-form, Shorts and live audiences differ, so success looks different; use the Content tab chips to compare within a format
how: keep Shorts and long videos in separate comparison groups

name: Trial reels: test with non-followers first
what: a trial reel is shown to accounts that don't follow you; followers don't see it in feed/Reels and it isn't on your profile unless you share it to everyone; insights arrive within 24 hours
how: post two hook variants of a FireCraft reel as trial reels, then "Share to everyone" with the better one

name: Trial-reel eligibility
what: needs a public account with at least 200 followers (professional) or 1,000 (personal), and an account eligible for recommendations (check Account Status)
how: check Account Status before planning a trial-reel test

name: Trial reels must be new content
what: a trial reel may get limited reach if Instagram detects you shared the same content before; trial reels are ranked independently and don't affect your standard reels
how: render a fresh cut (new hook/order) for each trial, never re-post the same file

name: Auto-share winning trials
what: "Share to everyone automatically" (Trial settings) shares a trial reel when it performs well soon after publishing, based on views and engagement; the setting sticks for future trials
how: turn it on when testing several hooks at once

name: Boostable reel rules
what: to boost: 90 s or less, full-screen 9:16, no licensed music (royalty-free or original audio), no third-party face/camera effects, GIFs, product tags or interactive stickers, not already shared to Facebook
how: if a reel may be boosted, keep it ≤90 s, 1080x1920, with our CC0/own music

name: Boost from the web to skip the Apple fee
what: in most regions a 30% Apple service fee may apply when adding funds in the Instagram iOS app; boosting via instagram.com avoids it
how: tell the owner to boost from a browser

name: Up Next keys on the current video
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: YouTube says the video being watched is the main signal for what plays next, while Home relies mainly on watch history
how: to win Up Next, make follow-ups that clearly continue a popular video (same topic, series name in title)

name: Satisfaction surveys, not just watch time
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: signals include watch and search history, subscriptions, likes, dislikes, "Not interested", "Don't recommend channel" and satisfaction surveys that help the system understand satisfaction beyond watch time
how: avoid packaging that misrepresents the video; deliver the promised payoff

name: AI-made videos recommended equally
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: YouTube states videos made with AI can be recommended as broadly as videos made without AI
how: our ACE-Step/AI-assisted promos face no recommendation penalty for being AI-assisted; judge them by the same metrics

name: Search = relevance, engagement, quality
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: YouTube search weighs relevance (title, tags, description and video content matching the query), engagement (e.g. watch time of that video for that query) and quality (channels showing expertise/authoritativeness); no paid placement
how: for search-driven tutorials, answer the query early so query-specific watch time stays high

name: Two goals of the algorithm
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: help each viewer find videos they want, and maximise long-term viewer satisfaction; it "follows the audience", so ask "does my audience like this?" not "does the algorithm like it?"
how: test cuts on real viewers (Discord preview) rather than chasing rumoured tricks

name: Consistent title/thumbnail style
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: YouTube says a consistent title and thumbnail style makes videos instantly identifiable
how: fix one FireCraft title pattern and one thumbnail layout per series

name: Series + "if you liked this, watch..." CTAs
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: YouTube suggests content series, clear CTAs ("If you liked this, then watch..."), playlists and end screens to help viewers find more of your content
how: end each episode with a spoken CTA to the next one, matched by an end-screen element

name: Each video gets fresh judgement, but misses add up
section: How YouTube recommendation and search work (official explainers)
what: the algorithm uses fresh performance data per video, so one failed experiment won't necessarily hurt; frequently posting content that doesn't resonate can affect channel performance over time
how: experiment freely, but don't upload many weak test videos in a row

name: Chapter list validator
section: Tested pre-upload checks (scripts for this repo)
what: YouTube chapters need a first timestamp of 00:00, at least three timestamps in ascending order, each chapter at least 10 s
how: `python3 library/tools/youtube_chapters.py "0:Intro" "42:Rules" "95:Heart steal"` prints `00:00 Intro / 00:42 Rules / 01:35 Heart steal` and aborts with an error if a rule is broken (script in scratchpad sk2_15/tools/chapters.py; tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Candidate chapter points from scene cuts
section: Tested pre-upload checks (scripts for this repo)
what: list hard cuts as possible chapter starts, then pick real topic changes by hand
how: `ffmpeg -i v.mp4 -vf "select='gt(scene,0.4)',showinfo" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o 'pts_time:[0-9.]*'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Will it become a Short? check before upload
section: Tested pre-upload checks (scripts for this repo)
what: square/vertical up to 3 min is a Short; over 1 min with any claim is blocked
how: `python3 -c "import subprocess,json;d=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['ffprobe','-v','error','-show_entries','stream=width,height:format=duration','-of','json','in.mp4']));w,h=d['streams'][0]['width'],d['streams'][0]['height'];t=float(d['format']['duration']);print('Short' if h>=w and t<=180 else 'long-form',t,'over60' if t>60 else 'under60')"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: End-screen length check
section: Tested pre-upload checks (scripts for this repo)
what: end screens need a video of at least 25 s and sit in the last 5-20 s
how: `python3 -c "import subprocess;d=float(subprocess.check_output(['ffprobe','-v','error','-show_entries','format=duration','-of','csv=p=0','in.mp4']));print('ok' if d>=25 else 'too short', 'window from', round(max(0,d-20),2))"` then keep that window free of key on-screen text (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Measure the loop seam
section: Tested pre-upload checks (scripts for this repo)
what: for clips that will loop (LinkedIn ads under 30 s loop; Shorts loops don't add engaged views), compare the first and last frame numerically
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -frames:v 1 first.png; ffmpeg -sseof -0.04 -i in.mp4 -frames:v 1 last.png; ffmpeg -i first.png -i last.png -lavfi ssim -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"` (tested here 2026-10-24; this only reports similarity, it doesn't judge how the loop looks)

name: Studio upload vs Get suggestions
what: under "Thumbnail" in Studio you either Upload file or click Get suggestions to have one generated; custom upload needs a verified account
how: Studio > Content > video > Thumbnail > Upload file; hand the owner our JPG for this step.

name: Shorts custom thumbnail: computer only
what: custom Shorts thumbnails can currently only be added in YouTube Studio on a computer (Content > Shorts tab), recommended 9:16
how: tell the owner to set it from a desktop browser, not the phone app; export 2160x3840 or 1080x1920.

name: Upload size limit depends on device
what: mobile 2 MB for video thumbnails (10 MB for podcasts), desktop 50 MB for video, Shorts and podcast thumbnails
how: if the owner uploads from the phone, deliver a JPG under 2 MB; from desktop a big PNG is fine.

name: Podcast playlists are 1:1
what: podcast playlist thumbnails should be 1:1, not 16:9
how: render a separate square cover for podcast playlists, e.g. `ImageOps.pad(im,(1080,1080))` (see PIL section).

name: Vertical video + 16:9 thumbnail gets replaced on Home
what: a vertical video with a 16:9 custom thumbnail is shown with an auto-generated 4:5 thumbnail on Home, Explore and Subscriptions; the custom one still shows on the watch feed, history and non-mobile
how: for vertical uploads make the custom thumbnail 9:16 so YouTube has no reason to swap it.

name: Daily custom thumbnail limit
what: channels have a daily upload cap ("Daily custom thumbnail limit reached": try again in 24 h); limits vary by country and channel history, and strikes reduce it
how: finalise A/B variants before uploading; don't upload many test versions in one day.

name: Strikes for thumbnails
what: thumbnails with nudity/sexual content, hate speech, violence or harmful content can be rejected and bring a strike; repeat offences can remove custom-thumbnail rights for 30 days
how: check every FireCraft/PvP thumbnail for gore before export.

name: Custom thumbnails can be hidden in search
what: YouTube may turn off custom thumbnails in certain search results when considered inappropriate
how: keep a clean version; if impressions in Search drop, check the thumbnail first.

name: Ask Studio thumbnail ideas
what: Ask Studio analyses the transcript and themes to suggest thumbnails; prompt "Create a thumbnail", add the video or reference images, refine with follow-ups (e.g. "make the text larger")
how: owner-side tool in the publishing flow; use our render as reference image if wanted.

name: Misleading thumbnail = policy violation
what: the thumbnails policy bans a thumbnail that makes viewers think they'll see something not in the video, plus vulgar text, gore and sexual imagery
how: only show moments that are in the video.

name: Age-restriction instead of strike
what: a borderline thumbnail may get the video age-restricted or the thumbnail removed without a strike; YouTube looks at whether violent/gory imagery or sexualised body parts are the focal point and whether text is meant to shock
how: keep weapons/blood out of the focal point for PvP thumbnails.

name: First-strike warning and 90-day training
what: a first violation usually gets a warning; a policy training lets it expire after 90 days; three strikes in 90 days can end the channel
how: reason to never test borderline thumbnails.

name: Impersonation in thumbnails
what: copying another channel's branding, or using AI to copy someone's likeness so the channel looks authorised by them, is not allowed
how: never put a real creator's face/brand on our thumbnails; the default host is the owner's own skin.

name: API thumbnails.set limits
what: the Data API upload accepts image/jpeg, image/png or application/octet-stream, max 50 MB, ~50 quota units per call; 429 uploadRateLimitExceeded when the channel uploaded too many recently
how: `POST https://www.googleapis.com/upload/youtube/v3/thumbnails/set?videoId=ID` with scope youtube.upload (needs owner OAuth; not set up here).

name: API resizes with black bars, never crops
what: an uploaded thumbnail that doesn't match the dimensions is resized without changing aspect ratio, may get black bars, not cropped
how: always export exactly 16:9 so no bars appear.

name: The 5 served sizes
what: video thumbnails are served as default 120x90, medium 320x180, high 480x360, standard 640x480, maxres 1280x720
how: preview our design at 320x180 and 120x90: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf scale=320:180:flags=lanczos m.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 4:3 sizes letterbox a 16:9 design
what: default/high/standard are 4:3 (120x90, 480x360, 640x480), so some surfaces/embeds get a 4:3 frame
how: check a 4:3 pad preview: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf "scale=480:270,pad=480:360:0:45" h.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fetch an existing thumbnail for reference
what: the API's snippet.thumbnails gives URLs per size (maxres when available)
how: for the owner's own videos, `curl -sO https://i.ytimg.com/vi/<ID>/maxresdefault.jpg` (i.ytimg.com was allowlisted, per CLAUDE.md) to compare old vs new.

name: Choose Title only, Thumbnail only, or both
what: the A/B Testing button sits in the Title box or under Thumbnail; pick one of three modes and upload up to 3 variants
how: deliver 3 files named A/B/C; test only thumbnails if the title is fixed.

name: Editing during a test stops it
what: changing the title or thumbnail while a test runs stops it automatically and it must be restarted
how: tell the owner not to tweak anything until the result.

name: Low-res variant downgrades all
what: if any test thumbnail is under 720p (1280x720), all experiment thumbnails are downscaled to 480p (854x480)
how: check every variant: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=width,height -of csv=p=0 v*.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Not for Shorts, Premieres, scheduled lives, kids/mature/private
what: Live archives can be tested; Premieres only after they become long-form; uploads up to 3 min that are square/vertical count as Shorts
how: don't prepare A/B variants for Shorts or the vertical promo.

name: Needs advanced features, desktop only
what: A/B testing works only in Studio on a computer with advanced features enabled
how: owner sets it on desktop.

name: Control group sees the default
what: a small share of traffic may be held back and only sees the default title/thumbnail; it's excluded from the calculation
how: read results under Analytics > Reach > "How your A/B test is going" > Manage test.

name: Test old videos first
what: YouTube recommends starting tests on older videos to limit the impact on overall views
how: first test a back-catalogue FireCraft video before a launch video.

name: Native vs third-party testers
what: YouTube's tests are concurrent A/B/C; many third-party tools test sequentially and optimise CTR, so they can pick a different winner
how: trust the Studio result over sequential swaps.

name: Same video, different results
what: results can vary like a coin flip, and early impressions come more from people who know the channel, later from new viewers
how: don't over-read one test; repeat the idea on another video.

name: Not enough impressions = no winner
what: YouTube says a "Winner" is more likely the more views the video gets; low-impression videos often end Performed Same or Inconclusive
how: test on videos that still get impressions.

name: Target subscribers vs casual viewers
what: for subscribers highlight familiar features (e.g. your best friend); for casual viewers show universally relatable actions and emotions (e.g. a shocked face)
how: FireCraft returning players: familiar server landmarks; new players: a big reaction.

name: 90% of best performers use custom thumbnails
what: YouTube states 90% of the best-performing videos have custom thumbnails
how: always deliver a custom one with every long video.

name: Shoot thumbnail stills during the shoot
what: take pictures during your shoot so you have several options at upload
how: ask the owner for 3-5 phone photos (posed reaction) per shoot.

name: Measure CTR on Home/Suggested in the first 24 h
what: for general audiences check CTR from Home and Suggested in the first 24 h on videos with above-average impressions; for subscribers check CTR in the Subscriptions feed
how: ask the owner for these two numbers when judging a new style.

name: Use the Audience tab for ideas
what: the Audience tab shows other videos your audience watched, useful for thumbnail and title ideas; research insights show what they search
how: owner shares a screenshot; we pull those thumbnails as style references.

name: Limit ALL CAPS and emoji in titles
what: use them carefully to emphasise emotion, e.g. "Our KIDS Built A ROBOT!"; keep titles short, key words first, episode numbers and branding at the end
how: pair the thumbnail text with a title that doesn't repeat it.

name: Reel cover is cropped 3:4 on the profile grid
what: Instagram's grid shows Reels at 3:4 (1080x1440) since January 2025; a 1080x1920 cover loses 240 px top and bottom
how: keep title and face inside the centred 1080x1440 box; preview `ffmpeg -i cover.png -vf crop=1080:1440:0:240 grid.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Reel cover cannot be changed after posting
what: Instagram's Help Center (as quoted) says you can't edit the cover photo after the Reel is uploaded, so choose it before sharing
how: send the owner the cover file together with the video, not later.
refs: Superprofile (quoting Instagram Help, read 14 Oct 2026), https://superprofile.bio/guides/instagram-reel-size.md, checked 2026-10-24

name: Reels over 3 min aren't recommended to new audiences
what: per Instagram Help (as quoted), long Reels still reach followers but not non-followers
how: keep FireCraft promos under 3 min if reach matters.

name: Reel safe zone ~950x980 centred
what: Meta's percentage safe zones convert to roughly a centred 950x980 px area on 1080x1920; bottom clearance deepens on the right where buttons stack
how: draw a guide box when designing the cover: `ffmpeg -i cover.png -vf drawbox=x=65:y=470:w=950:h=980:color=yellow@0.6:t=4 guide.png` (tested here 2026-10-24) (box placement centred is our approximation, check it in Ads Manager's Safe zone overlay)

name: One look across all covers
what: same font, colour band and placement across Reels makes a grid look deliberate; Oktopost says to keep one primary ratio for 80% of posts
how: save the cover as a HyperFrames/PIL template in library/ and reuse it.

name: Design posts at 4:5 for feed + grid
what: uploading 4:5 (1080x1350) gives the most control across feed and 3:4 grid; square and landscape posts get letterboxed or cropped
how: carousel first slides / photo posts: 1080x1350 canvas.

name: TikTok: cover locked after posting
what: TikTok doesn't let you edit the cover after the video is live; the workaround is re-uploading the video with a new cover
how: decide the cover frame before handing over the file.

name: TikTok: upload a custom cover image
what: on the post screen tap Edit cover, drag the timeline to a frame or tap Upload for a gallery image; add cover text in a chosen font style, pinch to resize/rotate
how: give the owner a 1080x1920 cover PNG in the gallery.

name: Brand colour across TikTok covers
what: Kapwing's example: Summer Fridays keeps a pastel green on every cover so the profile looks curated; consistency = same font, palette or recurring character
how: FireCraft covers: one fixed accent colour + host skin.

name: Pinterest safe zones
what: keep text/key elements away from: top 270 px, left 65 px, right 195 px, bottom 790 px (image and video Pins)
how: `ffmpeg -i pin.png -vf "drawbox=x=65:y=270:w=iw-260:h=ih-1060:color=red@0.7:t=4" pinsafe.png` on 1080x1920 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pinterest video Pin ratios
what: 9:16 (1080x1920) for full-bleed, also 1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 4:5, 1:1; MP4/M4V (MOV on mobile), H.264/H.265, 4 s to 5 min
how: our vertical render fits as is.

name: Pinterest tints white/black image backgrounds
what: image Pins with near-white backgrounds get a 4% black layer in light mode; near-black ones get 10% white in dark mode (not videos)
how: pure white/black cover backgrounds won't look exactly as exported; prefer a coloured background.

name: Pinterest image limits
what: BMP, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WEBP; web upload up to 20 MB; title 100 characters, description 800 (descriptions aren't shown in feeds but used for relevance)
how: export PNG/JPG under 20 MB.

name: LinkedIn video ad thumbnail
what: optional, JPG or PNG, max 2 MB, aspect ratio and resolution should match the video
how: same render as the video size, JPG q 2-3 under 2 MB.

name: Facebook video/Reel thumbnail
what: per Ayrshare's Facebook Pages guide: no dimension requirement but same aspect ratio as the video; BMP/GIF/JPEG/PNG/TIFF, max 10 MB (Reels thumbnail JPEG/PNG, 10 MB)
how: reuse the 16:9 or 9:16 render.

name: Facebook feed images shown ~470 px wide
what: Ayrshare: images appear in feed at max 470 px wide (page 504 px), recommended upload 1200x630, max 2048x2048
how: check the cover at 470 px wide: `ffmpeg -i c.png -vf scale=470:-2 fb.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Eye contact with visible whites
what: humans evolved to detect eye contact; close-ups with eye contact, especially with the whites of the eyes visible, are more eye-catching (Frederator's top tactic)
how: pick frames where the subject looks into the lens, eyes open wide.

name: Strong emotion through empathy
what: strong emotions are easily identified and the viewer feels them through empathy; target surprise, shock, empathy, excitement, confusion, intrigue
how: ask the owner for an exaggerated reaction photo.

name: Collage of several emotions
what: when one emotion isn't enough, compile several images of your face to show the range the video goes through
how: PIL paste 2-3 cutouts side by side.

name: Familiar + unfamiliar
what: a familiar face or object catches attention; pairing it with something surprising creates curiosity
how: host skin + one unexpected item from the video.

name: Cartoon/caricature version
what: turning your face or content into a cartoon is a way to switch up the look
how: our blocky host (`library/tools/blocky_character.py`) is exactly that.

name: Tight crop wins at small size
what: a chest-up shot leaves the face ~30 px tall at 120 px width: reads as "a face", not an emotion; get close and let the expression read
how: crop so the face is large before adding text.

name: Two people must both fit large
what: with two people in a thumbnail both faces need to stay readable; equally weighted subjects give the eye no place to land
how: make one dominant, the other smaller.

name: Sunburst behind the face
what: Frederator had success with a sunburst/pinwheel background whose vanishing point sits directly behind the face, pulling the eye back to the subject
how: draw rays with PIL `ImageDraw.polygon` from the face centre (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bright backgrounds stand out on white YouTube
what: bright backgrounds pop against YouTube's white page and against other thumbnails
how: prefer saturated background colours over dark photos for light-mode feeds.

name: Outline the subject
what: contrast and outlines separate the subject from the background and add depth; outline layered images with a solid colour on busy backgrounds
how: dilate the rembg alpha and fill it white behind the cutout (see PIL section).

name: Nothing important bottom-right
what: YouTube covers the lower-right corner with the timestamp or watch-later button, and Western readers look there last
how: keep text/logo out of the bottom-right ~20%.

name: Thumbnail should match the first 15-30 s
what: viewers who feel duped click away; if the thumbnail moment is late, reorder the video or say early that it's coming
how: pick the thumbnail moment, then check it appears (or is announced) in the opening.

name: Show the result, not the process
what: Frederator's rainbow-cake example: the bright shot of the finished cake with a smiling person beat a dark shot of pouring liquid
how: for build/PvP videos show the finished build or the win.

name: Copy what the target audience is trained to click
what: Frederator's Toy Pizza changed to the style similar-audience channels used (full toy, muted background, text, one toy) and performance rose
how: pull 10 thumbnails from top Minecraft lifesteal channels as references before designing.

name: Small bug/logo for recognition
what: a small logo or watermark signals "this is one of yours"; keep it in one fixed corner every time
how: FireCraft logo top-left, same size every thumbnail.

name: Consistency of layout
what: consistent palette, layout, number of subjects, arrangement and font make your videos identifiable; Frederator ran 8 templates over 20 months on one channel
how: keep one template per series.

name: Series/playlist themes
what: give each series or playlist its own colours/layout/images for a tidy channel page
how: one accent colour per FireCraft series.

name: Negative space
what: don't fear empty space; it emphasises what matters
how: leave the side opposite the subject plain for text.

name: Plain background for emphasis
what: a solid colour or subtle pattern makes the important things obvious
how: rembg cutout on a flat colour canvas.

name: Before/after thumbnail
what: before and after photos with obvious differences make people curious about the process
how: `ffmpeg -i before.png -i after.png -filter_complex hstack=inputs=2,scale=1280:720 ba.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Story in several photos
what: multiple images can show a progression; good for story-time videos
how: 3-panel `hstack=inputs=3`.

name: Arrows lead the eye
what: arrows and directional symbols guide viewers to the important part
how: PIL polygon arrow pointing at the key object.

name: Blur the reveal
what: blur the one thing viewers want to see so they have to watch
how: `ffmpeg -i t.png -filter_complex "[0]crop=200:200:500:200,boxblur=20[b];[0][b]overlay=500:200" out.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Magnify the key detail
what: show the image but also a magnified part so viewers see exactly what earns interest
how: crop + scale x2 + overlay with an outline circle.

name: Use a key moment from the video
what: most thumbnails are made-up images, but a real exciting moment immerses viewers
how: grab the frame with ffmpeg (see frame-grab section).

name: One strong image, no extras
what: if the image is compelling, don't distract from it; the title carries the info
how: for a striking frame skip text.

name: Statistic or chart as hook
what: a shocking statistic or graph makes viewers want the context
how: big number as the only text.

name: Symbols and emoji replace words
what: thumbs up, X and check marks, stars or emoji communicate faster than words (viewers decide in about two seconds)
how: PIL with `embedded_color=True` and Noto Color Emoji (see PIL section).

name: Font matching the topic
what: e.g. a pixel font for Minecraft, a flourish font for Paris
how: FireCraft: blocky/pixel display font for the title word.

name: Clear focal point upper third or centre
what: winners point the eye to one focal point in the upper third or centre; the rest supports it
how: place the face on a thirds intersection or centre.

name: Busy background = noise when small
what: simplify, blur heavily or replace with flat colour; the thumbnail isn't for environment storytelling
how: `ffmpeg -i bg.png -vf gblur=sigma=25 bgb.png` then paste the cutout (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Triage order: text, face, then detail
what: what fails first when shrunk: text, then facial expression, then background detail; lose detail, never title or expression
how: fix in that order when the 120 px test fails.

name: Too many elements
what: face + product + background is already three; adding text makes four, past clarity for most
how: drop text when the other three are strong.

name: Complementary colours
what: opposite colours on the wheel stand out against each other, e.g. a blue subject on yellow-orange
how: compute the complement hue in Python: `colorsys.rgb_to_hsv`, add 0.5 to hue (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Analogous backgrounds
what: colours next to each other on the wheel are pleasing; Frederator sometimes used them in backgrounds
how: gradient between two neighbouring hues.

name: Use yellow
what: Frederator reports thumbnails with yellow performed statistically better (their data, explained by M and L cones both firing)
how: yellow text or accent where it fits.

name: Monochrome/dichromatic channel theme
what: shades and tints of one colour, or a two-colour scheme repeated across a channel, is a popular alternative to contrast
how: fix two brand colours for FireCraft.

name: Highlight one word in another colour/font
what: make the most intriguing word stand out with a different colour or font, high contrast (light vs dark or big size difference)
how: draw that word separately in PIL with its own fill.

name: Think in luminance, not hue
what: two saturated colours of similar luminance (red on orange, teal on green) merge when shrunk; foreground and background must differ in lightness
how: compare relative luminance (WCAG formula, see checks section).

name: Saturated primaries on neutral backgrounds
what: after a 10x shrink saturated primaries against neutrals tend to win, pastel-on-pastel loses
how: check the 128 px version.

name: Hard-edged subject/background contrast
what: subject much brighter, much darker, or on a flat colour block
how: darken the background: `ffmpeg -i bg.png -vf eq=brightness=-0.15:saturation=0.7 d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Niche sets the execution
what: finance: clean text, restrained colour, one face; gaming: saturated chroma, exaggerated expression, bold sans-serif
how: FireCraft = gaming execution.

name: 3-4 words max, heavy outline
what: Frederator avoids text generally, but when used (e.g. gaming) 3-4 words max with heavy outline or contrasting colours
how: PIL `stroke_width` (see PIL section).

name: Fewer, bigger words
what: one word at 200 px tall beats five at 60; 2-3 words survive the shrink
how: cut the line to its strongest word.

name: Cap height 16-20 real px on phone
what: CreatiCalc's rule of thumb (their testing, not a study) for comfortable legibility at thumbnail size
how: at 120 px wide display that means very large letters; test the 120 px export.

name: Text 15-20% of thumbnail height
what: TubeCore: at least 108-144 px tall on a 720 px thumbnail
how: in PIL size the font until `textbbox` height >= 0.15*H (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Text must add info, not repeat the title
what: text helps when it narrows the promise ("$10,000", "Day 1", "FAILED"); repeating the title wastes a channel
how: write title first, then a 1-3 word thumbnail line that's different.

name: Numbers as text
what: numbers are visually distinct and imply specificity ("7 Mistakes", "30 Days")
how: "SEASON 2" / "DAY 1" style for FireCraft.

name: Series labels
what: "Part 3", "Week 12", "Season 2" help viewers place an episode
how: fixed corner badge per episode.

name: Skip text when the image explains itself
what: before/after, unboxing or a dramatic game screenshot often needs none
how: test text vs no-text variant.

name: Bold sans-serif fonts
what: Impact, Montserrat Bold, Oswald Bold, Bebas Neue, Anton survive downscaling; thin, serif or decorative fonts don't
how: we already have `library/fonts/Anton-Regular.ttf` (OFL).

name: All caps for 1-2 words only
what: for 3+ words mixed/title case reads faster
how: caps only on the short punch word.

name: 2-4 px outline or shadow for light and dark mode
what: YouTube shows thumbnails on white and dark interfaces; a strong outline/shadow keeps text readable in both
how: check the thumbnail pasted on #ffffff and #0f0f0f (see checks section).

name: Text opposite the face
what: face left = text right; face centred = text above/below; never overlapping
how: layout rule for the PIL template.

name: Text on the highest-contrast area
what: yellow on blue, white on dark, black on bright
how: sample the region's mean luminance before choosing the fill.

name: Thumbnail text isn't indexed for search
what: per TubeCore, YouTube doesn't read thumbnail text for ranking; it's purely for humans
how: put keywords in title/description, not the image.

name: Some languages need fewer words
what: languages needing more characters per idea need fewer words or bigger font
how: Roman Urdu lines are long: keep 1-2 words.

name: Text vs no-text test protocol
what: alternate text/no-text for 10 uploads, keep face, background and composition constant, compare CTR after 1,000+ impressions each
