how: suggest to the owner for Shorts/older videos where A/B isn't available.

name: Turn the searched question into text
what: make the question people search the thumbnail text so they know the answer is inside
how: e.g. "Join kaise karein?" for a FireCraft how-to.

name: Curiosity: leave a "how/why"
what: don't give everything away; e.g. "How I was able to…"
how: text that states the outcome, not the method.

name: "FAIL" text
what: admitting a failure in big bold text is relatable and eye-catching
how: for blooper/challenge videos.

name: 55-70% of impressions are small
what: Frederator estimated 55-70% of their thumbnail impressions were small-scale; design for small
how: always judge the 168-320 px version.

name: 120 px test size
what: CreatiCalc designs against ~120 px wide (their test size; YouTube publishes no render width); up-next ~100 px, suggested rail ~160 px by their estimate
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf scale=120:-2:flags=area t120.png` and look at it (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 168 px desktop sidebar
what: TubeCore names 168 px wide as the desktop sidebar size where text must still read

name: Squint test
what: blur your eyes/blur the preview; if you still know what it's about, it holds up small
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf gblur=sigma=6 squint.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Three questions at 120 px
what: can I read the text, can I tell the expression, do I know what the video is about? If not: bigger text, tighter crop, simpler background
how: run this on the small export before delivering.

name: View it on a real phone
what: design tools and Studio preview at desktop size; open the export on an actual phone
how: send the owner the small preview via SendUserFile to look at on the phone.

name: Frederator's TrueView CTR trick
what: they compared thumbnail templates by running cheap TrueView ads (a few dollars a day) and reading relative CTR; without ads use views per unique and views from subscribers as rough signals
how: only if the owner wants to spend; native Test & Compare is free.

name: Gaze toward the object
what: eye-tracking on banner ads: when a face gazed toward the product, viewers were more likely to look at it and reported higher purchase intention than with gaze away
how: have the host look toward the text/item, not out of frame.
refs: Frontiers in Psychology via PMC, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5454066/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Averted vs direct gaze
what: the same paper cites print/banner studies where gaze at the product beat gaze at the viewer for attention to the product and brand memory
how: direct gaze for a reaction thumbnail; gaze-to-item when the item is the hook.

name: Faces beat banner blindness
what: the cited literature: faces capture attention faster and more automatically than non-social objects
how: include a face (or the blocky host's face) when the topic allows.

name: Title + thumbnail before filming
what: in the leaked MrBeast production guide the creative process starts with title and thumbnail; they set viewer expectations and the first minute must prove them
how: draft the FireCraft thumbnail idea before editing the promo.
refs: Simon Willison on the MrBeast PDF, https://simonwillison.net/2024/Sep/15/how-to-succeed-in-mrbeast-production/, checked 2026-10-24

name: Pick the more visual concept
what: MrBeast: "50 Hours In My Front Yard" vs "50 Hours In Ketchup": similar effort, the ketchup image is far more clickable
how: choose the concept whose single image is the strangest.

name: CTR dictates the video
what: the guide says CTR "is what dictates what we do for videos"
how: treat the thumbnail as part of the edit, not an afterthought.

name: Dedicated thumbnail beats a random still
what: Clipchamp's movie-poster analogy: a random still (the hero eating breakfast) won't sell an action film; make a dedicated image
how: never ship the auto frame.

name: LinkedIn picks a random frame
what: without a custom thumbnail LinkedIn auto-generates one from a random (maybe blurry/awkward) frame; upload JPG/PNG under 2 MB matching the video ratio
how: export with the video.

name: Gestalt figure-ground
what: clear separation between subject and background is essential; desaturated backgrounds let saturated foreground elements dominate
how: `ffmpeg -i bg.png -vf hue=s=0.5 bgd.png` on the background layer only, then paste the cutout (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Text where the eye lands, 3 words max
what: Fluxnote: top third or alongside the face, one big primary word, small context text; test at 168x94
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf scale=168:94 f.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 3-5 px shadow/outline on busy images
what: white or black text works on most backgrounds; add 3-5 px shadow or outline on complex images
how: drawtext `borderw=4` or PIL `stroke_width=4` at 1280 wide.

name: Vibrant colours, bold Hindi text, expressive faces
what: Boss Wallah notes Indian YouTubers often use vibrant, colourful images; red, yellow and blue to grab attention; a close-up face for personal/story videos
how: apply to Roman-Urdu/Hindi promo thumbnails for the owner's clients.

name: Bold Devanagari fonts
what: IndiaFont: AMS Shaurya (most popular), AMS Rudra, AMS Bhima for extra-bold Hindi thumbnail text; avoid highly decorative fonts; Hindi text 3-5 words
how: those are commercial; here use the free OFL `library/fonts/Kalam-Bold.ttf` or `RozhaOne-Regular.ttf` (both have the Devanagari subset per Google Fonts METADATA).

name: Export the regional text as transparent PNG, stroke later
what: IndiaFont's workflow: make the Hindi text as a transparent PNG, then add stroke/shadow in the editor; text ~30-50% of the thumbnail (their advice)
how: in PIL render text on an RGBA canvas, then stroke/shadow (see PIL section).

name: Mobile size ~120x68 for regional text
what: IndiaFont's readability target: about 120x68 px on mobile
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf scale=120:68 i120.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Look at big Indian channels, keep your own style
what: Boss Wallah cites Ashish Chanchlani and BB Ki Vines; study popular Indian channels but stay unique; keep logo subtle and colour scheme consistent
how: reference board of 5-10 desi thumbnails before designing.

name: Hindi/Urdu text in PIL needs Raqm
what: `direction`, `features` and `language` in `ImageDraw.text` require libraqm; without it Devanagari conjuncts and Urdu joining break. Here `features.check('raqm')` is True (raqm 0.10.5)
how: `python3 -c "from PIL import features;print(features.check('raqm'))"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Devanagari line in PIL
how: `ImageDraw.Draw(im).text((60,300),'नया सीज़न',font=ImageFont.truetype('library/fonts/Kalam-Bold.ttf',120),fill='white',stroke_width=6,stroke_fill='black',language='hi')` rendered correct conjuncts (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Urdu Nastaliq line in PIL
how: download Noto Nastaliq Urdu (OFL) `curl -sSLo NotoNastaliqUrdu.ttf "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/notonastaliqurdu/NotoNastaliqUrdu%5Bwght%5D.ttf"`, then `d.text((1220,300),'نیا سیزن',font=f,direction='rtl',language='ur',anchor='rm',stroke_width=5,stroke_fill='black')`: joined correctly (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bold weight of a variable font
what: Noto Nastaliq Urdu is a variable font with Regular/Medium/SemiBold/Bold named instances
how: `f=ImageFont.truetype('NotoNastaliqUrdu.ttf',110); f.set_variation_by_name('Bold')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ffmpeg drawtext shaping for RTL
what: drawtext `text_shaping=1` (default) reverses RTL and joins Arabic characters before drawing
how: prefer PIL for Urdu (we saw it render correctly); drawtext with text_shaping ran here on Latin text only (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fast input seek grab
what: `-ss` before `-i` seeks to the nearest seek point, and with accurate_seek (default when transcoding) decodes the gap so the frame is exact
how: `ffmpeg -ss 1.5 -i t.mp4 -frames:v 1 g.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Output-side seek
what: `-ss` after `-i` decodes and discards until the time; slower on long files but simple
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -ss 1.5 -frames:v 1 g2.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Grab near the end
what: `-sseof` seeks relative to the end (negative = earlier)
how: `ffmpeg -sseof -0.5 -i t.mp4 -frames:v 1 last.png` for the payoff/freeze frame (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Single image with -frames:v 1
what: image2 writes one file when the name has no pattern; `-frames:v 1` stops after one frame
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -frames:v 1 img.jpeg` (tested here 2026-10-24 as g.png)

name: JPEG grab quality
what: `-q:v` is a codec-dependent fixed quality scale
how: `ffmpeg -ss 1 -i t.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 g.jpg` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: thumbnail filter picks a representative frame
what: selects the most representative frame per batch of n frames (default 100; big n costs memory)
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf thumbnail,scale=300:200 -frames:v 1 tf.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One candidate per batch
what: `thumbnail=n=30` gives one pick per 30 frames (≈1/s at 30 fps) to review as candidates
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf thumbnail=n=30 -fps_mode passthrough tf_%02d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24: 3 files from 3 s)

name: Keyframes-only contact sheet
what: `-skip_frame nokey` decodes only keyframes; tile them 8x8; `-fps_mode passthrough` stops frame duplication
how: `ffmpeg -skip_frame nokey -i t.mp4 -vf 'scale=128:72,tile=8x8' -an -fps_mode passthrough key%03d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: First frame of each scene, as mosaic
what: `select='gt(scene,0.4)'`; 0.3-0.5 is a sane range
how: `ffmpeg -i cuts.mp4 -vf "select='gt(scene,0.4)',scale=160:120,tile" -frames:v 1 preview.png` (tested here 2026-10-24; on a clip with no cuts it writes nothing)

name: Scene-change stills with scdet
what: scdet threshold good range 8-14 (default 10); `s=1` passes only scene-change frames
how: `ffmpeg -i cuts.mp4 -vf scdet=t=10:s=1 -fps_mode passthrough sc_%02d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24: 2 cuts -> 2 files)

name: Every Nth frame sheet
what: `select='not(mod(n,10))'` + tile with padding/margin
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf "select='not(mod(n,10))',scale=160:-2,tile=3x3:padding=4:margin=2" -frames:v 1 sheet.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: All frames in a window
what: `select='between(t,1,2)'` to dump candidates around a known moment
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf "select='between(t,1,2)'" -fps_mode passthrough b_%02d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Timed contact sheet
what: `fps=2.5` + tile for a 0.4 s sheet (the repo's "look first" step)
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf "fps=2.5,scale=200:-2,tile=4x2" -frames:v 1 cs.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One image per second
what: `-fps_mode cfr -r 1` with a %03d pattern
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -fps_mode cfr -r 1 img-%03d.jpeg` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Name stills by timestamp
what: image2 `frame_pts` puts the PTS in the filename so you know where a candidate came from
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf fps=2 -frame_pts true pts_%d.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Overwrite one preview file
what: image2 `-update 1` keeps overwriting one filename
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf fps=1 -update 1 latest.jpg` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Brightness per frame
what: signalstats YAVG (0-255 average luma) per frame, printed with the metadata filter
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf "fps=2,signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=yavg.txt" -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Colourfulness per frame
what: signalstats SATAVG (0-~181) to prefer saturated frames
how: same command with `key=lavfi.signalstats.SATAVG` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Reject blurry frames
what: blurdetect gives a no-reference blur value (Marziliano); doc example uses 80% of the most significant 32x32 blocks
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf "fps=2,blurdetect=block_width=32:block_height=32:block_pct=80,metadata=print:file=blur.txt" -f null -`; keep low-blur frames (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Detail via entropy
what: entropy filter measures greylevel histogram entropy per channel
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf "fps=2,entropy,metadata=print:file=ent.txt" -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Skip black frames
what: blackframe logs frames where >= amount% (default 98) pixels are below threshold (default 32)
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf blackframe=amount=98:threshold=32 -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Find held moments
what: freezedetect reports stretches with no significant change (noise default -60 dB, duration 2 s); frozen poses can be clean stills
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf freezedetect=n=-60dB:d=2 -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Remove letterbox before using a frame
what: cropdetect prints a crop= for the non-black area (limit default 24, round 16; 2 for even sizes)
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf cropdetect=limit=24:round=2 -frames:v 10 -f null -` then apply the printed crop (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bounding box of non-dark content
what: bbox prints the box of pixels above min_val, plus a ready crop=/drawbox=
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf bbox=min_val=16 -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spatial detail (SI/TI)
what: siti computes spatial and temporal information; print_summary gives a summary
how: `ffmpeg -i t.mp4 -vf siti=print_summary=1 -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Luma check with histogram/heat
what: histogram filter draws the levels; pseudocolor preset heat shows bright vs dark zones
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf histogram hist.png`, `-vf pseudocolor=preset=heat heat.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Outlined title with drawtext
what: `borderw`/`bordercolor` draw a text outline
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf "drawtext=fontfile=library/fonts/Anton-Regular.ttf:text='SEASON 2':fontsize=160:fontcolor=yellow:borderw=10:bordercolor=black:x=60:y=60" dt.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Drop shadow text
what: `shadowx/shadowy/shadowcolor`
how: `drawtext=...:fontcolor=white:shadowx=8:shadowy=8:shadowcolor=black@0.8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Text on a coloured block
what: `box=1:boxcolor=red:boxborderw=20` puts a padded block behind text
how: `drawtext=...:text='NEW':box=1:boxcolor=red:boxborderw=20` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Centred text
what: `x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2`
how: `drawtext=...:text='DAY 1':fontsize=200:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Dark band for text
what: drawbox `t=fill` with alpha
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf "drawbox=x=0:y=ih*0.7:w=iw:h=ih*0.3:color=black@0.6:t=fill" band.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Vignette to pull the eye inward
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf vignette=PI/4 vig.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sharpen the still
what: unsharp (luma 5x5, amount 1.0) or cas (contrast adaptive sharpen)
how: `-vf unsharp=5:5:1.0` / `-vf cas=strength=0.6` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Saturation boost
what: vibrance boosts less-saturated colours; hue=s scales saturation
how: `-vf vibrance=intensity=0.4` / `-vf hue=s=1.3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Warm/cool a frame
what: colortemperature in Kelvin
how: `-vf colortemperature=temperature=5000` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Contrast pop with a curves preset
how: `-vf curves=preset=increase_contrast` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Levels stretch
what: colorlevels input min/max per channel
how: `-vf colorlevels=rimin=0.05:gimin=0.05:bimin=0.05:rimax=0.95:gimax=0.95:bimax=0.95` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 2x2 variant board
what: xstack with layout for comparing 4 thumbnails side by side
how: `ffmpeg -i a.png -i b.png -i c.png -i d.png -filter_complex "[0]scale=640:360[a];[1]scale=640:360[b];[2]scale=640:360[c];[3]scale=640:360[d];[a][b][c][d]xstack=inputs=4:layout=0_0|w0_0|0_h0|w0_h0" grid4.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 16:9 to 9:16 by padding
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf "scale=1080:-2,pad=1080:1920:0:(oh-ih)/2:color=0x101010" padv.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 16:9 to 9:16 with blurred fill
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -filter_complex "[0]scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1080:1920,gblur=sigma=30[bg];[0]scale=1080:-2[fg];[bg][fg]overlay=0:(H-h)/2" bfv.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 16:9 to 9:16 centre crop
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf "crop=ih*9/16:ih,scale=1080:1920" ccv.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Upscale to the 3840x2160 recommendation
what: lanczos with scale, or zscale filter=lanczos
how: `-vf scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos` or `-vf zscale=w=3840:h=2160:filter=lanczos` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Logo bug in a fixed corner
what: overlay at `W-w-40:40` (top-right, away from the duration badge)
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -i logo.png -filter_complex "overlay=W-w-40:40" out.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Light vs dark UI mock
what: paste the 320x180 version on #0f0f0f and white
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=0x0f0f0f:s=400x260 -i m.png -filter_complex "overlay=40:40" -frames:v 1 darkui.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Value check in grey
what: greyscale at small size shows if subject and background separate by lightness
how: `ffmpeg -i thumb.png -vf "format=gray,scale=160:-2" g160.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Edge map for clutter
what: edgedetect shows how busy the background is
how: `-vf edgedetect=low=0.1:high=0.4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: WebP/AVIF/JXL exports
what: this ffmpeg has libwebp, libaom-av1 and libjxl encoders (YouTube asks for JPG or PNG, so these are for web/blog use)
how: `-c:v libwebp -quality 85 t.webp`; `-frames:v 1 -c:v libaom-av1 -still-picture 1 t.avif`; `-c:v libjxl t.jxl` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Outlined text in one call
what: `ImageDraw.text(..., stroke_width=10, stroke_fill='black')`; stroke_fill defaults to the fill colour
how: `d.text((60,60),'SEASON 2',font=ImageFont.truetype('library/fonts/Anton-Regular.ttf',160),fill='yellow',stroke_width=10,stroke_fill='black')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Centre text on a point with anchors
what: `anchor='mm'` puts the text's middle on xy (default is top-left 'la')
how: `d.text((640,360),'DAY 1',font=f,anchor='mm',stroke_width=8,stroke_fill='black')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Size text to a target height
what: measure with `textbbox` (includes stroke_width when passed) and grow the font until the height reaches 15% of H
how: loop `ImageFont.truetype(font,size)` + `d.textbbox((0,0),'WIN',font=f)`; Anton reached 110 px tall at size 128 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fit thumbnail text to a width with Pillow
what: `ImageDraw.textlength` returns the advance width; shrink the size until it fits the free side
how: `while d.textlength('LIFESTEAL',font=ImageFont.truetype(F,size))>600: size-=4` (tested here 2026-10-24: 164)

name: Two-line stacked title
what: `multiline_text` with `spacing` (pixels between lines) and `align`
how: `d.multiline_text((60,60),'NEW\nSEASON',font=f,spacing=-10,align='left',stroke_width=6,stroke_fill='black')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Accent word in a second colour
what: draw word by word, advancing x by `textlength`
how: `for w,c in [('FREE ','white'),('DIAMONDS','#ffd400')]: d.text((x,60),w,font=f,fill=c,stroke_width=6,stroke_fill='black'); x+=d.textlength(w,font=f)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Soft drop shadow
what: draw the text on a transparent layer, `GaussianBlur`, alpha-composite under the sharp text
how: `sh=sh.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(8)); im=Image.alpha_composite(im,sh)` then draw the text (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Colour emoji
what: `embedded_color=True` uses the font's colour glyphs (COLR/CBDT/SBIX)
how: `d.text((900,60),'🔥',font=ImageFont.truetype('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/noto/NotoColorEmoji.ttf',109),embedded_color=True)` (size 109 worked here; tested 2026-10-24)

name: Episode badge
what: `rounded_rectangle(xy, radius, fill, outline, width)` + centred text
how: `d.rounded_rectangle((40,560,420,680),radius=40,fill='#e00000',outline='white',width=6); d.text((230,620),'EP 3',font=f,anchor='mm')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Arrow
what: `polygon` with outline and width

name: Circle highlight
what: `ImageDraw.circle(xy, radius, outline, width)`
how: `d.circle((900,400),120,outline='red',width=14)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sunburst rays
what: alternate triangle polygons from the subject centre
how: 12 rays: `d.polygon([(cx,cy),(cx+R*cos(a0),cy+R*sin(a0)),(cx+R*cos(a1),cy+R*sin(a1))],fill=...)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gradient background
what: numpy linear blend of two colours to a 1280x720 array
how: `a=np.linspace(0,1,1280)[None,:,None]; g=(c1*(1-a)+c2*a).repeat(720,0).astype(np.uint8); Image.fromarray(g)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cut-out outline (sticker edge)
what: grow the alpha with `MaxFilter` (picks the largest value in the window), fill it white under the cutout
how: `a=fg.getchannel('A').filter(ImageFilter.MaxFilter(21)); ol=Image.new('RGBA',fg.size,(255,255,255,0)); ol.putalpha(a); Image.alpha_composite(ol,fg)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Glow behind a cutout
what: blurred alpha in a bright colour under the subject
how: `a=fg.getchannel('A').filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(25)); g=Image.new('RGBA',fg.size,(255,220,0,0)); g.putalpha(a)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cutout drop shadow
what: shift a blurred, 60%-alpha copy of the mask
how: `sh.putalpha(fg.getchannel('A').point(lambda v:int(v*0.6))); sh=sh.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(12)); bg.alpha_composite(sh,(220,40)); bg.alpha_composite(fg,(200,20))` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Measure subject size
what: share of opaque alpha pixels = how much of the frame the subject fills
how: `(np.asarray(fg.getchannel('A'))>128).mean()` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Crop to any ratio around a point
what: `ImageOps.fit(image,size,centering=(x,y))` resizes and crops to the ratio; centering moves the crop
how: `ImageOps.fit(im,(1080,1920),centering=(0.3,0.5))` keeps a left-side face in a vertical cover (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: contain / cover / pad
what: contain fits inside, cover fills the box, pad fits and fills the rest with a colour
how: `ImageOps.pad(im,(1080,1080),color='#101010')` for a square podcast cover from a 16:9 still (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix phone photo rotation first
what: `ImageOps.exif_transpose` applies the EXIF Orientation tag and removes it
how: `im=ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open('photo.jpg'))` before any layout (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Auto-contrast
what: removes a cutoff % of darkest/lightest pixels and stretches; `preserve_tone` keeps the tone Photoshop-style
how: `ImageOps.autocontrast(im,cutoff=1,preserve_tone=True)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Colour, contrast, sharpness factors
what: ImageEnhance: 1.0 = original; Color 0 = greyscale; Sharpness 2.0 = sharpened
how: `ImageEnhance.Color(im).enhance(1.3)`, `Contrast(...).enhance(1.15)`, `Sharpness(...).enhance(1.5)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Unsharp mask on the face
what: `ImageFilter.UnsharpMask(radius=2, percent=150, threshold=3)` defaults
how: `im.filter(ImageFilter.UnsharpMask(radius=2,percent=120,threshold=3))` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Poster look
what: `ImageOps.posterize(im,bits)` cuts colour levels for a flat graphic background
how: `ImageOps.posterize(bg,3)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Flip for text room
what: `ImageOps.mirror` flips left-right so the subject faces into the text side (avoid when text/logos appear in the photo)
how: `ImageOps.mirror(im)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: JPEG export options
what: quality default 75 (avoid >95), `optimize`, `progressive`, `subsampling=0` (4:4:4) keeps red text edges crisp
how: `im.save('t.jpg',quality=90,optimize=True,progressive=True,subsampling=0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stay under 2 MB for phone upload
what: step quality down until the file is < 2 MB (mobile limit)
how: loop `im.save('t.jpg',quality=q,optimize=True)` for q in 95..70 and check `os.path.getsize` (tested here 2026-10-24: a 3840x2160 test card was 0.35 MB at q95)

name: PNG size
what: `optimize=True` makes the PNG writer search for the smallest file (compress_level then ignored)
how: `im.save('t.png',optimize=True)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: WebP for web pages
what: quality default 80, `method` 0-6 (6 slower, better)
how: `im.save('t.webp',quality=85,method=6)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Previews at served sizes
what: resize to 120, 168 and 320 wide with LANCZOS and look at all three
how: `for w in (120,168,320): im.resize((w,round(w*9/16)),Image.LANCZOS).save(f'p_{w}.png')` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Duration badge mock
what: draw a black rounded box with a time at the bottom-right of the 320x180 preview to see what it hides
how: `d.rounded_rectangle((262,154,314,174),radius=4,fill=(0,0,0)); d.text((288,164),'12:34',fill='white',anchor='mm',font_size=13)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rule-of-thirds overlay
what: draw lines at W/3, 2W/3, H/3, 2H/3 on a copy to place the face on an intersection
how: `d.line([(W*i/3,0),(W*i/3,H)],fill='cyan',width=2)` for i in 1,2 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: A/B/C sheet for the owner
what: paste the three variants at 320x180 side by side so the owner picks at real size
how: PIL paste into a white sheet (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Use the Python API, not the CLI here
what: the rembg CLI needs the cli extra (gradio, fastapi...), which isn't installed; the library works
how: `/home/user/tools/venv/bin/python -I -c "from rembg import remove,new_session; from PIL import Image; remove(Image.open('in.png'),session=new_session('u2netp')).save('cut.png')"` (tested here 2026-10-24: 3.4 s at 640x360 incl. model load)

name: Never rely on the default model here
what: the default `bria-rmbg` is ~1.02 GB at 1024x1024; in this container it OOM-killed at 14 GB
how: always pass a model, e.g. `new_session('u2net_human_seg')` for people (as bg_blur.py does) or `u2netp` for a fast draft.

name: Model per subject
what: u2net_human_seg for humans, isnet-anime for anime characters, birefnet-portrait for portraits, u2netp lightweight
how: for the blocky host render, cut it from a plain HyperFrames background instead (no model needed).

name: Mask only
what: `only_mask=True` returns the L-mode mask for your own compositing/outline
how: `remove(im,session=s,only_mask=True)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Binary mask
what: `post_process_mask=True` (-ppm) thresholds the mask into a fully binary one: hard edges for a sticker outline
how: `remove(im,session=s,post_process_mask=True)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fill a solid background directly
what: `bgcolor=(r,g,b,a)`
how: `remove(im,session=s,bgcolor=(0,255,0,255))` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Remove colour halos
what: `decontaminate=True` (-dc) fixes edge colour from a strongly coloured background (grass, sky, painted wall); cheap enough for every batch
how: `remove(im,session=s,decontaminate=True)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Hair: alpha matting
what: `alpha_matting=True` re-estimates edge coverage (slow); its solver can fail to converge and then falls back to a decontaminated cutout
how: `remove(im,session=s,alpha_matting=True)` (tested here 2026-10-24: 8.4 s, printed the non-convergence warning and still saved)

name: Model storage
what: new models go to `~/.rembg/models/<name>/` (REMBG_HOME overrides; legacy ~/.u2net still read)
how: `ls ~/.rembg/models` to see what's already downloaded before fetching another.

name: Threads
what: `OMP_NUM_THREADS` sets ONNX Runtime threads
how: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=4` on this 4-core box; don't run it next to ACE-Step/Whisper.
refs: repo: CLAUDE.md "NEVER run two heavy torch jobs"

name: Render the thumbnail as a still
what: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <s> --no-end --output <dir>` writes one PNG at that time (without --no-end it adds an end frame)
how: in the project folder: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at 2 --no-end --output /tmp/.../hf_snap2` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Phone legibility sheet
what: `snapshot --review` writes review-phone.jpg: beat frames 360 px wide to judge legibility at phone size
how: `npx hyperframes snapshot --review` then open review-phone.jpg.

name: Zoom on a detail
what: `snapshot --zoom "#title"` or an exact region `--zoom "100,50,400,300" --zoom-scale 2`
how: check the outline edge of the title at 3x density.

name: Variant sheet with compare
what: `npx hyperframes compare a b c --at 0 --labels A,B,C --out compare.png --cols 3` (max 16 variants)
how: A/B/C thumbnail compositions as separate HTML files.

name: Batch variants from one template
what: `render --batch` takes a JSON array (or {rows:[...]}) of variables like headline
how: one thumbnail template, rows for each episode title.

name: Grade the frame before the text
what: `npx hyperframes grade-compare --for frame.png --grades grades.json --out grade-compare.png` (neutral baseline included)
how: pick the grade for the thumbnail photo.

name: WCAG contrast ratio
what: (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05), lighter over darker, range 1:1 to 21:1
how: Python helper; white/black = 21.0, yellow #ffd400 on blue #1e5adc = 4.13, red on orange = 1.97 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Relative luminance formula
how: use it to pick text colour against the sampled background. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Sample the text area
what: mean colour of the region where text goes, then luminance
how: `np.asarray(im.crop((40,40,640,260))).reshape(-1,3).mean(0)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Complementary colour from a hex
what: rotate HSV hue by 180°
how: `h,s,v=colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(r,g,b); colorsys.hsv_to_rgb((h+0.5)%1,s,v)` gives (220,160,30) for (30,90,220) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CRF +6 halves the size
what: the CRF scale is exponential: +6 gives roughly half the bitrate/file size, -6 roughly double. Use it to jump to a size you want in one step
how: encode once, then move CRF by 6 to halve or double: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 29 -c:a copy half.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 10-bit x264 has a 0-63 quantizer scale
what: the 0-51 CRF scale applies only to 8-bit x264; a 10-bit build uses 0-63, and the ffmpeg console shows yuv420p (8-bit) or yuv420p10le (10-bit). 8-bit is more common among distributors
how: check what you encode in the log line, or force 10-bit: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -crf 20 out10.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: List x264 presets and tunes from your own build
what: ffmpeg can print every preset and tune your libx264 knows. It prints the lists and then stops with an encoder error; that is expected
how: `ffmpeg -hide_banner -f lavfi -i nullsrc -c:v libx264 -preset help -f mp4 - 2>&1 | grep Possible; true` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Placebo is not worth it
what: placebo helps at most ~1% over veryslow; veryslow helps ~3% over slower, slower ~5% over slow, slow 5-10% over medium
how: stop at veryslow (or slow when time is short); never use placebo.

name: Preset time cost
what: for a 2-pass 1080p example: medium to slow costs ~40% more time, slower ~100% more, veryslow 280% of medium; fast saves ~10%, faster ~25%, ultrafast ~55% at much lower quality
how: plan render time from these ratios before a batch export.

name: tune animation for cartoons
what: animation tuning uses higher deblocking and more reference frames; good for cartoons and flat-colour motion graphics
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -tune animation -crf 20 -c:a copy anim.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: tune grain to keep film grain
what: grain tuning preserves the grain structure in old, grainy film material
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -tune grain -crf 18 -c:a copy grain.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: tune stillimage for slideshows
what: stillimage tuning is for slideshow-like content
how: photo slideshows and podcast still-image videos: `ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -framerate 2 -i cover.jpg -i in.wav -c:v libx264 -tune stillimage -crf 18 -c:a aac -shortest -pix_fmt yuv420p still.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: tune fastdecode for weak players
what: fastdecode allows faster decoding by disabling certain filters
how: for old phones/TV boxes that stutter: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -tune fastdecode -crf 20 -c:a copy fd.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: tune zerolatency for live
what: zerolatency is for fast encoding and low-latency streaming
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -tune zerolatency -f mpegts zl.ts` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Leave -profile alone unless a device needs it
what: x264 picks the profile itself; set baseline or main only for old devices, or to match other files before the concat demuxer. -profile:v is incompatible with lossless and high444 does not work as a profile setting
how: only for an old device: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v main -crf 20 -c:a copy main.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: High 4:2:2 Intra profile
what: high422 with -g 1 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le gives High 4:2:2 Intra Profile (an intra-only 10-bit 4:2:2 H.264)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libx264 -profile:v high422 -g 1 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le -crf 12 intra422.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lossless H.264
what: use -qp 0 (or -crf 0 with High 4:4:4 Predictive); High 10 does not support lossless. Use ultrafast for speed or veryslow for size. Most non-FFmpeg players can't decode lossless
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -qp 0 lossless.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: RGB sources: libx264rgb for true lossless
what: if lossless output does not look lossless, the RGB to YUV conversion is the cause; libx264rgb accepts packed RGB
how: `ffmpeg -y -i frames/img_%04d.png -c:v libx264rgb -qp 0 rgb_lossless.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x264-params overrides a preset
what: preset values can be overridden with -x264-params key=value pairs (x264opts is deprecated); the wiki warns tweaking is usually a waste of time
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 22 -x264-params keyint=123:min-keyint=20 -c:a copy kp.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Simulated CBR for broadcast-style TS
what: x264 has no true CBR; simulate it with nal-hrd=cbr plus equal -b:v/-minrate/-maxrate and a -bufsize. nal-hrd cbr is not allowed in MP4, so write TS
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -x264-params nal-hrd=cbr -b:v 1M -minrate 1M -maxrate 1M -bufsize 2M cbr.ts` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Capped CRF (VBV) for streaming
what: -crf with -maxrate and -bufsize targets the CRF but raises it when the rate would exceed the cap; libx264 does not strictly hold the max, use two-pass for a perfect cap
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 23 -maxrate 1M -bufsize 2M -c:a copy capped.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Two-pass with a cap
what: average bitrate plus maxrate/bufsize in two passes gives the tightest control
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 1M -maxrate 1M -bufsize 2M -pass 1 -an -f mp4 /dev/null && ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 1M -maxrate 1M -bufsize 2M -pass 2 -c:a aac capped2p.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: MiB to kbit/s for a size target
what: bitrate = size / duration; 200 MiB x 8388.608 / 600 s = ~2796 kbit/s total, minus audio (e.g. 128) for the video rate. 1 kbit is 1000 bit, hence 8388.608 not 8192
how: compute it before pass 1: `python3 -c "print(round(200*8388.608/600-128))"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Two-pass gives no better quality than CRF
what: the FAQ says two-pass is not better quality than CRF; it only hits a file size more accurately
how: use CRF unless a size or bitrate is required.

name: First pass segfault fix
what: if -an in pass 1 gives a segfault or a broken file, drop -an and add -vsync cfr to the first pass
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 1M -pass 1 -vsync cfr -f null /dev/null` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Name the two-pass log
what: -passlogfile sets the log prefix (default ffmpeg2pass, file PREFIX-N.log) so parallel two-pass jobs don't overwrite each other
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 800k -pass 1 -passlogfile jobA -an -f null /dev/null && ls jobA-0.log` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Test settings on a slice first
what: encode a random section with -ss and -t/-to to judge settings quickly
how: `ffmpeg -y -ss 0.5 -t 1 -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -an slice.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: yuv420p for QuickTime and dumb players
what: QuickTime and most players only decode YUV 4:2:0 H.264, so add -pix_fmt yuv420p when the source is 4:2:2/4:4:4 or RGB
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 20 qt.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Force IDR keyframes
what: forced-idr makes forced I-frames IDR frames, so they are true random-access points
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -force_key_frames 0,1 -forced-idr 1 -an idr.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Open GOP with -flags -cgop
what: flags -cgop disables closed GOP (similar to x264 --open-gop). Platforms that need closed GOP (X, YouTube) should not get it
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -flags -cgop -an opengop.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CAVLC for very old decoders
what: coder vlc disables CABAC (same as --no-cabac)
how: only for very old hardware; YouTube asks for CABAC. `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v baseline -coder vlc -an cavlc.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Set the H.264 level
what: the private -level option takes a level IDC name like 3.1 or 4.1
how: for Apple-compatible HLS variants (High 4.1): `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -level 4.1 -an l41.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Limit B-frames with -bf
what: bf maps to x264 bframes (B-frames between I and P)
how: YouTube's spec is 2 consecutive B-frames: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -bf 2 -an bf2.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fixed GOP: -g plus -keyint_min plus no scenecut
what: g = max GOP, keyint_min = min GOP, sc_threshold = scene change threshold; fixed GOPs make segment cuts exact
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -g 30 -keyint_min 30 -sc_threshold 0 -an fixedgop.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Access unit delimiters
what: aud=1 adds access unit delimiters; some broadcast and Blu-ray chains want them
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -x264-params aud=1 -an aud.ts` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Blu-ray compatible x264
what: bluray-compat is a shorthand for bluray-compat=1 force-cfr=1
how: full Blu-ray authoring needs more (see the wiki's Blu-ray page). `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -bluray-compat 1 -an bd.264` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Print SSIM after encoding
what: -ssim 1 makes libx264 print SSIM stats at the end. Here x264 warned that SSIM with psy on is invalid, so turn psy off for the measurement run
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -ssim 1 -psy 0 -an -f null - 2>&1 | grep -i ssim` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Intra-only H.264 for frame-accurate review
what: with -g 1 -bf 0 every frame is an I-frame, so scrubbing backwards is easy; needs a lower CRF (7-11 in the VFX test)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -g 1 -bf 0 -crf 9 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an review.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CRF 19 for review copies
what: in the VFX wiki's tests CRF 19 gave very good movies at small size that play on ordinary laptops; playback trouble eased from CRF 15 up
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 19 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a copy daily.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 CRF 28 ~ x264 CRF 23
what: x265's default CRF 28 should look like x264 CRF 23 at about half the size; the max is always 51, even 10-bit
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -crf 28 -preset medium -c:a aac -b:a 128k hevc.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 savings grow with resolution
what: libx265 saves around 25-50% over libx264 at the same quality, most at 1080p and above
how: prefer HEVC for 1080p/4K masters to platforms that accept it.

name: Preset changes the size at the same CRF
what: CRF values differ by preset: veryslow at one CRF may be bigger than ultrafast but better per bit
how: compare presets at equal file size, not equal CRF.

name: x265 two-pass uses x265-params pass
what: for libx265 the -pass option does not apply; use -x265-params pass=1 / pass=2
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -b:v 600k -x265-params pass=1 -an -f null /dev/null && ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -b:v 600k -x265-params pass=2 -c:a aac h265_2p.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lossless HEVC
what: use -x265-params lossless=1 (no -crf 0 needed); the log shows a lossless compression ratio
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params lossless=1 -an hevc_ll.mkv 2>&1 | grep -i lossless` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: All-intra HEVC
what: use -g 1 (ffmpeg 4.3+) for intra-only HEVC
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -g 1 -crf 20 -an hevc_intra.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: hvc1 tag for Apple
what: add -tag:v hvc1 so Final Cut/Apple players accept the HEVC file
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -crf 24 -tag:v hvc1 -c:a copy apple_hevc.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Main 10 for 10-bit HEVC
what: x265 10-bit profiles include main10 and main422-10; 8-bit main and main444-8
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -profile:v main10 -crf 22 m10.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 tunes
what: x265 tunes: psnr, ssim, grain, zero-latency, fast-decode, animation; generally not required
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -tune animation -crf 24 -an h265anim.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: tune grain turns on rc-grain
what: rc-grain minimises QP fluctuations and removes pulsing of grain; it is enabled by --tune grain, which is the recommended way
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -tune grain -crf 22 -an h265grain.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 keyint default 250
what: x265 keyint defaults to 250; -1 is one keyframe at the start, 1 is all-intra; set min-keyint equal for a fixed interval
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params keyint=60:min-keyint=60:scenecut=0 -an h265gop.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 open GOP is on by default
what: x265 allows non-IDR I-slices by default (--open-gop). Turn it off when a platform needs closed GOP
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params no-open-gop=1 -an closedgop.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 B-frames default 4
what: x265 --bframes defaults to 4 (0-16); 0 forces low-latency P/I only
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params bframes=0 -an h265nob.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 level and tier
what: --level-idc sets the minimum decoder level (as 5.1 or 51); it can force VBV on CRF encodes. high-tier is default enabled, used only if needed
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params level-idc=4:no-high-tier=1 -an h265l4.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 VBV in CRF mode needs both values
what: in CRF mode both vbv-bufsize and vbv-maxrate (kbit) are needed; VBV also turns on emergency denoising when QP > 51
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -crf 24 -x265-params vbv-maxrate=2000:vbv-bufsize=4000 -an h265vbv.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 strict-cbr
what: strict-cbr keeps ABR within ~5% of target, prioritising bitrate over quality, useful for short segments
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -b:v 800k -x265-params strict-cbr=1:vbv-maxrate=800:vbv-bufsize=1600 -an h265cbr.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: aq-mode 3 against banding in dark 8-bit
what: x265 aq-mode 3 biases to dark scenes and is recommended for 8-bit or low-bitrate 10-bit encodes to prevent banding/blocking
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -crf 24 -x265-params aq-mode=3 -an h265aq3.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Repeat headers for raw HEVC streams
what: --repeat-headers emits VPS/SPS/PPS at every keyframe, for when no container holds the headers
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params repeat-headers=1 -an rh.hevc` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Drop the x265 info SEI for bit-exact tests
what: --info (default on) writes encoder version and settings into the stream; it can make bitstreams differ between builds. Turn off for regression tests
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params info=0 -an noinfo.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Zones: more bits for one scene
what: --zones start,end,b=multiplier (or q=QP) changes bitrate for frame ranges; later zones win
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -crf 24 -x265-params zones=0,29,b=1.5 -an zones.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: x265 picture hash SEI
what: --hash 1/2/3 writes MD5/CRC/checksum SEI so a decoder can validate pictures and detect data loss
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -x265-params hash=1 -an hashsei.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 CRF default 35
what: libsvtav1 CRF is the default rate control; ffmpeg range 0-63 (default 35). The upstream guide says crf=30 is a good 1080p start
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -crf 35 -c:a copy svt.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 presets 0-13
what: higher presets are faster; 13 is only for debugging; 4-6 is a common quality/time trade-off; 10+ for fast/realtime
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -preset 10 -crf 35 -c:a copy svt_fast.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 personal-archive line
what: the upstream example: preset 5, crf 32, -g 240, 10-bit, tune=0 (subjective), film-grain=8
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -preset 6 -crf 32 -g 240 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -svtav1-params tune=0:film-grain=8 -c:a copy svt_home.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Film-grain level by content
what: film-grain 1-50 denoises and re-synthesises grain at decode; ~8 for normal live action, 10-15 very grainy, 4-6 for 2D animation; omit if no grain. SVT-AV1 1.7.0 here warned that film grain above preset 6 is for debugging only
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -preset 6 -crf 35 -svtav1-params film-grain=8 -an fg.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep detail with film-grain-denoise=0
what: film-grain-denoise=0 encodes the original frames instead of the denoised ones, to avoid detail loss at high grain levels
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -preset 6 -crf 35 -svtav1-params film-grain=10:film-grain-denoise=0 -an fg0.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 keyframe interval
what: SVT-AV1's default keyint is short (2-3 s per the wiki, ~5 s in current docs); the wiki suggests up to 5 s or more, e.g. -g 150 for 30 fps
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -crf 35 -g 150 -an svtgop.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 fast-decode
what: fast-decode=1 makes bitstreams cheaper to decode (not effective on every preset)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -crf 35 -svtav1-params fast-decode=1 -an svtfd.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 lossless needs v3.0
what: lossless is supported since SVT-AV1 v3.0.0 via svtav1-params lossless=1. Our build is v1.7.0: ffmpeg printed 'Error parsing option lossless: 1.' and still exited 0 with a lossy file, so read the log, not the exit code
how: needs SVT-AV1 >= 3.0 (missing); check: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -crf 35 -svtav1-params lossless=1 -an ll.mkv 2>&1 | grep 'Error parsing'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: SVT-AV1 max bitrate in CRF
what: mbr (kbps) caps bitrate for CRF encodes in SVT-AV1's parameter list (current docs; check your version)
how: needs a newer SVT-AV1 if 1.7.0 rejects it. `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libsvtav1 -crf 35 -svtav1-params mbr=2000 -an svtmbr.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pipe to SvtAv1EncApp for a newer SVT
what: if ffmpeg's SVT is too old, pipe y4m into the standalone encoder, then mux audio back
how: needs SvtAv1EncApp (missing): `ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0:v:0 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -f yuv4mpegpipe -strict -1 - | SvtAv1EncApp -i stdin --preset 5 --crf 32 -b out.ivf`

name: libaom constant quality
what: libaom-av1 -crf (0-63) is constant quality; CRF 23 ~ x264 CRF 19. Before ffmpeg 4.3 also add -b:v 0
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libaom-av1 -crf 30 -cpu-used 8 -row-mt 1 -an aom.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: libaom constrained quality
what: -crf with a non-zero -b:v gives constrained quality (quality target with a ceiling)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libaom-av1 -crf 30 -b:v 2000k -cpu-used 8 -an aomcq.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: libaom speed with cpu-used
what: -cpu-used 0-8 (default 1) trades speed and quality; -row-mt 1 plus tiles uses more cores
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libaom-av1 -crf 30 -cpu-used 8 -row-mt 1 -tiles 2x1 -an aomfast.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: libaom keyframes every 10 s max
what: libaom's default max keyframe interval is 9999 frames (slow seeking); up to 10 s is reasonable: -g 300 at 30 fps
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libaom-av1 -crf 30 -cpu-used 8 -g 300 -an aomg.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AV1 10-bit stays in Main profile
what: AV1 Main profile includes 10-bit, so yuv420p10le is safe for hardware decoders; 4:4:4 needs High, 12-bit Professional
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libaom-av1 -crf 30 -cpu-used 8 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le aom10.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: libaom grain synthesis
what: denoise-noise-level enables grain synthesis in libaom (0 = off)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libaom-av1 -crf 30 -cpu-used 8 -denoise-noise-level 10 -an aomgrain.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: rav1e speed and params
what: librav1e has speed 0-10, qp 0-255 and rav1e-params
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v librav1e -speed 10 -qp 100 -an rav1e.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Retag AV1 colour without re-encoding
what: av1_metadata sets color_primaries/transfer/matrix and range in the sequence header
how: `ffmpeg -y -i svt.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v av1_metadata=color_primaries=1:transfer_characteristics=1:matrix_coefficients=1 svt_tag.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9: never leave out -b:v
what: the default libvpx-vp9 settings without -b:v give mediocre quality
how: always give a bitrate or -crf with -b:v 0.

name: VP9 constant quality needs -b:v 0
what: constant quality needs -crf plus -b:v 0 exactly; CRF 0-63, 15-35 recommended, 31 for 1080p
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 31 -b:v 0 -deadline good -cpu-used 4 -c:a libopus vp9.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 two-pass constant quality
what: two-pass is the recommended libvpx-vp9 method, because some quality features only run in 2-pass; -b:v 0 -crf N in both passes
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 30 -pass 1 -an -f null /dev/null && ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 30 -pass 2 -cpu-used 4 -c:a libopus vp9_2p.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 first pass speed is fixed
what: for VP9 -speed 0-4 give the same first-pass speed and results; above 4 the first pass goes single-core and slower, so omit -speed in pass 1

name: VP9 constrained quality
what: -crf with a non-zero -b:v bounds the bitrate; easy clips behave like CQ, hard clips like VBR
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 30 -b:v 2000k -cpu-used 4 -an vp9cq.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 CBR
what: set -minrate, -maxrate and -b:v to the same value
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -minrate 1M -maxrate 1M -b:v 1M -cpu-used 4 -an vp9cbr.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Lossless VP9
what: -lossless 1 enables lossless libvpx-vp9
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -lossless 1 -cpu-used 4 -an vp9ll.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 deadline good, not best
what: deadline good is the recommended default; ffmpeg docs say best is poorly named, slow and may be worse than good; realtime for live
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 33 -b:v 0 -deadline realtime -cpu-used 8 -an vp9rt.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 row-mt
what: -row-mt 1 enables row-based multithreading (off by default in libvpx 1.7); gains grow with resolution
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 33 -b:v 0 -row-mt 1 -cpu-used 4 -an vp9mt.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 4:2:0 for players
what: 4:2:2/4:4:4 sources may give output some players can't handle; force -pix_fmt yuv420p
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libvpx-vp9 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 33 -b:v 0 -cpu-used 4 vp9_420.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VP9 tune-content screen
what: tune-content: default, screen, film
how: for screen recordings: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 33 -b:v 0 -tune-content screen -cpu-used 4 -an vp9screen.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: WebM audio is Opus or Vorbis
what: WebM takes Vorbis or Opus; the default WebM audio encoder is libopus
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 33 -b:v 0 -cpu-used 5 -c:a libopus -b:a 96k webm_opus.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cues at the front of WebM/MKV
what: -movflags +faststart does nothing for Matroska; use -cues_to_front 1
how: `ffmpeg -y -i vp9.webm -c copy -cues_to_front 1 vp9_front.webm` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Use prores_ks, not prores/prores_aw
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: the VFX wiki found prores_ks the best of ffmpeg's ProRes encoders and the only one with 4444; colour from prores and prores_ks looked the same
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le -c:a pcm_s16le hq.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ProRes profile names
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: prores_ks profiles: proxy, lt, standard, hq, 4444, 4444xq (0-5)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v prores_ks -profile:v lt -pix_fmt yuv422p10le lt.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ProRes 4444 with alpha
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: 4444 profiles take yuva444p10le; alpha_bits 0/8/16 (0 disables alpha coding); 4444 and 4444 XQ are the only ProRes with alpha
how: `ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=320x180:r=30 -t 1 -vf format=yuva444p10le -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 4444 -alpha_bits 16 alpha4444.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ProRes qscale 9-13
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: in the VFX wiki's tests -qscale:v 9-13 was a good size/quality balance (11 a good bet, 9 a bit better; 5 or less when space is no problem; 0 best, 32 worst)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -qscale:v 11 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le q11.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: vendor apl0
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: -vendor apl0 makes QuickTime/Final Cut treat the file as made by Apple's encoder
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -vendor apl0 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le apl0.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ProRes speed: raise bits_per_mb
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: prores_ks honours frame size limits; detailed frames take longer. A higher bits_per_mb (profiles use 200-2400, max 8000) speeds it up
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -bits_per_mb 2400 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le bpm.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: ProRes target rates at 1080p29.97
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: Apple targets: 4444 XQ ~500 Mbps, 4444 ~330, 422 HQ ~220, 422 ~147, 422 LT ~102, Proxy ~45 Mbps
how: use these to estimate disk space for a delivery.

name: ProRes GB per hour
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: Apple's table: 1920x1080 30p 422 HQ = 220 Mb/s = 99 GB/hr; 3840x2160 30p 422 HQ = 884 Mb/s = 398 GB/hr; 1080 30p Proxy = 45 Mb/s = 20 GB/hr
how: budget storage from the table before exporting a master.

name: ProRes is VBR with a ~10% ceiling
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: ProRes varies bits per frame around a target; the maximum is about 10% above the target bits per frame

name: ProRes HQ for Vimeo
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: Vimeo accepts H.264, ProRes 422 HQ or HEVC, and suggests ProRes if H.264 shows quality issues and you have storage
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v prores_ks -profile:v hq -pix_fmt yuv422p10le -c:a aac -b:a 320k -ar 48000 vimeo_hq.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: DNxHR profiles in ffmpeg
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: the dnxhd encoder here lists dnxhr_lb, dnxhr_sq, dnxhr_hq, dnxhr_hqx and dnxhr_444; pixel formats yuv422p, yuv422p10le, yuv444p10le, gbrp10le
how: `ffmpeg -hide_banner -h encoder=dnxhd` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: DNxHR HQ (8-bit 4:2:2)
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: the dnxhr_hq profile takes yuv422p (8-bit 4:2:2)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v dnxhd -profile:v dnxhr_hq -pix_fmt yuv422p -c:a pcm_s16le dnxhr_hq.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: DNxHR HQX (10-bit)
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: the dnxhr_hqx profile takes yuv422p10le (10-bit 4:2:2)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v dnxhd -profile:v dnxhr_hqx -pix_fmt yuv422p10le dnxhr_hqx.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Photo JPEG review movies
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: Photo JPEG plays on any OS; only qscale matters and should be 1; fine up to ~1K, struggles at 2K+
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v mjpeg -q:v 1 -pix_fmt yuvj422p -an pjpeg.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: FFV1 is the archive codec
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: FFV1 is lossless and a good choice for archiving and preservation; the Library of Congress made FFV1 v3 in Matroska a Preferred Format in Dec 2023
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v ffv1 -level 3 -g 1 -slicecrc 1 -slices 24 -c:a copy archive.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: FFV1 archival settings
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: for archival use GOP 1 (error resilience, frames lost independently) and slice CRC on; two-pass may win back size
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v ffv1 -level 3 -coder 1 -context 1 -g 1 -slices 24 -slicecrc 1 ffv1_arch.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: FFV1 two-pass
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: FFV1.3 can run 2 passes with -pass and -passlogfile to improve compression
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -an -c:v ffv1 -level 3 -pass 1 -passlogfile ffv1log -f nut /dev/null && ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v ffv1 -level 3 -pass 2 -passlogfile ffv1log ffv1_2p.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Read an FFV1 file's settings
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: ffprobe -debug 1 prints the FFV1 header (version, coder, slices, ec, CRC)
how: `ffprobe -v debug -debug 1 -i archive.mkv 2>&1 | grep -i 'ver:'` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep re-edit intermediates lossless
section: Mezzanine and intermediate codecs (ProRes, DNxHR, FFV1, MJPEG)
what: MDN advises lossless compression for media that will be manipulated, to avoid noise piling up from repeated recompression
how: keep re-edit intermediates lossless (FFV1) and only the final export lossy.

name: Native aac is the AAC to use here
what: the wiki ranks for AAC-LC: native aac > aac_at > libfdk_aac; libfdk_aac is non-free and not in prebuilt ffmpeg. Default output is AAC-LC
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a aac -b:a 160k out.m4a` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: aac VBR with -q:a
what: native aac VBR via -q:a (effective ~0.1-2 on older builds) is experimental and not guaranteed better than CBR
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a aac -q:a 2 vbr.m4a` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: aac coders in this build
what: ffmpeg 6.1 here offers aac_coder anmr, twoloop (default) and fast; docs: fast is worse below 64 kbps but better and faster at higher rates
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a aac -aac_coder fast -b:a 256k fastcoder.m4a` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Don't use HE-AAC above 64 kbps
what: HE-AAC v1 suits <64 kbps stereo, v2 down to 32 kbps (stereo only); many AAC-LC devices can't play HE-AAC. Apple's HLS spec says not to use HE-AAC above 64 kbit/s
how: stay on AAC-LC (native aac has no HE profile).

name: 64 kbps per channel for transparency
what: rule of thumb for libfdk_aac CBR: 64 kbps per channel (128 stereo, 384 for 5.1)

name: Multichannel bitrate formula
what: estimate multichannel bitrate as stereo bitrate / 2 x channels (e.g. 128/2 x 6 = 384)

name: Opus quality guide
what: libopus: usable >= 32 kbps, recommended >= 64; music near-transparent at the default 96, 160+ for real transparency; speech transparent ~32
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 96k out.opus` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Opus VBR modes
what: libopus -vbr on (default), off (hard CBR), constrained
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 64k -vbr constrained cvbr.opus` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Opus for voice: application voip
what: -application voip favours speech intelligibility; audio (default) favours faithfulness; lowdelay for lowest delay
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 32k -application voip voice.opus` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Opus surround mapping family 1
what: -mapping_family 1 enables surround masking and LFE optimisations; the default -1 disables them
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in51.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 256k -mapping_family 1 surround.opus` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Better mono downmix from Opus
what: apply_phase_inv 0 disables phase inversion for intensity stereo, improving mono downmixes (slightly worse stereo)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 96k -apply_phase_inv 0 monosafe.opus` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Avoid the native opus encoder
what: ffmpeg's own opus encoder implements only CELT and is usually worse than libopus
how: always say -c:a libopus.

name: AC-3 at 160 kbps or more
what: ac3/eac3 usable and recommended >= 160 kbps; 5.1 eac3 bad at 192k, good at 256k
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in51.wav -c:a ac3 -b:a 384k surround.ac3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AC-3 dialnorm
what: -dialnorm (-31 to -1, default -31 = no change) tells decoders how far average dialogue sits below full scale
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in51.wav -c:a ac3 -b:a 384k -dialnorm -24 dn.ac3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: AC-3 downmix levels
what: -center_mixlev 0.707/0.595/0.500 and -surround_mixlev 0.707/0.500/0.000 set stereo downmix gains
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in51.wav -c:a ac3 -b:a 384k -center_mixlev 0.707 -surround_mixlev 0.707 mix.ac3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: E-AC-3 belongs in MP4
what: E-AC3 is only officially supported (per Dolby) in MP4, which needs an edit list to remove 256 padding samples
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v copy -c:a eac3 -b:a 256k eac3.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Which audio fits which container
what: MP4/M4A: Opus, MP2, MP3, AAC (LC/HE), AC3, E-AC3, TrueHD; WebM: Vorbis, Opus; MKV: almost anything; M2TS: AC3, E-AC3, TrueHD
how: check before -c:a copy into a new container.

name: Don't transcode lossy to lossy
what: re-encoding lossy audio can degrade it even at the same or higher bitrate; copy the lossy track or encode from the lossless source
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -c:a copy keepaudio.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: FLAC compression levels
what: flac -compression_level 0-12, default 5
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a flac -compression_level 8 out.flac` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: MP3: -aq 2 or more
what: libmp3lame usable >= 128 kbps; recommended VBR -q:a 2 (>= 192 kbps)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2 out.mp3` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: WAV over 4 GB: rf64 auto
what: plain RIFF WAV breaks past 4 GB; -rf64 auto switches to RF64 only when needed (default never)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a pcm_s24le -rf64 auto big.wav` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Broadcast WAV bext chunk
what: -write_bext 1 adds a BEXT chunk with extended audio metadata
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -c:a pcm_s24le -write_bext 1 -metadata description=Mix bwf.wav` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Vimeo audio: AAC-LC 320k 48 kHz
what: Vimeo recommends AAC-LC, 320 kb/s CBR (more than needed for transparency), 48 kHz; other rates are converted to 48 kHz
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 320k -ar 48000 vimeo_audio.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: HLS audio rates
what: Apple suggests stereo AAC 32-160 kbit/s, 5.1 AAC 320, Dolby Digital 5.1 384, DD+ 5.1 192

name: X audio: AAC-LC, mono or stereo
what: X requires AAC Low Complexity (HE-AAC not supported), mono or stereo only (no 5.1), recommended >= 128 kbps
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v copy -c:a aac -ac 2 -b:a 128k x_audio.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fragmented MP4 survives a crash
what: a fragmented MP4 is decodable if writing is interrupted and uses less memory on long files, but is less compatible
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +frag_keyframe+empty_moov frag.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Reserve moov space at the start
what: moov_size reserves bytes for the moov atom at the beginning; muxing fails if too small
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -moov_size 200000 moovres.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Drop Nero chapters
what: movflags disable_chpl writes only the QuickTime chapter track; Nero chapters can break some tagging programs
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -i chapters.txt -map 0 -map_metadata 1 -map_chapters 1 -c copy -movflags +disable_chpl chap_qt.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Add chapters from an ffmetadata file
what: -map_chapters copies chapters from the given input; an FFMETADATA file can supply them
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -i chapters.txt -map 0 -map_chapters 1 -c copy chap.mp4 && ffprobe -v error -show_chapters chap.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Copy or clear metadata with -map_metadata
what: -map_metadata picks global/stream/chapter metadata from an input; a negative index disables automatic copying
how: strip all inherited metadata: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -map_metadata -1 -c copy clean.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Set stream language
what: -metadata:s:a:0 language=eng sets the first audio stream's language; an empty value deletes a key
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -metadata:s:a:0 language=urd -metadata title=Promo lang.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Default track with -disposition
what: -disposition sets flags like default; with several streams of one type ffmpeg marks the first default
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -i in.wav -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac -disposition:a:0 default -disposition:a:1 0 twoaudio.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Matroska default flags: default_mode
what: matroska default_mode infer marks the first track of each type default if none is; passthrough (default) copies dispositions
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -default_mode infer dm.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Attach a font to MKV
what: -attach adds attachment streams (e.g. subtitle fonts); Matroska needs a mimetype tag
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -attach /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf -metadata:s:2 mimetype=application/x-truetype-font -c copy font.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cover art in MP4
what: the -disposition docs example adds an image as a second video stream encoded to png with disposition attached_pic
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -i cover.jpg -map 0 -map 1 -c copy -c:v:1 png -disposition:v:1 attached_pic covered.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Add or remove one disposition flag
what: a + or - prefix edits flags without clearing the others, e.g. +original-comment
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -disposition:a:0 +original-comment disp.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Matroska reserve index space
what: reserve_index_space puts cues at the start without shifting data; ~50 kB per hour of video is a safe size
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -reserve_index_space 50000 resv.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stereo 3D tag in Matroska
what: -metadata stereo_mode=left_right (and other layouts) tags stereo video in matroska/webm
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -metadata:s:v:0 stereo_mode=left_right sbs.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Write a timecode track
what: -timecode hh:mm:ss:ff (';' for drop frame) sets the start timecode; mov/mp4 write a tmcd track by default (write_tmcd auto)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -timecode 01:00:00:00 tc.mov && ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream_tags=timecode tc.mov` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Force a codec tag
what: -tag:v forces a fourcc (e.g. hvc1 for Apple, avc1)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -tag:v avc1 tagged.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Stop at a file size with -fs
what: -fs stops writing after the byte limit (the file ends slightly over)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -fs 100000 capped_size.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Copy AAC from TS into MP4
what: aac_adtstoasc converts ADTS AAC for MP4/MOV/FLV; it is auto-inserted for MP4/MOV
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.ts -c copy -bsf:a aac_adtstoasc fromts.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: MP4 to TS without re-encoding
what: h264_mp4toannexb turns length-prefixed H.264 into Annex B start codes; auto-inserted for mpegts and raw h264
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb out_annexb.ts` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Strip SEI from H.264 without re-encode
what: filter_units=remove_types=6 removes all SEI (including captions) from H.264
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v copy -bsf:v filter_units=remove_types=6 -an nosei.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Change the H.264 level flag only
what: h264_metadata level=4.1 (or auto) rewrites the SPS level without re-encoding
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v h264_metadata=level=4.1 relevel.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix rotation flag in the bitstream
what: h264_metadata display_orientation=insert with rotate/flip writes a display orientation SEI
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v h264_metadata=display_orientation=insert:rotate=90 rot.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Inspect headers with trace_headers
what: trace_headers logs every header syntax element (AV1, H.264, H.265, JPEG, MPEG-2, VP9) for debugging
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -bsf:v trace_headers -f null - 2>&1 | grep -m1 level_idc` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One encode, many outputs: tee
what: the tee muxer writes the same encoded streams to several outputs, each with its own options
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -map 0 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -flags +global_header -f tee "[movflags=+faststart]tee.mp4|[f=mpegts]tee.ts"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Machine-readable progress
what: -progress pipe:1 prints key=value lines (last key progress=continue/end); -stats_period sets the interval
how: `ffmpeg -y -progress pipe:1 -stats_period 1 -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -an prog.mp4 | grep -m1 progress=` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keyframe at a chapter or time
what: -force_key_frames takes times, chapters[delta], expr: or source
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -force_key_frames 0:00:01 -an kf1.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keyframe every N seconds by expression
what: -force_key_frames expr:gte(t,n_forced*5) forces a keyframe every 5 s
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -force_key_frames "expr:gte(t,n_forced*1)" -an kfexpr.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Keep the source keyframes
what: -force_key_frames source forces a keyframe wherever the source frame was a keyframe
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -force_key_frames source -an kfsrc.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Constant frame rate output
what: -fps_mode cfr duplicates/drops frames to an exact rate; passthrough keeps timestamps; vfr drops duplicates
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -fps_mode cfr -r 30 -c:v libx264 -an cfr.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: -shortest when muxing music under video
what: -shortest ends at the shortest stream (may buffer; -shortest_buf_duration default 10 s)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -stream_loop -1 -i in.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac -shortest shortest.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: HLS needs closed GOPs sized to the segment
what: the hls muxer docs: require a closed GOP and set GOP size to fit the segment time
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -flags +cgop -g 30 -c:a aac -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod hls/out.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: VOD playlist type
what: -hls_playlist_type vod writes #EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD and forces hls_list_size 0 (all segments kept). Apple: VOD playlists MUST carry it
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -g 30 -c:a aac -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod hls/vod.m3u8 && grep PLAYLIST-TYPE hls/vod.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Name HLS segments
what: -hls_segment_filename sets the segment pattern; with several variants it must contain %v
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -g 30 -c:a aac -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_segment_filename 'hls/seg_%03d.ts' hls/named.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: fMP4 HLS segments
what: -hls_segment_type fmp4 writes fragmented MP4 segments (HLS v7+). Apple: HEVC in HLS MUST be fMP4
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx265 -tag:v hvc1 -g 30 -c:a aac -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_segment_type fmp4 hls/hevc.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Single-file HLS with byte ranges
what: hls_flags single_file stores all segments in one file using byte ranges (playlist version 4)
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -g 30 -c:a aac -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_flags single_file hls/single.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Two-rung HLS ladder in one command
what: var_stream_map groups streams into variants and master_pl_name writes the master playlist
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -c:v libx264 -g 30 -c:a aac -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 300k -s:v:1 320x180 -b:a:0 128k -b:a:1 64k -f hls -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod -var_stream_map "v:0,a:0 v:1,a:1" -master_pl_name master.m3u8 -hls_segment_filename 'hls/v%v_%03d.ts' hls/v%v.m3u8 && cat hls/master.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Name variants in var_stream_map
what: add name:my_hd to a variant to get out_my_hd.m3u8 instead of an index
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -map 0:v -map 0:a -c:v libx264 -g 30 -c:a aac -f hls -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod -var_stream_map "v:0,a:0,name:hd" hls/n_%v.m3u8 && ls hls/n_hd.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Mark independent segments
what: hls_flags independent_segments adds #EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS when every segment starts with a keyframe; Apple says use it when segments start with an IDR
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -g 30 -c:a aac -hls_time 1 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_flags independent_segments hls/ind.m3u8 && grep INDEPENDENT hls/ind.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Apple: 6 s segments, IDR every 2 s
what: Apple's HLS spec: target and nominal segment duration 6 s (6.006 for 29.97), segments MUST start with an IDR, IDRs SHOULD be every 2 s, never exceed target by > 0.5 s
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -force_key_frames "expr:gte(t,n_forced*2)" -c:a aac -hls_time 6 -hls_playlist_type vod hls/apple.m3u8` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Apple's H.264 ladder
how: use it as a starting ladder; default variant is the 2000 kbit/s one.

name: Peak vs average bandwidth rules
what: VOD: average segment bitrate within 10% of AVERAGE-BANDWIDTH, measured peak within 10% of BANDWIDTH, peak no more than 200% of average
how: measure each variant's segment bitrates against these rules; a capped encode like this one ran here, with no claim that it meets them: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 2000k -maxrate 4000k -bufsize 4000k -g 60 -c:a aac -b:a 128k ladder2000.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Same aspect ratio across variants
what: Apple: all video variants SHOULD have identical aspect ratios; frame rate above 60 SHALL NOT be used

name: H.264 level limits for Apple HLS
what: for compatibility some H.264 variants SHOULD be <= High 4.1; all MUST be <= High 5.2; prefer High over Main/Baseline
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -level 4.1 -g 60 -c:a aac hlsl41.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: HEVC limits for Apple HLS
what: some HEVC variants SHOULD be <= Main10 Level 4.0 Main tier; all MUST be <= Main10 5.1 High tier
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in10.mkv -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -x265-params level-idc=4:no-high-tier=1 -tag:v hvc1 hevcl4.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: avc1/hvc1, not avc3/hev1
what: Apple: use formats with parameter sets in the sample description (avc1, hvc1, dvh1) rather than in the samples (avc3, hev1, dvhe)

name: Deinterlace 30i to 60p for HLS
what: Apple: interlaced content MUST be deinterlaced; 30i SHOULD become 60p, not 30p
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -vf bwdif=mode=send_field -c:v libx264 -an deint60.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: DASH output
what: the dash muxer writes an MPD plus segments; adaptation_sets groups streams; seg_duration default 5 s
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -map 0 -map 0 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -b:v:0 800k -b:v:1 300k -s:v:1 320x180 -g 30 -keyint_min 30 -sc_threshold 0 -use_template 1 -use_timeline 1 -seg_duration 1 -adaptation_sets "id=0,streams=v id=1,streams=a" -f dash dash/out.mpd` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: CMAF fragmented MP4
what: movflags cmaf writes CMAF-compatible fragmented MP4
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags cmaf+frag_keyframe cmaf.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Cut segments with the segment muxer
what: segment writes files of nearly fixed length, each starting on a keyframe; for exact cuts make keyframes match the cut times
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -force_key_frames "expr:gte(t,n_forced*1)" -c:a aac -f segment -segment_time 1 -reset_timestamps 1 seg/part_%02d.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube: MP4 with no edit lists
what: YouTube's container rules: MP4, no edit lists (else processing may fail), moov atom at the front
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c copy -use_editlist 0 -movflags +faststart yt.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube HDR bitrates
what: YouTube HDR upload rates: 1080p 10 Mbps (15 at 48-60 fps), 1440p 20/30, 4K 44-56/66-85, 720p 6.5/9.5; 480p and below not supported for HDR

name: YouTube deinterlace rule
what: interlaced content should be deinterlaced before upload: 1080i60 to 1080p30
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -vf bwdif=mode=send_frame -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -c:a copy yt_deint.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: YouTube audio: AAC-LC or Opus at 48 kHz
what: YouTube accepts AAC-LC, Opus or Eclipsa Audio; stereo, stereo + 5.1; 48 kHz
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v copy -c:a libopus -b:a 384k -ar 48000 yt_opus.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Upscale low-res uploads to get a better YouTube rung
what: higher upload resolutions get higher streaming bitrates; nearest-neighbour 2x/4x upscaling of VHS/DVD/retro game footage keeps peak quality
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -vf scale=iw*2:ih*2:flags=neighbor -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -c:a copy up2x.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Upload the best you practically can
what: YouTube/Vimeo re-encode everything, so upload the highest practical quality, ideally the original
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -pix_fmt yuv420p upload.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Music video from an MP3 with cover art
what: if an MP3 has embedded album art (shows as an mjpeg video stream) it can become the upload's picture
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.wav -i cover.jpg -map 0 -map 1 -c:a libmp3lame -c:v mjpeg -disposition:v attached_pic art.mp3 && ffmpeg -y -i art.mp3 -c copy art.mkv` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Vimeo bitrate table
what: Vimeo VBR ranges (Mbps): SD 2-5, 720p 5-10, 1080p 10-20, 2K 20-30, 4K 30-60, 8K 50-80; CRF 18 or below recommended
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -crf 18 -maxrate 20M -bufsize 40M -c:a aac -b:a 320k -ar 48000 vimeo1080.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Vimeo: High profile, CFR, square pixels
what: Vimeo: choose H.264 High (not Main) profile; constant frame rate; frames over 60 fps are reduced; 1:1 pixel aspect; deinterlace
how: `ffmpeg -y -i in.mp4 -vf setsar=1 -fps_mode cfr -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -crf 18 -c:a aac -b:a 320k vimeo_cfr.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)
