section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: v2 dropped `moviepy.editor` (import from `moviepy`), renamed `set_*` to `with_*`, `subclip` to `subclipped`, `resize/crop/rotate` to `resized/cropped/rotated`, and effects to classes via `with_effects()`
how: with 2.1.2, `clip.subclip(0,1)` raised AttributeError; `subclipped(0,1)` worked. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: MoviePy docs, "Updating from v1.X to v2.X", https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/getting_started/updating_to_v2.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Out-place edits
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: every `with_*`/effect returns a modified copy; `clip.with_volume_scaled(0.1)` alone changes nothing
how: always reassign: `clip = clip.with_effects([...])`.
refs: MoviePy docs, "Modifying clips and apply effects", https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/user_guide/modifying.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Cut and join
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `subclipped(start, end)` (negative = from the end), `concatenate_videoclips([...])`
how: `concatenate_videoclips([VideoFileClip("t.mp4").subclipped(0,1), VideoFileClip("cuts.mp4").subclipped(-1)])` → 2.0 s, written with `write_videofile("cat.mp4", preset="ultrafast", logger=None)`. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: MoviePy docs, "Modifying clips and apply effects", https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/user_guide/modifying.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Remove a middle section
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `with_section_cut_out(t1, t2)`
how: `with_section_cut_out(1,2)` on a 3 s clip → 2.01 s file. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Speed and volume effects
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `vfx.MultiplySpeed`, `afx.MultiplyVolume`
how: `with_effects([vfx.MultiplySpeed(2), afx.MultiplyVolume(0.5)])` → duration 1.5 s. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: MoviePy docs, "Modifying clips and apply effects", https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/user_guide/modifying.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Render options and frame dumps
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `write_videofile(..., preset, threads, ffmpeg_params=[...])`, `save_frame(path, t)`, `write_images_sequence("%04d.png", fps=)`
how: `ffmpeg_params=["-crf","30"]` rendered; 0.5 s at `fps=10` gave 5 PNGs. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: MoviePy docs, "Previewing and saving video clips", https://zulko.github.io/moviepy/user_guide/rendering.html, checked 2026-10-24

name: Timed overlays
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `CompositeVideoClip` stacks clips; `with_start`, `with_position`, `with_duration` place them
how: a red `ColorClip(size=(100,50), color=(255,0,0), duration=1).with_start(1).with_position((10,10))` over a video rendered fine. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Close clips (or use with)
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: VideoFileClip/AudioFileClip lock the file via a subprocess; call `close()` or use them as context managers
how: `with VideoFileClip("t.mp4") as c: c.save_frame("f1.png", t=1)`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Point MoviePy at the system ffmpeg
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: MoviePy reads the `FFMPEG_BINARY` (and `FFPLAY_BINARY`) environment variables, set before importing moviepy or in a `.env` file
how: `FFMPEG_BINARY=/usr/bin/ffmpeg python ...` → `moviepy.config.FFMPEG_BINARY` printed `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` and a render succeeded. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Read video properties with OpenCV
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `cap.get(cv.CAP_PROP_FPS / FRAME_COUNT / FRAME_WIDTH / FRAME_HEIGHT)`
how: OpenCV 5.0.0 (tools venv) gave `True 30.0 90 640 360` for the test clip. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: OpenCV docs, "Getting Started with Videos", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencv/opencv/4.x/doc/py_tutorials/py_gui/py_video_display/py_video_display.markdown, checked 2026-10-24

name: Seek to a frame
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES` is the 0-based index of the next frame to decode
how: `cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, 45); ok, f = cap.read()` → `CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC` 1500.0; saved with `cv2.imwrite`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Frame-difference cut finder
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
how: grey 64x36 frames, mean absolute difference > 30 between consecutive frames flagged frames [30, 60] on the 3-shot test clip (own tested code, not a library detector). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: OpenCV docs, "Getting Started with Videos", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencv/opencv/4.x/doc/py_tutorials/py_gui/py_video_display/py_video_display.markdown, checked 2026-10-24

name: VideoWriter size must match
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: the frame size given to VideoWriter must equal the frames, otherwise writing fails
how: a 640x360 frame into a 320x180 MJPG writer logged "Failed to write frame" and left a file with no frames; matching sizes with `VideoWriter_fourcc(*"MJPG")` wrote a valid mjpeg AVI. (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: OpenCV docs, "Getting Started with Videos", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencv/opencv/4.x/doc/py_tutorials/py_gui/py_video_display/py_video_display.markdown, checked 2026-10-24

name: Rotation metadata
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
what: `CAP_PROP_ORIENTATION_META` (read-only) and `CAP_PROP_ORIENTATION_AUTO` (rotate frames per metadata, FFmpeg/AVFoundation backends)
how: for phone clips check both; on the test clip they read 0.0 and 1.0 (auto on). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Contact sheet in numpy
section: Scripting edits in Python: MoviePy 2 and OpenCV
how: grab every 15th frame, `cv2.resize` to 160x90, `np.hstack` rows of 3 and `np.vstack` them, `cv2.imwrite("sheet.jpg", ...)` (6 tiles from 90 frames). (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: OpenCV docs, "Getting Started with Videos", https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencv/opencv/4.x/doc/py_tutorials/py_gui/py_video_display/py_video_display.markdown, checked 2026-10-24

name: -nostdin in loops and background jobs
what: ffmpeg reads stdin for interaction by default; `-nostdin` disables it (useful when ffmpeg is in the background), roughly like `< /dev/null`
how: every ffmpeg inside a loop, `xargs` or background job gets `-nostdin` (used in all batch tests here). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: -n skips existing outputs, but exits 0 here
what: `-n` doesn't overwrite and exits immediately if the output exists; on ffmpeg 6.1 the exit code was still 0 ("already exists. Exiting.")
how: test yourself: `o="${f%.*}_proxy.mov"; [ -e "$o" ] && { echo "skip $o"; continue; }` — a rerun printed `skip in dir/clip one_proxy.mov`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Collect failures instead of stopping
how: `ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -i "$f" ... "$o" || echo "FAILED $f" >> failed.txt`; a truncated clip landed in `failed.txt` while the good clips converted. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spaces in names, parallel workers
how: `find "in dir" -name '*.mp4' -print0 | xargs -0 -P 2 -I{} sh -c 'ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -y -i "$1" -frames:v 1 "${1%.mp4}.jpg"' _ {}` made `clip one.jpg` and `clip two.jpg` (GNU parallel isn't installed). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Full log per job without -v debug spam on screen
what: `-report` or `FFREPORT=file=...:level=32` writes the command line and log to a file
how: `FFREPORT=file=ffrep.log:level=32 ffmpeg -v error -i in.mp4 -t 1 -c copy out.mp4` wrote `ffrep.log` while the terminal stayed quiet. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Tag log lines with their level
what: `-loglevel level+info` (flags `level`, `time`, `datetime`, `repeat`)
how: `ffmpeg -v level+info -i in.mp4 -f null -` prefixed lines with `[info]`; grep `\[error\]` afterwards. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Quick tail preview
what: `-sseof` seeks relative to the end
how: `ffmpeg -sseof -1 -i in.mp4 tail1.mp4` → 1.02 s of the ending for a quick check of end cards. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: -fs is a rough stop, not a size target
what: `-fs` stops writing after the limit and the file is "slightly more"; here `-fs 50000` on a libx264 MP4 stopped at 1.44 s but the file was 267 KB, and an MKV ignored it entirely
how: control size with bitrate, not `-fs`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Long filtergraphs from a file
what: `-filter_script:v file.txt` (6.1) avoids shell quoting
how: `echo "scale=160:-2,hflip" > f.txt && ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_script:v f.txt -frames:v 1 fs.png` → 160 px wide. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Live-updating thumbnail
what: image2 `-update 1` overwrites one file instead of a numbered sequence
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf fps=1 -update 1 latest.jpg` for a status image of a long job. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Distributed transcoding rarely pays for one file
what: splitting one transcode across machines and recombining gives diminishing returns; distribution helps bulk jobs
how: on this 4-core box run separate files in parallel (`xargs -P 2`), never several heavy torch jobs at once (repo rule).

name: Scaffold non-interactively
what: outside a TTY `init` scaffolds the centred blank; `--non-interactive` forces it; `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` skips the skills check; `--video/--audio` auto-transcribe unless `--skip-transcribe`
how: `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1 npx hyperframes init proj --non-interactive` made index.html, hyperframes.json, package.json. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fix the scaffold's GSAP CDN line first
what: the 0.8.191 blank scaffold loads GSAP from cdn.jsdelivr.net; repo learning: load `assets/vendor/gsap-3.14.2.min.js` or renders fail
how: copy `video/assets/vendor/gsap-3.14.2.min.js` into the project and point the script tag at it (the test project then rendered). (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Project facts in one call
what: `info --json` (name, resolution, duration, element counts, size, version), `compositions --json` (every data-composition-id)
how: both returned JSON with `duration` and the `main` composition. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: lint while writing, check as the gate
what: `check --json` returns `{ok, browserSkipped, lint, runtime, layout, motion, contrast, craft, ...}`; lint errors skip the browser so empty sections then mean "not checked"
how: `npx hyperframes check --json > check.json; jq '{ok, browserSkipped}' check.json` → `ok: true, browserSkipped: false`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Craft warnings to read
what: `line_unread`, `dead_stretch` (>3 s with no change), `text_below_floor`, `first_frame_empty` (frame 0 is the social thumbnail), `film_silent` (>15 s without audio)
how: fix them unless the film breaks the rule on purpose; `data-hold` exempts deliberate stillness.

name: Snapshots at chosen times
what: `snapshot --at t1,t2` adds an end frame unless `--no-end`; `--output` sets the folder and a contact sheet is written
how: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at 0.5,2.5 --output snaps` → frames at 0.5, 2.5, 2.91 s plus `contact-sheet.jpg`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Review sheets: beats, seams, phone size
what: `snapshot --review` writes `review-beats.jpg`, `review-seam-NN.jpg` (±0.2 s around every cut) and `review-phone.jpg` (360 px wide)
how: `snapshot --review --json` returned the sheet paths; with fewer than two scenes it spreads 5 beats evenly. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Render quality ladder
what: `draft` while iterating, `looks` (default, CRF 16) for the first real encode, `delivery` (= high) for final; default output is timestamped `renders/<project>_<date>_<time>.mp4`, `--output` gives a stable name
how: `npx hyperframes render --quality draft --output out.mp4` → 3.0 s file in 6.4 s. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Verify the render's duration
what: confirm the file is non-empty and its ffprobe duration equals the root `data-duration`
how: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 out.mp4` → 3.000000 for `data-duration="3"`. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Read the render summary line
what: it shows capture path, GPU mode and stage timings; `screenshot capture` + `software gpu` on Linux is the slow path
how: the draft MP4 reported `beginframe capture · software gpu`, the PNG-sequence render `screenshot capture` with the BeginFrame hint. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Frames for compositing tools
what: `--format png-sequence` writes RGBA frames to a folder; `--format mov/webm` render with transparency
how: `render --quality draft --format png-sequence --output seq` → 90 PNGs (`frame_000001.png` …) for 3 s at 30 fps. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: GIF for READMEs/PRs
what: `--format gif` (two-pass palette, fps capped at 30, prefer `--fps 15`, no audio)
how: `render --quality draft --format gif --fps 15 --output out.gif` → ffprobe codec gif. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Gate on doctor's checks, not its exit code
what: `doctor --json` always exits 0; gate on the payload
how: here `doctor --json` exited 0 with `ok: false` because optional whisper-cpp, Kokoro, MusicGen and Docker were missing; `jq -r '.checks[] | select(.ok==false) | .name'` shows which, so gate on the ones you need. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Project history around each turn
what: `history begin --who <you> --label "<plan>"`, `history --since mine --who <you>` to see the person's edits, `history undo` to revert, `history end`
how: the test listed snapshot/check files as "Changed outside the app" and `history end` reported "Nothing changed in this turn". (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Disk housekeeping without losing history
what: `clean --dry-run` lists what it would remove; `--snapshots` also discards snapshot evidence; never delete `.hyperframes` (history lives there)
how: `clean --dry-run` → "Nothing to clean" plus the reclaimable snapshot sizes. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: One run id per verification loop
what: use one `HYPERFRAMES_RUN_ID` for all commands in the same loop; telemetry off with `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1`
how: `export HYPERFRAMES_RUN_ID=job42 HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1` before lint/check/snapshot/render. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Terminal docs
what: `docs` lists topics (data-attributes, examples, rendering, gsap, troubleshooting, compositions); `docs rendering` prints one
how: `npx hyperframes docs` listed them, no browser needed. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Find the fastest render preset for this machine
what: `benchmark` renders 5 preset configs (draft/standard/high, 2 or 4 workers, 30/60 fps) and compares render speed and file size
how: run `npx hyperframes benchmark --runs 1` once per new container type and note the winner in the job notes.

name: Creative brief questions for a video job
what: a typical brief covers background, target audience, objectives (and how success is measured), single message, desired viewer action, tone of voice, mandatories (logo, address, phone), deliverables, timeline incl. number of revision rounds, budget, and who approves
how: send these as a numbered Roman Urdu/English questionnaire before quoting.

name: Use the brief to settle "off-brief" arguments
what: the brief is the mutually agreed document to check where a cut diverged from what was asked
how: when feedback contradicts the brief, quote the brief line and price the change.

name: Video requirement questions (Fiverr's explainer brief)
what: ask: product/features to focus on, main concept, business name/contacts/social links, target audience, reference videos, timeline; script ready or needed, platform, format and duration, last-screen content (logo, contact, CTA), voice-over (gender, age, language, accent, tone)
how: paste these into the gig Requirements tab.

name: Requirement questions that prevent revisions
what: beyond the two default questions (industry, part of a larger project), add: your expectations, style references, upload logos/files/style guides, what the project will be used for
how: add these as questions in the gig's Requirements.

name: One decision-maker on the client side
what: AIGA's client responsibilities include coordinating decision-making with other parties (plus supplying content ready to use)
how: ask the client to name one person who consolidates everyone's notes per round.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Statement of work sections
what: purpose, scope of work, period of performance, deliverables schedule, applicable standards, acceptance criteria, special requirements, payment schedule (upfront vs phased); an SOW is often binding, and a master service agreement can govern several SOWs
how: for a repeat client sign one master agreement and a short SOW per video.

name: Objective acceptance criteria
what: the SOW's acceptance criteria say how the client decides the work is acceptable, usually with objective criteria
how: write e.g. "60 s, 1080x1920, captions burned in, logo end card" so approval isn't a matter of mood.

name: Change orders: add, omit, substitute
what: a change order adds, removes or alters agreed work and may change price and/or completion date
how: log every client change as a one-line change order (what, price, new date) and get a written OK.

name: Name scope creep early
what: scope creep is uncontrolled growth of scope after a project starts, often from a poorly defined scope, vague documents, or "small, simple" changes that add up; teams also add unasked extras to impress
how: write deliverables (length, formats, rounds) in the brief and treat each extra as a priced change.

name: One-way or mutual NDA
what: a unilateral NDA protects one side's disclosures; a bilateral (mutual) NDA protects both
how: one-way when only the client shares secrets (e.g. unreleased product footage); mutual when both sides share confidential material.

name: Fixed price vs time-and-materials
what: fixed price = one lump sum for the job regardless of your hours; T&M = paid for time spent (plus materials); many T&M deals add a guaranteed maximum price as a cap
how: quote fixed price for a defined reel; quote hourly + cap for open-ended edits like "clean up 3 hours of footage".

name: Value-based price
what: price set by the client's perceived value and willingness to pay, not by your production cost; works best with a distinct, differentiated, high-quality offer
how: for a launch promo that drives sales, price on the outcome for the client rather than hours.

name: Monthly retainer for repeat clients
what: a retainer sits between a one-off contract and employment; the fee can be fixed or hourly, a single advance or recurring monthly, and absent agreement otherwise it is refundable if work isn't performed
how: for a client wanting e.g. weekly reels, write the monthly fee, included videos and what happens to unused work.

name: Three-tier video packages
what: build Basic/Standard/Premium tiers that differ in scope (e.g. length, formats), revisions and extras, each with its own price and delivery time
how: Gig edit > Pricing > 3 Packages toggle; packages from $5 up to the tier maximum; upgrades are added at checkout, extras are separate add-ons.

name: Standardized category minimums
what: some Fiverr categories force a minimum package price/scope (e.g. Video & Animation > 3D Product Animation min $100)
how: check dashboard notices; fix within 30 days or the gig loses visibility.

name: Custom Offer for non-standard edits
what: a client whose reel doesn't fit your packages (longer, cheaper, extra formats) gets a Custom Offer instead of you changing gig prices
how: reply in Inbox with a Custom Offer at the agreed price/scope; standardized package rules apply to packages only, not custom offers.

name: Paid extra for out-of-scope work
what: when a revision is really new work (extra format, extra minute), send an order extra
how: Activity tab > Offer more extras > custom extra with price and added days (price can't be $0; days may be 0).

name: Pad delivery time for revision rounds
what: on Fiverr, set the delivery time longer than the real work time so a round or two of revisions doesn't drift far past the due date (which can get flagged as delayed)
how: e.g. 3 days of work -> list 7-day delivery, as the Fiverr success manager advises.
refs: Fiverr Community (Adrian Rodrigues, Senior Success Manager), https://community.fiverr.com/public/blogs/navigating-client-revisions-while-protecting-your-success-score-metrics-2026-04-09, checked 2026-10-24

name: No "unlimited revisions" packages
what: unlimited revisions remove the client's reason to give complete notes and create scattered rounds that hurt the Conflict-Free metric
how: set a fixed revision count per package and stick to it.
refs: Fiverr Community (Adrian Rodrigues, Senior Success Manager), https://community.fiverr.com/public/blogs/navigating-client-revisions-while-protecting-your-success-score-metrics-2026-04-09, checked 2026-10-24

name: Gig page sets expectations
what: thorough FAQs, package descriptions that say what is and isn't included, a portfolio that matches what the package really delivers, a realistic summary: fewer revisions start here
how: don't show a high-end ad reel on a basic $-tier package.
refs: Fiverr Community (Adrian Rodrigues, Senior Success Manager), https://community.fiverr.com/public/blogs/navigating-client-revisions-while-protecting-your-success-score-metrics-2026-04-09, checked 2026-10-24

name: Outside costs billed separately
what: AIGA pricing covers the designer's fee only; equipment rental, talent, music licences, hosting etc. are billed to the client unless the proposal says otherwise
how: list "music/stock licences billed at cost" as its own line in the quote.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Out-of-scope changes at an hourly rate
what: client changes outside scope are billed time-and-materials at your standard hourly rate, on top of any fixed price, and deadlines may move
how: write your hourly change rate into the quote.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Big changes = new proposal
what: if changes exceed a set percentage of the original time/scope, submit a new proposal and don't start until it's signed (and any extra retainer paid)
how: set the percentage in your terms, e.g. as a blank you fill per client.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Price for the Upwork fee
what: the Freelancer Service Fee is 0-15% per contract, shown on the offer/proposal and locked once sent
how: gross rate = wanted net / (1 - fee); Upwork's example: net $20/h at 10% -> charge $22.22/h. `python3 -c "print(round(20/(1-0.10),2))"` -> 22.22 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fiverr milestones for big edits
what: gig milestones need a basic package of at least $100, each milestone at least $50, 2-5 milestones, and only in listed subcategories (e.g. E-Commerce Product Videos, 3D Product Animation); custom offers allow up to 6 milestones regardless
how: Inbox > Create an offer > order type Milestones, e.g. 1) rough cut 2) final 3) formats.

name: Proposal + attached terms = the contract
what: AIGA's model is a custom proposal per project with standard terms and conditions attached; together and signed they form the agreement
how: keep one reusable terms sheet for edits and write a short proposal (scope, price, schedule) per client.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Proposal validity window
what: state how many days the quote stays valid; if not signed in time, price, terms and deliverables may change
how: add "This quote is valid for N days" to every quote.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Rights only after full payment
what: licences/ownership transfer are conditioned on full payment; the designer may withhold deliverables while invoices are overdue
how: hold the final master until the invoice is paid, and say so in the terms.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Client review deadline and written notes
what: client agrees to review each deliverable within the stated time and either approve in writing or give written comments clear enough to act on; client delays don't count as your breach
how: add "notes in writing (Frame.io/Vimeo comments or numbered list) within N days".
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Five-business-day acceptance
what: under the model's testing-and-acceptance clause, if the client sends no written objection within five business days of receiving a deliverable, it is deemed accepted
how: say in the delivery message: "If no notes by <date>, this version counts as approved."
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Suspension fee for client delays
what: when a client stalls the project you reserved time for, the model charges hourly fees for idle time unless you fill that time with other work
how: include it in terms for long jobs with fixed slots.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Client is responsible for final proofreading
what: if the client approved a deliverable that still has typos/misspellings, the client pays to correct them; the client also ensures their content/claims are accurate and legal
how: ask the client to proof all on-screen text before final approval.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Portfolio and credit rights
what: the model reserves the designer's right to show final and preliminary works in portfolios/websites (unless it contains client confidential info) and to be credited
how: write a portfolio clause into the quote; for personal/family footage, never use it (owner rule).
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Termination fee for convenience
what: if the client cancels for convenience, the model pays work done (greater of advance, prorated fee or hourly) plus an early termination fee of 25% of the total project fee, and the client gets no usage rights without consent
how: add a cancellation clause to the quote.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Kill fee for motion work
what: AIGA's motion supplement says a lump-sum "kill fee" is standard for motion design/VFX contracts and replaces progress billing if the client cancels an active project
how: state a fixed kill fee amount in motion/edit contracts.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Work stoppage on non-payment
what: if the client breaches (e.g. doesn't pay) and doesn't cure within 10 days of written notice, the designer may suspend work until cured and fees/schedule are amended
how: send a written breach notice, wait the cure period, then pause.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Choose the IP option explicitly
what: the model offers four IP options: limited-usage licence, exclusive licence, assignment of rights, work made for hire; motion/VFX is typically work made for hire
how: tick one option in each contract instead of leaving ownership vague.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Limited licence fields
what: a limited usage licence lists category of use, medium, duration and geographic territory; extra uses need separate pricing
how: e.g. "social media ads, 12 months, Pakistan" in the quote.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Modification right is a choice
what: the licence options let you say whether the client may edit/crop/re-cut the final works or must use them as delivered
how: tick "may modify" or "original form only" in the IP section.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Project files stay yours unless sold
what: the model reserves preliminary works and working files (project files, drafts) to the designer and has the client return them within 30 days
how: quote project-file handover as a separate priced item if the client wants it.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Third-party materials are licensed, not owned
what: third-party materials (stock, music) stay owned by their owners; the designer tells the client which ones need a licence and obtains it for the agreed usage; the client covers missing releases for material it asked to include
how: list every third-party asset with its licence in the delivery notes.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Client warrants its own footage
what: the client represents it owns or may use the content it supplies and that it doesn't infringe others' rights
how: include this line when clients send footage, logos and music.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Technical-spec warranty
what: the motion supplement warrants delivery meets the client's technical requirements (duration, file format, resolution, colour specs)
how: get those specs in writing in the brief, then verify with the ffprobe report before delivery.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: "No new live action" clause
what: for edit-only jobs, state you won't shoot any new footage
how: add "editing of client-supplied footage only; no filming" to the scope.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Content restrictions clause
what: the motion supplement lets you list content you won't work on (e.g. adult, gambling, violence, politics, religion, alcohol) or accept mature content with adult-only staff
how: state your no-go list in your gig/terms.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Not responsible for defects in client footage
what: the motion supplement says the designer isn't responsible for defects in client-provided footage or effects
how: note "quality depends on supplied footage" in the quote.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Non-solicitation of your subcontractors
what: the model bars the client from hiring your subcontractors for six months, with a 25% commission if they do
how: include it if you use helpers on a job.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Changes authorised by email count
what: the model lets invoices include changes/costs the client authorised by email or the project platform, while other modifications need signed writing
how: get "yes, go ahead with the extra" in writing before billing extras.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Your templates stay yours
what: under AIGA terms "Designer Tools" (software incl. source code, authoring tools, fonts, application tools) and their IP are owned solely by you; the client gets a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use them as part of the final work
how: state that HyperFrames blocks, presets and scripts in the edit stay yours.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Expenses at cost plus markup
what: AIGA terms bill incidental out-of-pocket expenses at cost plus your stated markup and travel only with the client's prior approval
how: list the markup % in the quote; get travel approval in writing.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Confidentiality both ways
what: each party keeps the other's confidential information secret and uses it only for the project; public-domain info is excluded; confidential info is returned/destroyed at the end
how: add this before receiving unreleased product footage.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Independent contractor and no exclusivity
what: you decide the manner and means of the work; the client may hire others and you may work for other clients
how: include both lines so a client can't demand exclusivity without paying for it.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Originality warranty
what: except third-party materials and client content, you warrant the final deliverables are your original work, but you don't run trademark/copyright clearance searches
how: say so in the quote when a client asks you to "check if the name is free".
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: "Work made for hire" needs a signed paper
what: for a commissioned (non-employee) edit, US law treats the client as author only if the work is in an eligible category (a part of a motion picture/audiovisual work qualifies) AND both parties signed a written agreement expressly calling it a work made for hire; miss any one and it isn't
how: if a US client wants full ownership, put an explicit work-made-for-hire clause in the contract and get both signatures.

name: Who owns the edit by default
what: unless the contract says otherwise, the commissioned editor is the author; under work-for-hire the commissioning party is author and initial owner
how: write in the quote who owns the final video, the project file and raw assets.

name: WMFH term and no take-back
what: copyright in a work made for hire lasts 95 years from publication or 120 from creation (whichever first) and the author's termination rights don't apply
how: note it when a client asks for a work-made-for-hire clause.

name: NYC clients: written contract from $800
what: under NYC's Freelance Isn't Free Act (Local Law 140 of 2016, effective May 15 2017) a hiring party must give a written contract when work is $800 or more, and pay within 30 days of completion when no date is set; rights include timely full payment and no retaliation, with statutory and double damages
how: for NYC clients send the contract before starting and quote the 30-day rule if late.

name: Single-frame Frame.io note
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: ask the client to pause on the exact frame and type, so every note carries the timecode the editor needs
how: tell the client "pause, type in the comment box, Enter"; typing auto-pauses playback; clicking a comment card jumps back to that frame.

name: Range comment for a whole scene
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: for notes about a stretch (music bed, a full scene), use an A-to-B range comment instead of one frame
how: in Frame.io press I to start the range and O to end it, write the note, Send; clicking the card loops only that range, Esc returns to full playback.

name: Anchored (pinned) comment on the picture
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: when the note is about one spot in the frame (a logo, a face, a typo), the client clicks the picture to pin the note there
how: click the white pin icon in the playbar (turns purple), click the spot; works in full screen too and on images/PDFs.

name: Internal comments the client never sees
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: discuss a client note with your team on the same asset without the external reviewer seeing it
how: in the comment box switch the tab next to Send from Public Comment to Internal Comment before sending; a lock icon marks it.

name: Draw-on-frame annotation
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: let the client draw an arrow/box/line on the frame so a vague note ("move that") becomes exact
how: write the note first, then click the annotation icon and draw; the annotation shows only when the comment card is clicked, not during normal playback.

name: Reference file attached to a note
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: client or colourist attaches a reference image/clip to the comment itself
how: use Attach Files in the comment (Pro plan or higher, up to 6 attachments per comment; non-media files like ZIPs get no preview).

name: General note without a timestamp
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: for overall notes ("whole video feels slow") switch off the timestamp so it doesn't pin to a random frame
how: click the timestamp toggle next to Send before posting.

name: Hashtag notes to sort a feedback round
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: tag notes like #music #text #colour and filter the round by tag, so you fix one kind at a time
how: type #tag in the comment; use the Hashtag section in the comment filter; hashtags are indexed and suggested later.

name: Hex colour codes in grade notes
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: client can type an exact brand colour into a note
how: type # plus six hex characters (e.g. #FF0000) and Frame.io shows the colour swatch.

name: @mention to pull the decision-maker in
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: when a note needs the boss's call, @mention them so they get notified into the review
how: type @ and pick the user; Frame.io sends them a notification.

name: Filter a long comment list
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: on a round with dozens of notes, filter by annotations, attachments, reactions etc. and link people to one comment directly
how: use V4 comment filtering; each comment has its own link to send.

name: Frame-accurate scrub for checking notes
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: use hover-preview seeking to land exactly on a client's noted frame
how: hover over the Frame.io V4 timeline to preview each frame.

name: One Share link that updates itself
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: share a folder, not single files, so new cuts appear for the client without sending a new link
how: share the folder; files added/removed update the Share dynamically, sub-folder structure is kept.

name: Passphrase + expiry on client links
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: protect unreleased cuts
how: Share Settings > Security: set a Passphrase and an Expiration date/time after which access is removed.

name: Comment-only link (no download) until paid
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: let the client review but not download the final until the invoice clears
how: Share Settings > Permissions: turn Download off, keep Comment on; admins can set an account default of Downloads Off.
refs: AIGA (designer may withhold deliverables while invoices are overdue), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Show only the latest version to the client
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: avoid the client reviewing an old cut
how: in Share Settings switch off "Show all versions" so only the top of each version stack shows.

name: Check if the client actually opened the cut
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: before chasing feedback, look at the Share activity
how: Share Settings > Recent Share Activity > View: tracks Opened Share Link, Viewed Asset, Commented, Download with names and dates; All Shares shows Last Viewed and a view counter.

name: Single-asset link straight to the player
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: when sending one cut, skip the landing page
how: Share Settings > Layout: turn on "Open in Viewer". Grid/List/Reel layouts exist for multi-asset shares.

name: Branded review page
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: make the review link look like your studio (logo, header image, description, accent colour)
how: Share custom branding options; save a branding template in Account Settings > Branding to reuse.

name: Kill a link after delivery
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: revoke access to old cuts once the job is closed
how: All Shares > Visibility toggle off (link stops working) without deleting it.

name: Reviewers need no account
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: tell nervous clients they don't need to sign up
how: external reviewers just open the link; after the first comment they enter name + email (saved only for that session) and get email updates on replies/mentions.

name: Compare versions side by side in review
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: client checks what changed between v2 and v3
how: upload the new cut onto the old one to make a version stack; in a review link versions can be switched and compared side by side.

name: Approve / Needs work decision
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: make sign-off explicit: each approver picks Approve or Needs work; Needs work means a new version and another round
how: in Frame.io-Workfront approvals the asset only becomes approved when all assigned approvers choose approved; the owner is emailed on each decision.

name: Legacy approval statuses
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: in Frame.io Legacy review links, enabling Approvals lets reviewers mark Approved, In Progress or Needs Review
how: Link Settings > enable Approvals.

name: Frame.io watermark is a plan feature
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: before promising "watermarked review links", check the client-review plan: static watermarking and watermark templates are listed for Full User/Enterprise entitlements, session-based and forensic watermarking only in the Enterprise tiers (Select with SBWM, Prime)
how: otherwise burn a DRAFT watermark into the review copy with ffmpeg yourself (see the review-copy skills below).

name: Let the client set the status on the share
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: V4 Shares have a "Featured field" that recipients can edit, and the change shows on the asset in the project
how: set the Featured field to Status so recipients can update it from the link.

name: Send the share by email from Frame.io
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: "Share Link Via Email" emails the same link to anyone, inside or outside your workspace
how: Share Settings > Share Link Via Email with the client's address.

name: Captions/transcript on the review link
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: V4 shares can display transcriptions and captions if available
how: toggle it on for clients reviewing Urdu/English subtitles.

name: Order assets in a multi-video share
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: Custom sort lets you drag assets into order (root level only, Grid/List views; not in Reel view)
how: put the hero cut first, then cut-downs.

name: Save default share settings (Legacy)
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: Legacy review links can remember permission settings via "Save Share settings"; review links are free and unlimited on all plans; private assets are not shown
how: set download off/comments on once and save.

name: Frame.io V4 version stack
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: upload the new cut, wait until it has fully uploaded, then drag it onto the original; the newest opens first, older versions via the version number; reorder via three-dot > Version History; remove via manage version stack > Remove from stack
how: keep one stack per deliverable (e.g. "Promo 9x16") so all rounds' comments stay together.

name: Status field + Collections to track deliverables
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: V4 ships 32 built-in Fields (e.g. Status, Date Uploaded) plus custom fields (text, single select, date, toggle); Collections are live saved views filtered/grouped by those fields and can be shared
how: add a Platform single-select and a due-date field, then a "Needs work" collection for the current round.

name: Print the notes as a PDF checklist
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: turn a feedback round into a printable list with annotated thumbnails, timestamps and Completed/Incomplete state
how: Frame.io (Legacy) Comments Bar down-arrow > Print > save as PDF; sort by timecode first so the PDF follows the timeline.

name: Comments to CSV/XML
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: export a round's notes to a spreadsheet to track fixes
how: Comments Bar > Download As File > CSV or XML (Legacy).

name: Comments as NLE markers
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: bring client notes straight into the edit as markers
how: Frame.io Legacy "Download as File" for FCPX, Avid Media Composer or Resolve EDL; Resolve imports the EDL as markers.

name: Copy notes to the next version
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: Frame.io Legacy Copy puts all comments on the clipboard to paste onto another (e.g. newer) video
how: Comments Bar > Copy, open the new version, paste.

name: Premiere: notes in the timeline
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: with Frame.io V4, Premiere 25.2+ has a native Comments panel (Window > Frame.io > Frame.io V4 Comments): Export & Share the sequence, reviewers' comments arrive live, clicking a card moves the playhead, comment markers appear on the timeline
how: only V4 accounts work in this panel; older Premiere (down to 20.0) via Adobe Exchange.

name: One-button new version from Premiere
section: Feedback rounds in Frame.io (timecoded notes, shares, approvals)
what: the V4 panel detects sequence changes and offers New Version, which auto-stacks on the previous cut in Frame.io
how: after fixing a round, click New Version so the client's link shows the latest.

name: Vimeo review link per audience
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: make several review links for one video with different settings (e.g. one with download for the agency, one without for the end client)
how: Video Settings > Share > Create review links; each link has its own name, expiry, password, permissions. Free plan: one review link per video and expiry up to one month out; password needs a paid plan.

name: Vimeo "Change status" for sign-off
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: let the client mark the video Approved on the review link
how: in "What can people with this link do?" turn Change status on (Download off, Comment on).

name: Vimeo link ignores video privacy
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: anyone with a Vimeo review link can watch regardless of the video's own privacy
how: always add an expiry (and a password on paid plans); disable it in Share > Manage review links when done.

name: Vimeo notes as to-dos
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: treat each time-coded note as a to-do and check it off when fixed
how: reply on notes and mark them resolved on the review page.

name: Replace the clip, keep the link
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: after a round, upload the new edit as a new version so the same review link shows it
how: Vimeo Version Management; enable "View previous versions" on the link if the client should compare.

name: Drive delivery without downloads
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: sharing a review copy on Google Drive: Viewer/Commenter can download by default; the owner can stop viewers and commenters downloading, printing or copying
how: in Drive's advanced sharing settings stop viewers and commenters from downloading, printing or copying; use Restricted access instead of Anyone with the link for unreleased cuts.

name: Drive link levels
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: Public (findable on Google), Anyone with the link (no sign-in), Restricted (only added people)
how: use Restricted + named client emails for a final master; "Anyone with the link" only for public promo copies.

name: Vimeo version history
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: replace a cut as a new version (V5 -> V6), restore an old one (creates a new version), or download any previous version
how: Video Settings > version history > + New version / Restore / Download.

name: Vimeo folder review for multi-video jobs
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: share a whole folder (e.g. all reel formats) with one review link; folder links default to 30-day expiry and can have password, comment/download/status/version permissions and team logo
how: Folder > Share > Review tab > New review link (paid plans; team folders must be in Team Library).

name: Collaborator vs viewer comments on Vimeo
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: collaborator comments on review links are private (Can Edit members can resolve, download, delete); viewer comments on the public page are public and can be locked
how: keep client feedback on review links, not on the public video page.

name: Unlisted vs Private for client previews on YouTube
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: Unlisted: anyone with the link (no Google account needed) can watch, comment and reshare; Private: only invited emails, no comments
how: use Private + "Share privately" for unreleased cuts; Unlisted when the client must forward it or comment.

name: Private YouTube videos can't take comments
section: Feedback on Vimeo, Google Drive and YouTube links
what: if the client needs to comment on YouTube itself, use Unlisted; Unlisted videos can appear in public playlists if someone adds them
how: for feedback prefer Frame.io/Vimeo review links.

name: Chase requirements, don't wait silently
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: a Fiverr order doesn't start until the client submits requirements; the page shows Requirements Needed and you can send a reminder
how: send the reminder; if you already have the footage and brief, click Skip requirements to move to In Progress; unanswered requirements auto-cancel the order 14 days after creation.

name: Extend before you go Late
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: request a delivery extension early instead of letting the timer run out
how: order page > Extend delivery date (under Deliver Now), pick date + reason; the client has 48 h, silence = accepted; days are added to the ORIGINAL deadline, max 60 days per request.

name: Late order danger window
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: know the clock: after the deadline the order is Late (hurts on-time metric); after 24 h Late the client can cancel alone; a very late order auto-cancels 30 days after it was placed
how: message the client before the deadline and use Extend delivery date.

name: Order Timeline for bigger edits
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: for orders over $200 and longer than 7 days, publish a step plan (draft, video call, progress update) the client can follow
how: click Create timeline within 3 days of order creation; up to 24 steps; editable only before the first delivery; not for milestone/subscription/hourly orders.

name: Share Draft for a rough cut
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: send a work-in-progress cut without starting the 3-day review clock and without it counting as a revision
how: order page/Inbox > Share Draft, add message + files; drafts get a Fiverr watermark on files/images, don't change order status, aren't available on mobile, and not for hourly orders.

name: Progress update every 2-3 days
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr's best practice: thank the client, explain your first step (e.g. storyboard) and send it for review, then update every two to three days in the order chat
how: a short Roman Urdu status message with what's done and what's next.

name: Zoom call auto-ticks the timeline
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: an Order Timeline "Video call" step completes automatically if a Zoom meeting held through the Fiverr Inbox lasts over 4 minutes; elsewhere mark it manually
how: hold the kickoff call via Fiverr's Zoom.

name: Recap revision notes before touching the timeline
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: when a delivery is rejected, first message back: acknowledge, list what you will change, ask if anything else should change
how: reply template in Roman Urdu/English with numbered changes, then edit only after the client confirms.
refs: Fiverr Community (Adrian Rodrigues, Senior Success Manager), https://community.fiverr.com/public/blogs/navigating-client-revisions-while-protecting-your-success-score-metrics-2026-04-09, checked 2026-10-24

name: Ask instead of guessing vague notes
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: "make it pop" style notes get a short friendly clarifying question, not a guess
how: ask for an example video or a timecode.
refs: Fiverr Community (Adrian Rodrigues, Senior Success Manager), https://community.fiverr.com/public/blogs/navigating-client-revisions-while-protecting-your-success-score-metrics-2026-04-09, checked 2026-10-24

name: Fiverr pre-delivery checklist
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: before Deliver Now: scope and quality match, every requirement addressed, files correctly named/formatted/easy to open, all files included, delivery message summarises contents
how: run your ffprobe delivery report (below) and paste the summary in "Describe your delivery".

name: 1 GB per file on Fiverr: link the master
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: a single delivery file is limited to 1 GB
how: for files over the limit, Fiverr suggests Dropbox or another file-sharing link in the delivery.

name: Never deliver a placeholder
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Deliver Now is only for completed work or proof of completion; empty, partial or placeholder deliveries can violate Fiverr's ToS
how: use Share Draft for partial cuts instead.

name: Know the 3-day auto-complete
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: after delivery the client has 3 days to accept, request revisions or extend review (up to 5 days at a time, repeatable); with no action the order auto-completes (8 days for milestone orders)
how: mention the review window in the delivery message so the client watches it.

name: Revision count lives in the package
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: the number of revisions a client may request comes from the gig package or agreed scope
how: state revisions per tier in packages; while In Revision you can add Gig Extras or request a new date for out-of-scope changes, then re-deliver with a short summary of what changed.

name: Plan cash flow around clearance
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr earnings become available 14 days after completion (7 days for Seller Plus, TRS and Pro Talent)
how: don't promise yourself the money the day the client accepts.

name: Live Portfolio sample on delivery
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: pick one delivery file as a public sample when delivering (only if the client and the footage allow it)
how: in the Deliver Now pop-up select the delivery file to use as a Live Portfolio sample; never select personal/family footage.

name: Fiverr image watermark until acceptance
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr can watermark delivered image files (jpg, png...) until the client accepts; only files in the delivery message, not inbox files
how: send thumbnails/posters through Deliver Now, not chat.

name: Cancellation requests are 48-hour clocks
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: either side's cancellation request through the Resolution Center auto-cancels if the other side doesn't answer in 48 hours; you can't force-cancel
how: check the order page daily during a dispute.

name: Which cancellations hurt your Order Completion Rate
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: cancellations before the client submitted requirements: no impact; very late orders force-cancelled by the client and cancellations you request: affect OCR
how: prefer extensions, extras or a partial refund over cancelling.

name: Unresponsive client from the start
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr advises initiating a mutual cancellation through the Resolution Center when a client is unresponsive from the start
how: Order > View > Resolution Center > Cancel order with a short reason.

name: Partial refund instead of cancelling
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: for scope changes, delays or minor dissatisfaction, offer a partial refund (up to 60% of the original price); if accepted, performance metrics aren't affected, but only one per order
how: Resolution Center > Offer a partial refund > amount + reason.

name: Fiverr partial refund rules
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: only the freelancer can send it; order must be active and over $50; min $5, max 60% of the original price (extras added later aren't covered); one per order, irreversible; client has 3 days before the offer expires; milestone orders only on the first milestone
how: agree the amount in Inbox first, then Resolution Center > Offer a partial refund.

name: One open request at a time
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: you can't open a new Resolution Center request while an extension, update or cancellation request is open; withdraw the open one first. Unanswered requests auto-accept after 48 hours
how: withdraw an old extension request before asking for cancellation.

name: Pause the gig when away
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: use the Availability feature (dates + note, turns off automatically) instead of taking orders you can't finish
how: set Availability before Eid/holidays.

name: Keep payment on Fiverr
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: offering or accepting off-platform payment is against Fiverr's rules and removes Fiverr's protections; Fiverr gives polite sample replies to decline
how: reply: "Moving payments off Fiverr means we both lose protection and it's against Fiverr's Terms of Service."

name: WhatsApp only after the order, and document it
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: third-party communication is permitted only after an order is placed; summarise those chats and share the notes on Fiverr
how: after a WhatsApp voice note from the client, paste a written summary of the changes into the order chat.

name: No remote-access tools for clients
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr says don't let others control your device via TeamViewer/AnyDesk and avoid untrusted links
how: ask the client to upload footage instead of "fixing it on your PC".

name: Success Score is private, Level is public
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr's Success Score (six areas incl. client satisfaction, communication, conflict-free orders, cancellations, delivery time) is visible only to you; clients see your Level; bigger, recent orders weigh more
how: prioritise clear expectations and fast replies on high-value orders.

name: Never coach or bribe for reviews on Fiverr
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: Fiverr counts even "If you had a good experience, please leave a review" as feedback manipulation, along with guilt-tripping, bribes ("something extra for a good review") and threats; feedback boosting (fake orders, paid reviews) leads to a permanent block
how: end the delivery message with the summary and review window only.

name: Fiverr review windows
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: both sides have 14 days after completion to leave a public review (30 days in some categories); the client reviews first, you see it after you submit yours; clients can attach order files to your Live Portfolio; public ratings show the last two years
how: leave your client review promptly after theirs arrives.

name: How Fiverr milestone orders run
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: client pays each milestone as it starts; 8 days to accept/request revision per milestone delivery (else completed); 10 days to pay the next one after accepting or the order stops; a stopped order can't resume; once one milestone is complete, cancelled later milestones don't hurt your stats
how: set revisions per milestone in the offer.

name: Gig video for the Video & Animation category
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: a gig video is required in Video & Animation: 20-60 s, under 50 MB, no copyrighted audio/visuals or watermarks you don't own; the video is reviewed separately
how: cut a 45 s showreel with CC0 music and compress under 50 MB; check size with `ls -l`.

name: Gig images: own work, right size
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: up to three gig images, own work only; recommended 1280x769 px (min 712x430)
how: `ffmpeg -ss 5 -i reel.mp4 -frames:v 1 -vf "scale=1280:769:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1280:769" gig.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Don't repurpose an established gig
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: fundamentally changing a gig's service can remove it from search, since reviews and portfolio are tied to the original service; batch edits to avoid visibility dips; use all five search tags
how: create a separate gig for a new service (e.g. "Shorts editing").

name: Commercial Use licence wording
section: Fiverr orders, revisions, delivery and metrics
what: know what a Fiverr "Commercial Use License" grants the buyer: perpetual, exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide licence for business uses, and IP assigned to the buyer unless your gig page says otherwise; "Commercial Use - 1 Year" limits it to 12 months from delivery
how: if you reuse your own templates/music in client videos, state the exclusions on the gig page.

name: Only start on a "Funded" milestone
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: Upwork can't help recover pay for fixed-price work done before a milestone was funded
how: check for the "Funded" label next to the milestone before editing anything.

name: Submit Work for Payment, always
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: delivering through the Submit Work for Payment button is a condition of Fixed-Price Payment Protection and starts the 14-day automatic payment countdown
how: deliver through that button, not just in chat.

name: Change scope = update milestone first
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: if the client adds a second video or more formats mid-job, ask them to update/add a milestone before you do it; work that doesn't match the milestone description isn't protected
how: reply "please add a milestone for the extra cut, I'll start once it shows Funded".

name: Small milestones per stage
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: split an edit into milestones (e.g. rough cut, final, formats) so you are paid as you go
how: propose 2-3 milestones in the offer, each with a clear deliverable description.

name: Keep files and messages on Upwork
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: Upwork's protection checklist says keep file delivery, messages and project details on the platform; disputes are possible when a client won't release, releases part, asks a refund, or ends the contract with funds still held
how: send files and project decisions through Upwork Messages.

name: Don't submit after the Upwork contract ends
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: work submitted after the contract has ended (without written agreement) isn't covered by Fixed-Price Payment Protection
how: submit the final cut before anyone closes the contract; put any post-contract fixes in writing.

name: Fee refunded with client refunds
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: if money paid to you is refunded to the client, Upwork returns the service fee on that amount
how: account for it when offering a partial refund.

name: Direct Contracts for your own clients
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: a client you bring to Upwork via Direct Contracts gets you a reduced service fee; Any Hire contracts pay no fee
how: for a client you brought to Upwork yourself, set the job up as a Direct Contract to pay the reduced fee.

name: Connects cost money: bid selectively
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: Upwork Connects (needed for proposals, boosts, Availability Badge) cost $0.15 each in bundles; badges (Rising Talent, Top Rated, Top Rated Plus) give 30 free Connects each
how: only bid on video jobs whose brief you can deliver.

name: Free "test" work is a red flag
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: Upwork lists unrealistic pay, vague descriptions, pressure to talk off-platform before a contract, free work requests (including a big unpaid "test") and off-platform payment as scam signs
how: decline unpaid "tests" and report free-work requests to Upwork support, as Upwork advises.

name: Don't start before billing is verified
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: Upwork can't pay you until the client completes billing-method verification; starting before that is your risk
how: confirm the client's billing-method verification is complete before you start.

name: Hourly protection needs the desktop time tracker
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: Upwork Hourly Payment Protection covers time logged with the Upwork Desktop App time tracker, with screenshots related to the contract, memos/activity labels describing the work, fair activity levels and within the weekly limit; plus verified identity and a client with verified billing
how: write a memo per segment like "colour grade scene 3".

name: What hourly protection excludes
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: manually added time, idle/empty segments, time over the weekly limit, non-work activity, and segments with missing or poor memos
how: don't add manual time for render waits you didn't track.

name: Hourly dispute: stop and answer in 3 days
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: when a client disputes hours, Upwork pauses the contract and sets the weekly limit to zero; you have three days to accept or decline
how: stop editing and respond in the dispute flow immediately.

name: Upwork hourly dispute outcomes
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: accept = all disputed hours refunded to the client; decline = a specialist checks the work diary within one business day and refunds only non-compliant hours
how: Deliver work > Contract history > See dispute; review your hours each week before billing to fix errors.

name: Upwork hourly payment calendar
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: billing week Mon 00:00-Sun 23:59 UTC; you have until Monday 11:59 UTC to fix your diary; client reviews until Friday; money usually available the following Wednesday; bonuses 5 days after processing
how: check your work diary every Monday morning (Pakistan time = UTC+5).

name: Upwork milestone dispute: 7-day window
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: if a client ends a fixed-price contract and asks a refund of the deposit, you have seven calendar days to file a dispute or the remaining funds go back to the client
how: Deliver work > Contract history > See Request > Dispute; leave feedback (required), describe the milestone, attach proof — you can't add details later.

name: After you file a milestone dispute
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: the client has five calendar days; no reply = funds released to you; decline = an agent gives a non-binding resolution (usually ~2 days), each side has two days to accept; then optional paid binding arbitration
how: keep your delivery files and chat ready to attach on day one.

name: Active contract, unpaid milestone
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: ask the client to end the contract and release payment; if they refuse, contact Upwork Support with evidence the work is complete
how: send a polite written request first, then Support.

name: Client goes silent mid-job (fixed price)
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: don't end the contract before submitting; finish the milestone, Submit work, and wait 14 days for automatic release. Hourly: properly logged protected hours are still billed even if the client is silent
how: submit the finished cut through Deliver work > active contracts.

name: Refunds only inside Upwork
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: refunding a client off Upwork breaks the ToS; you can refund up to the lower of 180-day net contract total and your available balance; the service fee on refunded money is returned
how: contract workroom > (...) > Give a refund > Add invoices > amount + note.

name: A refund doesn't erase a bad rating
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: a full refund removes public written feedback, but the client's private 1-5 ratings still count in your Job Success Score
how: resolve concerns by communication instead of refunding to dodge a review.

name: Upwork JSS basics
section: Upwork contracts, payment protection and disputes
what: JSS (calculated daily over 6/12/24-month windows, best shown) weighs client feedback, why contracts ended, higher-value projects and long-term relationships; 90%+ is excellent, below 79% makes winning work hard; flagged/suspended clients' feedback doesn't count
how: close finished contracts cleanly and keep repeat clients.

name: Burn-in timecode on review copies
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: put a running timecode on the review cut so WhatsApp/email clients can quote exact times even without Frame.io
how: `ffmpeg -i cut.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=library/fonts/Anton-Regular.ttf:timecode='00\:00\:00\:00':rate=30:fontsize=28:fontcolor=white:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.6:x=(w-tw)/2:y=h-th-12" -c:a copy review_tc.mp4` (drawtext timecode needs timecode_rate/rate) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: "DRAFT" text on unpaid review cuts
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: a semi-transparent text overlay marks a cut as not final when your review platform lacks watermarking
how: `ffmpeg -i cut.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=library/fonts/Anton-Regular.ttf:text='DRAFT v2 - NOT FOR PUBLISHING':fontsize=36:fontcolor=white@0.35:x=(w-tw)/2:y=(h-th)/2" -c:a copy review_wm.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: On-screen "Ad / Sponsored" label
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: add the FTC-style disclosure inside the video itself
how: `ffmpeg -i cut.mp4 -vf "drawtext=fontfile=library/fonts/Anton-Regular.ttf:text='Ad / Sponsored':fontsize=26:fontcolor=white:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.5:x=16:y=16:enable='lt(t,3)'" -c:a copy ad.mp4` (enable controls when it shows; the FTC wants it noticeable, so judge the duration yourself) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Small review copy for slow connections
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: a light low-resolution copy for a client on mobile data
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -vf scale=-2:240 -c:v libx264 -crf 28 -preset veryfast -c:a aac -b:a 96k review_small.mp4` (change 240 to the height you want) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: v1 vs v2 side by side for the client
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: show what changed in one player
how: `ffmpeg -i v1.mp4 -i v2.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]drawtext=fontfile=...:text='v1':x=10:y=10[a];[1:v]drawtext=fontfile=...:text='v2':x=10:y=10[b];[a][b]hstack=inputs=2[v]" -map "[v]" -map 0:a -c:a aac compare.mp4` (inputs must share height) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Contact sheet for shot approval
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: one PNG of frames for a quick "which shots do you like" message
how: `ffmpeg -i cut.mp4 -vf "fps=2,scale=320:-2,tile=3x2" -frames:v 1 sheet.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Still frame at a client's noted time
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: grab the exact frame of a note to paste into a fix list
how: `ffmpeg -ss 1.5 -i cut.mp4 -frames:v 1 note_00-00-01-15.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Master to YouTube's recommended upload settings
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: MP4, moov at front, H.264 High, 2 consecutive B-frames, closed GOP of half the frame rate, 4:2:0, AAC-LC 48 kHz, BT.709 tags
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -bf 2 -g 15 -flags +cgop -pix_fmt yuv420p -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709 -c:a aac -ar 48000 -b:a 384k -movflags +faststart master.mp4` (-g 15 for 30 fps; 384k = YouTube's stereo audio recommendation) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Spec report before handover
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: print codec, profile, size, fps, pix_fmt, colour tags, B-frames, sample rate, channels, duration and file size, and compare with the brief's specs
how: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,profile,width,height,r_frame_rate,pix_fmt,color_primaries,color_transfer,color_space,has_b_frames,sample_rate,channels:format=duration,size -of json master.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Verify moov-before-mdat yourself
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: confirm a delivered MP4 is really fast-start (YouTube asks for the moov atom at the front)
how: Python top-level atom walk: read 8-byte headers (size, type), handle size==1 64-bit; assert order.index('moov') < order.index('mdat'); got ['ftyp','moov','free','mdat'] here. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Exact frame count check
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: confirm the delivered length in frames (e.g. a 15 s ad at 30 fps = 450)
how: `ffprobe -v error -count_frames -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=nb_read_frames -of csv=p=0 master.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Loudness number for the delivery note
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: measure integrated loudness and report it with the delivery
how: `ffmpeg -nostats -i master.mp4 -af ebur128 -f null - 2>&1 | grep -A3 "Integrated loudness"` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Catch accidental black gaps before delivery
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: find black stretches (a missing clip) in the export
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -vf blackdetect=d=0.5 -f null - 2>&1 | grep black_start` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Catch accidental audio dropouts
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: find silent stretches that shouldn't be there
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -af silencedetect=n=-50dB:d=0.5 -f null - 2>&1 | grep silence_` (tested here 2026-10-24)
