name: Checksum list with the handover
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: let the client verify big downloads arrived intact
how: `sha256sum master.mp4 review_small.mp4 > SHA256SUMS.txt`; client/you check with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt` (md5sum works the same way) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Zip the handover and test it
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: package master, subtitle version and checksum list, then test the archive before sending
how: `zip -q -r handover.zip master.mp4 master_subs.mp4 SHA256SUMS.txt && unzip -tq handover.zip` (tested here 2026-10-24)
refs: Info-ZIP unzip 6.00, local `unzip -h`: "-t test compressed archive data", checked 2026-10-24

name: Soft subtitles inside the MP4
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: deliver captions the client can switch on/off, tagged with a language
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -i subs.srt -map 0 -map 1 -c copy -c:s mov_text -metadata:s:s:0 language=urd master_subs.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Title and copyright tags on the master
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: write a clean title/copyright into the delivered file
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -map_metadata -1 -metadata title='Client promo v3' -metadata copyright='(c) 2026 Studio' -c copy out.mp4`; ffprobe showed TAG:title and TAG:copyright. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Strip source metadata before handover
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: drop phone/editor metadata (and chapters) from the source when delivering
how: `ffmpeg -i master.mp4 -map_metadata -1 -map_chapters -1 -c copy stripped.mp4`; only muxer tags (brand, encoder) remained here. (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Under-1-GB check for Fiverr uploads
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: Fiverr limits a single delivery file to 1 GB; check before uploading
how: `python3 -c "import os;s=os.path.getsize('master.mp4');print(s, s<10**9)"` (10**9 bytes = the stricter reading of 1 GB) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Fit a gig video under 50 MB with two-pass
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: compute video bitrate from the size limit and duration, then encode in two passes
how: kbps = 50*8*1000/duration_s*0.95 - audio_kbps; `ffmpeg -i reel.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 63205k -pass 1 -passlogfile p2 -an -f null /dev/null && ffmpeg -i reel.mp4 -c:v libx264 -b:v 63205k -pass 2 -passlogfile p2 -c:a aac -b:a 128k gigvideo.mp4` (6 s test -> 23 MB, under the limit) (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 3-2-1 for client projects
section: Review copies, delivery QA and file handover (tested commands)
what: keep three copies of the project/masters, on two different devices, one off-site (e.g. cloud)
how: e.g. working drive + external drive + cloud copy, as in Backblaze's example.

name: What an invoice must show (UK rules, good everywhere)
what: unique invoice number, your name/address/contact, client name and address, clear description of what you charge for, supply date, invoice date, amounts, VAT if applicable, total owed; sole traders add their name and business name
how: keep a numbering scheme like INV-2026-031 and fill every field.

name: Simple invoice PDF with the required fields
what: make a one-page PDF invoice locally (number, from/to, item, supply date, invoice date, amount, tax, total, due date)
how: Python Pillow: draw the lines on a white A4-size image with ImageDraw and save with `im.save("invoice.pdf","PDF",resolution=150)` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Net 30 / Net 15 / "2% 10, net 30"
what: net N = full payment within N days of service completion; "2% 10, net 30" gives a 2% discount if paid within 10 days; net 10/15 are common for service contractors; "net 30 end of month" (UK) means by end of the following month
how: print the term and the actual due date on every invoice.

name: Invoice due days + monthly late charge
what: the model terms fill in N days to pay and allow a 1.5% monthly service charge (or the maximum the law allows) on overdue balances, with payments applied to late charges first
how: put both on the invoice footer for clients where that is lawful.
refs: AIGA Standard Form of Agreement for Design Services (2022 update), https://www.aiga.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/Standardformofagreement_2022update.pdf, checked 2026-10-24

name: Default "late" date for UK business clients
what: if no payment date was agreed, payment is late 30 days after the client gets the invoice or the service is delivered (whichever later); agreed terms are usually within 60 days for businesses
how: always write a due date on the invoice; quote this rule to UK clients.

name: UK statutory late interest
what: for UK business clients, statutory interest is 8% plus the Bank of England base rate (unless the contract sets another rate); send a new invoice to add it
how: daily interest = debt x (0.08 + base) / 365; GOV.UK example £1,000 at 0.5% base = £85/yr, ~23p/day. `python3 -c "print(round(1000*0.085/365,2))"` -> 0.23 (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: UK fixed debt-recovery charge
what: on top of interest you can charge once per payment: £40 (debt up to £999.99), £70 (£1,000-£9,999.99), £100 (£10,000+)
how: add it as a line on the reminder invoice to UK business clients.

name: Freelancer bank account in Pakistan
what: banks offer freelancer accounts opened with a CNIC and a self-declaration of freelance income (platform, nature of services, approximate volume); Payoneer withdraws to any Pakistani bank account by IBAN
how: keep your Fiverr/Upwork profile screenshot and a client contract ready as supporting evidence.

name: Keep part of earnings in USD (ESFCA)
what: a linked Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account can retain up to 50% of foreign earnings in USD; eligibility needs PSEB or P@SHA registration
how: register with PSEB first, then ask the bank for the linked ESFCA.

name: FBR filing threshold for freelancers
what: freelancers earning above PKR 600,000 a year must register with FBR and file a return (filing even below it keeps you on the Active Taxpayer List per the second source)
how: note yearly totals from bank credit advices.
refs: beancount.io blog (secondary; confirm with FBR/PSEB), https://beancount.io/blog/2026/08/13/pakistan-it-freelancers-0-25-percent-pseb-2029-guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: PSEB registration: 0.25% vs 1%
what: PSEB-registered IT/IT-enabled exporters get a 0.25% final tax on remittances via banks (reported extended to June 30 2029); unregistered default is 1%. Conditions include remitting at least 80% of export proceeds through formal banking channels
how: register with PSEB, renew yearly, keep bank withholding certificates and remittance advices with purpose code. Confirm current rates with FBR/PSEB before advising anyone.
refs: beancount.io blog (secondary; confirm with FBR/PSEB), https://beancount.io/blog/2026/08/13/pakistan-it-freelancers-0-25-percent-pseb-2029-guide, checked 2026-10-24

name: Pakistan National Freelancing Policy (draft)
what: a 2023 draft proposed PSEB freelancer registration at Rs 1,000 and Rs 3,500 yearly renewal, SBP freelancer FX accounts retaining 35% of inflows, and an income-tax holiday till 2030 on export income via SBP purpose codes; it was a DRAFT
how: treat as background only; check what was enacted before telling anyone.

name: PSEB freelancer registration portal
what: since Sept 2021 freelancers register with PSEB through MoITT's online portal (pseb.org.pk)
how: register there before claiming the PSEB-linked tax/bank benefits above.

name: Pakistan: Copyright Ordinance 1962
what: copyright covers cinematographic works, records, musical works etc.; the first owner is generally the author (exceptions incl. works for hire); copyright can be assigned (s.14) or licensed (s.35); registration is optional but is prima facie evidence
how: for Pakistani clients, put assignment/licence in writing in the contract.

name: Pakistan terms and moral rights
what: cinematographic works, records and photographs: 50 years from the year after publication; assigning rights does not assign moral rights (s.62); fair dealing covers research, private study, criticism, review, reporting current events
how: don't promise clients US "fair use" for music; rely on licences.

name: Pakistan related rights
what: performers' and phonogram producers' rights last 50 years; broadcasting organisations 25 years
how: check broadcast/recording rights separately from the composition when a client wants an old TV clip or recording.

name: CC0 music: no permission, no credit
what: CC0 waives copyright worldwide; you may copy, modify, distribute, even commercially, without asking
how: prefer CC0 tracks (owner rule: no credit-needed music); note CC0 doesn't clear trademark, publicity or privacy rights.

name: CC BY means a credit line + licence link
what: CC BY 4.0 allows commercial use but requires appropriate credit, a link to the licence and noting changes
how: because the owner rejects credit-needed music, skip CC BY for paid client videos unless the client accepts a credit.

name: YouTube Audio Library "Attribution not required" filter
what: for a client's YouTube video, use Audio Library tracks filtered to Attribution not required; they are copyright-safe and won't be Content-ID claimed
how: YouTube Studio > Audio library > filter > Attribution not required > Download MP3. CC-licensed Audio Library tracks still need the credit in the description.

name: Monetisation with Audio Library music
what: YouTube Partner Program channels can monetise videos that use Audio Library music and SFX
how: tell monetising clients YouTube says only Audio Library music is known to it to be copyright-safe and it isn't responsible for "royalty-free" music from other channels/libraries.

name: Searching the YouTube Audio Library
what: filter music by title, genre, mood, artist, attribution and duration (seconds), star tracks to a Starred tab, and sort by title/artist/duration/date; new releases arrive twice a month; SFX filter by category and duration
how: filter Attribution not required + duration close to the edit length, star candidates and send the client the shortlist.

name: Short over 60 s: music limits
what: vertical/square uploads up to 3 min are Shorts; Shorts Audio Library songs mostly allowed up to 90 s (some 60 or 30 s); YouTube Audio Library royalty-free music won't get a Content ID claim; any claimed Short over one minute is blocked globally
how: for client Shorts over a minute, use Audio Library "attribution not required" or CC0 music.

name: Content ID claim is not a strike
what: a claim (block/monetise/track, can differ by country) affects the video, usually not the channel; strikes come from valid removal requests
how: reassure the client, then check Studio > Content > filter Claims > Restrictions > See details > Claimant.

name: Fix a valid claim without re-uploading
what: options: Erase song (mute song or all audio), Trim out segment, or Replace song with Audio Library audio; each removes the claim
how: use these in YouTube Studio for the client instead of deleting the video.

name: Shorts 1-3 min with a claim are blocked
what: any active claim blocks a 1-3-minute vertical Short regardless of policy
how: for client Shorts over 60 s, use music that can't be claimed (CC0 or YouTube Audio Library).

name: Don't dispute without rights
what: disputing a claim without a valid reason can lead to a removal request and a copyright strike
how: dispute only when you hold the licence (keep the licence PDF/link in the project folder).

name: Claim dispute timeline
what: after a dispute the claimant has 30 days (release, reinstate, removal request, or let it expire); a rejected dispute can be appealed (claimant then has 7 days); "Escalate to Appeal" exists only for claims that block the video; a dispute can't be cancelled
how: tell the client the realistic wait before promising the video will be monetised.

name: Studio edits to claimed videos are permanent
what: since June 2025 a saved Studio Editor change can't be reverted; "Erase song" may fail on hard-to-separate music, "Mute all sound in claimed segments" is faster and more likely to clear the claim
how: keep the original master on disk before editing in Studio.

name: Freesound: pick CC0 for client SFX
what: Freesound sounds are CC0 (do almost anything, even sell, but don't claim authorship), CC BY (always credit) or CC BY-NC (credit, no money-making use); old Sampling+ sounds also bar commercial advertising
how: for paid client work use only CC0 sounds (owner rule: no credit-needed audio).

name: Freesound credit format (when credit is allowed)
what: Freesound's suggested credit lists "sound" by user (link) licensed under <licence>; a long list can point to a credits web page; your account's attribution list shows everything you downloaded
how: use the Freesound attribution list to find where each downloaded sound came from.

name: Raw SFX can trigger Content ID
what: unedited Freesound effects used inside songs registered with Content ID can cause claims on your video; modified/stretched sounds are less likely to match. Dispute with the Freesound page link and the date proving it predates the claimed song
how: keep the source URL of every SFX in the project notes.

name: "No copyright intended" protects nothing
what: YouTube: credit lines, "I do not own", "no infringement intended" or "for entertainment only" don't make a use fair; transformativeness and the four factors decide, and Content ID can't judge fair use
how: tell clients who want a famous clip/song that a disclaimer won't stop a claim.

name: Other libraries may not cover YouTube
what: YouTube warns that some royalty-free/licensing sites don't grant rights to use or monetise on YouTube
how: read the library's terms for YouTube/monetisation before using a track in a client channel video; or use the Audio Library.

name: Outside the US it's not "fair use"
what: the EU allows specific categories (quotation, criticism, review, caricature, parody, pastiche); other countries use fair dealing
how: don't promise Pakistani or UK clients US-style fair use.

name: Four fair-use factors (US)
what: purpose/character (non-profit education and transformative uses favoured), nature of the work (factual favoured), amount used (small bits favoured, but not the "heart"), effect on the market
how: use this only to explain to clients why a claimed clip is risky; prefer licences.

name: A famous song needs two licences
what: syncing a recording needs the composition (publisher) and the master recording (label); producers on tight budgets use covers or commissioned work-for-hire music to avoid the master side
how: when a client asks for a hit song, explain both licences and offer CC0/Audio Library/commissioned music instead (owner rule: never download copyrighted songs).

name: Pixabay media: free, no credit, but limits
what: Pixabay allows free use and modification without attribution, but no standalone resale, no commercial use of content with recognisable trademarks/logos in relation to goods/services, no misleading or illegal use of recognisable people, no use as a trademark
how: check stock clips for visible brands before using them in an ad.

name: Pexels stock in client ads
what: Pexels photos/videos are free, no attribution needed, may be modified; not allowed: identifiable people shown in a bad light, implying endorsement by people/brands in the imagery, reselling unaltered copies, redistributing on stock sites, use in a trademark/business name
how: for a client product ad, don't cut a Pexels person into a shot that looks like they endorse the product.

name: Release is about publishing, not filming
what: a model release grants permission to publish someone's image; it is a privacy matter separate from copyright, and the need rises sharply for advertising/commercial use
how: for client ad edits ask the client to confirm releases for every recognisable person in their footage before you deliver.

name: Minor release signed by a parent
what: a minor's release must be signed by a parent/legal guardian, otherwise it may give the publisher no protection; group releases add signature lines for several people
how: for school/kids footage in a promo, ask for guardian-signed releases.

name: Free licences don't clear people
what: CC0 and CC BY say they don't cover publicity/privacy rights of people in the work
how: even a CC0 clip with a recognisable face is risky in a client's commercial ad; prefer shots without identifiable people.

name: Consent to film is not consent to publish
what: Wikimedia Commons separates consent to take, to upload/publish and to re-use; private-place shots need consent; minors' consent comes from parents/guardians; many countries need consent for commercial use even in public (its table lists commercial use needing consent in e.g. the UK; India "yes, with exceptions")
how: for client ads ask who appears and whether they agreed to an advert, not just to being filmed.

name: Paid promotion checkbox for sponsored videos
what: if the client's video contains sponsorship/branded content, tick Paid promotion so YouTube adds a disclosure label at the start
how: Studio > Upload > Show more > Paid Promotion > "Yes, my video includes branded content"; age/country restrictions appear only after Yes.

name: Disclosure inside the video, not only the description
what: FTC: in a video the disclosure should be in the video itself (ideally said and shown), clear words like "ad"/"sponsored", same language as the endorsement, repeated in live streams
how: in client influencer edits put an on-screen "Ad"/"Sponsored" caption in the video and have it said in the voice track too.

name: Avoid vague disclosure tags
what: FTC says don't use "sp", "spon", "collab" or a lone "thanks"/"ambassador", and don't bury the disclosure among hashtags
how: write "Sponsored by <brand>" or "#ad" visibly.

name: Free product = disclose too
what: FTC: a brand relationship includes free or discounted products; if a brand gave free products and the creator then mentions one of its products, disclose even if they weren't asked to mention that product
how: for influencer client edits, ask whether the product was gifted and add the disclosure if so.

name: Ad scripts: no untried or unprovable claims
what: FTC: you can't talk about experience with a product you haven't tried, call it terrific if you thought it terrible, or make claims the advertiser can't prove (e.g. health claims)
how: flag such lines in a client's voiceover/caption script before editing them in.

name: Instagram paid partnership label
what: branded content on Instagram must use the paid partnership label tagging the brand; first tag sends the brand an approval request; until approved the label shows without the brand name; brand partner needs a professional account and gets the post's insights
how: tell influencer clients to add it in the app when posting your edit.

name: AI-use disclosure for realistic AI
what: YouTube requires disclosure when AI makes a real person appear to say/do something, alters real events/places, creates a realistic scene that didn't happen, or creates music that is the main focus
how: Studio upload > Attributes > AI use > Yes. AI-generated music is on the must-disclose list.

name: What AI edits don't need a label
what: colour/lighting filters, background blur, captions, upscaling/repair, voice/audio repair, AI scripts/thumbnails, cloning one's own voice for voiceovers are listed as not needing disclosure
how: tell the client which of their edits need the AI-use Yes and which don't.

name: Get channel access, never the password
what: YouTube channel permissions are safer than sharing passwords; roles: Owner, Manager, Editor, Editor (Limited, no revenue data), Subtitle Editor, Viewer
how: ask the client to invite you as Editor (Limited) to upload and schedule; invites expire after 30 days; client removes access when done.

name: Schedule the client's premiere time
what: upload as Private/Scheduled and set date, time and time zone; the watch page "published on" date follows Pacific time
how: Studio upload > Schedule card; for a Pakistan launch date near midnight, check the PST date.

name: Showreel length and purpose
what: a showreel (demo/sizzle reel) is usually 2-3 minutes of footage from different projects, supplementing a CV
how: cut yours to 2-3 min from client work you have permission to show (AIGA-style portfolio clause), never family/personal media.

name: The `subtitles` filter breaks Urdu and Hindi here; the `ass` filter doesn't
section: Rendering Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi text on this box
what: on this box's ffmpeg 6.1 the same .ass file drew Noto Nastaliq Urdu as boxes and broke Devanagari conjuncts (सिर्फ → सरि्फ, श्री → शरी) through `subtitles=`, but rendered both correctly through `ass=` (our 6.1 `subtitles` has no shaping option; complex shaping is "required for correct rendering of complex scripts such as Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari"). Complements skill 2836 (Nastaliq needs complex shaping)
how: burn Urdu/Hindi captions with `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "ass=caps.ass:fontsdir=library/fonts:shaping=complex" out.mp4`, never `subtitles=` (tested here 2026-10-24, T32/T33 vs T34)

name: drawtext cannot draw Nastaliq
section: Rendering Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi text on this box
what: drawtext's `text_shaping` (needs libfribidi) only reverses RTL order and joins Arabic letters; with Noto Nastaliq Urdu, Gulzar, Lateef and Scheherazade New it printed empty boxes or nothing, Mirza half-broken. Those fonts map almost no Arabic Presentation Forms (Noto Nastaliq Urdu 0 of U+FE70-FEFF), which the fribidi path needs
how: don't use drawtext for Urdu Nastaliq; render the line in Chrome/HyperFrames or PIL+Raqm and overlay the PNG (tested here 2026-10-24, T25 + fontTools count)

name: drawtext also breaks Hindi conjuncts and the i-matra
section: Rendering Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi text on this box
what: `drawtext` with Mukta drew "सिर्फ ₹499" as "सरि्फ ₹499" (pre-base ि in the wrong place, half-form not joined), though plain "शादी मुबारक" looked fine
how: for any Hindi with ि, reph or conjuncts (क्ष, श्री) use the `ass` filter (5121) or a Chrome/PIL PNG; keep drawtext for Latin/Roman Urdu (tested here 2026-10-24, T07)

how: `drawtext=fontfile=NotoNaskhArabic.ttf:textfile=ur.txt:fontsize=48:borderw=3:x=(w-tw)/2:y=h-90` (UTF-8 text in a file avoids shell quoting) (tested here 2026-10-24, T04)

name: Loop a still title before fading it
section: Rendering Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi text on this box

name: Shaadi = Nikah + Walima at its core
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: a typical Pakistani wedding (shaadi) consists of two main events, the Nikah (contract) and the Walima (reception); the other functions vary by ethnicity and family
how: build the full film around those two anchors and slot the optional functions before them; write an ffmetadata chapter file and `ffmpeg -i film.mp4 -i chapters.txt -map_metadata 1 -map_chapters 1 -c copy out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24, T08)

name: Chapter names in the client's words
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: Pakistani pages name the steps mangni/nisbat (engagement), dholki, rasm-e-heena/mehndi, baraat, nikah, rukhsati, walima
how: use these exact Roman Urdu labels as chapter titles and section cards (`title=Mehndi` in the ffmetadata file) (tested here 2026-10-24, T08)

name: Mangni: rings, dua, sweets
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: at the engagement rings are exchanged (traditionally placed on the bride by the groom's mother or sister, now usually by the couple), then a dua and blessings are recited and the wedding date is fixed
how: mark ring placement and the dua as must-have moments; let the dua play with music ducked or out

name: Dholki is often folded into the mehndi
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: dholki (named after the drum) was many nights of women singing at the bride's house; today it is often one night and often combined with the Rasm-e-Heena
how: ask whether it was a separate night; if combined, cut it as the opening sequence of the Mehndi chapter, not its own chapter

name: Mehndi: two possible hosts
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: some regions hold two Rasm-e-Heena functions, one by the groom's family and one by the bride's; others none
how: label them "Mehndi (Larki wale)" / "Mehndi (Larke wale)" so the family can find each

name: Mehndi rituals to catch
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: married women close to the bride apply henna and feed her sweets (for luck and long married life); performances and family-vs-family competitions are common, and men now take part
how: cover rasm (henna + sweets) as one sequence, then each performance as its own beat-cut block

name: Hidden initials in the bride's mehndi
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: designs often hide the bride's and groom's names/initials, and the groom may be challenged to find them
how: shoot a macro of the hidden initial and slowly push in on it in the edit: `zoompan=z='1+on*0.0015':x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps=30` (tested here 2026-10-24, T20)

name: Mehndi detail list
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: arrive early for henna-stained hands, decorations and anticipation; overhead shots of application, shooting through hanging decor, low angles on the dance floor, reflective surfaces (mirrors, water, glass), lanterns and fabrics as backdrops
how: when logging footage, tag these shot types so the mehndi sequence can alternate wide energy with detail inserts (contact sheet every 0.4 s, repo recipe)

name: Keep henna brown
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the standard colour of mehndi is brown (white, red, black and gold designs exist)
how: after any warm grade, check a henna close-up hasn't turned orange: compare frames with `npx hyperframes grade-compare --for frame.png` (repo)
refs: repo: CLAUDE.md "Editing a phone video" step 4

name: Doodh pilai
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the bride's family (usually her younger sister) presents the groom a decorated glass of milk; he sips, passes it to the bride, and must pay for it
how: cut it as a short playful scene with natural audio (the bargaining is the story) between Baraat arrival and Rukhsati

name: Door blocked at the baraat
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the bride's sisters, cousins and friends block the entrance and let the groom in only for money
how: cover both sides (sisters and groom's party) for a back-and-forth cut; it plays as comic relief before the nikah

name: Joota chupai
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the bride's sisters/cousins hide the groom's shoes and return them for money (in Hindu/Sikh weddings when he takes them off before the mandap or gurdwara)
how: shoot the theft early and the payoff at departure; place both in order so the joke lands

name: Nikah: signing with witnesses
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the nikahnama is signed by bride and groom before close family, performed by a (government-licensed) religious scholar, with two witnesses each
how: get close-ups of both signatures and the witnesses; keep this sequence quiet and unhurried

name: Family group photos right after the Nikah
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: dedicate time to posed family groups immediately after the Nikah; key relatives matter a lot
how: in the full film include a short posed-group montage after the Nikah chapter so every key relative appears

name: Rukhsati is the emotional peak
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the bride's farewell from her family; the doli marks her leaving, games are juxtaposed with the parents' sadness, and the Qur'an is held over her head as she leaves
how: let rukhsati carry the slowest pacing and softest music of the film; the Qur'an-over-head walk is the hero shot

name: Black-and-white for farewell moments
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: B&W has a place in Indian weddings for emotional moments like the vidaai, bridal entry or father-daughter dance
how: quick version `-vf hue=s=0` (tested); for a better mono see existing skill #254 (tested here 2026-10-24, T11)

name: Walima: the public reception
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: hosted by husband and wife (costs usually borne by the groom's side), it makes the marriage public; once at home, now in halls, restaurants or hotels
how: treat it as the "elegant" chapter: formal couple portraits and group photos, slower cuts than baraat

name: Turban ceremony for the groom
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: in some regions elders place a turban on the groom's head, formally including him in the "circle of men"
how: if it happens, it's a strong opening for the groom-side story; capture the elders' hands and the groom's face together

name: Baloch weddings are short
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: Baloch weddings are lavish and take one or two days; Jol Bandi opens them (the bride covered with a decorated cloth sewn by the groom's family), money is held over the bride's head at the henna
how: for a 1-2 day wedding plan a single highlight with no per-event chapters; capture the Jol Bandi cloth reveal

name: Pashtun weddings: Attan at the end
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: the Attan dance is usually performed at the end of the marriage ceremonies (traditionally at both start and end)
how: reserve the Attan for the closing montage of a Pashtun wedding film

name: Sindhi pre-wedding songs
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: in Sindhi customs ladies sing sehra/lada/geech folk songs at the mangno and during the wanah period
how: record these songs clean (they are family-sung, not copyrighted releases) and use them as the film's live-audio bed; check consent per 5109 of skills2/19

name: Bold reds, golds, greens, blues
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: Pakistani weddings are full of these colours in decor and attire; the photographer's job is to highlight them
how: measure average saturation before and after your grade so the grade doesn't mute the clothes: `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vf signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.SATAVG:file=- -f null -` (tested here 2026-10-24, T39)

name: Grade each event on its own
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: lighting swings from bright outdoor mehndi to dim indoor receptions; consistency across events must be worked for
how: grade per chapter (pick the grade on a real frame of each event with `npx hyperframes grade-compare`), then check skin matches across chapters
refs: repo: CLAUDE.md "Editing a phone video" step 4

name: Swirling dupattas and motion blur
section: Pakistani wedding events: structure and coverage
what: slow shutter for swirling dupattas and the dhol beat; intentional motion blur and light flares are used for sangeet performances and baraat entries
how: add blur in post on fast dance shots: `-vf tmix=frames=5` (tested here 2026-10-24, T12)

name: Punjabi wedding chapter template
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: pre-wedding: Roka, Kurmai, Sangeet, Mehndi, Mayian, Haldi, Jaggo; wedding day: Milni, Varmala, Joota chupai; post-wedding: Vidaai, Reception, Phera Dalna
how: start every Punjabi project from this chapter list and delete what didn't happen

name: Roka and Chunni Chadana
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: Roka ("to stop") unites the families, gifts like fruit and sweets are exchanged; in Chunni Chadana the groom's family drapes a chunni on the bride to welcome her
how: the chunni drape is the hero moment of a Roka reel

name: Kurmai: phulkari, tikka, rings
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the bride is draped in a phulkari (often an heirloom), a dot of henna goes on her palm, the bride's father applies a tikka to the groom, rings and sweets follow
how: shoot the heirloom phulkari as a detail insert and mention it in a caption

name: Sangeet: "sung together"
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: historically a female-only evening of folk songs and Giddha; now in bigger venues with men joining
how: cut each performance to its own song on the beat; keep a few wide shots of the whole family singing

name: Mayian / Vatna / Haldi
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: one day before a Punjabi wedding the bride/groom sits on a wooden patri under a red cloth held by four female relatives while married women rub turmeric, flour and mustard-oil paste on face, arms and legs, singing; usually in the morning
how: plan this as a daylight, close-up-heavy sequence; the red cloth overhead makes a natural top frame

name: Four diyas lit for the bride
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: four lamps are lit and oil keeps being poured so their glow reflects on her face
how: expose for the face lit by the diyas; this is a natural warm close-up for the haldi chapter opener

name: Choora and kaleeras
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the bride's maternal uncle gifts red (and ivory/white) bangles; relatives tie kaleeras; after the wedding the bride shakes the kaleeras over unmarried girls, and whoever a piece falls on is said to marry next
how: run the kaleera shake in slow motion (repo minterpolate recipe) and cut to the girl's reaction

name: Ghara gharoli
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: a sibling's spouse fills a decorated pitcher at a nearby temple and the bride is bathed with it, then dresses in wedding attire (also at the groom's house)
how: a short transition sequence from haldi to getting ready

name: Jaggo is a night procession
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: in the last hours of the night, the maternal aunt carries a brass vessel with lit clay lamps on her head while another woman shakes a stick with bells, moving house to house with dancing and fireworks; also practised in Pakistan
how: treat it as a low-light sequence: keep the lamps as the key light and let the bells/fireworks carry the sound

name: Groom-side morning: sehrabandi, varna, ghodi chadna
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the groom's sister ties the sehra (everyone gives gifts), his bhabi lines his eyes with surma, cash is waved to ward off the evil eye, sisters feed and adorn the mare, then he rides off
how: cut these four in order as the groom's "getting ready" act

name: The sarbala
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: a young nephew/cousin dressed like the groom accompanies him
how: a matching two-shot (groom + sarbala) is a reliable cute insert

name: Milni: introductions by seniority
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: senior male relatives of both families are introduced and exchange garlands; shagun is given in descending order of age
how: cut the pairs in the order they happened (oldest first) — families notice the order

name: Varmala: the lift
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the bride traditionally places the varmala first; friends playfully lift the bride or groom so the other can't reach
how: slow-motion the lift and the garland landing; it's a teaser-worthy beat

name: Hindu ceremony order for the mandap chapter
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: Ganesh pooja; the bride brought in by her maternal uncle (antarpat held before the groom); varmala; kanyadaan; offerings to agni and the pheras; sindoor in the hair parting; mangalsutra; exchange of sweets; touching elders' feet
how: use this order as sub-chapters of the ceremony so nothing is cut out of sequence

name: Sindoor Daan
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the groom first applies sindoor to the bride on the wedding day; afterwards she applies it herself daily, as the mark of a married woman
how: a tight close-up of the first application is the ceremony's key insert

name: Anand Karaj: four laavaan, gurdwara only
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the Sikh ceremony has four laavaan (hymns) while the couple walks around the Guru Granth Sahib; Sikh authorities say it can take place only in a gurdwara, not destination/resort venues
how: make four sub-chapters, one per laav; plan no destination-venue ceremony shots

name: Vidaai
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the bride throws puffed rice over her head as wishes for her parents, says goodbye, relatives throw coins after the procession, and the mother-in-law circles a glass of water around her
how: shoot the rice throw from behind the bride toward the family; cut the vidaai slow with B&W as an option (5220)

name: Bengali chapter set
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: Gaye Holud (turmeric, the groom's family visits the bride's house in the morning), Mala Badal (garland exchange), Sindoor Daan at the chadnatala, Bou Bhat (the groom's family introduces the bride at a reception)
how: use these names, not Punjabi ones, for Bengali clients

name: Baraat shot list
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: the groom travels to the venue with family and friends, once on a mare/chariot/elephant, now often vintage cars; a band, dancers, fireworks and the dhol; the groom carries a sword and usually doesn't dance (the baraatis do); he's welcomed with garlands, tilak, aarti and shehnai/nadaswaram
how: split coverage: groom stillness vs baraati energy, and intercut them

name: Ask about ritual timings first
section: Indian, Punjabi, Sikh and Bengali wedding events
what: photographers now consult families or priests to understand rituals and their timings, documenting the meaning, not just the action (saat phere to nikah)
how: before the wedding, get a timed ritual list and turn it into the chapter skeleton (5229/5205)

name: 30-60 s Instagram highlight is standard
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: Indian wedding content is designed for Instagram: short 30-60 s highlight reels with transitions, trending audio and captions; some teams have dedicated social-media editors
how: cut a 9:16 reel version alongside the film: `-vf "crop=ih*9/16:ih"` (tested here 2026-10-24, T23)

name: Teaser: pop in the first 3 seconds
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: teasers are vertical 9:16 for Reels/TikTok/Shorts, transitions shouldn't drag and the grade should "pop" in the first 3 seconds
how: `-vf "crop=ih*9/16:ih,eq=saturation=1.3"` on the opening shots, then check skin (tested here 2026-10-24, T23)

name: SDE delivered by big screen and WhatsApp
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: same-day edits are shown on big screens at the event or sent to guests via WhatsApp
how: export a full-quality screen copy and a WhatsApp copy (`-c:v libx264 -crf 23 -preset slow -c:a aac -b:a 160k -movflags +faststart`, repo recipe)
refs: repo: CLAUDE.md "Editing a phone video" step 8

name: SDE: ~3 minutes by dinner
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: the editor works on site, imports clips as they're shot and makes a ~3-minute piece by dinner time
how: lock a 3:00 music bed first and fill it; don't start a longer cut on the day

name: SDE: transcode while you shoot
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: copy cards to the laptop through the day and batch-convert to an edit codec (one videographer converts H.264 to ProRes LT continuously, even in the car)
how: `ffmpeg -i card/MVI_0001.MP4 -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 1 -c:a pcm_s16le edit/MVI_0001.mov` in a background loop (profile 1 = lt) (tested here 2026-10-24, T09)

name: SDE: transfer only the seconds you'll use, named by sequence
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: mark ins/outs and bring in only the 2 s you need, labelled bride_dress_1, bride_dress_2…; labelling does much of the editing
how: `ffmpeg -ss 12 -i card/MVI_0042.MP4 -t 2 -c copy sde/bride_dress_1.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24, T10)

name: SDE: plan ~15 sequences ahead
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: map out about 15 sequences that will fill the SDE (bride make-up, groom dressing, etc.) and brief the other shooters so angles match
how: for a desi wedding name them by ritual (mehndi hands, sehrabandi, baraat arrival, nikah signing, rukhsati) and create the empty folders before the day

name: SDE: transcode the key moments first
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: capture/transcode the main moments (entrance, vows, rings, announcement) first and the long speeches last
how: order the transcode queue by your ritual list (nikah signing and rukhsati first)

name: SDE: budget the render
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: one editor's 4-minute SDE took about 20 minutes to export at 720p and 30 at 1080p; travel and render time must be counted before you start
how: time a test export of 30 s on your machine early in the day and scale it

name: BTS reels from the wedding
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: couples ask for unfiltered behind-the-scenes: make-up sessions, outfit trials, bloopers and pre-function jitters edited into informal reels
how: tag BTS clips while logging and cut a separate light reel (Roman Urdu captions)

name: Documentary pre-wedding shoots
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: instead of choreographed poses: a day in the life, walking through a market, cooking at home, revisiting the college where they met
how: cut it like a mini-doc with natural sound; save music for transitions

name: Cinematic film with interviews
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: offerings now include script-writing, couple interviews and mini-docs featuring family members, plus voiceovers and drone shots
how: record short family interviews (Urdu/Hindi), transcribe with Whisper, subtitle with the `ass` filter (5121) (tested here 2026-10-24, T32/T33)

name: Film-style muted look
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: a growing trend is film-style images: muted colours, grainy textures, natural light
how: lower saturation and add temporal grain: `-vf "eq=saturation=0.85,noise=alls=8:allf=t"` (tested here 2026-10-24, see T40)

name: Mehndi motifs as the film's graphic language
section: Teasers, reels and same-day edits for desi weddings
what: common mehndi motifs are flowers, vines and leaves, paisleys, peacocks, mandalas, religious symbols and hidden names/initials; South Asian designs are small, intricate patterns and lines
how: draw section-card ornaments from these motifs (paisley, peacock, vine) rather than generic Western florals, and pull the colour from the henna close-up

name: Qawwali party = shot list
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: a qawwali party is usually eight or nine men: lead singer, one or two side singers, one or two harmoniums, tabla and dholak, and a chorus of four or five who repeat key verses and clap; front row singers + harmoniums, back row chorus + percussion
how: cover lead singer, harmonium hands, tabla/dholak hands and the clapping chorus separately so you can cut on claps

name: Qawwali builds from gentle to very high energy
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: qawwalis begin gently and build steadily to a very high energy level
how: let shot length shrink as the piece builds: find the hits with `npx hyperframes audio song.wav` and cut every 2 beats late in the piece vs every 2 bars early

name: Qawwali sections for chapters
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: songs usually open with an instrumental prelude (melody on harmonium with tabla), then the alap (long improvised notes in the raga), then preamble verses before the main song
how: mark prelude/alap/verses as chapters or cut points; an excerpt for a reel can start at the end of the alap

name: Qawwalis are long
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the longest commercial qawwali runs slightly over 115 minutes and Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan has songs over 60 minutes
how: never plan to use a whole qawwali; pick one section boundary to the next (5265)

name: Qawwali is devotional
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: traditionally performed at Sufi shrines (dargahs) to invoke remembrance of God and spiritual ecstasy
how: ask the client before cutting a qawwali under party/dance footage; for mehndi dances use dhol/dholak music instead

name: Keherwa: the 8-beat grid
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: 8 beats in two divisions; sam (beat 1) starts the cycle, khali (beat 5) is waved; theka "dha ge na ti | na ka dhi na"; qawwali is one of its variations
how: cycle length = 8×60/BPM; at 96 BPM a cycle is 5.0 s, so cut on sam every 5.0 s: `python3 -c "bpm=96;cyc=8*60/bpm;print([round(i*cyc,3) for i in range(8)])"` (tested here 2026-10-24, T18)

name: Teentaal: the 16-beat grid
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the most common Hindustani taal: 16 beats in 4×4, claps on 1, 5 and 13, a wave on 9 (khali); used for fast (drut) tempo
how: cycle = 16×60/BPM (10.0 s at 96 BPM); put big transitions on sam (beat 1) and quieter cuts on khali (beat 9): `cyc=16*60/bpm`, khali at `cyc/2` (tested here 2026-10-24, T18)

name: Pick the dhol rhythm by scene
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: common dhol rhythms are bhangra, dhamaal (associated with Sufi devotional dance) and kaharva (also called luddi); since the 1990s Punjabi pop evoking bhangra used kaharva
how: baraat/bhangra energy → bhangra/kaharva dhol; shrine or Sufi content → dhamaal

name: Dhol = baraat
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: dhols are used in wedding processions such as the baraat; the baraat reaches the meeting point to the rhythm of the dhol
how: if live dhol audio was recorded at the baraat, use it under the arrival instead of a music track (clean it with clean_voice.py only if voices must stay)

name: Bhangra's sound
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the dhol (heavy beater on one side, light stick on the other) is bhangra's best-known instrument, with tumbi, sarangi, dholak and modern synth/guitar; dancers perform to short songs called boliyan; bhangra is tied to the Vaisakhi harvest festival
how: for Punjabi energy edits, cut on the dhol's heavy-beater hits

name: Luddi at weddings
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: a Punjabi circle dance with finger clicks, hand claps, jumps and half-turns, performed at weddings in both Punjabs to dhol and shehnai
how: a wide overhead of the circle plus tight clap inserts on the beat

name: Attan speeds up
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the Pashtun Attan, danced to a dohol, lasts 5-30 minutes and usually starts slow and finishes fast, with clapping in sync with the drums
how: compress it into a montage whose cut rate follows the drum tempo (long shots early, beat cuts at the end)

name: Dholak/dholki for mehndi nights
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the dholak is a two-headed hand drum used in qawwali, bhangra, Hindi film music and lokgeet; the dholki ceremony is named after it
how: a dholak-led track (or the family's live dholki) is the natural mehndi bed; the repo's romance-bollywood track has a dholak-style keherwa

name: Tabla: classical and qawwali
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: since the 18th century the tabla is the principal percussion of Hindustani classical music, one of the main qawwali instruments, and features in kathak
how: for elegant (walima, nikah) beds prefer tabla-led tracks over dhol; the repo has a CC0 "Electronic Indian tabla tune"

name: Shehnai welcomes the groom
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: in traditional baraats the groom is welcomed with shehnai or nadaswaram, considered auspicious at Hindu weddings; the shehnai (double-reed, A3-A5) was one of the nine instruments of the Mughal court
how: sketch a shehnai welcome cue with General MIDI program 112 "Shanai" (0-based 111) in FluidSynth: `mido.Message('program_change',program=111)` then `fluidsynth -ni -F cue.wav -r 44100 /usr/share/sounds/sf2/FluidR3_GM.sf2 cue.mid` (tested here 2026-10-24, T24)

name: GM sitar for quick desi mock-ups
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: General MIDI's ethnic group has Sitar at program 105 (0-based 104); the repo's Magenta arranger already writes for sitar, flute and dholak-style percussion
how: `mido` program_change 104 → `fluidsynth -ni -F out.wav -r 44100 /usr/share/sounds/sf2/FluidR3_GM.sf2 in.mid` (tested here 2026-10-24, T24)

name: Bansuri for romance
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the bansuri is a side-blown bamboo flute of the subcontinent (traditionally seven finger holes) used in many folk songs; the repo's "90s Bollywood romantic" track uses a bansuri melody with sitar intro
how: reuse `romance-bollywood-72bpm.wav` (owner-approved own music only when asked; see CLAUDE.md rule)

name: Alghoza for Sindhi films
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the alghoza (beenon) is a paired woodwind of Sindhi culture
how: for Sindhi wedding/heritage edits ask the family for live alghoza audio or search Freesound/Commons with licence checks

name: Tumbi and chimta for Punjabi colour
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the tumbi is a high-pitched one-string plucked instrument of Punjabi folk, popular in Western bhangra; the chimta (tongs with brass jingles) is used in Punjabi folk, bhangra and Gurbani kirtan
how: when choosing a Punjabi track, these two timbres signal "Punjab" even without vocals

name: No-credit desi music already in the repo
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: 29 CC0 tracks include a desi/eastern set (electronic Indian tabla tune, electric piano with sitar style, oriental, desert pieces)
how: check `library/music/cc0/README.md` before searching the web (owner rule: CC0/PD only)

name: Real desi field recordings with licences checked
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: the repo's research lists Freesound items such as Damal drumming in Pakistan (Lahore, 2:29) and Hindu wedding ceremony music (2:56), and found no CC0/PD Urdu/Pashto songs with vocals anywhere
how: for vocals, make them with the repo tools (ai_song.py) only if the owner asks; otherwise instrumental beds

name: Old film songs are not public domain
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: 1940s-50s film songs are still under copyright (lyricist/composer life + 60 years in India/Pakistan)
how: never rip filmi classics for client work; the owner rule forbids copyrighted songs

name: Bollywood songs dominate Indian music
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: Bollywood soundtracks account for nearly 80% of India's music revenue; films usually have six to ten songs
how: "trending audio" on Indian reels is mostly film songs: don't bake them into exports; deliver with a no-credit bed and let the client pick app audio themselves

name: Playback = audio is the master
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: in South Asian cinema songs are pre-recorded by playback singers and actors lip-sync to them
how: for lip-sync or song-picturisation reels lay the final audio first and cut picture to it, never the reverse

name: Ghazal/shayari overlays
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: a ghazal has five to fifteen relatively independent couplet lines on love and separation; Bollywood lyrics draw heavily on Urdu poetry and the ghazal tradition
how: one couplet (two lines) per shot in Nastaliq via Chrome (5126), held for the length of one sung/recited line

name: Naat for Rabi ul Awwal / Ramadan content
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: naat is poetry in praise of the Prophet Muhammad, popular in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh in Urdu, Punjabi and Bengali
how: treat as devotional: slow, respectful visuals, no beat-cut gimmicks; ask whether the client wants voice-only

name: Coke Studio-style live sessions
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: Coke Studio Pakistan (Rohail Hyatt, from 8 June 2008) is a multi-camera live-performance music show
how: for a multi-camera family/band performance, sync cameras by audio cross-correlation (numpy FFT xcorr found a 0.75 s offset exactly) and cut between musicians on phrase ends

name: Kathak coverage by gharana
section: Qawwali, folk and classical music for desi edits
what: Jaipur gharana stresses technical long pure-dance compositions with fast spins and footwork; Banaras footwork and Krishna stories; Lucknow grace and elegance
how: ask the dancer's style: for Jaipur get foot close-ups and spins (slow-mo), for Lucknow longer, wider takes

name: Masala structure for family films
what: masala films blend action, comedy, romance and drama/melodrama, are often musicals with songs in picturesque locations, and move the audience through moods (anger at villains, tears at loss, laughing at a clown, amazement at song sequences, happiness at the couple's union)
how: plan a "family film" edit as mood blocks in that order (tension → tears → comedy → song → union)

name: Song sequence in a scenic location
what: masala films typically include songs filmed in picturesque locations
how: a pre-wedding "song" edit = one scenic location per verse, lip-sync per 5286

name: The dance number goes in the trailer
what: item numbers don't add to plot continuity and are used in trailers to sell the film
how: in a wedding teaser lift the best family dance performance as the energy peak, even though it isn't in story order

name: Pakistan flag colours and proportions
what: 3:2, a white vertical stripe at the hoist one quarter of the length, the rest dark green; Pakistan green #00401A (RGB 0,64,26), Pantone 19-5917 TCX
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=0x00401A:s=960x640:d=1 -vf "drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=iw/4:h=ih:color=white:t=fill" -frames:v 1 pk_card.png` as a title background (tested here 2026-10-24, T16)

name: What the Pakistan flag stands for
what: green for the Muslim majority, the white stripe for religious minorities; crescent = progress, star = light and knowledge
how: use these meanings in Independence Day captions instead of inventing symbolism

name: India flag colours and proportions
what: 3:2, three equal bands; approximate RGB: India saffron #FF671F, white #FFFFFF, India green #046A38, navy #06038D (Pantone 165 C, 2258 C, 2735 C); Ashoka Chakra with 24 evenly spaced spokes
how: drawbox the bands (T17) and never use generic orange/green

name: Chakra size
what: the flag code doesn't fix it, but IS1's chart pairs a 6300×4200 mm flag with a 1295 mm chakra (≈0.31 of the height)
how: ring of diameter 0.31×H centred: geq ring `between(hypot(X-W/2,Y-H/2),H*0.135,H*0.155)` (tested here 2026-10-24, T17)

name: Indian flag display is regulated
what: display and use are governed by the Flag Code of India, 2002 and the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
how: before warping, cropping or costume-styling the flag in an edit, read the Flag Code

name: 14 August B-roll list
what: Pakistan's Independence Day colours are green and white; parades, award ceremonies, patriotic songs and the anthem, leaders' speeches, fireworks at Minar-e-Pakistan, candles lit at midnight, illuminated buildings, change-of-guard at monuments including Jinnah's tomb
how: use these as the shot list for a 14 Aug promo (FireCraft-style server promo too)

name: 14 August 1947 fell on 27 Ramadan
what: the night of 14-15 August 1947 coincided with 27 Ramadan 1366, which Muslims regard as a sacred night
how: a historically correct caption line for Independence Day films

name: 15 August B-roll list
what: India's Prime Minister raises the flag at the Red Fort (as Nehru did over the Lahori Gate in 1947) and addresses the nation, broadcast by Doordarshan; flag hoisting, parades, fireworks, patriotic songs and Jana Gana Mana across the country
how: shot list for 15 Aug content; render titles in Devanagari via 5121/5126

name: 26 January Republic Day
what: the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950; the main parade is on Kartavya Path in New Delhi and the President addresses the nation on the eve
how: schedule Indian clients' Republic Day posts for the morning of 26 Jan

name: 23 March Pakistan Day
what: commemorates the Lahore Resolution (1940) and the 1956 constitution; marked by a joint inter-services military parade and national honours, at Minar-e-Pakistan's site of the resolution
how: don't confuse with 14 August in captions; Minar-e-Pakistan imagery fits both

name: Chaand Raat content
what: on the eve of Eid al-Fitr families gather outdoors to spot the new moon, then wish "Eid Mubarak"; women and girls apply mehndi, desserts are made, last shopping happens, and malls/markets stay open late
how: for shops/salons this is the peak reel night: plan a moon-sighting opener and late-night market B-roll

name: Make two Eid versions
what: the Islamic month starts with the crescent sighting; Pakistan sometimes starts Ramadan a day later than the Gulf, and some regions celebrate Eid a day apart
how: export "Eid Mubarak" posts for both possible days and publish when the moon is announced

name: Eid al-Fitr basics for captions
what: 1 Shawwal, marks the end of Ramadan fasting; celebrations include Eid prayers, gift-giving (Eidi), family gatherings and festive meals; Wikipedia gives 9-11 March for 2027
how: plan Eidi/gift reels for shops in the days before

name: "Eid Mubarak" means blessed feast
what: an Arabic greeting used for both Eids, a cultural tradition rather than a religious obligation
how: set it in Urdu as عید مبارک in Nastaliq (Chrome) with Roman "Eid Mubarak" below

name: Eid al-Adha
what: commemorates Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son; celebrations include Eid prayers, animal sacrifice, Eidi and family meals (10-13 Dhu al-Hijjah)
how: for general audiences keep sacrifice footage out of thumbnails and hooks; focus on family and food

name: Ramadan TV formats
what: Pakistan's Ramadan media includes iftar and sehri transmissions, religious talk shows, cooking programmes and game shows
how: for creators, sehri/iftar-timed cooking and Q&A formats match what audiences already watch that month

name: Iftar timing for food reels
what: iftar is eaten just after the Maghrib call around sunset, traditionally starting with (three) dates and water; in South Asia fried snacks are popular
how: publish restaurant/food-shop iftar reels an hour or two before sunset, opening on dates and the fried platter

name: Fanous lanterns as a Ramadan motif
what: the fanous as Ramadan decoration comes from medieval Egypt and has spread to many Muslim countries
how: lantern shapes/bokeh for Ramadan title cards

name: Star and crescent
what: the green star-and-crescent is commonly used as a symbol of Islam (and is on Pakistan's flag)
how: crescent graphics for Eid/Independence cards; keep the star five-pointed as on the flag

name: Diwali 2026 is five days, 6-10 November
what: Dhanteras (6), Naraka Chaturdashi/Chhoti Diwali (7), Lakshmi Puja (8), Govardhan Puja (9), Bhai Dooj (10); celebrations: diya lighting, puja, rangoli, fireworks, gifts and sweets
how: plan a 5-post series, one per day

name: Diya emoji 🪔
what: DIYA LAMP was added to Unicode as U+1FA94 in 2019; on this box Chrome draws it in colour with Noto Color Emoji
how: `🪔` in HyperFrames captions (tested here 2026-10-24, T37)

name: Rangoli time-lapse
what: rangoli is made at the threshold of the main entrance in the early morning, most often for Diwali (also Onam, Pongal)
how: shoot top-down and speed up 8×: `ffmpeg -t 40 -i in.mp4 -vf setpts=PTS/8 -an tl.mp4` (put `-t` before `-i`, or it limits the output instead) (tested here 2026-10-24, T38)

name: Holi
what: the festival of colours: playing with coloured powder and water, with Holika Dahana the night before; on Phalguna's full moon, around mid-March
how: pair a night bonfire opener with the colour day; slow-mo the powder throws (repo minterpolate recipe)

name: Garba and dandiya
what: Navaratri's garba is danced in concentric circles around a pot with a flame (or an image of Amba); at the end of each night Gujaratis play dandiya raas with a stick in each hand, tapping a partner's
how: an overhead/high wide for the circles and close-ups of sticks striking on the beat

name: Basant = yellow and kites
what: Basant is celebrated across Punjab in India and Pakistan; kite flying grew under the Mughals at Lahore, and Ranjit Singh's court wore yellow for it
how: yellow-led palette and rooftop kite shots for Basant content

name: Kite fighting from rooftops
what: kite fighting festivals are notable in Gujarat, Bihar, UP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab; kites (patang) are flown in thousands at Makar Sankranti, from rooftops, trying to cut each other's lines
how: two-camera coverage (flyer + sky) and cut on the line-cut moment

name: Lohri dates
what: Lohri is the day before Maghi (Makar Sankranti), generally 13 or 14 January in the 21st century; it shifts over decades
how: confirm the year's date before scheduling Punjabi clients' Lohri posts

name: Raksha Bandhan
what: sisters tie a rakhi on brothers' wrists and receive a gift, on the last day of Shravana, typically in August
how: sibling reels for gift, sweet and jewellery shops in the week before

name: Karva Chauth: fast until moonrise
what: women fast from sunrise to moonrise for their husbands, on the fourth day of the waning moon in Kartika (north India)
how: the moonrise is the climax shot; plan a low-light sequence

name: Festival reels for local shops
what: Diwali reels let local businesses launch products, run educational content and build brand recall with just a phone camera
how: festival launch reel: product hero shot, one use tip, offer card

name: Truck art (phool patti) as Pakistani pop graphics
what: floral patterns, calligraphy, poetic verses, folklore, mirror work and carved doors; chains and pendants on bumpers make the "jingle"
how: borrow its flowers + calligraphy + bright frames for Pakistani street-style title cards; a chain-jingle SFX sells it
refs: Wikipedia: Truck art in South Asia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truck_art_in_South_Asia, checked 2026-10-24

name: Phulkari in Punjabi films
what: phulkari embroidery is part of Punjabi bridal trousseaux, passed between generations, and draped on the bride at the kurmai
how: use a phulkari close-up as a section background or transition texture in Punjabi wedding films

name: Ajrak palette
what: Sindhi block-printed ajrak centres on deep indigo and crimson, with white and black defining geometric motifs
how: start swatches from CSS indigo #4B0082 and crimson #DC143C (approximations, sample the real cloth if you have it): `color=c=indigo` / `color=c=crimson` (tested here 2026-10-24, T27)

name: Paisley = boteh/buta
what: a teardrop motif with a curved upper end, from Persia, spread via Mughal-era Kashmir shawls
how: paisley borders/ornaments for mehndi cards (ties to 5262)

name: Jali screens as frames
what: jali is a perforated stone/latticed screen with calligraphy, geometry or natural patterns, common in Indo-Islamic architecture
how: shoot through a jali for foreground framing or patterned light at Mughal venues

name: Choora colours
what: the bridal chura is usually red and white
how: keep these reds from clipping in the grade (check with signalstats, 5226)

name: Kaleera details
what: kaleeras are tied to the bride's wrists by sisters, friends or maternal aunt, with dangling trinkets and bells around a dome shape
how: a macro with a soft bell sound effect is a natural transition into the kaleera-shake moment (5235)

name: Sehra words for captions
what: sehra in Urdu سہرا, Hindi सेहरा, Punjabi ਸੇਹਰਾ: a forehead garland of flowers or beads tied to the groom's turban; tying it is sehra bandi
how: use the client's script for the word in the caption

name: Sherwani + churidar
what: the sherwani is famous as a wedding outfit and is generally worn with churidar
how: groom detail inserts: buttons, collar, embroidery (the visualartistry list also names the groom's embroidered sherwani)

name: Lehenga embroidery
what: gota patti embroidery is often used on lehengas for festivals and weddings
how: a slow push-in on the embroidery (5211 zoompan) for the bride's outfit reveal

name: Dupatta draping
what: the dupatta is long and light for flow; worn over the shoulder, across the neck, or as a veil when entering a mandir; with shalwar kameez it forms a U or V
how: spin shots catch its flow; at religious moments it may be worn as a veil — don't crop it oddly

name: No TikTok in India
what: TikTok and 58 other Chinese-created apps (including Likee) were banned in India on 29 June 2020
how: for Indian audiences deliver for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and Indian apps (Moj, Josh), not TikTok

name: TikTok in Pakistan has been on/off
what: over 15 months up to November 2021 the PTA imposed and lifted four TikTok bans
how: for Pakistani clients always also deliver YouTube/Facebook/Instagram versions so a ban doesn't strand the campaign

name: YouTube Shorts began in India (history)
what: the Shorts beta opened in India on 15 September 2020 after the TikTok ban; since September 2024 vertical videos up to 3 minutes become Shorts (60 s before)
how: check duration ≤180 s: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 v.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24, T15)

name: Instagram Reels and captions
what: Instagram introduced Reels in August 2020 to compete with TikTok and added closed captions for Reels and Stories in May 2021
how: burn Urdu/Hindi captions in yourself (5121/5126) when the language or font matters; app captions can't do Nastaliq styling

name: Moj: Indian, multilingual
what: Moj (Mohalla Tech, ShareChat's parent) launched 29 June 2020, available in 12 languages incl. Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi and English
how: same 9:16 export as Reels; caption in the audience's language

name: Josh: "Instagram for Bharat"
what: Josh (VerSe Innovation) launched right after the June 2020 ban, focused on regional languages, with 150 million monthly users in April 2022; it has since evolved into a live call and chat app
how: check whether a client's "Josh" channel is still a short-video outlet before planning content for it

name: WhatsApp Status: 90 s pieces with forced keyframes
what: WhatsApp beta for Android 2.25.12.9 allows 90 s Status videos (from 60 s, earlier 30 s), rolling out gradually. Splitting with `-c copy` gave 100 s pieces because cuts snap to keyframes
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -force_key_frames "expr:gte(t,n_forced*90)" -c:a aac -f segment -segment_time 90 -reset_timestamps 1 status_%02d.mp4` → 90/90/20 s (tested here 2026-10-24, T13/T13b)

name: Status limits change: keep the splitter parametric
what: in 2020 WhatsApp temporarily cut Status videos in India to 15 seconds (and Facebook/others dropped to 480p) to save bandwidth
how: same command with `n_forced*15` / `-segment_time 15` produced three 15 s parts (tested here 2026-10-24, T30)

name: Google Business Profile video spec
what: up to 30 seconds, up to 75 MB, 720p or higher
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -t 30 -vf scale=-2:720 -c:v libx264 -crf 23 -movflags +faststart gbp.mp4` (40 s 720p test → 30 s, well under 75 MB) (tested here 2026-10-24, T14)

name: Google Business Profile photos
what: JPG or PNG, 10 KB-5 MB, recommended 720×720 px, minimum 250×250
how: export shop stills square: `ffmpeg -ss 1 -i v.mp4 -vf "crop=ih:ih,scale=720:720" -frames:v 1 -q:v 3 gbp.jpg` (tested here 2026-10-24, T36)

name: GBP media shows only after review/verification
what: media stays "pending" while processing or if the profile isn't verified, and can take 24-48 hours to appear; flagged media doesn't show
how: tell shop clients to verify the profile first and allow two days before announcing the video

name: Show the product in real use
what: a kurta in natural light, a necklace with an outfit, a food serving size, a notebook in use: a product shown in use answers questions a photo can't
how: each shop reel needs at least one "in use" shot before the price card

name: Start with the interesting part
what: instead of a long introduction, start with the interesting part, and don't list every fabric, colour, size and offer in one video
how: first shot = the product's best moment; one offer per reel

name: Real over polished for small brands
what: a founder speaking to camera, a customer using the product, packaging, a busy counter, the making process or behind-the-scenes can feel more believable than staged shots
how: mix one founder-to-camera line with process B-roll; light grade only

name: Festival and wedding hooks only when natural
what: festivals, weddings, family routines and regional styles give ideas, but there's no need to add a festival to every video; ask of a trend "can this work for us?"
how: jewellery → wedding season, food → family gatherings; skip unrelated trends

name: Consistency is a schedule, not daily posting
what: post on a schedule you keep, then see which formats get better responses and make more of those
how: propose a fixed weekly slot to shop clients and batch-edit 4 reels per session

name: Owner on camera, no flashy editing
what: a local Indian camera shop with 220k+ followers posts plain video reels featuring the owner, a niche range (DJI, GoPro, warranties, EMI) and influencer giveaways (one giveaway reel got 2.6 million views)
how: for shop clients put the owner in the hook and keep edits simple; a giveaway reel needs a clear prize shot and rules card

name: Local discovery: geotag, WhatsApp link, short demos
what: reels paired with geotags help local people discover a shop; add the area name, hours and a direct WhatsApp link in the bio; post short ~15-second product demos or shop activity
how: cut 15 s demo versions (`-t 15`) alongside the main reel and remind the client to geotag

name: Mangalsutra rasam
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: after the sindoor, the groom ties a black-bead and gold necklace (mangalsutra) on the bride; then sweets are exchanged and elders' feet touched
how: cover hands + clasp in a close-up and the bride's face in a second angle; this pair closes the ceremony chapter (5242)

name: Who ties the sehra differs
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: in Punjabi Hindu weddings the groom's sister ties it (sehrabandi); in the Dogra tradition the maternal uncle does
how: ask the family who ties it so you're on the right person's face when it happens (sequence order 5238)

name: The mehndi-darkness joke
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: a common superstition says the darker the bride's mehndi turns, the more her mother-in-law loves her
how: a ready-made Roman Urdu/Hindi caption line for the next-day mehndi colour reveal shot

name: Bengali Muslim walima = Bou Bhat
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: Wikipedia captions the Bou Bhat as the Bengali version of the walima
how: for Bengali Muslim clients, title the reception chapter "Bou Bhat" if that's what the family calls it (chapter file, T08)

name: Walima timing varies
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: scholars differ on when the walima should be (at the contract, after it, at the bride's procession; the majority hold after the marriage is consummated) and cultures differ
how: never assume the walima is "day 3": take the date and order from the family's schedule before building chapters

name: Second Eid greeting
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: besides "Eid Mubarak", the Prophet's companions greeted each other with "Taqabbalallahu minna wa minkum" (May God accept from us and you)
how: an alternative end-card line for religious clients (Arabic in Amiri/Noto Naskh via Chrome)

name: Kite strings cut people
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: fighting-kite strings are made abrasive to cut competitors' lines and can also injure people
how: on Basant/Sankranti rooftop shoots keep crew, cables and any drone well clear of flying lines and shoot the fights from the side

name: Poppins is a Devanagari font too
section: More wedding, festival and font details
what: Google's 5th most popular family (Indian Type Foundry, Jonny Pinhorn, Ninad Kale; 18 styles) includes Devanagari: 56/60 checked letters, ₹ present, and "क्षत्रिय श्री" shaped correctly in Chrome
how: one family for Latin + Hindi lines in Hinglish brand promos

name: Box edge that shows on any background
what: drawbox `color=invert` draws the edge with the video's inverted luma, so a framing box stays visible on bright and dark shots
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawbox=x=100:y=60:w=200:h=120:color=invert:t=4" -frames:v 1 box.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Highlight box only for a time range
what: drawbox supports the generic `enable` timeline option, so a "look here" box can appear only from 1 s to 2 s
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawbox=x=200:y=100:w=200:h=120:c=yellow:t=6:enable='between(t,1,2)'" -an out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Box sized from the picture's own aspect
what: drawbox x/y/w/h/t are expressions that can use iw, ih, dar, sar and each other, e.g. `h=w/dar` keeps the box in the frame's display aspect
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawbox=x=20:y=20:w=iw/2:h=w/dar:c=cyan:t=3" -frames:v 1 box.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Punch a transparent window into an RGBA layer
what: with an alpha input, drawbox `replace=1` overwrites colour and alpha instead of compositing, so a `black@0` filled box cuts a fully transparent hole (checked here: pixel inside = (0,0,0,0), outside alpha 255)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "format=rgba,drawbox=x=220:y=120:w=200:h=120:c=black@0:t=fill:replace=1" -frames:v 1 hole.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Jump a box to new positions at set times
what: drawbox accepts its options as commands, so sendcmd can move it at 1 s and 2 s without re-running
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "sendcmd=c='1.0 drawbox x 300;2.0 drawbox x 450',drawbox=x=20:y=150:w=120:h=60:c=lime:t=fill" -an out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Rule-of-thirds overlay on a review copy
what: drawgrid with cells of iw/3 x ih/3 draws a 3x3 grid; the docs example uses white@0.5 and t=2
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawgrid=w=iw/3:h=ih/3:t=2:c=white@0.5" review.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Pixel measuring grid
what: a fixed 100x100 px drawgrid helps read positions for overlay/drawtext x and y values from a still
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawgrid=width=100:height=100:thickness=2:color=red@0.5" -frames:v 1 grid.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Offset grid in inverted colour
what: drawgrid x/y set one grid intersection (an offset), and `c=invert` uses inverted luma so the lines read on any picture
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "drawgrid=x=50:y=30:w=64:h=64:t=1:c=invert" -frames:v 1 g.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Weighted top/bottom margin fill
what: fillborders `mode=margins` fills top and bottom rows with weighted averages of pixels near the borders
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "fillborders=top=10:bottom=10:mode=margins" out.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Bucket-fill a flat area
what: floodfill replaces the connected region at (x,y) whose components equal s0..s3 with d0..d3, like a paint-bucket on flat graphics. In the test on rgba input the d values landed in G,B,R,A order (planar gbrap), so check the result colour
how: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=c=white:s=320x180,drawbox=x=100:y=50:w=120:h=80:c=black:t=4,format=rgba" -vf "floodfill=x=5:y=5:s0=255:s1=255:s2=255:s3=255:d0=0:d1=128:d2=255:d3=255" -frames:v 1 fill.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Graph brightness over a whole clip as one picture
what: drawgraph plots a frame-metadata key; feeding it signalstats YAVG with `slide=picture` gives a single graph of average luma (flicker and exposure jumps show at a glance)
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "signalstats,drawgraph=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:min=0:max=255:slide=picture:size=640x200" -frames:v 1 -update 1 yavg.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Two metrics as a scrolling graph video
what: drawgraph takes up to four keys (m1..m4) with fg colours as 0xAABBGGRR, `mode` line/bar/dot and `slide` scroll
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "signalstats,drawgraph=m1=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:fg1=0xff00ff00:m2=lavfi.signalstats.SATAVG:fg2=0xff0000ff:min=0:max=255:slide=scroll:mode=line:size=640x200" -an graph.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Momentary loudness as a graph video
what: adrawgraph draws audio frame metadata; ebur128 with `metadata=1` exports lavfi.r128.M (the docs example)
how: `ffmpeg -i mix.wav -filter_complex "ebur128=metadata=1,adrawgraph=lavfi.r128.M:min=-70:max=5:slide=scroll:size=640x240" graph.mp4` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Debug a stuck filtergraph visually
what: graphmonitor (and agraphmonitor for audio) draws each link's queued frames, pts, format and size; `mode=compact` shows only links with queued frames. Useful when a complex graph stalls or eats RAM
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex "[0:v]split[a][b];[b]boxblur=10,graphmonitor=flags=queue+pts+format+size:mode=compact[g];[a]scale=1280:720[s];[s][g]overlay" -an mon.mp4`; audio: `[0:a]asplit[a][b];[b]agraphmonitor=s=640x360:flags=queue+sample_count_in[v]` (both tested here 2026-10-24)

name: Canny edges on chosen planes only
what: edgedetect `mode=canny` applies the detector to the selected planes (`planes` bitmask; 1 = first plane) and copies the rest
how: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "edgedetect=mode=canny:planes=1" -frames:v 1 e.png` (tested here 2026-10-24)

name: 3x3 sharpen kernel
what: convolution takes a 3x3/5x5/7x7 matrix per plane; the docs sharpen is `0 -1 0 -1 5 -1 0 -1 0`

name: Laplacian edge map with bias
what: after the four matrices, convolution takes rdiv per plane then bias per plane; the docs laplacian (with diagonals) uses rdiv 5 and bias 128 so negative values stay visible

name: 5x5 kernels
what: convolution also takes 25-value (5x5) and 49-value (7x7) matrices; with rdiv unset it divides by the sum of the matrix, so a 1-4-6-4-1 binomial kernel is a smooth blur without writing a divisor

name: Edge-enhance kernel
what: the docs edge-enhance matrix `0 0 0 -1 1 0 0 0 0` with rdiv 5:1:1:1 and bias 0:128:128:128

name: One-direction blur with a 1-D kernel
what: convolution `Nmode=row` (horizontal) or `column` (vertical) takes 1 to 49 odd elements, e.g. nine 1s for a horizontal-only smear
